families.name: Infrastructure manager: assets, maintenance and construction
Corporate functions, safety, education and research

roles.name: Federal Minister of Transport
roles.organisation: Federal Ministry of Transport (Bundesministerium für Verkehr, BMV), Berlin and Bonn; the EBA and the BEU belong to its portfolio (the BNetzA to the economics ministry's)
roles.summary: Heads the federal ministry that finances the federal railway infrastructure, steers the Bund's 100 % ownership of Deutsche Bahn AG and supervises the EBA and the BEU. Sets federal rail policy (Deutschlandtakt, the Generalsanierung corridor renewals, digitalisation, the Bund's share of the Deutschlandticket) and answers to the Bundestag and the public for the state of the railway.
decisions: Propose the split of the federal rail money in the cabinet's draft budget: renewal (LuFV), new and upgraded lines (Bedarfsplan under the BSWAG), digitalisation (ETCS, digital interlockings), charge subsidies; the Bundestag has the last word
Agree with DB InfraGO the corridor programme of the Generalsanierung, its order and its months of full closure
Push for changes in DB's supervisory board or board of management through the Bund's representatives (shareholder rights, not instructions)

Choose between grants (Baukostenzuschüsse) and equity injections into DB: equity counts as a financial transaction outside the debt brake but raises DB InfraGO's capital base and so the track access charges
Negotiate the Bund's share of the Deutschlandticket and the growth of the Regionalisierungsmittel with the Länder; the ticket price itself is set by the Länder transport ministers' conference
Decide which draft laws (AEG, ERegG, BSWAG and Bedarfsplan amendments, planning acceleration, the steering of DB InfraGO) the ministry takes to cabinet
Defend rail against road and other ministries in the cabinet's budget round under the debt brake
Respond to a crisis (strike, serious accident, summer of delays) with a statement, a summit or a measure
effects: The network's condition and delay minutes 5 to 15 years later follow today's renewal money, not today's announcements
Closure programmes cut capacity for months and hurt operators and freight now, for fewer faults later
Charge subsidies and the Deutschlandticket move ridership and rail freight's share against road (rail carries about 19 % of tonne-km)
Board changes and reforms shape DB's priorities and the public's trust in the minister
Money promised beyond the debt brake triggers conflict with the finance minister and the budget committee
resources: Einzelplan 12 (transport) with federal rail infrastructure money of roughly €20-25 bn a year from the core budget and the special fund for infrastructure (Sondervermögen Infrastruktur und Klimaneutralität, €500 bn over 12 years for all sectors, of which €100 bn go to the Länder)
LuFV III replacement and maintenance agreement with DB InfraGO: €86 bn for 2020-2029 (about €62 bn from the Bund, €24 bn from DB), about €8.6 bn a year; its successor from 2030 is being prepared
Regionalisierungsmittel of about €11-12 bn a year to the Länder (from the Bund's tax revenue, fixed in the RegG) plus €1.5 bn a year for the Deutschlandticket
A ministry of about 1,300-1,500 staff, two parliamentary and two to three permanent state secretaries
Shareholder rights of the Bund in DB AG (100 %) via the shareholder meeting and the Bund's seats on the supervisory board; legal and technical supervision of the EBA
Cabinet seat, party, media access
limits: Art. 87e GG (Bund's responsibility for the federal railways' network, infrastructure majority-owned by the Bund; para. 4: the public interest must be taken into account in building and maintaining the network) and Art. 106a GG (regionalised local rail)
Debt brake (Art. 109, 115 GG; special fund under Art. 143h GG) and the Federal Budget Code (BHO)
Aktiengesetz (§§ 76, 84, 111) and the Deutsche Bahn Gründungsgesetz: no direct instructions to the DB board, only through the supervisory board and the shareholder meeting
Directive 2012/34/EU and ERegG: independence of the infrastructure manager's essential functions (path allocation, charging)
EU state aid law (Art. 93, 107, 108 TFEU) for capital injections and charge subsidies
Bundesrat consent for laws touching the Länder (Regionalisierungsgesetz); coalition agreement
Bundesministergesetz (§§ 6a-6d): cooling-off period (Karenzzeit) of up to 18 months before lobby jobs
risks: Dismissal by the Chancellor or losing office at the next federal election
Constant public exposure for punctuality, closures and accidents; threats against politicians
Parliamentary committee of inquiry (Untersuchungsausschuss) after a failed project, as with the car toll
Bundesrechnungshof reports criticising the ministry's control of DB
Long working weeks, travel, little private life

career.entry: No formal qualification. A party career: usually years as MP or state minister, often spokesperson for transport or budget; appointed by the Federal President on the Chancellor's proposal after coalition talks.
career.chances: Official salary of about €20,000 a month plus half the MP allowance when also an MP (roughly €300,000 a year); average tenure 3-4 years; transitional allowance for up to two years after leaving; later board, association or consulting posts after the cooling-off period.

kpis: Punctuality of long-distance and regional trains
Network condition grade (DB InfraGO's Netzzustandsbericht) and LuFV quality targets
Money actually spent (Mittelabfluss) against the budget
Major projects on time and on budget
roles.timescale: Hours to days in a crisis, the yearly budget cycle, a 4-year legislature; the effects on the network show after 5-15 years.

game.title: Four Years at the Ministry (Vier Jahre im Ministerium)
game.loop: Each round is a quarter of a 4-year legislature. The player proposes the split of the federal rail money between renewal, new lines, digitalisation and charge subsidies (the budget committee may cut or move it), chooses grants or equity injections, picks one or two initiatives (a law, a corridor closure, a management change at DB), and answers random crises (strike, accident, cost overrun, summer of delays) with a statement or a measure. In the background the infrastructure module runs the network's year fast (condition, faults, delay minutes) and the operations module turns that into punctuality; voters react to what they notice now, while the network reacts to money spent years ago.
game.win: The round ends at the election after 16 quarters. Success: approval of at least 40 %, the network grade no worse than at the start and the debt brake kept. Failure: a resignation scandal or a lost election; in career mode the player drops back to the backbench or, after the cooling-off period, to a lobby job.
game.knowledge: Art. 87e GG, the debt brake and why equity injections sit outside it, which money flows through LuFV, BSWAG, GVFG and the Regionalisierungsmittel, the lag between investment and condition, the Bund as owner versus the independent infrastructure manager.
game.bigGame: Gives: the proposed budget envelopes (replacement money, upgrade funding, charge subsidies, equity) to the budget MP, the funding officer and the infrastructure manager's asset manager, policy targets to the shareholder officer, and laws that change the rules all roles play under. Takes: network grade, punctuality, accidents and BEU reports, strikes, the budget committee's cuts, audit findings. In career mode the top of the political ladder.

roles.name: Member of the Bundestag, transport committee
roles.organisation: German Bundestag, transport committee (Verkehrsausschuss), and the MP's parliamentary group (Fraktion)
roles.summary: Shapes the rail laws (AEG, ERegG, BSWAG with its Bedarfsplan, planning acceleration) as rapporteur in the transport committee, controls the ministry with questions and hearings, and fights for the projects of the constituency (Wahlkreis).
decisions: Table amendments to a draft law in the rapporteurs' meeting (Berichterstattergespräch) of the coalition
Propose the group's experts for the committee's public hearing (Anhörung)
Ask written questions (up to four a month) or get the group to file a minor interpellation (Kleine Anfrage) to expose delays or costs
Lobby the ministry to lift a constituency project into the urgent need (vordringlicher Bedarf) at the Bedarfsplan review, then vote on the Bedarfsplan as part of the BSWAG
Vote with the group line or against it
Meet or decline a lobby group, the union, a citizens' initiative
Back a reactivation, noise protection or station programme
effects: Laws set track access charge rules, priority rules and planning procedures for years for every operator and project
Constituency projects advance or wait a decade
Public pressure on the ministry and DB through questions and hearings
Group discipline decides the MP's rapporteur role and next nomination
resources: MP allowance of €11,833 a month (taxable, from July 2025, adjusted every July to the wage index) plus a tax-free expense allowance of about €5,300
About €25,000 a month for 3-6 staff in Berlin and the constituency
Research Services of the Bundestag (Wissenschaftliche Dienste), right to ask questions, committee hearings
Speaking time allotted by the group; about 20 sitting weeks a year
limits: Art. 38 GG (free mandate) against group discipline; Rules of Procedure of the Bundestag (GO-BT; minor interpellations need a group or 5 % of the members)
Abgeordnetengesetz: declaration of side income; Lobby Register Act (LobbyRG); § 108e StGB (bribery of MPs)
BSWAG § 4: Bedarfsplan review every five years; projects need a benefit-cost ratio above 1 under the federal transport plan's method (BVWP), not under the law itself
Bundesrat participation; EU law (Directive 2012/34/EU, TEN-T Regulation 2024/1679) limits national choices
risks: Losing the nomination or the list place; not re-elected after 4 years (only a transitional allowance)
Public exposure, social-media attacks, threats
Scandal over side jobs or lobby contacts
Long days and weekends split between Berlin and the constituency

career.entry: Elected by direct mandate or on the Land list; usually years of local party work and a municipal or Landtag career; rail expertise often from a job in the sector, a union or administration.
career.chances: €11,833 a month; committee chairs and parliamentary state secretaries are paid more; pension rights after one term; after leaving often association or consulting jobs.

kpis: Constituency projects funded or in the Bedarfsplan
roles.timescale: Sitting weeks; a law takes 6-18 months; a legislature of 4 years.

game.title: Committee Week (Sitzungswoche)
game.loop: A draft law (e.g. a reform of track access charges or a planning-acceleration act) arrives with 8-12 clauses. Over five game days the player reads hearing statements and must tell evidence from lobby claims (knowledge cards), trades support with the coalition partner, the union and the freight and passenger lobbies, and tries to get a reactivation for the constituency in the town module into the Bedarfsplan. Friday's vote fixes the clauses; the simulation then applies them (charges, priorities, procedure durations) in the following game years.
game.win: Success: the law passes with your amendments, the later simulation shows them to help (capacity, punctuality, cost), and the constituency project is in the Bedarfsplan. Failure: the group takes away the rapporteur role or the nomination is lost; career mode drops the player back into municipal politics or lobby work.
game.knowledge: Legislative procedure (readings, committee, hearing, Bundesrat: objection or consent law), the rights of a single MP versus a group, AEG, ERegG and BSWAG basics, Bedarfsplan and benefit-cost ratio, lobby register, judging the quality of evidence.
game.bigGame: Gives: rule changes (charge rules, priority rules, procedure durations, funding eligibility) that all other roles then play under, and projects for the Bedarfsplan. Takes: the constituency's satisfaction from the town, lobby pressure from other roles, scandals from the journalist.

roles.name: Member of the Bundestag, budget committee (rail rapporteur)
roles.name_de: Berichterstatter/in für den Verkehrsetat (Schiene) im Haushaltsausschuss des Bundestages
roles.organisation: German Bundestag, budget committee (Haushaltsausschuss), rapporteur group for the transport budget (Einzelplan 12), one rapporteur per parliamentary group
roles.summary: As one of the budget committee's rapporteurs for the transport budget negotiates every rail title of the federal budget and the rail lines of the special fund, can block money until the ministry or DB deliver (qualified blocking note), and approves the commitment appropriations for multi-year financing agreements and DB's capital measures.
decisions: Move money between titles in the final all-night session (Bereinigungssitzung)
Put a qualified blocking note (qualifizierter Sperrvermerk) on InfraGO or project money until a report or reform is delivered
Approve commitment appropriations (Verpflichtungsermächtigungen) for multi-year financing agreements
Approve or refuse an equity injection into DB or a higher borrowing limit, knowing that equity raises the capital base on which track access charges are calculated
Ask the Bundesrechnungshof for an advisory report (§ 88 (2) BHO)
Release blocked money after a report (Entsperrung)
Tie money to conditions in a committee resolution (Maßgabebeschluss)
effects: Projects start or wait a year; unspent money (Ausgabereste) becomes a political issue
Blocks force DB and the ministry to deliver reforms and transparency
Construction industry capacity follows the reliability of multi-year money
Equity instead of grants keeps the debt brake but shifts cost to operators through higher track access charges
The budget stays within the debt brake or the coalition fights
resources: One rapporteur per parliamentary group for Einzelplan 12, the committee secretariat and the group's budget staff
Ministry's detailed budget documents and Bundesrechnungshof reports
Rail titles of roughly €20-25 bn a year in the core budget and the special fund; the Regionalisierungsmittel are fixed by the RegG outside these titles
MP allowance of €11,833 a month plus the staff budget
limits: Art. 110-115 GG (budget, debt brake), Art. 143h GG (special fund)
BHO § 7 (economy and efficiency), § 22 (blocking notes), § 38 (commitment appropriations), §§ 23 and 44 (grants), § 45 (carry-overs)
Annual Budget Act; coalition agreements; the government's right to propose the budget
EU state aid rules for DB capital injections (Art. 107 TFEU, Commission approval)
risks: Blamed in public for cuts or for money that is not spent
Accused of pork-barrel politics for the constituency
Not re-elected; burnout from all-night negotiations
Heavy lobby pressure from industry and DB

career.entry: Elected MP sent by the group to the budget committee, a prestigious seat; rapporteurs are often experienced MPs with a finance or administration background.
career.chances: €11,833 a month as MP; the budget committee is a route to parliamentary state secretary and minister posts.

kpis: Share of rail money actually spent (Mittelabfluss)
roles.timescale: The yearly budget cycle (government draft in summer, Bereinigungssitzung in November, adoption in December) and commitments over 5-10 years.

game.title: The Night Session (Bereinigungssitzung)
game.loop: The player receives the ministry's draft of the rail titles (LuFV, Bedarfsplan projects, digitalisation, charge subsidies, an equity injection into DB, special-fund lines) with 20-30 lines, a debt-brake ceiling and the coalition partner's demands. Through one night on a game clock they move money, set qualified blocks with conditions, choose grants or equity, and check figures against the auditors' hints (some lines are padded, some projects cannot spend). Then the next game year runs in the infrastructure simulation: blocked or underfunded lines show as delayed projects, overfunded ones as unspent money, equity as higher track access charges in the operators' accounts.
game.win: Success: a budget agreed before the clock runs out, within the ceiling, with high Mittelabfluss and no project stopped for lack of money. Failure: the coalition breaks over the budget, or a blocked project causes a collapse in the closure season that the media pin on you.
game.knowledge: Budget law terms (title, commitment appropriation, qualified block, carry-over, cover rules), the debt brake and financial transactions, the difference between LuFV and Bedarfsplan money, why the Regionalisierungsmittel are not a title, reading a project's cash-flow plan.
game.bigGame: Gives: the year's money and its conditions to the minister's programme, the funding officer and the infrastructure manager's budget years. Takes: audit findings from the federal auditor, money spent and overruns from the infrastructure projects, lobby pressure.

roles.name: Federal rail infrastructure funding officer
roles.organisation: Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV), directorate for railways; the Eisenbahn-Bundesamt prepares and checks the grant decisions and proofs of use
roles.summary: Turns the budget into contracts with DB InfraGO and other infrastructure managers: negotiates and monitors the replacement and maintenance agreement (LuFV), prepares financing agreements (Finanzierungsvereinbarungen, FinVe) for Bedarfsplan projects under the BSWAG, and checks whether a measure is eligible, economical and properly accounted for.
decisions: Assign a measure to the right pot: LuFV renewal, BSWAG new or upgraded line, BSWAG maintenance share in a Generalsanierung (possible since the 2024 amendment), GVFG, EKrG shares or the IM's own money
Check an upgrade's benefit-cost ratio and accept it, ask for a recalculation or reject it
Negotiate the LuFV quality targets and penalties (theoretical journey-time loss from slow orders, bridge condition, platform functionality)
Sign or hold back the financing agreement for a project's next phase
Check proofs of use (Verwendungsnachweis) and claim back ineligible costs
Approve or refuse a cost increase of a funded project
Decide whether planning costs are funded as a lump sum or at actual cost in a financing agreement
effects: Projects start, wait or lose funding
The infrastructure manager's renewal programme and so the network grade
Repayment claims and audit findings when money went to the wrong pot
Money flow by the year's end: unspent money only carries over if the title allows it, and counts against the ministry politically
resources: LuFV: about €8.6 bn a year in total (Bund and DB); BSWAG upgrades of several € bn a year
A division (Referat) of 5-15 officers, the EBA's funding and audit departments
The BVWP evaluation method, the Standardisierte Bewertung (GVFG), the infrastructure condition report (Infrastrukturzustands- und -entwicklungsbericht)
limits: BSWAG (§§ 8-11) and its Bedarfsplan; LuFV III contract (2020-2029)
BHO §§ 23 and 44 with the administrative rules and grant conditions (ANBest)
GVFG, EKrG (§ 13 cost shares), Art. 87e GG
VwVfG §§ 48-49a (revoking grants and repayment)
Grant recipients must follow GWB, SektVO and VOB/A in their procurement
EU state aid approval of the funding schemes
risks: Disciplinary liability and recourse for gross negligence (§ 75 BBG)
Named in Bundesrechnungshof reports
Blamed for blocked projects; political pressure to sign quickly

career.entry: Master in civil engineering, economics or law; higher civil service, often from the EBA, a state administration or the infrastructure manager; induction in the ministry.
career.chances: A13-A15 (about €5,500-8,500 gross a month); head of division A16 or B3; secure job and pension.

kpis: Share of money allocated correctly (no repayments)
roles.timescale: Weeks per application, the yearly LuFV report and settlement, contracts over 5-10 years.

game.title: Which Pot? (Welcher Topf?)
game.loop: Funding applications arrive from the infrastructure module (renewals, the electrification to Waldau, the underpass at Talstraße, digital interlockings) with a cost estimate, benefits and documents. The player puts each into the right pot (LuFV, BSWAG, GVFG, EKrG shares, own money), recalculates the benefit-cost ratio (yearly benefit x annuity factor / cost incl. fees), spots padded costs and missing documents, and approves, asks for more or rejects. The infrastructure year runs on: correctly funded projects start, wrongly funded ones are caught by the audit, late ones wait for next year's money.
game.win: A round is a budget year with 10-20 applications. Score: correct allocations, money out before 31 December, no repayment claims. A misallocation found by the auditors costs reputation; in career mode it stalls promotion.
game.knowledge: Funding rules and eligibility (a like-for-like renewal is LuFV, an upgrade is BSWAG), benefit-cost ratio (component lifetimes, 1.7 % discount rate as in the BVWP 2030), EKrG cost shares, LuFV quality indicators, proof of use.
game.bigGame: Takes over the funding part of the infrastructure game's funding authority role. Takes: budget envelopes from the budget MP and minister, applications from the asset manager and planner. Gives: funded projects and money to the infrastructure manager, records for the federal auditor.

roles.name: State minister of transport
roles.organisation: State ministry of transport of a Land (Landesministerium für Verkehr; in some Länder combined with economy or infrastructure), state government
roles.summary: Responsible for regional rail in the Land: distributes the federal Regionalisierungsmittel and state money to the transport authorities (or, in some Länder, runs the authority as a state company), co-finances the Deutschlandticket, decides on reactivations, station programmes and state vehicle pools, and lobbies the Bund for upgrades in the Bundesrat and the transport ministers' conference.
decisions: Split the Regionalisierungsmittel between rail services, buses and investment
Choose which disused lines to reactivate, based on the Standardisierte Bewertung
Agree the Deutschlandticket price and the Länder's half of its shortfall in the transport ministers' conference (Verkehrsministerkonferenz)
Fund a state vehicle pool or vehicle guarantees for tenders
Co-fund station modernisation and step-free platforms
Pre-finance planning of a line upgrade to push it into the federal Bedarfsplan
Back an emergency award when an operator fails
Vote in the Bundesrat on federal rail laws that need the Länder (RegG, planning acceleration)
effects: Train-km ordered and so services in every region
Ridership and the Deutschlandticket's uptake
Cost pressure when energy and wage indices rise: cuts later if over-committed
Reactivations bring rail back to towns (or stall in planning)
resources: Regionalisierungsmittel of about €0.1-1.9 bn a year per Land (distributed by the Kieler Schlüssel; about €11-12 bn in total)
State money for public transport investment of €100-800 M a year
A ministry with a rail department of 20-50 staff
Powers under the state's public transport act; owner of state transport companies or vehicle pools in some Länder
limits: Regionalisierungsgesetz (RegG) and Art. 106a GG
State public transport act (ÖPNV-Gesetz) and the state budget code with the state debt brake
VO (EG) 1370/2007 and GWB for awarding services
Standardisierte Bewertung for federal GVFG co-funding
Coalition agreement; EU state aid rules
risks: Dismissal or election loss (mostly 5-year terms)
Public anger at cancellations, strikes, overcrowding
Political blame for an operator's insolvency

career.entry: Politician (usually a member of the Landtag) or an external expert; appointed by the Minister-President.
career.chances: About €14,000-18,000 a month depending on the Land; transitional allowance after leaving.

kpis: Punctuality and cancellations in the Land
Kilometres reactivated, share of step-free stations
roles.timescale: Months; the state budget (often two years); a 5-year legislature; projects of 5-15 years.

game.title: The Land's Rail Plan (Landesnahverkehrsplan)
game.loop: On a map of the Land with its lines, towns and disused branches, the player sets each year's split of Regionalisierungsmittel, picks reactivations and station upgrades, and decides on the Deutschlandticket co-financing. The town, passengers and journeys modules show ridership and who is left without service; the operations module shows contract costs rising with energy and wage indices. Events: an operator's insolvency, a strike, a federal cut.
game.win: End of a 5-year legislature. Success: more passengers, budget balanced, at least one reactivation running, no region without service. Failure: over-commitment forces cuts (cancelled trains in the operations simulation) and the election is lost.
game.knowledge: Regionalisierungsgesetz and Kieler Schlüssel, the cost of a train-km (access and station charges, energy, staff, vehicles, maintenance, overhead: about €12-25 per train-km), Standardisierte Bewertung.
game.bigGame: Gives: budgets to the transport authorities (planner, tender manager, contract manager) and co-funding to stations and municipalities; lobbying to the federal minister. Takes: Regionalisierungsmittel from the Bund, contract costs from the economics simulator, ridership from the town.

roles.name: Transport authority service planner
roles.organisation: Transport authority for regional rail (Aufgabenträger SPNV), e.g. a Zweckverband of districts and cities such as the ZVOE around Dresden, or a state company
roles.summary: Designs the regional rail service the authority will order: lines, frequencies, train lengths and the connections of the integrated clock-face timetable (ITF, Deutschlandtakt), within the train-km budget and years before the trains run; writes the rail part of the local transport plan (Nahverkehrsplan).
decisions: Set frequencies and operating hours per line (hourly, half-hourly, peak extras)
Choose train lengths and seats per trip from passenger counts
Fix the connection nodes and their minutes in the clock-face timetable
Decide which stations express and stopping trains serve
Ask the infrastructure manager for capacity or a measure (a passing loop, a faster junction), or request paths directly as an access-entitled body
Shift train-km between lines when the budget is cut
Coordinate the bus feeders with the districts
effects: Ridership and fare revenue
Operating costs of about €12-25 per train-km for 10-15 years of contract
Travel times and connections for every traveller
Infrastructure needs and overcrowding complaints
resources: A train-km budget of 5-40 M train-km a year (€100-800 M)
Passenger counts, surveys and ticket data (Deutschlandticket revenue sharing)
Timetable and demand models (e.g. VISUM), a team of 3-15 planners
limits: The Nahverkehrsplan under the state public transport act
Path allocation under ERegG §§ 52 ff and the infrastructure manager's rules (Ril 402 path management); annual timetable requests by the second Monday in April
Running times, headways and node capacities; the Deutschlandtakt target timetable
Budget and Regionalisierungsmittel; accessibility duties (EBO § 2 (3))
risks: Low personal risk
Public criticism and mayors' pressure for cut lines or missed connections
Workload peaks around timetable deadlines

career.entry: Master in transport engineering (Verkehrsingenieurwesen), transport economics or geography; trainee programme; or from an operator's or infrastructure manager's timetable planning.
career.chances: TVöD E11-E13 (about €4,300-7,200 a month); team lead E14/E15.

kpis: Passengers per train-km and cost per passenger-km
Connections kept at the main nodes
roles.timescale: Timetable years; concepts 3-8 years before operation; yearly timetable change in December.

game.title: Clock-Face (Taktfahrplan)
game.loop: On the layout's network and line map, the player builds a service: lines, frequencies, train lengths and the arrival and departure minutes at each node, within a train-km budget and the running times. The journeys and passengers modules then send the town's travellers on their travel plans: who catches the connection, who waits 55 minutes, which trains are overfull. The player iterates a few times and commits the concept to tender.
game.win: Score: passengers carried per euro, connections made at the main node, no train over 100 % load, budget kept; a round is one concept (10-20 minutes). Failure: an infeasible timetable (headway conflict at the station or on the single-track branch) is rejected by the timetable planner.
game.knowledge: Integrated clock-face timetable, symmetry minute, edge running times as multiples of half the cycle, running time and headway, crossing points on single track, cost per train-km, demand reacting to frequency.
game.bigGame: Gives: the service concept (train-km, lines, vehicle needs) to the tender manager and as the timetable of the operations module; capacity requests to the timetable planner. Takes: the budget from the state minister, demand from the town and journeys, paths from the infrastructure manager.

roles.name: Transport authority tender manager
roles.organisation: Transport authority for regional rail (Aufgabenträger SPNV)
roles.summary: Runs the competitive award of a regional rail transport contract (Verkehrsvertrag) worth hundreds of millions to billions of euros: lots, contract model, vehicle financing, award criteria, staff transfer, then the procedure up to the award and any review proceedings.
decisions: Cut the network into lots (one big lot or several small ones)
Choose a gross contract (authority keeps the fare risk) or a net contract (operator keeps it)
Choose the vehicle model: operator brings trains, authority owns them or guarantees their reuse or capital service (Wiedereinsatzgarantie, Kapitaldienstgarantie)
Set the award criteria and weights, e.g. 70 % price, 30 % quality
Require the transfer of staff (GWB § 131 (3)) and wage compliance (state Tariftreue act)
Set the index clauses for energy, wages and access charges
Answer bidders' questions, extend deadlines or not
Award, exclude an abnormally low bid (§ 60 VgV) after asking for explanations, or cancel the procedure
effects: The contract price for 10-15 years
Whether there is competition at all (few operators bid today)
The operator's financial stability and the risk of insolvency
Staff security and union peace at the change of operator
Whether vehicles are ready on the first day
resources: Contract value of €0.3-5 bn over 10-15 years
A team of 3-8 plus external lawyers and technical advisers (€0.5-2 M per procedure)
Market knowledge: a handful of active bidders
limits: GWB Part 4 (§§ 97 ff, § 131 for rail passenger services, § 134 standstill of 10 days, §§ 155-184 review by the public procurement chamber), VgV

VO (EG) 1370/2007: in Germany competitive award has been the rule since the BGH ruling of 2011; the general rail exemption for direct awards expired in December 2023, leaving the narrow performance-based direct award (Art. 5 (4a)) and emergency measures (Art. 5 (5)); net contracts as service concessions follow Art. 5 (3)
EU publication (TED) and minimum deadlines; state wage-compliance acts
Budget approval of the authority's board
risks: Review proceedings that delay or void the award
Damage claims of bidders
Career damage if no one bids or the operator fails
Deadline stress

career.entry: Law degree with both state exams, or economics or engineering with procurement expertise; years in an authority, an operator's bid team or a law firm.
career.chances: TVöD E13-E15 (about €5,000-8,500 a month) or above-tariff pay in state companies; head of the authority.

kpis: Price per train-km against the estimate
Award on schedule (2-3 years before start)
roles.timescale: A procedure takes 1-3 years; the contract runs 10-15 years.

game.title: Award the Network (Netz vergeben)
game.loop: The player designs the tender for the planner's concept: lots, gross or net, vehicle model, index clauses, award weights, staff transfer. Computer bidders (or a player as bid manager) decide whether to bid and at what price, given the risks; a procedural error may trigger a review. The winning bid then runs in the operations module's contract for ten fast-forwarded years with penalties, cost indices and crises.
game.win: Success: at least two bids, an award that survives review, and an operator that delivers good quality to the contract's end. Failure: no bids (re-tender or emergency award), a review voids the award, or the operator becomes insolvent in year four because the price was too low and the risks too high.
game.knowledge: GWB and VgV procedure and deadlines, gross and net contracts, risk allocation, index clauses, staff transfer, abnormally low bids.
game.bigGame: Gives: the contract (price, penalties, risk allocation) that the railway undertaking plays under in the economics simulator. Takes: the planner's concept, the minister's budget, bids from the bid manager. In career mode the step from planner to contract manager or head of authority.

roles.name: Transport authority contract manager
roles.organisation: Transport authority for regional rail (Aufgabenträger SPNV)
roles.summary: Manages a running transport contract: checks the operator's performance and invoices, deducts penalties for cancelled and late trains, approves replacement buses and emergency timetables, and keeps the service going when the operator struggles (staff shortage, insolvency).
decisions: Assess the monthly performance report and decide which failures are the operator's fault
Deduct, waive or dispute penalties; grant quality bonuses
Accept or reject a reduced emergency timetable during a staff shortage
Approve replacement buses (SEV) during closures and their quality
Negotiate a price adjustment when costs explode (as with energy in 2022)
Prepare an emergency award (Art. 5 (5) VO 1370/2007, up to 2 years) when an operator fails
Order quality checks (mystery travellers, cleanliness audits)
effects: The operator's revenue and liquidity
Service quality and passengers' trust
Savings that the authority can spend on more service
Continuity of service or a sudden collapse
resources: Contracts of €20-150 M a year each; penalties of 1-5 % of the contract value
Quality data (punctuality, cancellations, counts), 2-6 staff per contract
The contract's clauses: penalty catalogue, step-in rights, termination
limits: VO (EG) 1370/2007 and the Verkehrsvertrag
BGB § 313 (change of circumstances) and § 314 (termination for cause)
GWB § 132: limits on changing a contract without a new tender
Passenger rights (Regulation (EU) 2021/782, EVO)
Budget law of the authority
risks: Political blame for bad service
Legal disputes with the operator (arbitration, civil courts)
An operator's insolvency on one's watch
Daily escalations, stress

career.entry: Business, law or transport engineering degree; experience at an operator or authority.
career.chances: TVöD E12-E14 (about €4,600-7,800 a month).

roles.timescale: Monthly reports and settlement, daily escalations, a yearly final account; contract life 10-15 years.

game.title: Malus Month (Pönale)
game.loop: Each round is a contract month from the operations module: the incident list with causes (no crew, unit failure, infrastructure, external), cancelled and late trains, comfort defects. The player assigns each incident under the contract and computes the payment with an illustrative catalogue: train-km not run are not paid whatever the cause; on top, penalties apply only to causes in the operator's sphere (e.g. €12 per cancelled km, €40 per late trip, €4 per short-formed km). They handle the operator's objections and decide on emergency timetables and replacement buses. The operator's liquidity reacts: too harsh and it cuts maintenance or fails, too soft and quality slides.
game.win: Score: payments and penalties computed correctly against the model, quality trend up, operator solvent after 12 months. Failure: the operator's insolvency forces an emergency award about 20 % dearer, or an auditor finds penalties waived without reason.
game.knowledge: The penalty catalogue and exemptions, 'no service, no pay' versus penalty, cause attribution (operations, ECM, infrastructure), passenger rights, emergency award rules.
game.bigGame: Takes: the monthly results of the railway undertaking from the economics simulator and the operations roles. Gives: payments and penalties into the undertaking's profit and loss, emergency awards, quality pressure.

roles.name: Railway safety supervisor
roles.organisation: Federal Railway Authority (Eisenbahn-Bundesamt, EBA), safety supervision at one of its field offices (Außenstellen)
roles.summary: Supervises that railway undertakings, infrastructure managers, vehicle keepers and ECMs operate safely: audits safety management systems, inspects trains, track, workshops and records, follows up complaints and incidents, and orders measures up to a ban on operation.
decisions: Plan the risk-based supervision programme for the year (which companies, which topics)
Inspect a site, workshop or train run and record deviations
Issue an order with a deadline (Anordnung, AEG § 5a)
Impose a fine for violations (AEG § 28 with the OWiG)
Ban a vehicle or close a line section at immediate danger
Accept or reject a company's corrective action plan
Restrict or revoke a single safety certificate the EBA issued (operators running only in Germany) or a safety authorisation of an infrastructure manager, or ask ERA to act on a certificate ERA issued
effects: The safety level of the companies supervised
Trains stopped by a ban: penalties, chaos for passengers and freight
Compliance culture and precedents for the whole sector
Fewer precursors and accidents, or a missed warning
resources: An authority of about 1,500 staff in Bonn and its field offices; a supervisor covers dozens of companies
Rights to enter premises, inspect and demand documents (AEG § 5a)
Method of Regulation (EU) 2018/761 (CSM on supervision); travel budget
limits: Directive (EU) 2016/798 (railway safety) and the CSMs; ECM Regulation (EU) 2019/779
Train driver licence rules (TfV); the infrastructure manager's operating rules (Ril 408), binding through the safety management system
VwVfG: hearing before orders, proportionality; review by administrative courts
risks: Criminal liability for negligent omission if a known danger leads to an accident
Disciplinary proceedings and public scrutiny after accidents
Conflict with powerful companies; travel and on-site work in the track area

career.entry: Engineering degree (railway, electrical, mechanical; Bachelor for the upper service, Master for the higher service) plus practical railway experience; civil service training; the EBA also runs dual study programmes.
career.chances: A9-A13 upper service (about €3,600-6,900 a month), A13-A16 higher service (about €5,500-9,500).

kpis: Accidents and precursors in supervised companies
roles.timescale: Days and weeks for inspections; minutes to hours when a ban is needed; a yearly supervision plan.

game.title: Inspection Day (Aufsicht vor Ort)
game.loop: With a limited number of inspection days, the player picks companies and topics, then looks at what the simulations record: overdue inspections of assets (infrastructure), units running with maintenance overdue and crews over their rest-time limits (operations), a level crossing fault handled without the right safeguard (maintenance story). The player marks deviations and chooses a measure: advice, order with deadline, fine, ban. The simulations go on: a ban cancels trains and costs penalties, an ignored deviation raises the chance of a serious incident.
game.win: Success: the hidden serious deviations are found and closed before anything happens, with proportionate measures. Failure: an accident where you inspected and missed something; the BEU report names the supervision gap and career mode opens a disciplinary review.
game.knowledge: EBO and the core of Ril 408, ECM duties, driver licence rules, inspection intervals, the ladder of measures and proportionality, who issues which certificate (EBA or ERA).
game.bigGame: Gives: orders, fines and bans that change other roles' options (an ECM must take units out, a line runs slower); findings to the BEU and ERA. Takes: compliance data from the infrastructure and operations simulations. Replaces the computer's yearly EBA audit in the infrastructure game.

roles.name: Planning approval officer
roles.organisation: Federal Railway Authority (Eisenbahn-Bundesamt, EBA) as planning approval authority for the federal railways; the public hearing (Anhörungsverfahren) is held by the EBA itself or by a Land's hearing authority
roles.summary: Conducts the planning approval procedure (Planfeststellung) for new and upgraded federal railway lines, stations and crossings: decides first whether a procedure is needed at all, then checks the plans and the environmental report, weighs the objections of citizens, municipalities and associations raised in the hearing, and issues the decision with its conditions.
decisions: Decide whether a project needs planning approval, a simpler plan permission (§ 18b AEG) or none: since 2020 e.g. a catenary on an existing line, digital signalling or a platform raise need none if no EIA is required (AEG § 18 (1a))
Declare the documents complete for public display
Weigh each objection: reject, accept with a condition (noise barrier, compensation area, construction hours) or require a plan change
Require an environmental impact assessment or a species-protection exemption (§ 45 (7) BNatSchG)
Grant noise protection and compensation for land and residents
Issue, refuse or partly approve the decision
Run a supplementary procedure after a court finds an error
effects: The project's time and cost
Legal certainty against lawsuits
Protection of residents and nature
Years of delay if the decision is annulled
resources: Procedures with hundreds to thousands of objections; a team of lawyers and engineers
Expert reports paid by the project sponsor
The hearing and discussion meeting (Erörterungstermin), now often held or replaced online
limits: AEG §§ 18-18e and VwVfG §§ 72-78; the Planungssicherstellungsgesetz for online participation
UVPG (environmental assessment), BNatSchG (§§ 14-15 impact rules, § 34 Natura 2000, § 44 species protection), WHG
16. BImSchV (traffic noise limits, e.g. 59/49 dB(A) day/night in residential areas; calculated with Schall 03, no rail bonus since 2015)
AEG § 1 (3): rail projects in the overriding public interest; the planning acceleration acts of 2018, 2020 and 2023
Environmental associations' right to sue (UmwRG, Aarhus Convention)
risks: A court annulling the decision in public
Pressure from politics to be fast and from citizens to protect them
Hostile hearings; heavy workload

career.entry: Fully qualified lawyer (two state exams) or civil engineer in the higher civil service; EBA induction.
career.chances: A13-A15 (about €5,500-8,500 a month); head of section A16.

kpis: Cost and time of conditions imposed
roles.timescale: A procedure takes 1-5 years; the decision lapses if construction does not start within 10 years, extendable by 5 (AEG § 18c).

game.title: The Weighing (Abwägung)
game.loop: Projects of the infrastructure module arrive with plans. First trap: does it need a procedure at all? The electrification of the branch to Waldau is usually exempt under AEG § 18 (1a) if no EIA is needed; the underpass replacing the level crossing Talstraße is not. For a procedure, objections pop up on the town map: residents on noise, a farmer losing land, the environmental association on bats in the cutting, the town on construction traffic. For each the player rejects with reasons, accepts with a condition (each costs money and months) or demands a plan change. Then the administrative judge (player or computer) checks the decision; residents may sue.
game.win: Success: a decision that survives court with the least added cost and time, and no needless procedure. Failure: annulled for a missing species-protection check (supplementary procedure, 12-24 months more), or so many conditions that the benefit-cost ratio drops below 1 and funding is lost.
game.knowledge: When planning approval is needed (AEG § 18 (1a)), planning law terms, what must be weighed, noise limits, species protection, compensation measures.
game.bigGame: Takes: projects at the planning approval gate from the planner and project manager, corridors from the spatial planning officer. Gives: the decision with its cost and time back to the project, and the case to the administrative judge. Takes over the planning approval part of the infrastructure game's funding authority role (which today sends every federally funded upgrade, the Waldau electrification too, through planning approval).

roles.name: Authorisation officer for vehicles and infrastructure
roles.name_de: Referent/in Zulassung und Inbetriebnahmegenehmigung im Eisenbahn-Bundesamt
roles.organisation: Federal Railway Authority (Eisenbahn-Bundesamt, EBA), authorisation departments
roles.summary: Grants vehicle authorisations for an area of use in Germany only (or checks the German national part for ERA) and authorisations to place fixed installations (signalling, energy, infrastructure subsystems) into service, by checking the technical files, the reports of the assessment bodies (NoBo, DeBo, AsBo) and of EBA-recognised inspectors, and the national rules.
decisions: Check an application for completeness within one month (Regulation (EU) 2018/545)
Raise issues and request evidence
Accept or question an assessment body's or inspector's report
Grant, grant with conditions of use and restrictions, or refuse
Allow test runs on the network
Allow commissioning with temporary measures (e.g. a speed restriction until a test is passed)
effects: New vehicles and digital interlockings enter service on time or wait
Undetected design defects become faults or accidents later
Manufacturers' and operators' costs and schedules
Public debate on slow approvals
resources: Specialists for brakes, ETCS, EMC, structures; files of thousands of pages
Legal deadline of four months once the file is complete
limits: Directive (EU) 2016/797 (interoperability) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/545
TSIs (LOC&PAS, CCS, ENE, INF) and notified national technical rules
CSM-RA (Regulation (EU) 402/2013)
Eisenbahn-Inbetriebnahmegenehmigungsverordnung (EIGV), AEG, VwVfG
The EBA's administrative rules for building supervision (VV BAU, VV BAU-STE) with EBA-recognised inspectors (Prüfsachverständige) for national installations
risks: Criminal liability if an obvious defect is overlooked and leads to an accident
Pressure from manufacturers and operators whose trains are waiting
Public blame for approval delays

career.entry: Engineering degree (electrical, mechanical, railway systems); experience in industry, testing or assessment.

kpis: Incidents traced back to authorised products
roles.timescale: Weeks to months per file; years for a new vehicle type.

game.title: Complete File? (Antrag vollständig?)
game.loop: Files arrive: a battery train for the branch line, the digital interlocking from a renewal with new technology, a level crossing system from the plant. Each file is a set of cards (TSI certificates, NoBo, DeBo and AsBo reports, the inspector's report, test reports, conditions of use); some are missing, contradict each other or are out of scope. The player raises issues, waits for answers against the four-month clock, and decides. Meanwhile the infrastructure and operations modules go on: a late approval keeps a unit or interlocking out of service, a missed defect shows up later as faults.
game.win: Score: every hidden defect found, decisions within the deadline, no unnecessary refusals. Failure: a latent defect you let pass causes a dangerous failure that the BEU traces back, or the operator's new fleet stands idle for months.
game.knowledge: The authorisation process of the 4th railway package, the roles of NoBo, DeBo, AsBo and the recognised inspector, TSIs, area of use, conditions of use, CSM-RA.
game.bigGame: Gives: authorised vehicles and installations to the fleet and the infrastructure. Takes: files from manufacturers, assessors, the infrastructure manager and operators. Takes over the commissioning approval of the infrastructure game's funding authority role.

roles.name: Rail regulation officer
roles.name_de: Referent/in Eisenbahnregulierung (Entgelte, Zugang) bei der Bundesnetzagentur
roles.organisation: Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur, BNetzA), Bonn, an independent federal agency in the portfolio of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy; its rail department and ruling chamber (Beschlusskammer)
roles.summary: Regulates access to the railway network and service facilities under the ERegG: sets the cap on the infrastructure manager's total costs, approves the track access and station charges, reviews network statements and path allocation, and settles disputes between infrastructure managers and railway undertakings.
decisions: Approve the cap on total costs for a five-year regulatory period (incentive regulation, Obergrenze der Gesamtkosten) and the allowed return on capital
Approve, reduce or reject the proposed charges for the next timetable year (ERegG § 45)
Check market segments and mark-ups against what each segment can bear
Apply the cap on regional rail charges (Trassenpreisbremse, ERegG § 37)
Object to clauses in the network statement (Schienennetz-Nutzungsbedingungen)
Decide an access dispute (path refused, framework agreement, priority)
Review a declaration of congested infrastructure (ERegG § 55) and the capacity enhancement plan
Order a measure or impose a fine for discrimination
effects: Charges of a few euros to over €10 per train-km for every train
Operators' margins and freight's competitiveness against road
The infrastructure manager's revenue and the Bund's compensation
Every equity injection and the allowed return on it feed into the charges (the 2024-2025 charge debate)
Fair access for new entrants
resources: A rail department and ruling chamber of some 150-250 staff
Cost and traffic data from infrastructure managers, market studies
Information rights and the power to issue binding decisions
limits: ERegG (charges including the cost cap, mark-ups, the regional cap § 37 and approval § 45; allocation §§ 52-59; powers §§ 66-68)
Directive 2012/34/EU; Implementing Regulations (EU) 2015/909 (direct costs) and 2017/2177 (service facilities)
VwVfG; appeals to the administrative courts
Independence from the Bund as DB's owner and from the ministries
risks: Decisions overturned in court (repayments)
Lobby pressure; tension between independence and the federal owner's interests
Low public exposure

career.entry: Master in economics, law or engineering; higher civil service; experience in regulation or the rail sector.

kpis: Market development (share of competitors) and charge levels
roles.timescale: The yearly charge approval months before the timetable year; a cost cap every five years; weeks for access disputes.

game.title: Price of a Path (Trassenpreis)
game.loop: The infrastructure manager files its charges: total costs, direct costs, the return on equity and the mark-ups per market segment (long distance, regional, freight). The player checks the cost base (some items are not eligible, an equity injection inflates the return), tests which segments can bear which mark-up (the operations and economics simulation shows how many freight and long-distance trains disappear at each price), and applies the regional cap. The approved charges then run a year: traffic, the manager's revenue gap, the Bund's compensation. Disputes over a congested section come up as side cases.
game.win: Success: eligible costs covered, no segment loses more than a set share of traffic, the cap kept, the decision upheld on appeal. Failure: the court overturns it (repayments), or freight traffic shifts to the road.
game.knowledge: Full-cost and direct-cost principles, return on capital, mark-ups by market ability to bear, the regional cap, congested infrastructure and priority criteria.
game.bigGame: Gives: the track access charges per train-km that every railway undertaking pays in the economics simulator and the infrastructure manager earns; dispute rulings. Takes: costs and equity from the infrastructure manager and the Bund, market reactions of operators, federal subsidies.

roles.name: Railway accident investigator
roles.organisation: Federal Railway Accident Investigation Body (Bundesstelle für Eisenbahnunfalluntersuchung, BEU), Bonn, in the BMV's portfolio and independent in its investigations
roles.summary: Investigates serious accidents and incidents on railways, independent of blame and liability: secures evidence on site, analyses data recorders, interlocking logs, maintenance records and human factors, and publishes a report with safety recommendations to the EBA and others.
decisions: Decide whether to investigate (mandatory for serious accidents, discretionary for accidents and incidents that could have led to one)
Choose which evidence to secure before the site is released for recovery
Send parts to the lab, read the event recorder and the interlocking logs
Interview staff and witnesses
Determine direct, contributing and systemic causes
Formulate safety recommendations and their addressees
Publish an interim statement and the final report
effects: Rule and practice changes across the sector
Public trust after an accident
Learning instead of blame; tension with the parallel criminal investigation
resources: A small body of a few dozen staff with 24/7 on-call duty
External experts and laboratories
Rights of access to site, data and staff (EUV)
limits: Directive (EU) 2016/798, Chapter V; AEG; Eisenbahn-Unfalluntersuchungsverordnung (EUV)
Report within 12 months, otherwise an interim statement on each anniversary
StPO: the prosecution investigates in parallel with its own evidence
No apportioning of blame or liability
risks: Psychological strain from fatal accidents
Night call-outs and on-call duty
Injury on unsafe sites
Public pressure and criticism of late reports

career.entry: Engineering degree and years in operations, maintenance or safety (EBA, infrastructure manager, operator), plus training in accident investigation; human-factors specialists from psychology.

roles.timescale: Hours to reach the site, weeks of evidence, a report within 12 months.

game.title: Cause Chain (Ursachenkette)
game.loop: A derailment or collision happens in a live day of the simulation, for example at a switch whose inspection was overdue or after a wrong-side failure at the level crossing. The player arrives, decides which evidence to secure before the site is cleared, reads the event recorder, the interlocking log from the control system, the maintenance records and staff statements, and builds the cause chain from direct to systemic causes. Then they write one to three recommendations to the right addressees.
game.win: Scored against the hidden cause chain the simulation generated: causes found, no wrong blame, recommendations that address the systemic cause. Accepted recommendations change parameters in later rounds. Failure: blaming the driver when the cause was organisational, and the same accident happening again.
game.knowledge: Accident investigation without blame, the Swiss-cheese model, reading recorder data, human factors, the Safety Directive.
game.bigGame: Takes: accidents and incidents from the mistakes of operational roles. Gives: recommendations that become rules or inspections for the EBA, infrastructure manager, operators and ECMs; findings that feed the career consequences of the players involved and the minister's approval.

roles.name: European Union Agency for Railways officer
roles.name_de: Referent/in der Eisenbahnagentur der Europäischen Union (ERA)
roles.organisation: European Union Agency for Railways (ERA), Valenciennes and Lille, France
roles.summary: Works at the EU railway agency that issues single safety certificates and vehicle authorisations for operations in more than one member state (and on request for one), approves ERTMS trackside projects, drafts the TSIs, and monitors national rules and national safety authorities.
decisions: Assess a single safety certificate application and raise issues on the safety management system
Coordinate the national parts with the national safety authorities (e.g. EBA)
Grant or refuse a vehicle authorisation for an area of use across several countries
Give the ERTMS trackside approval before a tender (Art. 19 Directive 2016/797)
Draft a TSI change in a working party and close open points
Assess national rules and ask member states to withdraw them
Audit a national safety authority
effects: Operators and vehicles can run across borders, or not
Common technical rules lower costs for manufacturers and operators
Fewer national rules, more interoperability
Conflicts with member states
resources: An agency of about 200 staff
The One-Stop Shop IT for applications
Working parties with experts from the sector and the authorities
limits: Regulation (EU) 2016/796 (ERA), Directives 2016/797 and 2016/798
Implementing Regulations 2018/545 (vehicle authorisation) and 2018/763 (single safety certificate); Delegated Regulation 2018/762 (SMS requirements)
Four-month deadlines; ERA Board of Appeal
EU Staff Regulations
risks: Living abroad, limited-term contracts
Disputes with member states and companies
Slow processes; low public exposure

career.entry: Master in engineering or law plus 3 or more years of experience; selection as temporary or contract agent (AD5-AD7) or seconded national expert.
career.chances: EU grades AD5-AD12 (about €6,000-14,000 a month basic, EU tax), plus expatriation allowance.

roles.timescale: Months per application; TSI revisions every 3-5 years.

game.title: One-Stop Shop
game.loop: An operator applies for a single safety certificate to run freight from the container terminal into Poland and Czechia, or a manufacturer for a cross-border vehicle authorisation. The player reads the evidence against the criteria of Delegated Regulation 2018/762 (leadership, risk assessment, competence, monitoring), raises issues, coordinates with the national authorities (EBA and two others played by the computer, with their own rules and deadlines), and decides before the four-month clock runs out.
game.win: Success: correct decision with every real gap found and no unjustified issues; the operator starts cross-border trains. Failure: the deadline missed (appeal), or a certificate granted with a serious gap that later shows as incidents abroad.
game.knowledge: The EU railway packages, SMS criteria, the split of competences between ERA and national authorities, area of use, TSIs and national rules.
game.bigGame: Gives: certificates and authorisations that open cross-border markets in the economics simulator; TSI changes that alter requirements for vehicles and lines. Takes: applications from operators and manufacturers, cooperation with the EBA.

roles.name: European Commission transport policy officer
roles.name_de: Referent/in der Europäischen Kommission (GD MOVE: TEN-T, CEF)
roles.organisation: European Commission, Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport (DG MOVE), Brussels, with the executive agency CINEA
roles.summary: Shapes EU rail policy and money: prepares legislation (TEN-T, railway packages, the capacity regulation), runs the Connecting Europe Facility calls for rail with CINEA, monitors the TEN-T corridors and member states, and prepares infringement procedures.
decisions: Draft a CEF call's priorities and budget
Rank proposals with external evaluators and propose the selection
Accept or refuse a grant amendment when a project slips; decommit money
Monitor TEN-T requirements on a corridor (ETCS, 740 m trains, 22.5 t axle load, 100 km/h for freight)
Prepare an infringement procedure for a directive not transposed or applied
Support the Commission's negotiators in trilogues with Council and Parliament
Give DG MOVE's view when DG COMP assesses German charge subsidies or DB capital injections under state aid rules
effects: EU co-funding for cross-border sections, ETCS and terminals
Corridor standards that national plans must meet by 2030, 2040 and 2050
Pressure on member states to open markets and remove national rules
resources: CEF Transport 2021-2027: about €25.8 bn (of which about €11.3 bn from the Cohesion Fund)
A unit of 15-30 officials; CINEA's evaluation staff and external experts
limits: TFEU Art. 90-100 (transport), 170-172 (trans-European networks), 107-108 (state aid), 258 (infringements)
TEN-T Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 and CEF Regulation (EU) 2021/1153
EU Financial Regulation; the Multiannual Financial Framework
Council and Parliament decide legislation
risks: Low personal risk; living abroad
Political pressure from member states
Slow processes, blame for unspent money

career.entry: EPSO competition (AD5) or temporary agent; or seconded national expert from a ministry or regulator.
career.chances: EU grades AD5-AD14 (about €6,000-17,000 a month basic, EU tax); seconded experts keep their national pay plus an allowance.

kpis: CEF money absorbed by completed projects
roles.timescale: Yearly calls, 7-year budget periods, TEN-T deadlines 2030, 2040 and 2050.

game.title: CEF Call
game.loop: The player evaluates 8-12 rail proposals (a cross-border section, ETCS on a corridor, a terminal for 740 m trains, a bypass of a node) with documents of varying quality, scores them on relevance, maturity, impact and quality, and selects within the call budget. Then years fast-forward: projects slip (planning approval delays and overruns from the infrastructure module), and the player decides on amendments, extensions or decommitments and moves money.
game.win: Success: most of the money absorbed by projects that finish and raise corridor compliance. Failure: money decommitted unused, a 'mature' project stuck in planning approval or in court.
game.knowledge: TEN-T requirements and deadlines, CEF criteria and co-funding rates (up to 50 % for studies, 30 % for works, up to 50 % for cross-border works and 85 % in the cohesion envelope), EU added value.
game.bigGame: Gives: EU co-funding for upgrades and terminals (lowering the Bund's share), TEN-T targets. Takes: proposals from the federal funding officers and project managers.

roles.name: Mayor (with the municipal planning office)
roles.organisation: Municipality (Gemeinde, Stadt) with its town planning office (Stadtplanungsamt) and building authority
roles.summary: Leads a town with a station: plans the land around it, builds the forecourt, bus interchange, park-and-ride and bike parking, gives the town's statement in planning approval procedures and crossing agreements, deals with closures and replacement buses, and lobbies for more trains or a reactivation.
decisions: Propose the development plan (Bebauungsplan) around the station to the council: housing, commerce, parking
Fund the forecourt, park-and-ride and bike parking with state and federal programmes
Give the town's statement on a rail planning approval: support, demand noise protection, or sue
Agree or refuse a crossing agreement under the EKrG (underpass instead of the level crossing) and provide the land
Buy the old station building and give it a use
Mobilise the council and citizens for a reactivation or against a cut
Organise traffic and information during a long closure
effects: How many residents reach the train and how they get there
Street traffic, parking pressure and town development
Projects speed up or stall with the town's agreement and land
Votes at the next election
resources: A town budget of €20-300 M a year, investments of €2-30 M
A planning office of 5-50 staff, the building authority, the council majority
Funding programmes (GVFG, state station programmes, urban development funding)
limits: BauGB (§§ 1-10 land-use planning; the council adopts the plans), the state's municipal code
EKrG (§§ 3, 5, 13): since 2020 the municipality's third of a crossing measure on a municipal road is paid by the Bund (federal railways) or the Land
AEG § 23 (railway land released from railway use)
Role as public body in planning approval (Träger öffentlicher Belange)
Municipal budget law and supervision by the district
risks: Losing the election
Public anger over closures and noise; threats and attacks on local politicians
Criminal liability for breach of trust (§ 266 StGB) in budget matters

career.entry: Directly elected for 5-8 years depending on the Land (7 in Saxony); no formal qualification, often administration, law or local party experience.
career.chances: Full-time mayors are paid by town size, about €6,000-16,000 a month; mayors of villages receive an allowance.

kpis: Rail passengers from the town, park-and-ride use
roles.timescale: Weeks for council decisions, years for plans and projects, an elected term of 5-8 years.

game.title: Station Town (Bahnhofsstadt)
game.loop: In the town module around the layout's station, the player plans housing near the station, a bus interchange, park-and-ride and bike parking and the forecourt, and reacts to rail events: a long closure with replacement buses, the underpass project for the level crossing Talstraße that needs the town's agreement and land, a reactivation chance. The passengers and journeys modules show how many residents take the train, the streets and buses how the roads fill; council and voters react every quarter.
game.win: Success: re-election at the end of the term with more rail passengers, a balanced budget and the level crossing solved. Failure: an unpopular closure without information and a blocked project lose the election.
game.knowledge: Basics of land-use planning, EKrG cost shares (and that the town no longer pays a third at a municipal road), funding programmes, station catchment (about 800-1,000 m walking), parking demand.
game.bigGame: Gives: land, the town's statement and EKrG agreement to projects, feeders and park-and-ride to ridership, pressure upwards. Takes: closures and services from the infrastructure manager and transport authority, money from state programmes.

roles.name: District administrator
roles.organisation: District (Landkreis) and its administration (Landratsamt); usually on the board of the regional transport authority (Zweckverband)
roles.summary: Heads the district administration: the district is the transport authority for buses, shares the regional rail authority with other districts in a Zweckverband, pays for school transport and feeders, decides as lower authority on nature protection, building and water matters in rail projects, and leads disaster control after major railway accidents.
decisions: Vote on the Zweckverband board on which rail services to order and the district's contribution
Set the bus network and its timing at the stations (local transport plan for buses), adopted by the district council
Fund the district's share of on-demand buses and the Deutschlandticket shortfall
Give statements as lower nature-protection and water authority in rail planning
Declare a disaster and lead the crisis staff after a major accident
Propose the district levy (Kreisumlage) that the municipalities pay; the district council (Kreistag) decides
effects: Connections between bus and train in rural areas
School children's journeys and their cost
Speed and quality of the crisis response
Municipal finances through the levy
resources: A district budget of €200-800 M a year, of which €10-60 M for public transport
An administration of 1,000-3,000 staff
A vote share in the Zweckverband; the disaster-control staff
limits: The state's district code (Landkreisordnung) and public transport act
PBefG (§ 8a) and VO (EG) 1370/2007 for bus contracts
State disaster-control act (Katastrophenschutzgesetz)
BNatSchG and WHG as lower authority; budget law
risks: Losing the election
Official liability in a crisis (Amtshaftung, § 839 BGB with Art. 34 GG: the district pays, with recourse for gross negligence)
Public exposure and threats

career.entry: Directly elected for 5-8 years in most Länder (7 in Saxony); chosen by the district council in Baden-Württemberg and Schleswig-Holstein; usually experienced administrators, lawyers or mayors.
career.chances: B-grade salary of about €10,000-13,000 a month depending on the Land and district size.

roles.timescale: Weeks (board meetings), years (budget, transport plan), hours in a crisis; a term of 5-8 years.

game.title: Bus Meets Train (Anschluss im Landkreis)
game.loop: The player sets the district's bus lines and their timing at the stations against the regional trains from the planner's timetable, pays for school transport and on-demand buses, and votes in the Zweckverband on rail orders, all from one budget with the municipalities fighting the levy. Events: a train delayed beyond the bus's waiting time, a strike, a derailment with injured people where the player leads the crisis staff (where rescue goes, which roads close, buses as replacement).
game.win: Score: share of travellers with a connection under 10 minutes, every school child carried, budget kept, crisis handled in time. Failure: overspending forces a levy increase the council rejects, or a botched crisis response costs the re-election.
game.knowledge: Bus timetables at rail nodes, school transport duties, how a Zweckverband decides, the structure of disaster control.
game.bigGame: Gives: bus feeders and money to the transport authority, crisis management at incidents. Takes: the rail timetable, money from the Land, disruptions.

roles.name: Administrative court judge in planning approval cases
roles.organisation: Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, Leipzig), first and last instance for the rail projects listed in the annex to AEG § 18e (§ 50 (1) no. 6 VwGO); higher administrative courts (Oberverwaltungsgerichte) for others
roles.summary: Decides lawsuits of residents, municipalities and environmental associations against planning approval decisions for rail projects: whether the decision is lawful, has an error that can be cured, or must be annulled, and in urgent cases whether construction may start.
decisions: Decide an urgent application to stop construction (§ 80 (5) VwGO; rail planning approvals are immediately enforceable, AEG § 18e; since 2023 curable defects may be disregarded, § 80c VwGO)
Decide which facts need expert evidence
Check formal errors (participation, environmental assessment) and material errors (species protection, noise, weighing)
Rule: dismiss; declare the decision unlawful and not enforceable until cured; or annul
Refer a question of EU law to the Court of Justice (Art. 267 TFEU)
Suggest a settlement (e.g. more noise protection)
effects: Projects delayed by months or years, or cleared
Precedents that change how all planning approvals are written
Protection of residents and nature
Costs for the project sponsor
resources: A senate of five judges with research assistants
Case files of tens of thousands of pages, court-appointed experts
limits: VwGO (§§ 42, 48, 50, 80, 80c, 87c priority for infrastructure cases, 113, 114)
AEG § 18e; VwVfG § 75 (1a) (weighing errors matter only if obvious and influential; curable by supplementary procedure)
UmwRG § 4 (procedural errors), EU habitats and EIA directives
Art. 19 (4) and 97 GG (judicial independence)
risks: Low personal risk
Criticism from politics and media for 'blocking' projects
Heavy workload

career.entry: Two state law exams with top grades, judge on probation at an administrative court (3-5 years), later the higher administrative court; elected to the Federal Administrative Court by the judges' election committee after some 15-20 years.
career.chances: R1 at an administrative court (about €5,000-8,000 a month), R2 at a higher court, about €11,500 a month as judge at the Federal Administrative Court (R6); presiding judges higher.

kpis: Quality of rulings (consistency, not overturned by the Constitutional Court or the CJEU)
roles.timescale: Months per case (often about a year), oral hearings of one to three days, urgent decisions in weeks.

game.title: The Ruling (Das Urteil)
game.loop: The player gets a planning approval case, from the planning approval officer's game or a prepared one: the decision, the objections and three lawsuits (a resident on noise, the town on access, the environmental association on species protection). They check admissibility (standing, deadlines, objections raised in time), then each claimed error: is it real, did it influence the outcome, can it be cured? They decide the urgent application first (construction starts in the simulation or waits), then the main case.
game.win: Scored against a model solution step by step: the right outcome and remedy (dismiss, unlawful and not enforceable, annul) with the right reasons. A round takes 15-30 minutes. In the big game a wrong annulment delays a project by years; a wrong dismissal can come back as a CJEU ruling.
game.knowledge: Administrative procedure law, standing (§ 42 (2) VwGO, UmwRG for associations), error relevance and cure, remedies, species protection and noise law.
game.bigGame: Takes: planning approval decisions and lawsuits. Gives: delays and costs to infrastructure projects and case law that changes how planning approval officers weigh in later rounds.

roles.name: State railway supervisor for non-federal railways
roles.name_de: Referent/in der Landeseisenbahnaufsicht (oder Landesbevollmächtigte/r für Bahnaufsicht, LfB)
roles.organisation: State railway supervisory authority of a Land (Landeseisenbahnaufsicht), or the EBA acting for the Land as Landesbevollmächtigter für Bahnaufsicht where the Land has handed the task over
roles.summary: Supervises and licenses the non-federal railways (NE-Bahnen): regional and industrial lines, sidings, port railways, heritage and narrow-gauge railways; approves their infrastructure, vehicles and operating rules, and decides closure applications for non-federal lines.
decisions: Grant or revoke the licence (Unternehmensgenehmigung, AEG § 6) of a non-federal infrastructure manager
Approve operating rules, e.g. simplified train control (Zugleitbetrieb) on a branch line under the FV-NE
Approve vehicles and installations used only on non-federal lines
Order measures after inspections or incidents
Decide a closure application for a non-federal line (AEG § 11) after the offer to other infrastructure managers
Approve a heritage railway's operations with volunteer staff
effects: Reactivated branches open on time or not
Safety of small operators with thin staff
Freight access to sidings and ports
resources: A small team of 5-30 per Land, in some Länder delegated to the EBA by agreement
Inspection rights like the EBA's
limits: AEG §§ 5, 6, 11, 23; EBO and ESBO (narrow gauge); state rules for sidings (BOA, EBOA)
State railway acts (Landeseisenbahngesetze)
FV-NE (operating rules for non-federal railways) and VDV rules
VwVfG
risks: Criminal liability for negligent omission
Pressure from local politics to open lines fast
Small staff, broad responsibility

career.entry: Engineering degree and civil service of the Land; railway operations experience.

kpis: Licences and approvals processed on time
roles.timescale: Days and weeks; reactivations over years.

game.title: Branch Line Licence (Strecke wieder in Betrieb)
game.loop: The disused branch Bergheim – Kirchberg, given up by the federal infrastructure manager and taken over by a small regional infrastructure company, wants to reopen. The player checks the documents (operating rules under the FV-NE, level crossing safeguards, staff qualifications, vehicles) and inspects the simulation's assets on site, then approves with conditions or refuses. The operations module runs the line under those conditions.
game.win: Success: opening on time without a hidden safety gap. Failure: an incident at an unsecured crossing, or an opening delayed without need.
game.knowledge: EBO and ESBO, FV-NE, simplified train control (Zugleitbetrieb), level crossing safeguards (EBO § 11), federal versus state supervision, the closure procedure of AEG § 11.
game.bigGame: Gives: licences for non-federal lines and sidings (reactivations, freight access). Takes: applications from small operators and siding owners, reactivation decisions from the state minister.

roles.name: Auditor at the Federal Court of Auditors (rail)
roles.organisation: Federal Court of Auditors (Bundesrechnungshof, BRH), Bonn and Potsdam
roles.summary: Audits whether federal rail money is spent lawfully and economically: the LuFV, financing agreements, the EBA's grant practice and the Bund's control of DB as owner; reports to the budget committee, whose rail rapporteurs use the findings to block or redirect money.
decisions: Choose audit topics and sample projects
Request documents from the BMV and EBA and, through the Bund's rights as shareholder, from DB
Assess economy and efficiency; identify ineligible or double-funded costs
Write findings and recommendations; report to parliament (§ 88 (2) BHO) or in the annual report
Follow up whether recommendations are implemented
effects: Repayments and stricter grant practice
Qualified blocks and conditions in the budget committee
Public debate on the railway's finances
resources: An audit unit of 10-20 for rail within a court of about 1,000 staff
Rights to inspect files of federal bodies; limited rights at companies (§§ 92, 104 BHO, §§ 53-54 HGrG)
limits: Art. 114 (2) GG; BHO §§ 88-104; Bundesrechnungshofgesetz
No power to order, only to report and recommend
risks: Low personal risk
Criticism as a blocker; resistance from the audited bodies

career.entry: Degree in law, economics or engineering; higher civil service, often after years in a ministry or authority.
career.chances: A13-A16 (about €5,500-9,500 a month); members of the court are paid in B grades.

roles.timescale: Months per audit; the annual report every autumn.

game.title: The Audit (Die Prüfung)
game.loop: The player gets one or more budget years of the infrastructure simulation as records: projects with estimates, calculations, payments, funding pots, inspections and claims. With a limited number of audit days they sample records and spot misallocations (renewal money used for an upgrade, a cost claimed twice, overruns from lean planning, money left unspent), then write findings with the money at stake.
game.win: Score: seeded real findings found, false accusations avoided, money at stake estimated within a margin. Findings pass to the budget MP's game as hints.
game.knowledge: Funding rules, the economy principle (§ 7 BHO), sampling, reading project and payment records.
game.bigGame: Gives: findings to the budget MP and funding officer (repayments, blocks). Takes: the records the infrastructure and economics simulations write.

roles.name: Federal shareholder officer for Deutsche Bahn
roles.organisation: Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV), division for the Bund's shareholding in Deutsche Bahn AG, working with the finance ministry and the Bund's representatives on DB's supervisory board
roles.summary: Prepares what the Bund does as the 100 % owner of Deutsche Bahn AG: the positions of the state secretaries and MPs on DB's supervisory board, the public-interest targets of DB InfraGO, the business plan, sales of subsidiaries, board appointments and bonuses. Works where the Bund's money (LuFV, Bedarfsplan) meets the Bund's ownership, and where what is good for DB and what is good for the railway part ways.
