decisions: Draft the Bund's position on each item of a DB supervisory board meeting (business plan, investments, financing, board contracts)
Propose the public-interest targets of DB InfraGO (network condition, capacity, punctuality, customer satisfaction) and how they are measured
Tie the board's variable pay to punctuality and customer targets instead of profit, within the Bund's corporate governance code
Assess a sale of a subsidiary (as with DB Schenker in 2024/25) and how its proceeds are used to cut debt
Decide with the finance ministry whether InfraGO's profit stays in the infrastructure or flows to the holding
Prepare the shortlist and terms for a new chief executive or infrastructure board member
Check DB's borrowing against the agreed debt ceiling and the rating
effects: DB's priorities between profit, network and service
Debt, rating and the room for investment
Public trust after controversies over bonuses and punctuality
InfraGO's independence from the transport companies of the group (ERegG)
resources: Shareholder rights of the Bund as sole owner (shareholder meeting, articles of association, the Bund's members on the shareholder side of DB's co-determined 20-member supervisory board)
A group with revenue of about €26 bn a year (without Schenker) and net financial debt of about €20-35 bn
A division of 5-15 officers, external auditors and consultants
The Public Corporate Governance Code of the Bund (PCGK)
limits: Art. 87e GG (railways as private-law companies, the infrastructure majority-owned by the Bund) and the Deutsche Bahn Gründungsgesetz (DBGrG)
Aktiengesetz: the board runs the company on its own responsibility (§ 76), the supervisory board appoints and controls it (§§ 84, 111); confidentiality of supervisory board members (§§ 116, 394-395)
BHO §§ 65-69 (federal shareholdings) and the PCGK
ERegG: independence of DB InfraGO's essential functions (path allocation, charging) from the transport companies
EU state aid law for capital injections and the use of sale proceeds
risks: Low personal risk; criminal liability for breaching board confidentiality (§ 404 AktG)
Political blame when DB fails; caught between the ministry, the finance ministry and DB
Media attention on board pay

career.entry: Master in law, economics or business; higher civil service, often after years in a ministry, a bank, an audit firm or the funding division.
career.chances: A13-A16 (about €5,500-9,500 a month); heads of division A16 or B3; a move into DB's management must be reported under the rules for former civil servants (§ 105 BBG).

kpis: DB's debt within the ceiling, rating kept
Board decisions in line with the Bund's position
Bundesrechnungshof findings on the Bund's steering
roles.timescale: Quarterly supervisory board meetings, the yearly business plan, multi-year strategy and targets.

game.title: The Owner's Seat (Aufsichtsrat)
game.loop: Four supervisory board meetings a year, each with 4-6 items: the business plan, a large investment, a sale, InfraGO's targets, the board's bonus, a borrowing request. The player sets the Bund's position, negotiates with the employee side (half the seats, played by the computer or the union official and works council member) and votes. The economics simulator runs the group's year: debt, the network grade from the infrastructure module, punctuality from the operations module, and the press reacting to bonuses and delays.
game.win: After five years: network grade better than at the start, debt under the ceiling, no bonus scandal. Failure: profit targets starve the network (the grade falls and punctuality collapses) or debt breaks the ceiling and the budget committee has to step in.
game.knowledge: Corporate law basics (board, supervisory board, shareholder meeting, co-determination), the difference between owner and funder, public-interest targets, ERegG independence, reading a group's balance sheet.
game.bigGame: Gives: targets and limits to DB InfraGO's asset manager and the group's operators in the economics simulator; capital and debt limits. Takes: results of the group (network grade, punctuality, profit), the minister's policy, the budget committee's money and the auditors' findings.

roles.name: Transport association tariff and revenue-sharing manager
roles.organisation: Transport association (Verkehrsverbund), usually a company owned by the districts, cities and transport authorities of a region (e.g. the VVO around Dresden), sometimes with the operators as partners
roles.summary: Designs the common fare system of buses, trams and regional trains in a region (zones, tickets, the yearly fare change) and shares the pooled fare revenue among the operators (Einnahmeaufteilung), including the Deutschlandticket revenue and the compensation the Bund and the Länder pay for it.
decisions: Propose the yearly fare change to the association's bodies and the approval authority
Redraw fare zones or move to a distance-based e-tariff (check-in/check-out)
Set the keys for sharing revenue among operators (passenger counts, sales, surveys)
Calculate and claim the region's Deutschlandticket compensation and pass it on to the operators
Design social, job and school tickets with the districts that pay for them
Settle an operator's objection to its share, or send it to arbitration
effects: Prices that passengers pay and how many ride
Each operator's revenue and so the subsidy the authorities must add
Fairness between bus, tram and rail operators; disputes that last years
Overcompensation that must be paid back under EU law
resources: Fare revenue of €0.1-1.5 bn a year per association; the national clearing of the Deutschlandticket
Automatic passenger counters, surveys and ticket sales data
A team of 5-20 and external experts for surveys and revenue sharing
limits: PBefG § 39 (approval of bus and tram fares) and § 8 (3) (cooperation in fares and timetables)
AEG § 12 (railway fares) and the operators' transport contracts
VO (EG) 1370/2007 Art. 3 and 4 and its annex (compensation for maximum fares, no overcompensation)
RegG § 9 and the Länder's rules for the Deutschlandticket compensation; the national Deutschlandtarif
Competition law (GWB § 1) for fare agreements between operators
risks: Low personal risk
Public anger at fare rises; political pressure from districts and towns
Long disputes between operators, arbitration

career.entry: Degree in transport economics, business, mathematics or transport engineering; often from an operator's revenue or sales department.
career.chances: TVöD or company tariff about E11-E14 (about €4,300-7,800 a month); head of tariffs or managing director of the association above tariff.

roles.timescale: The yearly fare round (decided months before it takes effect), monthly clearing, final revenue-sharing accounts years later.

game.title: Zones and Shares (Zonen und Anteile)
game.loop: On the town map the player draws fare zones and sets the prices of single, monthly and school tickets next to the fixed Deutschlandticket. The passengers and journeys modules choose tickets and decide whether to ride. At the end of the year the player splits the pooled revenue among the bus, tram and rail operators with a key from counts and surveys; the simulation knows the true trips, so operators who are short-changed object.
game.win: Score: revenue target met, ridership not lost, every operator's share within 2 % of its true share, no overcompensation. Failure: a fare rise that empties the buses, or an arbitration lost to an operator.
game.knowledge: Fare zones and price elasticity (about -0.3), revenue-sharing methods (by trips, by passenger-km), the Deutschlandticket and its compensation, overcompensation under VO 1370/2007.
game.bigGame: Gives: fares to the passengers and fare revenue to the operators in the economics simulator; compensation claims to the Land. Takes: ridership from the journeys, the timetable from the planner, money from the state minister and districts.

roles.name: State spatial planning officer
roles.organisation: State planning authority of a Land (höhere Raumordnungsbehörde, e.g. the Landesdirektion Sachsen) and the regional planning associations
roles.summary: Before a new line goes to planning approval, assesses whether its route corridors fit the state's spatial plans and which alternative is least harmful (Raumverträglichkeitsprüfung, until 2023 Raumordnungsverfahren), as for the new line Dresden – Prague; and keeps land free for future rail lines in the state and regional plans.
decisions: Decide whether a project needs a spatial compatibility assessment or can go straight to planning approval (ROG §§ 15-16)
Agree with the project sponsor which corridor alternatives are compared
Weigh corridors against settlements, nature reserves, water protection zones, farmland, tourism and other plans
Conclude: compatible, compatible with conditions, or not compatible, within six months of complete documents
Reserve a corridor in the state or regional plan (priority area, Vorranggebiet) against housing or wind farms
Give the spatial planning statement in the later planning approval
effects: Which villages and landscapes a new line passes
Fewer objections and lawsuits later if the corridor was chosen well
Land kept free for decades, or lost to other uses
resources: The state development plan (Landesentwicklungsplan), regional plans and their geodata
A team of 3-10 planners per procedure; expert reports paid by the sponsor
limits: Raumordnungsgesetz (ROG §§ 15-16 as amended in 2023: six-month deadline, digital participation)
The state's planning act (Landesplanungsgesetz) and plans
UVPG and BNatSchG for the environmental parts
The result binds no one directly: the planning approval authority must take it into account
risks: Low personal risk
Hostile public meetings; pressure from towns and citizens' initiatives
Blame if the corridor fails later in planning approval

career.entry: Degree in spatial planning (Raumplanung), geography or civil engineering; higher civil service of the Land, often after the urban planning traineeship (Referendariat Städtebau).
career.chances: A13-A15 or TV-L E13-E15 (about €5,000-8,500 a month).

roles.timescale: Six months per assessment; regional plans over 10-15 years; lines built 15-30 years later.

game.title: Corridor (Korridor)
game.loop: On a map around the layout, the sponsor proposes three corridors for a new line (a bypass of Bahnhof or a new link Bergheim – Kirchberg). The player overlays layers (settlements and the town's growth areas, nature reserves, water protection zones, farmland, noise-sensitive uses), scores each corridor, adds conditions and concludes. The chosen corridor then goes to the planning approval officer's game: a corridor through a protected habitat brings objections, a lawsuit and years of delay.
game.win: Success: a conclusion within six months whose corridor passes planning approval without annulment, at a cost within 10 % of the cheapest corridor. Failure: the deadline missed, or a corridor that a court later stops.
game.knowledge: The spatial planning system (federal, state and regional plans), criteria for comparing corridors, protected areas, the link between spatial planning and planning approval.
game.bigGame: Gives: corridors and conditions to the project manager, the planner and the planning approval. Takes: projects from the Bedarfsplan and the Land's reactivations, the town's growth.

roles.name: Rail freight funding officer
roles.organisation: Federal Railway Authority (EBA), grant departments for the BMV's rail freight funding programmes
roles.summary: Runs the federal programmes that support rail freight: grants for private sidings (Gleisanschlüsse) and combined-transport terminals, and the subsidy on track access charges for freight; checks applications, sets the grant, and claws money back if the promised traffic does not come or access is refused.
decisions: Check whether a siding or terminal is eligible (open, non-discriminatory access for terminals; a traffic forecast that shifts freight from road)
Set the grant share and amount within the funding guideline
Ask for a better traffic forecast or a cheaper design
Approve the yearly track-charge subsidy and check it against the freight trains actually run
Check proofs of use and the traffic actually moved during the commitment period
Claw back a grant when a siding is closed or a terminal refuses access
effects: New sidings and terminal tracks get built or not
Freight operators' costs per train and their competitiveness against road
Tonnes moved from road to rail, and clawbacks where they were not
resources: Programmes worth several hundred € M a year in total (track charge subsidy for freight, sidings, terminals, single wagonload support)
A team of 5-20 officers; the funding guidelines and their forms
limits: The BMV's funding guidelines (sidings, combined-transport terminals, track charge subsidy) and BHO § 44 with ANBest
EU state aid law: Art. 93 TFEU, the railway state aid guidelines, the GBER; programmes notified to the Commission
ERegG and Regulation (EU) 2017/2177 on access to service facilities (terminals)
VwVfG §§ 48-49a (revoking grants)
risks: Low personal risk
Blamed when money is not spent or a funded terminal stays empty
Disciplinary liability for gross negligence

career.entry: Degree in transport economics, engineering or business; upper or higher civil service at the EBA.

roles.timescale: Weeks per application, yearly subsidy settlement, commitment periods of 5-20 years.

game.title: Track for the Terminal (Gleis für das Terminal)
game.loop: Applications arrive: the container terminal wants a further loading track for 740 m trains, a shipper a new siding, a freight operator its yearly track-charge subsidy. The player checks eligibility and the traffic forecast against the terminal and operations modules, sets the grant share and approves or asks for more. Years fast-forward: the terminal module shows the actual crane moves and train calls; where traffic falls short or a competitor is refused access, the player decides on clawbacks.
game.win: Score: tonnes moved to rail per euro of grant, no aid the EU would object to, clawbacks justified. Failure: a funded track stays empty, or a terminal that refuses competitors keeps its grant.
game.knowledge: Funding rules for sidings and terminals, open access to service facilities, state aid basics, road-km saved and their value.
game.bigGame: Gives: grants for terminal tracks and sidings and lower charges to freight operators in the economics simulator. Takes: applications from the terminal manager, siding owners and freight operators, money from the federal budget.

roles.name: Statutory accident insurance inspector
roles.name_de: Aufsichtsperson der gesetzlichen Unfallversicherung (UVB, BG Verkehr, BG BAU)
roles.organisation: Statutory accident insurers, public-law bodies: Unfallversicherung Bund und Bahn (UVB) for DB and the federal administration, BG Verkehr for private railway undertakings, BG BAU for construction firms
roles.summary: As supervisory person (Aufsichtsperson, SGB VII § 18) checks and advises how railway companies and contractors protect their staff: track work under traffic, work near the catenary, shift work; investigates occupational accidents and can order measures or stop work at immediate danger.
decisions: Plan site visits and company audits by risk
Check a work site's safety plan (Sicherungsplan): closed neighbouring track, automatic warning system or lookouts with enough warning time
Stop work at immediate danger (SGB VII § 19)
Order a measure with a deadline, or advise only
Investigate a serious or fatal occupational accident and report to the prosecution and the insurer
Propose a recourse claim against an employer who caused an accident by gross negligence (SGB VII § 110)
effects: Fewer injuries and deaths of track workers
Possessions and work sites stopped or slowed, costing time and money
Better safety plans and training across contractors
The companies' insurance contributions (hazard classes)
resources: Rights to enter, inspect, demand documents and order measures (SGB VII §§ 17-19)
A team of inspectors per region; the insurers' prevention budgets
Accident statistics of the sector
limits: SGB VII §§ 14-21 (prevention, supervision); ArbSchG; BetrSichV
DGUV Vorschrift 1 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 (work in the track area); the five safety rules of electrical work
Baustellenverordnung (health and safety coordinator); the infrastructure manager's rules for track work protection (Ril 132.0118)
Working-time law (ArbZG); VwVfG and proportionality for orders
risks: Injury on sites in the track area
Strain from fatal accidents
Liability for negligent omission if a known danger is left
Conflict with companies under time pressure

career.entry: Engineering degree (civil, electrical, safety engineering) plus several years of practice, then two years of preparatory service as supervisory person with an exam.
career.chances: Paid like the public service (comparable to A11-A14 or TVöD E11-E14, about €4,500-7,800 a month).

kpis: Site checks done and findings closed
roles.timescale: Site visits in hours, investigations over weeks, yearly prevention programmes.

game.title: Site Check (Baustellenkontrolle)
game.loop: During a possession of the maintenance story (signal repair, track renewal next to a line still in traffic), the player visits work sites. For each they check the safety plan: is the neighbouring track closed or is a warning system or lookout in place, is the warning time at least the time needed to clear the track (sight distance = line speed x warning time), is the catenary switched off and earthed, are rest times kept. They stop work, order a measure or let it run. The simulation plays on: a stop costs possession hours and delays the reopening; a missed hazard can end in a near miss or an accident.
game.win: Score: hazards found, no needless stops, no accident. Failure: a fatal accident on a site you checked, where the BEU or the prosecution names the gap.
game.knowledge: DGUV Vorschrift 77/78, track work protection (closed track, warning systems, lookouts), warning time and sight distance, the five safety rules of electrical work, working-time law.
game.bigGame: Gives: work stops and orders that delay possessions and cost the contractor and the infrastructure manager; accident data. Takes: possessions and work sites from the possession planner, site manager and safety supervisor.

roles.name: Signaller in a mechanical interlocking
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO; also regional infrastructure managers, NE-Bahnen)
roles.summary: Runs the train movements of one station from the command box (Befehlsstellwerk) of a mechanical or electro-mechanical interlocking, most of them built between about 1890 and 1960. Points, locks and signals are worked by levers and wires. There is often no track vacancy detection, so the signaller checks by sight, or through the points operator, that the route is clear (Fahrwegprüfung). Trains are reported to the neighbouring stations by telephone and secured by the line block (Streckenblock) where one is fitted. DB InfraGO still runs several hundred mechanical and electro-mechanical boxes, many of them more than 80 years old.
decisions: On a single line, or where there is no line block, accept or refuse a train offered by the neighbouring signaller (Zug anbieten und annehmen)
Check by sight, or by the points operator's report, that the route is clear before setting it (Fahrwegprüfung), because the box usually has no track circuits
Give the outlying points box its command through the station block (Befehlsabgabe), wait for its consent, then lock the route (Fahrstraßenfestlegung)
Clear the home or starting signal only when the route is locked and, on a line with block, the start field allows it
Watch for the tail signal (Zg 2) to see that the train arrived complete, then report it back or block back (Rückmeldung, Rückblock)
Write and dictate a written order (Befehl) when a signal cannot be cleared or a block field has failed
Decide crossings and overtakings at the station when the dispatcher does not step in
Report a fault to the maintenance dispatcher and enter it in the working and fault book (Arbeits- und Störungsbuch)
effects: Correct train reporting and block working keep two trains out of the same block section. A missed or wrong report, or a route checked carelessly by sight, is the classic cause of head-on and rear-end collisions in older interlockings.
Lever work, the points box's consent and telephone reporting take 1 to 3 minutes per train, against seconds in an ESTW. This limits the capacity of the whole line and spreads delays.
A train run on a written order instead of a signal loses 2 to 5 minutes and passes the station at caution.

The box cannot be left without a relief. An unfilled shift closes the station, or the whole line where the box is also a block post. The railway undertakings lose revenue and the IM pays under the performance regime (Anreizsystem).
A precise fault report shortens the technician's search and the time that trains run on written orders.
resources: One lever frame with 20 to 80 levers (points, locks, signals, route levers), block instruments for the line block to 1 or 2 neighbours and the station block to the points boxes
Telephone lines to the neighbouring boxes and the dispatcher, GSM-R train radio, the train register (Zugmeldebuch), the working and fault book and the written-order forms
Often one or two points operators (Weichenwärter) in outlying boxes
About 40 to 150 trains in a shift
Authority: sole say over which train may enter the station area. May stop any train for safety.
limits: Ril 408 (Fahrdienstvorschrift): train reporting, route checks, written orders, checking that trains are complete
Ril 482 (operating signalling installations) and the box's local operating instructions
The ESO and DB's signal book Ril 301: form signals Hp and Vr, supplementary signals Zs, Ne signals, train signals Zg
EBO §§ 47 and 48: operating staff (Betriebsbeamte) must be trained, examined and fit for duty, with medical and psychological examinations repeated at intervals
Physical: the mechanical locking prevents conflicting points and signals, but route clearance, train reporting and the completeness check depend on the human

Working Hours Act (ArbZG: 11 hours' rest, 8 hours a day, up to 10 if the average stays at 8) and the EVG agreements. Shifts usually last 8 hours, longer only where the agreement allows it for quiet posts with standby time. No leaving the box without a handover.
StGB § 315a (endangering rail traffic) and §§ 222 and 229 (negligent homicide and bodily harm)
risks: Criminal liability for a collision caused by a wrong train report, a careless route check or a wrong written order
Lonely night shifts in remote boxes, often without a canteen. Physical strain from heavy levers.
Loss of the local qualification after a long absence. Fitness examinations are repeated, and failing one ends the duty.
Job loss or transfer as mechanical boxes are replaced by ESTW and DSTW and controlled from afar
Shift work on early, late and night shifts, weekends and public holidays

career.entry: A three-year apprenticeship as railway operations worker, track (Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst, Fachrichtung Fahrweg), or about 7 to 12 months of functional training for career changers at DB InfraGO's training centres, with practice on training layouts and simulators. Then the signaller's examination, a local introduction to the specific box (several weeks, ending with a check of local knowledge) and the medical and psychological fitness check. Students of transport engineering learn the same procedures in operations labs such as the EBL in Dresden.
career.chances: EVG pay agreement of the DB group. A signaller's pay group follows the rated workload of the post (Arbeitsplatzbewertung), not the age of the technology: a busy mechanical box can rank above a quiet ESTW desk. Roughly 3,300 to 4,200 EUR gross a month basic, plus shift, night, Sunday and holiday allowances: about 42,000 to 55,000 EUR a year. DB hires signallers in large numbers every year, so moving to larger interlockings is open after 2 to 5 years.

kpis: Zero dangerous events (gefährliche Ereignisse) and irregularities
Delay minutes caused at the station
Correct entries in the train register and the working and fault book (spot checks by the district)
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes for each train, within shifts of usually 8 hours

game.title: Lever Frame (Hebelbank)
game.loop: The player works the command box of Bergheim, the mechanical interlocking of 1928 at the end of line 6250 in ARail's infrastructure network, with a points box at the far end of the station. The neighbour is Bf Neustadt, whose relay panel is the existing signaller game, played by the computer or by another player. Trains are offered by telephone ('Wird RB 33 angenommen?'). The player accepts or refuses, checks the route by looking out of the window (is a shunting move still on the track?), gives the points box its command, throws the point, lock and signal levers in the order the locking table allows, writes the train register line and blocks back after seeing the tail signal. Faults from the infrastructure module (a broken signal wire, a stuck block field) force written orders, filled in on the real form and dictated to the driver.
game.win: A round is part of a shift (30 to 90 simulated minutes, played in 10 to 25 minutes). The player wins when all trains are through with no dangerous event and the delay minutes stay below the target. The train register is scored line by line. Accepting a train into an occupied section, setting a route over an occupied track, skipping the tail-signal check or giving a wrong written order ends the round as a dangerous event. In career mode this opens an investigation by the district and the railway operations manager (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter), with the EBA informed and, after a serious accident, the BEU: suspension, retraining and a new examination. Repeated or serious events end the career as a signaller.
game.knowledge: Ril 408 train reporting (anbieten, annehmen, abmelden, rückmelden) and the route check by sight. The order of lever operations and the meaning of the block fields (start, end, permission, command and consent fields). The form signals of the ESO. When and how to write a written order. How to check that a train is complete (tail signal Zg 2).
game.bigGame: Shares the trains and the interlocking model of the existing signaller game (web/arail/game/signaller.js) and adds mechanical locking, block fields and telephone reporting. Takes the timetable (timetable-planner), the order of trains (train-dispatcher), possessions and slow orders (possession-planner) and faults from the infrastructure game. Gives delay minutes with their causes to the railway-undertaking simulator (penalties, performance regime), fault reports to the maintenance dispatcher, incidents to career mode and, when the box cannot be staffed, a closed line to everybody. The lab's model trains can drive it through the control-system interface.

roles.name: Signaller in a relay interlocking
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Controls one to several stations from a relay interlocking of the 1950s to 1990s: in the west mostly route-relay types such as the Siemens SpDrS60 and the Lorenz (SEL) SpDrL60, in the east the GS II types of the Deutsche Reichsbahn. A whole route is set by pressing a start and a destination button on a track-diagram desk, and the interlocking checks the track clear (track circuits or axle counters), locks the route and clears the signal. The critical moments come when the technology fails. Auxiliary operations (Hilfshandlungen) such as the substitute signal Zs 1, an axle-counter reset or an emergency route release bypass the technical safety, so they are counted on counters and logged.
decisions: Set routes with start and destination buttons and decide the order of trains in the area
Give the substitute signal Zs 1 or a written order when a main signal cannot clear, only after checking that the route is set, locked and clear
Reset an axle-counter section only after proving it clear (Räumungsprüfung)
Release a stuck route by hand (Fahrstraßenhilfsauflösung) only after checking that the train has passed
Log every counted auxiliary operation with the counter reading in the working and fault book
Close a track for a repair team, secure it with blocking aids, and open it only when the team has reported clear
Agree train reports with neighbouring boxes that still use telephone train reporting
Set up working on the opposite track (signalled two-way working, or by written order) for a possession or a fault
effects: Routine traffic flows with little risk, because the relay interlocking will not clear a signal into an occupied or conflicting route.

Each auxiliary operation moves safety from the machine to the human. At Bad Aibling on 9 February 2016 (12 dead, 89 injured), the signaller of a relay interlocking let a train onto the single line with the substitute signal while the opposing train was already on it. Distracted by a game on his phone, he then sent the emergency call to the wrong recipients.
Fast and correct auxiliary operations during a fault keep delays to a few minutes. Waiting for the technician instead costs 30 to 120 minutes for every train.
Spare relays and know-how are getting scarce, so faults last longer and the signaller works more often in degraded mode.
resources: A track-diagram desk for 1 to 5 stations and the lines between (50 to 300 routes), with relay rooms of thousands of relays
Train describer where fitted, telephones, GSM-R train radio
100 to 400 trains a day, usually one signaller per desk and shift
Counters (Zählwerke) on the desk for every auxiliary operation, which make each one traceable
limits: Ril 408 (train running, written orders, auxiliary operations, proving sections clear)
Ril 482 (operating signalling installations) with the rules for the specific relay design
The ESO and Ril 301: substitute and caution signals Zs 1, Zs 7 and Zs 8
TSI OPE (Regulation (EU) 2019/773, amended in 2023): safety-related communication with read-back
DB rules banning private mobile phones at operating workplaces, tightened after Bad Aibling
ArbZG and the EVG shift agreements
StGB § 315a and §§ 222 and 229
risks: Prison after an accident caused by a wrong auxiliary operation. The Bad Aibling signaller was sentenced to three and a half years for negligent homicide and bodily harm.
Guilt and trauma after an accident, needing psychological care
Night shifts where long monotony is broken by sudden stress
Closure of the box and transfer when the area moves to an ESTW or DSTW

career.entry: Signaller training (apprenticeship or 7 to 12 months of functional training), type training for the specific relay design and a local introduction of several weeks
career.chances: EVG signaller groups by the rated workload of the post: about 3,400 to 4,400 EUR gross a month basic, 45,000 to 57,000 EUR a year with allowances

kpis: Number of auxiliary operations and whether each was justified
Quality of fault reports and log entries
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Auxiliary Operation (Hilfshandlung)
game.loop: The first level is playable: the signaller of Bf Neustadt (game/signaller/), half an hour of a morning at a relay track-diagram panel with platform tracks G1 to G3, the double-track line from Bergheim to Talsee, an overtaking freight train and connections at the island platform. At 08:13 exit signal N2 fails. The player reports the fault, lets RB 33 leave on the substitute signal Zs 1 after the checks and with the counter reading recorded, closes track G2 for the repair team and opens it again only when the team has left. The next levels add what makes relay boxes dangerous: an axle-counter disturbance on the single-track branch to Waldau that must be proved clear before the reset, an emergency route release, opposite-track working for a possession, and distractions (the dispatcher calling, a driver asking, a crossing moved at short notice). Before each counted operation the game asks for the proof: which train report, which check.
game.win: A round is a disrupted period of 20 to 40 minutes. It is passed with 50 of 100 points, every train through and no danger to people (the playable level weights punctuality 35, safety 30, connections and platforms 15, the failure 10, questions 10). An unproven auxiliary operation is a hidden risk that the round may reveal, for example a train still in the section. A Zs 1 into an occupied or unlocked route, or opening a track with the team still on it, ends in a near-miss or collision scene. In career mode this means an investigation, suspension and a possible criminal case, and the IM's reputation drops.
game.knowledge: Ril 408 and Ril 482 rules for auxiliary operations. Signals Zs 1, Zs 7 and Zs 8. How axle counters work and what a reset means. How to prove a section clear. Working on the opposite track. The lessons of Bad Aibling (distraction, single line, emergency call).
game.bigGame: Built on the existing game (web/arail/game/signaller.js on the game core); its interlocking is the base the other signaller games share. Repair times come from the maintenance dispatcher and the repair team of the maintenance story and the infrastructure game, so better maintenance means fewer auxiliary operations. Delays go to the RU simulator, closures and reopenings to construction, incidents and their justification to career mode.

roles.name: Signaller in an electronic interlocking
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Controls a large area, often several stations and 30 to 150 km of line, from the screens of an electronic interlocking (ESTW). The workplace is in an ESTW control centre or in one of DB InfraGO's seven operations centres (Betriebszentralen, BZ), from which the field elements are controlled remotely. Automatic route setting (Zuglenkung) does most routine work. The signaller supervises, steps in on conflicts and handles faults, possessions and work crews across the whole area.
decisions: Let automatic route setting run, or take routes over by hand
Change the order of trains as the dispatcher orders, or locally within the dispatching rules
Give auxiliary commands (substitute signal, axle-counter reset, emergency release) with command release (Kommandofreigabe), only after the prescribed checks
Close a track for a work crew at the time in the operating instructions (Betra), secure it with blocking aids, and open it only after the on-site possession manager reports it fit for traffic
After a report of a defect, close the track or send trains by written order on sight or at reduced speed, until the technical side has assessed it and, if needed, set a temporary slow order (La)
Decide whether to stop all trains in an area after a report of danger (person on the track, damaged train) and send the emergency call
Decide which fault or call to deal with first when several arrive at once
effects: One signaller now moves 300 to 800 trains a day, so a mistake or a slow reaction hits many trains at once.
Auxiliary commands are still safety-critical, but they are logged automatically and reviewed.
Closing a track correctly protects the work crew. A forgotten closure or blocking aid is a leading cause of near misses with crews.
Workload peaks during faults (alarms, phone, radio, logs) are when errors happen. How big an area one desk controls is a design decision of the IM, and a too-large area shows up in incidents.
resources: An ESTW workstation (Bedienplatz) with 4 to 8 screens: area overview and detail views, train describer, alarm list, integrated logbook
Automatic route setting fed from the timetable
GSM-R radio to every train in the area, phone lines to the dispatcher, the emergency control centre (Notfallleitstelle) and maintenance
300 to 800 trains a day in the area, one or two signallers per workstation and shift
limits: Ril 408 and Ril 482 (ESTW operation, command release for auxiliary commands)
Ril 406 (Fahren und Bauen): possessions, the operating and construction instructions (Betriebs- und Bauanweisung, Betra), handing the track over and back
DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 and DB's Ril 132.0118: protection of work crews in the track
TSI OPE, the ESO and Ril 301
IT and OT security of the workplace: the BSI Act (BSIG) as amended for NIS2, the BSI-KritisV, no private devices
ArbZG and the EVG shift agreements; StGB § 315a
risks: Liability for collisions with work crews or trains after a wrong command
High mental workload and alarm fatigue, sitting for 8 hours or more in shifts
Remote control means little direct view of the trains, so the situation outside can be misjudged
Every action is recorded and examined after an incident

career.entry: Signaller training, then ESTW type training (several weeks) and an introduction to the area (2 to 6 months for a large area)
career.chances: EVG signaller groups by the rated workload of the post, ESTW desks mostly in the upper groups: about 3,700 to 4,700 EUR gross a month basic, 50,000 to 62,000 EUR a year with allowances. Work in an operations centre opens the way to dispatching.

kpis: Delay minutes attributed to the IM in the area
Number of auxiliary commands and whether each was justified
Possessions handed over and back on time
Zero dangerous events and zero unprotected work crews
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Control Desk (ESTW-Bedienplatz)
game.loop: The player supervises the ESTW area of line 6250 around Talsee (the ESTW of 2004 in ARail's infrastructure network): Talsee, Bf Neustadt (the ESTW Neustadt of the new layout, remote-controlled) and the open line between, shown as a schematic with the train describer. Automatic route setting runs the timetable of the operations module. Events stack up: a night possession for the renewal of track G3 (the maintenance story), a signal fault from the infrastructure module, a driver reporting a person near the track, a crowd of football fans on platform 2. The player decides when to take over from automatic route setting, which train goes first, and when to close and secure a track to protect the crew. A workload meter rises with every alarm and call, and slips become more likely while it is red.
game.win: A round lasts 20 to 30 minutes with 3 to 6 overlapping events. The score counts delay minutes, crews protected, auxiliary commands justified and workload kept in the safe band. A train sent into a closed track or an unprotected crew is a failure: an investigation with career consequences, plus high delay and compensation costs in the economics simulator.
game.knowledge: ESTW command logic and command release. The possession procedure (closure, blocking aids, Betra, handover and handback). How work crews are protected. When automatic route setting gets the order wrong. Reporting chains to the dispatcher and the emergency manager.
game.bigGame: Shares the interlocking model of the signaller game, scaled up to an area. Takes the timetable, dispatching orders, possessions with their Betra, and faults. Gives delays to the RU simulator and the performance regime, and actual possession times to construction: lost possession time costs the site manager money. Incidents go to career mode.

roles.name: Signaller in a digital interlocking with ETCS
roles.name_de: Fahrdienstleiter/in im digitalen Stellwerk (DSTW) mit ETCS Level 2
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Works at a digital interlocking (DSTW), whose field elements are controlled over IP networks with standardised interfaces (EULYNX), or at an ESTW combined with ETCS Level 2. A radio block centre (RBC) sends movement authorities to the cab, on lines 'without signals' instead of lineside signals. Examples are the high-speed lines of VDE 8 (ESTW with ETCS Level 2) and the digital node Stuttgart (DSTW with ETCS Level 2), commissioned in stages. Routine work is automated. The signaller manages ETCS degraded modes, temporary speed restrictions in the RBC and the transitions to lines with conventional signalling.
decisions: Set routes and let the RBC give movement authorities, or shorten them
Enter and remove temporary speed restrictions (TSR) in the RBC, as set by the slow-order list or reported by the technical side
Authorise a train to pass the end of its movement authority and run in Staff Responsible mode (SR) by written order after a radio or RBC failure, only after checking the route is clear
Choose how to recover trains after a failure of the radio network (GSM-R, later FRMCS) or an RBC restart
Deal with trains without ETCS or with a failed on-board unit: keep them out, send them over a line with fallback signalling, or divert them
Approve shunting and track occupation for maintenance in the ETCS area
effects: ETCS Level 2 allows shorter headways (short blocks, cab signalling), so the same track carries more trains, and a fault stops more of them at once.
Degraded modes on lines without signals are slow: in Staff Responsible mode, at DB's national limit of 40 km/h, every train needs a written order, so a 20-minute RBC outage costs hours of delay.
A correct TSR in the RBC enforces the speed limit automatically. A wrong one is a direct safety risk.
Trains without working ETCS cannot enter, which puts the RUs' fleet decisions and the funding of the ETCS rollout under pressure.
resources: DSTW workstation and an RBC operator terminal
Areas of 50 to 200 km with fewer field elements and no lineside signals
GSM-R radio (FRMCS in future) and a data link to every ETCS train
Diagnostic data on field elements, for predictive maintenance
limits: TSI CCS (Regulation (EU) 2023/1695) and the ETCS specifications of Baseline 3: modes and transitions
TSI OPE Appendix A: ETCS operating principles and rules (written orders, Staff Responsible mode)
Ril 408 with its modules for ETCS operation, Ril 482
Directive (EU) 2016/797: the EBA's authorisation to place the trackside subsystem in service, with ERA's prior approval of the trackside ETCS. Its conditions bind the installed software version.
OT security: BSI Act as amended for NIS2, BSI-KritisV, IEC 62443 and CLC/TS 50701 (cybersecurity for railway applications)
ArbZG, StGB § 315a
risks: Liability for a wrong TSR or a wrong authorisation in Staff Responsible mode
Pioneer stress: new systems with teething problems and frequent software updates
Manual skills fade while operations depend on technology that few people fully understand
Shift work, and being the face of a 'digital' failure in the press

career.entry: Experienced ESTW signaller with DSTW and ETCS type training (several weeks) and simulator training. New apprentice cohorts are now also trained for it.
career.chances: Upper EVG signaller groups: about 3,900 to 4,800 EUR gross a month basic, 52,000 to 65,000 EUR a year with allowances. ETCS operating know-how is scarce and sought by projects and the signalling industry.

kpis: Delay minutes from ETCS and RBC faults
Zero overspeed events from TSR errors
Time to recover traffic after an RBC or radio failure
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Movement Authority (Fahrerlaubnis)
game.loop: Line 6250 between Altstadt (the digital interlocking of 2023 in ARail's infrastructure network) and Talsee runs in ETCS Level 2 without signals, in short virtual blocks. The cab displays of the RE and S-Bahn units are shown as DMI symbols. The player sets routes and enters a TSR for a track defect reported by the infrastructure module. Then the failures come: an RBC restart, a train with a failed on-board unit, a radio gap at a GSM-R mast. Each one needs the right ETCS mode and a correctly worded written order for every affected train, while the queue of trains grows.
game.win: A round ends when the disturbance is cleared, or after 30 minutes. The player wins when all trains are recovered with the correct modes and orders, the TSRs are right and the delay is small. A wrong mode or order, such as Staff Responsible into an occupied section, is a dangerous event with the same career consequences as in the other signaller games. A comparison screen replays the same disturbance on a signalled line, showing the trade-off between capacity and resilience, which feeds the investment debate in the big game.
game.knowledge: ETCS levels and modes (FS, OS, SR, SH, TR, PT, UN, SN). Movement authorities, the RBC, TSRs. Written orders under TSI OPE. Why ETCS shortens headways.
game.bigGame: Takes the ETCS fitment of the RUs' vehicles (fleet manager, vehicle procurement) and faults from the infrastructure game, including the GSM-R masts. Gives capacity and resilience data to the digital-rail programme and to federal funding decisions, and delays to the RU simulator.

roles.name: Train controller on a branch line under simplified operation
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, or a regional infrastructure manager, NE-Bahn)
roles.summary: Runs a single-track branch line with few or no signals under simplified operation (Zugleitbetrieb). From a train-control office the controller gives each driver permission by radio or telephone to run to the next crossing station (Fahrerlaubnis), takes the arrival reports (Ankunftmeldung) and writes every message into the train controller's book (Zugleitbuch). Typical on DB branch lines (Ril 436) and at regional infrastructure managers (under the FV-NE): 10 to 40 trains a day on 20 to 80 km. In signalled simplified operation (signalisierter Zugleitbetrieb, SZB) technology supports the controller.
decisions: Give or withhold the permission to run (Fahrerlaubnis) to the next station, only after the section is reported clear
Move a crossing to another station when a train runs late (Kreuzungsverlegung)
Approve a possession or a works train in a section, and make sure no train gets permission into it
Tell drivers what to do at a level crossing whose protection has failed (stop and secure it themselves)
Accept or refuse an extra train or a trip to a siding
Close the line in a storm or snow, and order a check run before reopening
effects: The book and the exact message wording are the only protection. Two permissions into the same section can cause a head-on collision.
A well-chosen crossing move saves 5 to 15 minutes per late train and keeps connections at the junction station.
Simplified operation is cheap (no signals, few staff), and that is often what keeps a branch line open or makes a reactivation affordable.
Closing the line in winter or a storm strands passengers and pushes the transport authority to order replacement buses.
resources: One controller per shift for the whole line
Telephone or GSM-R radio, and the train controller's book (paper, or electronic with technical support in signalled simplified operation)
Drivers who set hand-operated or trailable points themselves
A single-track line of 20 to 80 km with 2 to 6 crossing stations and 10 to 40 trains a day
limits: Ril 436 (Zugleitbetrieb and signalisierter Zugleitbetrieb) at DB; at NE-Bahnen the FV-NE and the operating rules issued by the company's railway operations manager (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter)
EBO; for NE-Bahnen supervision by the Land's railway authority (Landeseisenbahnaufsicht, in many Länder carried out by the EBA or a Landesbevollmächtigter für Bahnaufsicht)
Fixed message wording (permission to run, arrival report, crossing move), read back word for word
EBO § 11 and the line's rules for level crossings
ArbZG. At small companies the job is often combined with dispatching or sales.
StGB § 315a
risks: Liability for a collision after a mistake in the book
Isolation and monotony, plus on-call duty at small NE-Bahnen
Closure of the line, or an upgrade to signalled operation, interlockings or ETCS, can remove the job
Lower pay at many NE-Bahnen

career.entry: At DB, functional training as signaller or train controller. At an NE-Bahn, internal training approved by the railway operations manager, often for drivers or shunters. In both cases, knowledge of the line.
career.chances: DB: EVG signaller groups, about 3,300 to 4,000 EUR gross a month basic. NE-Bahnen: company agreements (EVG or GDL), about 2,900 to 3,700 EUR. At a small NE-Bahn the path leads to deputy and then railway operations manager.

kpis: Connections kept at the junction station
Correct book entries (checked by the district or the railway operations manager)
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift

game.title: Train Controller's Book (Zugleitbuch)
game.loop: The branch line 6251 from Bf Neustadt to Waldau (single track, diesel, an S-Bahn every 30 minutes in ARail's network) is run in this game under simplified operation and extended beyond Waldau to a 35-km line with two crossing stations, drawn as a strip next to the station. The player answers the drivers' radio calls and writes each permission and arrival report into the book, field by field. When trains run late, the player moves crossings. A works train, a freight trip to a siding and the failed level crossing at the Waldweg complicate the day, and the passengers of the journeys module wait for their connections at Bf Neustadt.
game.win: One service day is compressed into 15 to 25 minutes. The player wins with no conflicting permissions, connections kept and few delay minutes. The game checks the book continuously. A permission into a section not yet reported clear is a dangerous event: the round fails and career mode opens an investigation. An extra round for transport-authority and politics players compares simplified operation with a signalled upgrade, cost against capacity, next to the electrification of the branch that the infrastructure game already prices.
game.knowledge: The Ril 436 and FV-NE procedure and its message wording. Crossing logic on a single line. How delays spread on single track.
game.bigGame: Takes the service ordered by the transport authority and the RU's trains. Gives punctuality and connections to the transport-authority contract (penalties) and the RU simulator, and cost and capacity data to reactivation and upgrade cases (district administrator, state transport minister).

roles.name: Block and crossing keeper
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO); temporary crossing guards often come from track-safety contractors (Sicherungsunternehmen)
roles.summary: Staffs a block post on the open line, a manned level crossing (Schrankenposten) or a points box in a mechanical station (Weichenwärter). The keeper closes the barriers by crank or button when a train is announced, checks that the crossing is clear, and at block posts passes trains on by train reporting and block. Few permanent posts remain. Today the work is mostly done as a temporary crossing guard (Bahnübergangsposten) when the protection of a level crossing fails for longer; without a guard, every train must stop before the failed crossing and pass it slowly on a written order.
decisions: Close the barriers on the announcement, neither too early nor too late
Check that the crossing is clear (cars, cyclists, a lorry stuck on it) before reporting it closed
Stop a train by hand signal or radio when the crossing cannot be made safe
Block a train on to the next post only after it has passed complete
In a points box, set the points and signals the signaller commands and give consent through the station block
Decide whether road traffic may cross between two trains
Report a barrier-runner or barrier damage to the signaller and the police
effects: Every closure costs road users 1 to 4 minutes. Long closures lead to barrier-running and complaints from the town.
Closing too late slows or stops the train: delay, and possibly an emergency brake.
Level-crossing accidents are among the most serious railway accidents in Germany: some 130 to 170 a year, with about 20 to 40 deaths.
A guard at a failed automatic crossing lets trains pass near line speed instead of stopping before it, saving 2 to 5 minutes per train.
resources: One post with barrier drive, bell or announcement and a telephone to the signaller
Hand lamp, flag and a radio
Shifts of 8 to 12 hours, often alone
limits: EBO § 11 (level crossings)
Ril 408 (train reporting, protecting crossings and failed crossings) and Ril 815 (level-crossing installations)
The ESO and Ril 301: hand signals
StVO § 19 (rules for road users at level crossings)
ArbZG. The post may not be left without a relief.
risks: Being hit by a road vehicle or a train
Criminal liability after a crossing accident
Isolation and boredom, and abuse from impatient drivers
Job loss as posts are automated or crossings removed (EKrG programmes)

career.entry: Short functional training (a few weeks to 3 months), a local introduction and a fitness check; for contractor guards a course and the track-safety qualification. Often an entry job, or for staff redeployed from other work.
career.chances: DB InfraGO: lower EVG groups, about 2,900 to 3,400 EUR gross a month plus shift allowances. Contractor guards: about 2,300 to 2,900 EUR. The job is a stepping stone to signaller, with the training paid by DB.

roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes

game.title: Barriers Down (Schranke zu)
game.loop: The player guards a level crossing near Bf Neustadt whose automatic protection has failed: a new level-crossing object on a town module of the Neustadt layout, so that the town's cars, buses and pedestrians use it (in ARail's network the Talstraße crossing on line 6250 is the model). Trains are announced by telephone and bell. The player closes and opens the barriers, scans the crossing for anything left on it and, if needed, gives the stop hand signal. Closing too early makes the queue grow until drivers start running the barriers. Closing too late makes the train stop.
game.win: A round has 8 to 15 trains in 10 to 15 minutes. The score adds train delay minutes and road waiting minutes. A vehicle or person on the crossing when a train passes is a failure: an accident scene and an investigation. In career mode, good rounds unlock signaller training.
game.knowledge: Hand signals. EBO crossing rules. Reading announcement times: how long a train takes from the announcement to the crossing at line speed.
game.bigGame: Takes the crossing fault and its repair time from the infrastructure game: the longer the repair, the longer the guard is needed, which costs the asset manager money. Gives delays to the RU simulator and road waiting time to the town (mayor, residents), which can start an EKrG case to remove the crossing.

roles.name: Train dispatcher in an operations centre
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Works in one of DB InfraGO's seven operations centres (Berlin, Duisburg, Frankfurt, Hannover, Karlsruhe, Leipzig, München) and steers the traffic of a dispatching area when trains deviate from the plan. The dispatcher decides the order of trains, overtakings, crossings, diversions and short-notice changes to paths, and the signallers carry the orders out. Cancellations, short turns and connections are the railway undertakings' decisions; the dispatcher fits them into the network and must stay neutral between undertakings.
decisions: Decide which train goes first at a junction or overtaking station
Hold a freight train in a loop to let a late ICE pass, or not
Divert trains around a closure and order the changed path
Fit the RUs' cancellations, short turns and connection requests into the network, and refuse what the network cannot take
Set up single-line working after a fault or for a possession
Assign the delay cause code to each deviation (Verspätungsursache)
Report disruptions above the threshold to the network control centre
effects: Every decision moves delay minutes from one train, and its passengers or freight customer, to another. A good decision cuts total delay; following the rules keeps it neutral.
The delay codes decide who pays under the performance regime, the IM or the RU.
Diversions keep trains moving but use capacity elsewhere and need drivers who know the route.
Wrong priorities cascade. An ICE that misses its slot at a node drags a whole cycle of the clock-face timetable.
resources: The dispatching system (LeiDis) with time-distance displays, train describer data and forecasts
A dispatching area with 500 to 1,500 trains a day and 5 to 15 signallers following its orders
Phone and data links to the RUs' control centres
Authority: binding orders to signallers, but none over RU staff or vehicles
limits: ERegG non-discrimination, and the dispatching rules published in the network statement (SNB): on-time trains before late ones, the least total delay, priority by train type
Performance regime (Anreizsystem, ERegG and Annex VI of Directive 2012/34/EU) and its delay-coding rules
Ril 408 for operating orders, Ril 406 for possessions
TSI OPE
ArbZG and the EVG shift agreements
risks: Blame from RUs and the public in big disruptions
Complaints to BNetzA about discrimination
Shift work, with high stress in snow, storms and strikes
Little criminal risk, because orders pass through the signallers' safety checks, but disciplinary consequences

career.entry: Experienced signaller (usually ESTW) plus dispatcher training of several months at DB InfraGO, or a degree in rail operations
career.chances: EVG groups above signallers: about 4,200 to 5,200 EUR gross a month basic, 55,000 to 70,000 EUR a year with allowances

kpis: Delay minutes and punctuality in the area
Punctuality at nodes and connections kept
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift

game.title: Who Goes First (Reihenfolge)
game.loop: The player watches a time-distance diagram (Bildfahrplan) of line 6250 from Altstadt via Talsee and Bf Neustadt to Bergheim (30 km, double track) and the single-track branch to Waldau, with live trains from the operations module and their forecasts. Delays arrive: a late intercity, a freight train with a slow locomotive, fans crowding platform 2 at Bf Neustadt. The player drags trains to change their order or sends them into loops. The forecast recomputes and shows passengers missing connections (journeys module) and the freight customer's penalty. RU dispatchers, played by the computer or by other players, phone in their wishes.
game.win: A round is one peak hour played in 15 to 20 minutes. The score counts total weighted delay (passenger-minutes and freight cost) and connections kept, followed by a neutrality audit. If the decisions favoured one RU against the published rules, a BNetzA complaint follows. In career mode the player builds a reputation as fair or as 'DB-first'. The round fails when rules are broken or the delay cost is far above the computer's baseline.
game.knowledge: The dispatching rules. Headways and the time lost by overtaking and crossing. Reading a time-distance diagram. Delay coding under the performance regime.
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable (timetable-planner), possessions, faults and the RUs' wishes, and gives its orders to the signaller games. Gives delay minutes with their codes to the performance regime (payments between IM and RUs, settled by track-access-sales), passenger delays to the transport authorities' penalties, and big events to the network controller.

roles.name: Network controller
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, network control centre in Frankfurt am Main)
roles.summary: Works in DB InfraGO's network control centre (Netzleitzentrale, Frankfurt) and coordinates across the operations centres when a disruption reaches national scale: corridor closures, storms, strikes, long-distance traffic. The controller activates prepared contingency plans, shares out scarce diversion capacity among long-distance, regional and freight trains, controls the inflow of trains into a disrupted area, and coordinates with neighbouring infrastructure managers along the European rail freight corridors.
decisions: Activate a prepared contingency plan, for example for a storm or a corridor closure
Decide which trains get the diversion capacity: long-distance, freight or regional
Limit the number of trains admitted into a disrupted corridor (inflow control), so that RUs hold freight trains at their origin instead of jamming lines and yards
Agree emergency timetables with RU control centres and neighbouring IMs
Decide when to restart traffic after a storm (inspection runs first)
Report the situation to management, the ministry and the press office
effects: Controlling the inflow prevents gridlock. When the Rastatt tunnel works collapsed in August 2017, the Rhine-Alpine corridor was closed for seven weeks and diversions carried only a fraction of the freight. The sector's losses were estimated at around 2 billion EUR.
Priority choices shift losses between RUs and sectors (passenger against freight) and are politically visible.
Fast, well-prepared plans shorten national disruptions from days to hours.
Restart decisions trade speed against the risk of trains stranded on lines blocked by fallen trees.
resources: A national overview of all operations centres and the network dispatching system
Weather data and storm warnings from the DWD
Prepared contingency and diversion plans
Direct lines to RU control centres, DB Fernverkehr, freight RUs and neighbouring IMs
A team of about 5 to 10 controllers per shift
limits: ERegG non-discrimination and the dispatching rules of the network statement
Regulation (EU) 913/2010 on rail freight corridors (coordination of works and disruptions) and the RNE handbook for international contingency management
Physical limits on diversions: electrification, loading gauge, train length, axle load, train protection equipment, and the drivers' route knowledge at the RUs
Ril 408 for operating orders and Ril 123 (Notfallmanagement)
risks: Public and political exposure in national chaos (press, ministry, parliamentary questions)
Shift work and very long incidents
Blame and legal complaints from RUs after priority decisions

career.entry: Several years as train dispatcher or ESTW signaller plus internal training. Some controllers have a rail engineering degree.
career.chances: Upper EVG groups or lower management: about 5,000 to 6,500 EUR gross a month. Leads into operations management.

kpis: Duration and extent of large disruptions
Trains and tonnes carried on diversions
Quality and timeliness of situation reports
roles.timescale: Minutes to days

game.title: Corridor Closed (Korridor gesperrt)
game.loop: A map extends line 6250 through Bf Neustadt into a freight corridor with three diversion routes, each with a different limit: one not electrified, one with short loops, one with a loading-gauge restriction. The main line closes for days. The player chooses a contingency plan, shares out the diversion slots hour by hour among passenger, freight and international trains, and throttles the inflow at the borders and the container terminal. RUs, played by the computer or other players, protest, and the press scores each day. The operations engine runs the days at full speed.
game.win: A round covers a 3- to 7-day closure in 15 to 30 minutes. The score counts trains and tonnes carried, gridlock avoided, the economic loss across RUs, and fairness. Gridlock (trains stuck on the open line for hours, full yards) is a failure: the ministry orders a review, and in career mode the player is removed from the post.
game.knowledge: The physical limits of diversions. Freight corridor coordination. Priority rules. The capacity of single-track and non-electrified lines.
game.bigGame: Takes long closures from the possession planner and from the infrastructure game (asset failures), and the RUs' fleets and drivers' route knowledge. Gives revenue losses to the economics simulator, political pressure to the minister and the Bundestag, and reputation to career mode.

roles.name: Emergency manager
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Is on call around the clock for an area of roughly an hour's drive, alerted through the IM's emergency control centre (Notfallleitstelle). Goes to every accident, person struck, fire, damaged overhead line or dangerous-goods leak and represents the IM on site. Secures the railway (closures, switching off and earthing the overhead line), works with the fire brigade, police and the federal accident investigator (BEU), and decides when the line goes back to traffic.
decisions: Order the line closed and trains stopped in both directions
Request the switch-off of the overhead line and earth it before rescue forces go near it, usually as the earthing person
Order recovery equipment: rescue train, crane, recovery vehicle
Agree with police, prosecutor and BEU when the site is released
Decide with the signaller whether trains may pass on the neighbouring track, and at what speed
Decide whether to evacuate a stranded train or tow it away
Hand the line back to traffic after inspection
effects: Every minute of closure delays dozens of trains. A person struck closes a line for 1 to 3 hours on average.
Releasing too early puts rescuers and investigators at risk. Releasing too late costs many delay minutes and distresses stranded passengers.
Correct earthing protects firefighters from the 15 kV overhead line.
Evacuating a train in heat or in a tunnel is dangerous, but waiting too long leads passengers to get out onto the track by themselves.
resources: An emergency vehicle with earthing poles, voltage tester, lighting and radios
The emergency control centre and its alarm chains
Rescue trains (for the tunnels of high-speed lines) and recovery cranes
Authority: in charge of all railway measures on site, working with (not under) the fire brigade incident commander
limits: Ril 123 (Notfallmanagement)
Eisenbahn-Unfalluntersuchungsverordnung (EUV): the BEU's rights at the site
Code of criminal procedure (StPO): police and prosecutor control the scene
DIN VDE 0105-100 (the five safety rules) and DB's rules for switching off and earthing the overhead line (Bahnerdung)
The fire brigade and rescue laws of the Länder (who commands what)
On-call rules (arrival targets, rest after a call-out) and ArbZG
risks: Trauma from fatal accidents and suicides (several hundred a year on German railways), with psychological follow-up care
Electric shock or being hit by a train at the site
Liability for releasing a line while people are still on it
Night call-outs, broken sleep, long hours
Press and public pressure at the scene

career.entry: Several years in operations (signaller, dispatcher) or technical maintenance, then emergency manager training (incident command, earthing authorisation, cooperation with the emergency services)
career.chances: Upper EVG groups: about 4,500 to 5,500 EUR gross a month plus on-call allowances. Leads into operations management or emergency planning.

kpis: Zero injuries to rescuers and staff
Feedback from the emergency services and the BEU
roles.timescale: Minutes to hours per incident, within on-call weeks

game.title: Call-Out (Alarmierung)
game.loop: At 02:47 the alarm comes in: after a storm a tree has fallen on the overhead line of line 6250 near Bf Neustadt (the infrastructure module's autumn storm), or a person has been struck. The player drives out, with the travel time from home counting. On site they work through a checklist under pressure: confirm all trains have stopped, request the switch-off from the energy controller, test and earth, brief the fire brigade commander, decide about a stranded train with 300 passengers (journeys module), coordinate with police and BEU, release the tracks. Every step takes simulated minutes while the operations module piles up delays and penalties.
game.win: A round ends when the line is released, after 15 to 25 minutes of play. The score counts safety steps done in the right order (nobody in the danger zone before earthing), closure time and how the passengers were looked after. A rescuer electrocuted or a train passing into the site ends the career, with the prosecutor involved. Being too slow brings heavy penalties in the economics simulator and a poor appraisal.
game.knowledge: The Ril 123 procedure. The five safety rules for electrical work. Who does what at an incident site (fire brigade, police, BEU). What the investigators need preserved.
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from the disruption generator and from mistakes in other roles' games (drivers, maintenance). Gives closure times to the RU simulator and the network controller, repair orders to the maintenance dispatcher, and reports to the BEU and to career mode.

roles.name: Possession and construction-operations planner
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Plans when and how the line is closed for construction and maintenance (Baubetriebsplanung). Bundles works into possessions and chooses between night closures, weekend closures, single-line working and long total closures. Consults and announces them to the railway undertakings and transport authorities within the EU notice periods, and issues the site's operating and construction instructions (Betra) and, with the timetable planners, the timetable changes (Fahrplananordnung, Fplo) and the slow-order list (La).
decisions: Bundle several works (track renewal, bridge, overhead line) into one possession
Choose total closure, single-line working or nights only
Fix the possession window and announce it to the RUs within the notice periods
Agree with RUs and transport authorities which trains are cancelled, diverted or replaced by buses, and who organises the buses
Write and approve the operating and construction instructions (Betra) and the slow orders
Move or cancel a possession when the contractor or the funding is not ready
effects: Long bundled closures cost less per km of work but hit passengers and freight harder. The general refurbishment (Generalsanierung) of the Riedbahn closed the line for five months in 2024.
Short night possessions keep traffic running but make the works roughly 30 to 50 % more expensive and slower.
Late changes cost the IM charge reductions or compensation to the RUs and cost the contractor idle time, which comes back as claims under VOB/B.
The possession plan drives replacement-bus costs, often several million EUR for a long closure.
resources: The annual construction plan and the planning systems for construction operations
A regional construction volume of hundreds of millions of EUR a year. Each possession carries works worth 10,000 EUR to tens of millions.
Regular consultation rounds with RUs and transport authorities
Authority: decides the possession plan within the rules. No budget of its own for the works.
limits: Delegated Decision (EU) 2017/2075 (Annex VII of Directive 2012/34/EU): restrictions with major impact are consulted from 24 months before the timetable change, smaller ones at shorter notice
ERegG and the network statement's rules on capacity restrictions: consultation, and charge reductions or compensation for late changes
Ril 406 (Fahren und Bauen): Betra, slow orders
Ril 402 (Trassenmanagement) for timetable changes
VOB/B (changes and claims in construction contracts)
DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 and Ril 132.0118: works next to running lines, restrictions on the adjacent track
risks: Blame from RUs, transport authorities and the press for badly planned closures
Deadline stress and overtime
Little personal liability, but an error in a Betra can endanger workers

career.entry: Rail operations training plus experience as signaller or dispatcher, or a degree in transport or civil engineering. Then internal training on Ril 406.
career.chances: EVG groups or the engineers' groups: about 4,000 to 5,800 EUR gross a month

kpis: Share of possessions carried out as planned
Delay minutes and cancellations caused by construction
roles.timescale: Months to years (24 months ahead down to the week before)

game.title: Possession Puzzle (Sperrpausen)
game.loop: The player gets a year of works on line 6250 and the branch to Waldau from the infrastructure game (renewals such as track G3 at Bf Neustadt, HOAI projects at their 'book the possession' step, maintenance windows) and a calendar with the timetable of the lines. They drag works into possessions: bundle them, choose total closure or single-line working, nights or weekends. Each choice shows the cost of the works, the RUs' losses (cancelled trains, replacement buses, diverted freight) and whether the EU notice periods are met. Then the year runs, and delayed works and late changes appear.
game.win: A round is one planning year in 15 to 30 minutes. The score counts works delivered, total cost (works, disruption and compensation) and deadlines met. A missed deadline means a short-notice closure that needs the RUs' consent or costs compensation. Works left undone make the assets' condition fall in the infrastructure game. In career mode the planner gains or loses standing with the asset managers and the RUs.
game.knowledge: Notice periods. The types of possession and their productivity. Betra, Fplo and La. What a closure costs whom.
game.bigGame: Takes measures and projects from the asset manager, the planners and the funding authority (infrastructure game). Gives closure windows to the timetable planner, the Betra to the signallers and the on-site possession managers, lost revenue and replacement-bus costs to the RU simulator and the transport authorities, and possession times to the site managers.

roles.name: Timetable and capacity planner
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Constructs train paths (Trassen) for the annual network timetable and for short-term requests. Computes running times with supplements, checks minimum headways and conflicts at nodes and on single-track lines, and resolves conflicting requests by coordination. Where capacity is short, declares lines congested and applies the legal priority criteria. Path allocation is an essential function that the IM must perform independently and without discrimination.
decisions: Construct a path for a request with running time, supplements and buffer
Resolve a conflict between two requests: shift, slow down, reroute or reject
Offer the applicant an alternative path within the deadline
Run the coordination procedure and, if it fails, apply the priority criteria and, as a last resort, the highest-price procedure (Höchstpreisverfahren)
Propose declaring a line congested and start the capacity analysis
Keep capacity back for possessions and future demand (capacity planning)
effects: Paths with enough buffer keep the timetable stable. Tight paths sell more capacity but spread delays.
A rejected or shifted path changes an RU's business: a lost freight customer, or a transport authority's clock-face timetable broken.
Declaring a line congested triggers a capacity analysis and a plan to raise capacity, and changes who gets capacity.
The annual timetable fixes most of the IM's revenue from track access charges, about 5 to 6 billion EUR a year at DB InfraGO.
resources: Path construction software (RUT-K) with infrastructure data and running-time calculation
Tens of thousands of path requests a year for the annual timetable, plus ad hoc requests (mostly freight) answered within days or hours
Capacity analysis tools
Authority: constructs and allocates paths within the rules; the allocation is the IM's own decision, reviewed by BNetzA
limits: ERegG path allocation: coordination, priority criteria, highest-price procedure, congested infrastructure
Delegated Decision (EU) 2017/2075 timetable calendar: requests by the second Monday of April, draft timetable in early July, timetable change at midnight on the second Saturday of December
Ril 402 (Trassenmanagement) and Ril 405 (Fahrwegkapazität)
The network statement (SNB): running-time supplements, minimum headways
Physics: braking, acceleration and the headway of the block system
risks: Little personal risk
Deadline pressure at the timetable milestones
Complaints to BNetzA when RUs feel disadvantaged
Mistakes show up as daily delays

career.entry: Rail operations apprenticeship plus training, or a degree in transport engineering (e.g. TU Dresden, RWTH Aachen, KIT)
career.chances: EVG groups or the engineers' groups, about 3,800 to 5,500 EUR gross a month. Specialists are sought by RUs, consultancies and the Deutschlandtakt planning.

kpis: Conflicts resolved without rejecting a path
roles.timescale: Months (the annual cycle) and hours to days (ad hoc requests)

game.title: Path Builder (Trassenbau)
game.loop: On a time-distance diagram of ARail's lines (the double-track line 6250 from Altstadt to Bergheim through Bf Neustadt, and the single-track branch to Waldau), the player gets 8 to 15 requests: the RE every hour, the S-Bahn every 30 minutes, the regional trains with their connections at Bf Neustadt, a freight train to the container terminal, an intercity, an extra charter. For each one they compute or check the running time with supplements, place the path, and resolve conflicts against the headway, shown as blocking-time stairs. Then the operations module runs the timetable for a test week with random delays, which shows how robust it is.
game.win: A round takes 15 to 25 minutes. The player wins when every request is placed or lawfully rejected, no headway conflicts remain and punctuality in the test week beats the target. Conflicting paths make the timetable unusable. A rejection without a lawful reason brings a BNetzA complaint in career mode.
game.knowledge: Running-time calculation (basic running time, standard supplement of about 3 to 7 %, construction supplements). Minimum headway and blocking times. Crossings on single track. Priority criteria and the timetable calendar.
game.bigGame: Takes the requests of the RUs and transport authorities (service-planner, freight-sales-manager, transport-authority-planner) and the possessions. Gives the timetable to all operating roles, revenue to track-access-sales and the IM's economics, and capacity data to politics (congestion, Deutschlandtakt investment).

roles.name: Track access sales manager
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Looks after the access parties (Zugangsberechtigte) as customers of the infrastructure manager: railway undertakings, and also transport authorities and shippers that may request paths. Advises them on path requests and framework agreements, explains and applies the track access charges (Trassenpreissystem), handles complaints, the performance regime and cancellation charges, and brings new customers onto the network, such as new freight operators and the winners of regional tenders.
decisions: Advise a customer on its path request and the alternatives
Negotiate a framework agreement for capacity over several years
Apply charges and cancellation fees by the price list, with no individual discounts
Settle a dispute over delay attribution in the performance regime
Escalate a customer complaint internally, or let it go to BNetzA
Prepare for new demand, such as a new freight terminal or a tender winner
effects: The IM's revenue: DB InfraGO earns about 5 to 6 billion EUR a year from track access charges.
Customer satisfaction and modal shift: freight operators leave rail when paths are poor or expensive.
A discount for one customer is discrimination. BNetzA can impose fines and reverse decisions.
Disputes settled early avoid regulatory proceedings.
resources: A portfolio of 10 to 50 customers, or a few large key accounts
The price list: roughly 3 to 12 EUR per train-km depending on the market segment, with the charges for regional passenger services capped
