The customer portal for ordering paths, and the network statement
No authority over the paths themselves (the timetable planners decide) and no discretion on prices
limits: ERegG: non-discrimination, charges approved by BNetzA, the cap on regional passenger charges
The network statement (SNB) and its conditions of use
Performance regime rules (Annex VI of Directive 2012/34/EU, ERegG)
GWB competition law
The rules of the federal support for freight track access charges (Trassenpreisförderung)
risks: Caught between customer and company, blamed by both
BNetzA proceedings when acting outside the rules
Little physical risk: office work with travel

career.entry: A degree (transport economics, business, engineering), or rail operations training plus experience. Trainee programmes.
career.chances: Upper tariff or non-tariff: about 5,000 to 7,500 EUR gross a month. Key account management leads to sales management.

roles.timescale: Weeks to years

game.title: Selling Paths (Trassenvertrieb)
game.loop: Customers bring requests, complaints and haggling: the regional RU at Bf Neustadt, a container operator from the terminal module, a charter operator, a transport authority, all played by the computer. The player answers from the network statement and the price list: offers alternatives, computes the charge for a path, applies cancellation fees, and settles a delay-attribution dispute using the delay records of the dispatcher game. Some customers offer favours or ask for a discount 'just this once'. One case explains the current conflict: the Bund's equity injections into DB InfraGO raised the cost base, and the cap on regional charges pushed the increase onto long-distance and freight.
game.win: A round has 10 to 15 customer cases in 15 to 20 minutes. The score counts correct charges and rules, revenue and customer satisfaction. An illegal discount or discrimination is found by the BNetzA audit at the end of the round: a fine, and a setback in career mode.
game.knowledge: Computing track access charges (train-km times the segment price, plus surcharges). Cancellation fees, framework agreements, the performance regime, non-discrimination, the cap on regional charges and the federal support for freight charges.
game.bigGame: Takes paths from the timetable planner and delay records from the dispatcher. Gives track charges as costs to the RU simulator, revenue to the IM's economics, and customer satisfaction to the passenger and freight RUs.

roles.name: Energy controller in the switching centre
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, which runs the switching centres for the 15 kV overhead line; DB Energie runs the 110 kV traction-power grid from its own control centre)
roles.summary: Works in a traction-power switching centre (Zentralschaltstelle, Zes) and controls the 15 kV, 16.7 Hz overhead-line network of a region remotely: the feeders in the substations, the switching posts and the section switches. Switches sections off and on for works, faults and emergencies, restores power after short circuits, and keeps the substations' loads within limits.
decisions: Switch off a section for an approved switching request at the agreed time
Switch off at once on an emergency request (person in danger, fire, tree on the wire)
Decide whether to re-energise after a trip, or keep the section off and send staff
Find a fault by switching sections back on one at a time
Confirm with the signaller that no electric train can enter a switched-off section
Re-energise only after every earth is reported removed and the area clear
effects: Finding and isolating a fault fast brings most of a line back in minutes instead of hours.
Switching onto an earthed or occupied section can kill workers or destroy equipment.
Long switch-offs strand electric trains, with heat and evacuations, and stop traffic.
Managing loads avoids overloading substations at peaks, for example when many heavy freight trains start at once.
resources: A SCADA control system for 50 to 200 switches, several substations and switching posts
The switching programme and the register of all switching requests
Phone and radio links to signallers, emergency managers and earthing persons
One to three controllers per shift per switching centre
limits: DIN VDE 0105-100 / EN 50110-1 (the five safety rules) and EN 50122-1 (protection against electric shock)
DGUV Vorschrift 3/4 (electrical installations and equipment)
DB rules for switching requests, switch-off confirmations and earthing reports
Ril 408 and the ESO's electric-traction signals El 1 to El 6 for running towards switched-off sections
ArbZG; StGB § 222 for fatal switching errors
risks: Criminal liability for a fatal switching error
Shift work, with heavy stress in storms when many sections trip at once
Responsibility at a distance, without ever seeing the site

career.entry: Electrician training (e.g. Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik) or an electrical engineering degree, experience in overhead-line maintenance, then switching-centre training and authorisation
career.chances: EVG technical groups: about 4,000 to 5,200 EUR gross a month plus shift allowances

kpis: Switching requests carried out on time
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Switching Centre (Zentralschaltstelle)
game.loop: The player sees a single-line diagram of the overhead line of line 6250 in ARail's network: the substations Talsee and Bergheim, sections, section insulators and switching posts, with the electric units of the operations module drawing current (the branch to Waldau is not electrified). Switching requests come in for a night possession at Bf Neustadt. Then the autumn storm of the infrastructure module brings trees onto the line and a circuit breaker trips. The player switches off, asks the signaller to stop electric trains, finds the faulty section by switching back step by step, and re-energises only after the earthing person reports the earths removed.
game.win: A round takes about 20 minutes. The score counts how fast power returns to most sections, trains not stranded, and switching requests met. Energising a section while earths are on or workers are present is a fatal accident: the career ends and the prosecutor investigates.
game.knowledge: How the overhead line is divided into sections. The five safety rules. Protection trips and reclosing. The El signals.
game.bigGame: Takes switching requests from switching applicants and site managers, and faults from the infrastructure game. Gives power availability to operations (electric trains), outage times to the RU simulator and situation reports to the emergency manager.

roles.name: Switching applicant and earthing person
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager or construction company
roles.summary: Works on site wherever there are works on or near the overhead line. Applies to the switching centre to switch off the sections concerned, tests for absence of voltage and puts on the earths before anyone may start, and takes them off at the end. Usually a catenary fitter, foreman or site supervisor holding this extra authorisation, at DB InfraGO or at a contractor, often also the person responsible for the work under DIN VDE 0105-100 (Arbeitsverantwortliche/r).
decisions: Apply for the switch-off with the exact sections and times
Check the switch-off confirmation against the site and the section plan
Test for absence of voltage and earth both sides of the work area
Release the work area to the team, or refuse when anything is unclear
Decide what to do when the switch-off comes late or the wrong section is off
Remove and count the earths and report the area clear for re-energising
effects: Correct earthing is the last barrier against 15 kV and induced voltages.
A late switch-off eats into a short night possession, and every lost hour costs tens of thousands of EUR in idle machines and crews.
An earth left on causes a short circuit at switch-on and delays the morning traffic.
Refusing to release keeps the team safe but may cost the possession.
resources: Earthing poles, a voltage tester, the section plans, radio and phone to the switching centre
The authorisation as switching applicant and earthing person
A possession window of 4 to 8 hours
limits: DIN VDE 0105-100: the five safety rules
DGUV Vorschrift 3/4 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 (work in the track area)
DB rules for switching requests and earthing
Ril 132.0118 and the site's safety plan (lookouts, adjacent tracks)
ArbZG for night possessions
risks: Electric shock, often fatal
Being hit by a train on the adjacent track
Criminal liability when a colleague is hurt
Night work and bad weather

career.entry: Electrical or catenary training, then the switching and earthing course with regular refresher instruction
career.chances: Catenary fitter's pay plus allowances: about 3,000 to 4,000 EUR gross a month (EVG or construction tariff). The authorisation is a requirement for foreman and supervisor jobs.

roles.timescale: Minutes, within a night possession

game.title: Five Rules (Fünf Sicherheitsregeln)
game.loop: The player is on a night site at Bf Neustadt and must do the safety sequence in the right order with the right equipment: apply for the switch-off, compare the confirmation with the section plan, test for voltage, earth both sides, mark the area, release it to the team. Traps are hidden along the way: the confirmation names the wrong section, a section insulator is bridged, the adjacent track is still live with a train due, an earth is missing at the far end.
game.win: A round covers the start and end of one possession in 5 to 10 minutes. The player wins with the correct sequence, every trap caught and the release on time. A mistake ends in an injury scene (not graphic) and the game explains which rule was missed. In career mode the authorisation is withdrawn until retraining.
game.knowledge: The five safety rules. The switching-request procedure. How the overhead line is divided into sections. Risks from the adjacent track.
game.bigGame: Takes possession windows from the possession planner and responses from the energy controller. Gives works finished on time to the site manager and the infrastructure condition, and safety incidents to career mode.

roles.name: Station manager
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager, stations (DB InfraGO, business unit Personenbahnhöfe, formerly DB Station&Service)
roles.summary: Runs a group of passenger stations for DB InfraGO's station business, which has about 5,400 stations organised in regional station management units (Bahnhofsmanagements). Responsible for the condition, cleanliness, safety and accessibility of platforms, buildings, lifts and passenger information, for the station staff and service contracts and the retail tenants, and for relations with towns and transport authorities.
decisions: Set the cleaning and security level for each station within the budget
Prioritise repairs (lift, escalator, roof, lighting) and small investments
Plan for crowds at events (football match, festival) with the police and the RUs
Decide how firmly to enforce the house rules, with the 3-S centre and the federal police
Negotiate with the town about the forecourt, bike parking and the bus interchange
Propose stations for modernisation and accessibility programmes of the Bund and the Länder
effects: Passenger satisfaction and the feeling of safety. Station quality reports feed into transport-authority contracts and disputes over station charges.
A lift out of service makes the station unusable for wheelchair users, often for weeks when parts are missing.
Spending on cleanliness and security competes with a tight budget.
Crowd management prevents dangerous crowding on platforms.
resources: A station management unit with 50 to 200 stations and 50 to 300 staff and contractors
An operating budget of a few to tens of millions of EUR a year. Investment comes through federal and Länder programmes.
Revenue from station charges (per train stop, by station category) and rents
Authority: the house rules (Hausrecht), and contracts with cleaning and security firms
limits: ERegG and the station access conditions: station charges approved by BNetzA
EBO (platforms), TSI PRM (Regulation (EU) 1300/2014) and the Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz
Regulation (EU) 2021/782 (passenger rights: assistance at stations, with up to 24 hours' notice)
State building and fire safety law
§ 34a GewO for security staff, and the GDPR for CCTV
LuFV III quality indicators for stations
risks: Public exposure in the press and local politics for dirty or unsafe stations
Civil liability under the duty of care (Verkehrssicherungspflicht), for example for slips on ice
Stress from juggling many stakeholders

career.entry: A degree (business, engineering, real estate) or long experience in station service, plus leadership training
career.chances: Non-tariff management: about 5,500 to 8,000 EUR gross a month

roles.timescale: Days to months, and years for programmes

game.title: My Station (Mein Bahnhof)
game.loop: The player runs Bf Neustadt, Talsee and Altstadt on line 6250. The town's passengers move through Neustadt's underpass, the platforms and the bus stops; Talsee has one lift and Altstadt two. Each game week, the player splits the budget between cleaning, security, repairs and information, and handles incidents: a lift fault, graffiti, a crowd of fans on platform 2 after a match, winter ice. The mayor and the transport authority call in with demands. Passengers' moods and complaints show the result, and wheelchair users cannot reach the platforms while a lift is down.
game.win: A round is a season of 12 weeks in 15 to 30 minutes. The score counts the station quality index, passenger satisfaction, accessibility and the budget, with no serious accidents. Overspending, or an accident from neglected safety (ice, crowding), brings a liability claim and a press scandal, and in career mode a transfer.
game.knowledge: Accessibility rules. Assistance under passenger rights. The house rules and the duty of care. Station charges.
game.bigGame: Takes revenue from station charges and the budget from the IM's economics, and crowds from events and the RUs' timetables. Gives station quality to the transport-authority contracts and to the RUs' passenger numbers (mood affects ridership), and complaints to the press and politics.

roles.name: Operations district manager
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Leads the signallers of an operations district, together with its train controllers and block and crossing keepers: 50 to 150 staff on 10 to 40 interlockings, around the clock. Responsible for staffing every shift, qualifications and local rules, supervision and checks, investigating irregularities, and the operating side of possessions and new interlockings in the district.
decisions: Build the monthly shift plan to cover every box around the clock
Close a box or a line at night when no qualified signaller is available
Approve overtime and leave, and borrow staff from other districts
Recruit and train new signallers, with HR and the training centre
Investigate an irregularity and decide the measures (talk, retraining, suspension)
Issue local operating instructions and check that they are followed (supervision visits)
effects: An unfilled shift closes stations or lines. In August 2013 many trains could not stop at Mainz Hbf for weeks for lack of signallers.
Overtime and long shifts raise the error risk and the sickness rate.
Good training reduces irregularities and delays.
Years of short staffing drive people away and lead to conflicts with the union and the works council.
resources: 50 to 150 staff, about 10 to 20 % of them in training
A staff budget of a few million to about 10 million EUR a year
Roster tools, a stand-by pool and instructors
Authority: line manager with disciplinary powers. The works council co-decides on rosters.
limits: ArbZG and the EVG working-time and shift agreements. Rosters need the works council's consent (BetrVG § 87).
Ril 408, Ril 482 and the local instructions. Required periodic training and checks.
Fitness rules (medical and psychological examinations)
The IM's safety management system (Regulation (EU) 2018/762) and monitoring (Regulation (EU) 1078/2012)
EBA supervision
risks: Accountable for organisational failures when a box closes or after an accident
Caught between staff, union and management
Long hours and on-call duty

career.entry: Experienced signaller or dispatcher with leadership training, or an engineering degree and a trainee programme
career.chances: Upper tariff or non-tariff: about 5,500 to 7,500 EUR gross a month

kpis: Delay minutes and closures caused by staff shortage
roles.timescale: Days to months

game.title: Fill the Boxes (Stellwerke besetzen)
game.loop: The player leads the district of ARail's network: the mechanical box of Bergheim (1928), the relay boxes of Bf Neustadt and Waldau, the ESTW Talsee and the digital interlocking of Altstadt, plus three block and crossing posts, with about 60 signallers, each with qualifications per box, a contract and wishes. Every month they build the roster, reusing the crew module of the operations simulation (duties, working-time rules, sick calls, leave). They hire and train, with 12 months' lead time, and decide what to do when a night shift cannot be filled: overtime, borrow staff, or close the box. Irregularities come in and must be investigated, and the works council can refuse the roster.
game.win: A round covers 6 to 12 months in 15 to 30 minutes. The score counts shift coverage, closures (trains lost), overtime, turnover and irregularities. Repeated closures or an incident caused by fatigue end in removal from the post, with a union and press crisis.
game.knowledge: ArbZG (11 hours' rest, 10 hours at most). Co-determination on rosters. Qualification rules (local knowledge per box). Recruiting and training lead times.
game.bigGame: Takes the budget and headcount from IM management and trainees from HR. Gives staffed boxes, or closures, to all signaller games and the RU simulator, incidents to career mode, and job openings to career-mode players.

roles.name: Railway operations manager of the infrastructure manager
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, or a regional infrastructure manager, NE-Bahn)
roles.summary: The person appointed under the Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung (EBV) and confirmed by the supervisory authority (the EBA for federal railways, the Land for non-federal ones), who is personally responsible for the safe operation of the infrastructure. Issues the operating rules and their local supplements, approves deviations from the company's own rules, supervises staff and procedures, and takes measures after incidents. At a small regional IM it is one person, often also the managing director. At DB InfraGO the function is held by an appointed EBL with deputies for the regions. (Not to be confused with the EBL, the railway operations lab in Dresden.)
decisions: Approve or refuse a deviation from the company's own rules, such as running for weeks with a known fault or a temporary procedure; deviations from the EBO itself need an exemption from the authority (EBO § 3)
Issue or change operating instructions and local supplements
Order an operating restriction or a closure for safety
Give the operational acceptance of a new or changed installation and its operating rules, once technical acceptance, the risk assessment (CSM-RA) and any EBA authorisation are in place
Decide the measures after a dangerous event: training, a rule change or technology
Answer EBA findings and set corrective actions
Set the qualification requirements for operating staff
effects: Sets the safety level of all operations in the area. Rules that are too strict cost capacity; rules that are too loose raise the risk.
Corrective actions after incidents shape signallers' work for years.
EBA findings can restrict or stop operations.
Personal accountability becomes visible in court after an accident.
resources: A staff of specialists, and access to all incident data of the safety management system
Authority over the operating rules. No large budget of its own; requests measures from asset and operations management.
Deputies and the operations district managers
limits: EBV (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung): qualification, appointment, confirmation and duties
AEG § 4 (safety duties) and the IM's safety authorisation (Sicherheitsgenehmigung) issued by the EBA
EBO
Regulations (EU) 2018/762 (safety management system), 402/2013 (CSM-RA) and 1078/2012 (monitoring)
EUV: reporting to the BEU
StGB: liability for organisational negligence
risks: Personal criminal and civil liability after accidents
Removal from office if the authority withdraws its confirmation
On call during serious incidents
Public exposure after accidents

career.entry: An engineering degree or a long operating career, meeting the EBV requirements (education, years of practice, proof of knowledge), then confirmation by the authority
career.chances: Non-tariff: about 7,000 to 10,000 EUR gross a month at DB. At small regional IMs the role is often combined with the managing director.

roles.timescale: Months, and hours during incidents

game.title: Sign or Stop (Freigabe)
game.loop: Each card is a situation coming from the other games. A district wants a temporary procedure because the box at Bergheim cannot be staffed. Exit signal N2 at Bf Neustadt stays faulty for weeks and operations want to keep running on substitute signals. A new interlocking software version at Altstadt has an open issue. A near-miss report arrives. The player reads the facts and the rules and chooses: approve, approve with conditions, refuse, or close; for a deviation from the EBO the right answer is to ask the authority. The simulation then draws the consequences over the following months: risk builds up, an EBA audit arrives, an accident may happen.
game.win: A round has 10 to 15 cases over a simulated year, played in 15 to 25 minutes. The score rewards keeping the risk low while operations continue, and passing the EBA audit. An accident traced back to an approval brings a court case and the withdrawal of the authority's confirmation, which ends operational leadership in career mode.
game.knowledge: The EBV. What the EBL may decide and what needs the authority. The significance test of the CSM-RA. The duties of a safety management system. Typical risk controls and how they wear down over time.
game.bigGame: Takes requests and incidents from all im-operations and im-assets roles. Gives rule changes and operating restrictions (capacity) to the network and the RU simulator, and EBA findings to career mode.

roles.name: Platform dispatcher and station supervisor
roles.organisation: Station operator (DB InfraGO, Personenbahnhöfe) or the railway undertaking, at large stations and on busy S-Bahn trunk lines; elsewhere the train crew or the driver dispatches the train
roles.summary: Stands on the platforms of a large station or an S-Bahn trunk line and gets trains away safely and on time. Watches boarding and the doors, gives the departure order (Abfahrauftrag, signal Zp 9) when the platform edge is clear, coordinates platform changes and late connections with the signaller and the railway undertakings, and keeps crowds in check with the 3-S centre and the federal police. The platform-train interface is where passengers are trapped in doors, fall between train and platform or are struck by passing trains.
decisions: Give the departure order (Zp 9) only when the doors are closed and nobody is trapped or too close to the edge
Hold a departure for a few seconds for running passengers or a wheelchair ramp, or send the train on time
Let a train wait for a late connection when the railway undertaking asks for it, within the time the signaller and the dispatcher allow
Agree a platform change with the signaller and make sure passengers are told in time
Close a platform section or stop people coming down when it gets too full, with the 3-S centre and the federal police
Stop trains by radio or the emergency call when a person falls onto the track or is trapped in a door
Call the mobility service and the train crew when a wheelchair user needs a ramp
effects: Every 30 seconds of extra dwell at a trunk-line station costs the following trains their slots: with headways of 2 to 3 minutes, one long dwell delays a whole series.
A departure order given too early can drag a trapped passenger along. The platform-train interface causes a large share of passenger injuries on the railway.
A late platform change without announcement leaves passengers behind and crowds the stairs.
Holding for a connection keeps travellers on their journeys but pushes delay into the next node.
resources: A radio linked to the signaller and the train crews, the departure-order disc or lamp (Befehlsstab), platform monitors and CCTV, the public-address system or a line to the announcer
1 to 4 dispatchers per shift at a large station with 600 to 1,500 trains a day
Authority: the departure order and platform safety; no say over the train order (signaller and dispatcher) or connections (railway undertakings)
limits: Ril 408: train dispatch (Zugabfertigung) and the dispatch procedures, including those where the driver dispatches with cameras
The ESO and Ril 301: departure signal Zp 9 and the other signals of the dispatch procedure
TSI OPE: train departure and safety-related communication
Regulation (EU) 2021/782 and TSI PRM: assistance for persons with reduced mobility
The station operator's house rules and the federal police's powers in stations (Bundespolizeigesetz)
ArbZG and the EVG shift agreements
risks: Criminal and civil liability when a passenger is trapped and dragged after a departure order
Shift work outdoors on draughty platforms in all weather
Abuse and aggression from passengers in delays and crowds
Trauma after suicides or people struck at the platform
Job loss as dispatch by the driver with cameras spreads

career.entry: Training in train dispatch and the station's local rules (a few weeks to a few months) after a railway operations apprenticeship or as a career changer, a fitness check and regular refresher training
career.chances: EVG groups for operating staff: about 2,900 to 3,600 EUR gross a month plus shift allowances. A common way into signaller training.

kpis: Dwell-time overruns and delay caused at the station
Zero accidents at the platform-train interface
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Right Away (Abfahrt!)
game.loop: The player stands on the island platform 2 of Bf Neustadt (tracks G2 and G3), where the regional trains of the signaller game meet for passengers to change, and the passengers of the passengers and journeys modules stream through the underpass. Train after train arrives: the player watches the doors and the platform edge on the camera view, gives the departure order, and decides whether to wait for a running passenger, a wheelchair ramp or a late connection. When track G2 is closed for the repair team, they agree platform changes with the signaller and get them announced. After the match the fans crowd platform 2 and the player must decide when to stop access.
game.win: A round is a peak hour of 15 to 25 trains in 10 to 15 minutes. The score adds punctuality (dwell overruns cost the following trains), passengers who caught their trains and connections, and calm on the platform. A departure order with a passenger trapped or too close to the edge is a danger to people: the round fails and career mode opens an investigation. Good rounds open the way to signaller training.
game.knowledge: The train-dispatch procedure of Ril 408 and its signals. Why dwell time is capacity. Crowd density limits on platforms. Assistance rules for persons with reduced mobility.
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable and the train order from the signaller and dispatcher games and the passengers from the passengers and journeys modules. Gives dwell times and delays to the signaller and the RU simulator, missed connections to the journeys and the passenger-rights agents, and crowding incidents to the station manager and the federal police.

roles.name: On-site possession manager (technically authorised person)
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO) or the construction contractor, named in the operating and construction instructions (Betra)
roles.summary: Is the operating link between a construction or maintenance site and the signaller. Named in the Betra for each possession, the technically authorised person requests the track closure from the signaller at the agreed time, makes sure the closure and its blocking aids are in place before machines and teams go onto the track, arranges the works trains into and out of the possession (Sperrfahrten), and at the end reports the track fit for traffic (Befahrbarkeit), with a temporary speed limit where the new track has not settled yet.
decisions: Request the closure from the signaller at the time in the Betra and check the confirmation (track, km, blocking aids) before anyone goes onto the track
Order works trains and track machines into the possession as closed-track movements (Sperrfahrten) and agree their moves with the signaller
Decide at the point of no return whether the works will finish in time, or stop them and restore the track
Ask the signaller and the possession planner to extend the possession, knowing that it delays the morning trains
Check the track after the works (gauge, points, fastenings, ballast) and report it fit for traffic
Set the handback speed, for example a temporary slow order after tamping until the ballast has settled
Refuse to start when the closure, the switch-off or the lookouts are not in place
effects: A possession started late or handed back late costs the works hours of their window or delays the first trains of the morning.
Reporting a track fit for traffic that is not (a fastening missing, a point not adjusted) can derail a train.
A handback slow order protects the new track but costs every train a minute or more for days.
Stopping in time at the point of no return protects the timetable; pushing on often ends in an overrun.
resources: The Betra, the closure confirmation, a radio and a phone to the signaller, the track gauge and measuring tools
A possession window of 4 to 8 hours at night or 2 to 3 days at a weekend, with machines and crews costing several thousand to tens of thousands of EUR an hour
Authority: the operating side of the site; no say over the timetable or the length of the window
limits: Ril 406 (Fahren und Bauen) and the Betra of the possession
Ril 408: closures, closed-track movements (Sperrfahrten), reporting the track fit for traffic
The IM's acceptance limits for track works (gauge, alignment, consolidation) and the handback speeds after tamping
DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 and Ril 132.0118: the site's safety plan (lookouts, protection of the adjacent track)
VOB/B: overruns, idle times and claims in the construction contract
ArbZG for night and weekend work; StGB § 315a
risks: Criminal liability after a derailment on a track wrongly reported fit for traffic
Being struck by a train on the adjacent track
Night and weekend work, with pressure from the site manager and the morning timetable at the same time

career.entry: A technical training (track, signalling or catenary) or a civil engineering degree, experience on sites, then the IM's course and appointment as technically authorised person
career.chances: DB InfraGO technical groups or construction-industry tariff: about 3,800 to 5,000 EUR gross a month plus night and site allowances.

kpis: Possessions started and handed back on time
Zero incidents to staff and trains
Handback slow orders and their duration
roles.timescale: Minutes to hours, within a possession

game.title: Handback (Gleis befahrbar)
game.loop: A night possession at Bf Neustadt: track G3 is renewed (the maintenance story's renewal) between 23:30 and 04:45. The player requests the closure from the signaller, checks the confirmation, lets the tamping machine and the ballast train in as closed-track movements, and follows the works on a progress bar fed by the infrastructure module (a machine breakdown, rain, a missing crew). At the point of no return the player decides: push on, extend, or restore the track. At the end they check the track against the acceptance limits and choose the handback speed.
game.win: A round is one possession in 10 to 15 minutes. The score counts works done, the handback time against the first train at 05:00, and the handback slow order. A track reported fit for traffic outside the limits ends in a derailment scene: the round fails, and career mode opens an investigation. An overrun costs the RU simulator delays and the contractor penalties.
game.knowledge: Ril 406 and the Betra. Closures and closed-track movements under Ril 408. The acceptance limits of new track and why tamped track needs a slow order. The cost of an overrun.
game.bigGame: Takes the possession window and the Betra from the possession planner, the works from the infrastructure game and the closure from the signaller games. Gives the handback time and slow orders to the signallers and the RU simulator, works delivered to the asset condition, and overrun costs to the contractor (site manager).

roles.name: Board member of the infrastructure manager (operations and capacity)
roles.name_de: Vorstand/Vorständin der DB InfraGO AG (Betrieb, Fahrplan und Kapazität)
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO AG, a subsidiary of DB AG and so owned by the Bund; at a regional IM, the managing director)
roles.summary: Leads the operations and capacity side of Germany's main infrastructure manager: about 33,000 km of line, some 5,400 stations, the operations centres and their signallers and dispatchers, and a network timetable of around a billion train-km a year. Decides with the board how capacity is split between traffic and construction (the Generalsanierung corridors), proposes the network statement and the track access charges for BNetzA's approval, sets staffing and training targets for operations, and answers to the supervisory board, to the Bund's steering targets for the common-good oriented InfraGO, and to the public for punctuality.
decisions: Set how much capacity goes to construction: long corridor closures (Generalsanierung) or works under traffic
Propose the track access charges and the network statement, and decide whether to challenge a BNetzA decision in court
Set the headcount and training targets for signallers and dispatchers, and which boxes may close at night
Set the order in which old interlockings are replaced by digital interlockings and ETCS, within the funding the Bund grants
Negotiate funding and quality targets with the Bund (LuFV, Generalsanierung, the steering targets)
Decide the company's response to a national disruption or a serious accident (task forces, public statements, measures)
effects: The split between construction and traffic shapes punctuality for years: long-distance punctuality fell to about 62 % in 2024, much of it from works on an old, overloaded network.
Charges set the RUs' costs and so modal shift: freight leaves rail when they rise.
Staffing decisions decide whether boxes and lines stay open.
Every decision is public and political: the Bund, the Länder, the RUs and the press watch.
resources: DB InfraGO: some 55,000 to 60,000 staff, about 33,000 km of line and some 5,400 stations
Investment from the Bund and own funds of roughly 15 to 20 billion EUR a year, with the LuFV III (about 86 billion EUR for 2020 to 2029) and, from 2025, the federal special fund for infrastructure
Revenue of about 5 to 6 billion EUR a year from track access charges, plus station charges
Authority: the board's corporate decisions, within the Stock Corporation Act, the supervisory board, the DB group and the Bund as owner and funder
limits: AEG and ERegG: independence of the essential functions (path allocation and charging), non-discrimination, charges approved by BNetzA
LuFV III and the funding agreements under the BSWAG, with their quality indicators and penalties
The Bund's steering of the common-good oriented InfraGO (Gemeinwohlorientierung)
Stock Corporation Act (AktG § 93: duty of care and liability of board members)
Directive 2012/34/EU (Single European Railway Area) and the Fourth Railway Package
BetrVG and the collective agreements with EVG (and GDL where it represents members)
risks: Dismissal or non-renewal of the contract when punctuality or projects fail
Civil liability to the company under AktG § 93 (with the business judgment rule)
Public exposure: Bundestag committee hearings, press campaigns
Very long hours and constant availability

career.entry: A degree (engineering, economics, law) and 15 to 25 years of management experience at an infrastructure manager, a railway undertaking, a consultancy or a ministry; appointed by the supervisory board for 3 to 5 years
career.chances: Board pay at a DB subsidiary: a fixed salary in the order of several hundred thousand EUR a year plus variable pay tied to targets such as punctuality, infrastructure condition and staff.

kpis: Condition of the network (LuFV quality indicators)
Works delivered and closures kept to plan
Financial result and the Bund's steering targets
roles.timescale: Months to years: the timetable year, the budget year, the LuFV period

game.title: Board Table (Vorstandssitzung)
game.loop: Each quarter the player sits at the board table of a regional infrastructure company built from ARail's network (line 6250 with the branch to Waldau, scaled up to a region). They split the capacity between traffic and construction, set the charges they propose to the regulator, the headcount of signallers, and the order of interlocking renewals: the mechanical box of Bergheim first, or the relay box of Waldau? The operations and infrastructure modules run the quarter: punctuality, condition, closures and staff shortages come back, with the Bund, the RUs and the press reacting.
game.win: A round covers 3 to 5 years in 20 to 30 minutes. The score weighs punctuality, network condition, works delivered, finances and staff. Failure: BNetzA rejects the charges, a funding target is missed and the Bund claws back money, or a series of closures from staff shortage hits the news; in career mode the supervisory board does not renew the contract.
game.knowledge: How the IM is financed and regulated (LuFV, BSWAG, track access charges, BNetzA). The trade-off between construction and capacity. The lead times of staff and of interlocking renewals.
game.bigGame: The hub between politics and operations: takes the budget and targets from the federal funding officer, the minister and the Bundestag, and approved charges from BNetzA. Gives possession policy to the possession planner, headcount to the district managers, charges to track-access-sales and the RU simulator, and renewal priorities to the asset manager.

roles.name: Asset manager
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), asset management of a regional unit (Regionalbereich), working with the production units (Produktionsdurchführung) that do the maintenance
roles.summary: Steers the condition of the assets in a regional network of DB InfraGO. Plans how maintenance money and federal replacement money (LuFV) are spent, approves, defers or declines the ALVs' proposals, sets the maintenance strategy and staff plan with the production unit, picks the winning bids with procurement, and answers for the network condition and the delays the infrastructure causes.
decisions: Split the year's money between maintenance (own funds) and LuFV-funded renewals, and rank the renewals in the regional investment plan
Approve, defer or decline the ALVs' repair, monitoring and renewal proposals
Bundle renewals into a few long closures or spread them over many short possessions (on a high-performance corridor, fit them into the Generalsanierung that the head office plans)
Set the staff plan per discipline with the production unit and the maintenance district managers: own technicians or framework contractors, and the on-call model
Choose the most economic bid with procurement (GWB § 127); procurement awards and signs the contract
Accept a permanent speed reduction instead of an expensive repair, knowing that a cut in capacity that is more than slight needs the EBA's approval (AEG § 11)
Fit condition monitoring (switch diagnosis, level crossing remote monitoring) instead of inspecting more often
effects: The network condition and the LuFV quality indicators (theoretical journey-time loss, infrastructure defects, bridge condition) change over years, not weeks

Federal money that is not drawn down in its budget year can lapse or go to other projects; a shortfall against the LuFV minimum replacement investment must be paid back, and missed quality targets cost money (LuFV sanctions)
Deferred renewals turn into faults, speed restrictions and performance-regime delay minutes for every railway undertaking
Bundled closures disrupt passengers and freight for months but save money and possession time
Thin staffing makes fault response slower at night and at weekends
resources: A regional network or production area of about 1,500–3,000 km of track with tens of thousands of assets (Germany: about 33,000 km of lines and 61,000 km of track)
Maintenance money of about €50–150 M a year (DB InfraGO's own funds, mainly from track access charges; the LuFV sets a minimum maintenance contribution)

Replacement money of about €200–600 M a year (federal, under LuFV III and, since 2025, the special fund for infrastructure (Sondervermögen Infrastruktur und Klimaneutralität)); federal money follows the budget year
300–800 maintenance staff in the production unit, framework contractors, and inspection and measurement services
Decision rights: approves measures and contracts up to internal value limits; larger ones go to the head of the regional unit or the board
limits: AEG § 4 and EBO § 2: the infrastructure must be kept safe and in order
AEG § 11: closing a line or reducing its capacity more than slightly needs the EBA's approval, after offering the line to other infrastructure managers

LuFV III (2020–2029, a successor is being negotiated): quality indicators, minimum replacement investment, minimum maintenance contribution and sanctions; BSWAG for federal money (since the 2023 amendment also some maintenance, e.g. in Generalsanierungen); BHO § 45 (budget year)
ERegG § 39: the performance regime (Anreizsystem) in the network statement (Schienennetz-Nutzungsbedingungen)
GWB / SektVO above the EU thresholds (works €5,404,000 from 2026); below them the federal funding conditions and the company's own procurement rules
Inspection periods of Ril 821 (track), Ril 892 (signalling), Ril 804.8001 (structures) and Ril 997 (overhead lines); EBA supervision (AEG § 5)
Major capacity restrictions must be announced to the market in advance (ERegG, EU Delegated Decision 2017/2075)
risks: Criminal liability for organisational fault (StGB §§ 13, 222, 315) when an accident follows a known defect that was left unrepaired; administrative fines for a breach of supervisory duty (OWiG § 130)
Public exposure: the network condition is reported in the press and discussed in the Bundestag
Blame for lost federal money or overspending; job loss in reorganisations
Long hours, and on call for major incidents

career.entry: Engineering degree (Diploma or Master in civil, electrical or transport engineering, e.g. TU Dresden), then 8–15 years as ALV, maintenance district manager, construction supervisor or project manager, and an internal leadership programme
career.chances: Paid above the tariff (AT): about €90,000–140,000 a year plus a bonus. Head of a regional unit or a seat on the board of DB InfraGO pays €200,000 and more.

kpis: Network condition grade (DB InfraGO condition report, school grades) against the target, and the LuFV quality indicators
Delay minutes caused by the infrastructure and money paid under the performance regime
Number and length of speed restrictions (La)
Replacement money drawn down and maintenance budget kept
Share of inspections on time (EBA audit)
roles.timescale: months to years (budget years, a 5–10 year renewal plan)

game.title: Budget Years (Haushaltsjahre)
game.loop: Each round is one budget year of the district on the layout's line map. The player splits the maintenance and LuFV money, sets the staff plan per discipline, approves or defers the ALVs' proposals, ranks the renewals and picks the winning bids. A fast run plays the year (wear, faults, inspections, the EBA audit) while a live day on the layout shows the faults holding trains. At the year's end the network grade, delay minutes and money come back, and they decide next year's money.
game.win: Three to five years with the network grade at or better than the target (3.2 in the example, standing in for the LuFV quality indicators), delay minutes below the starting level, at least 95 % of inspections on time and no replacement money left unused. A missed target cuts next year's money. Two misses end the round with a 'reassignment' in career mode. An accident caused by a known defect that was deferred ends the round at once and leads to an investigation.
game.knowledge: Life-cycle cost and the wear curve; use it or lose it (simplified from the federal budget year and the LuFV minimum replacement investment); the LuFV indicators; the performance regime; the value of information (inspecting against condition monitoring); the benefit-cost ratio and annuities; AEG § 11 for permanent capacity cuts.
game.bigGame: Takes LuFV and federal money from the funding officer and the budget committee MPs, and the track access charges the railway undertakings pay. Gives the network condition, speed restrictions and delay minutes to the operations simulator and the railway undertakings, posts and budgets to the maintenance district managers, renewal orders to planners and contractors, and possession requests to the possession planner.

roles.name: Asset responsible per discipline (ALV)
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), production unit (Produktionsdurchführung), maintenance district
roles.summary: Responsible for the assets of one discipline (track, signalling and telecoms, structures or electrical) in an area. Evaluates inspection findings, sets deadlines for defects, orders immediate measures and proposes repairs and renewals to the asset manager.
decisions: Classify an inspection finding against the limits and set the deadline for fixing it
Order an immediate speed restriction (Langsamfahrstelle) or take an asset out of service when a limit is reached
Propose a repair, condition monitoring, a like-for-like renewal or a renewal with new technology
Change the inspection plan, staying within the minimum the rules require
Order an extra inspection or measurement run when the known condition is too uncertain
Accept or refuse a contractor's small repair as done to the rules
effects: A speed restriction costs every train time and the railway undertakings delay minutes; a missing one risks a derailment
Good proposals become renewal projects; poor ones waste replacement money
Findings left overdue show up in the EBA audit
Accurate knowledge of the assets reduces the uncertainty of the asset manager's plans and the planners' cost risk
resources: A few thousand assets of one discipline over 100–300 km of line
The findings of 10–40 technicians and inspectors of the discipline (their line manager is the maintenance district manager)
Small repairs paid from the maintenance money (orders up to about €50,000); renewals only as proposals
Measurement train data, diagnostics, drone flights, and the asset register (SAP, asset information model)
limits: Ril 821 (inspecting the track, with the limits SR_A, SR_100 and SR_lim), Ril 892 (maintaining signalling), Ril 804.8001 (inspecting structures), Ril 997 (overhead lines)
EBO § 2 (safety); EN 13848 (track geometry quality); TSI INF
Internal deadlines per defect class; the asset manager's budget approval
EBA supervision of inspection records (AEG § 5)
risks: Personal criminal liability (StGB §§ 222, 229, 315) when a known defect causes an accident, because the ALV signs the findings (compare the derailment at Garmisch-Partenkirchen in June 2022, five dead, defective concrete sleepers, after which staff responsible for the track were charged)
Pressure from operations not to impose speed restrictions
Workload and backlog; on call for major faults

career.entry: Engineering degree (Bachelor or Master, civil or electrical), or a state-certified technician or master craftsman with long field experience, plus DB's ALV qualification for the discipline
career.chances: Upper groups of the DB tariff (EVG) or entry above the tariff: about €60,000–85,000 a year

kpis: Share of assets whose condition is known well
Inspection compliance and cost per km
roles.timescale: days to months (findings, deadlines, the yearly plan)

game.title: The Findings Desk (Befundbewertung)
game.loop: A stack of inspection findings arrives: measurement-train charts, photos of a switch, the diagnostic log of a signal, a bridge report, each with its known condition and its uncertainty. First the player classifies each finding against the rules, where a right answer exists. Then the player decides the measure under a budget and with a limited number of technicians: watch, inspect again, repair, monitor, impose a speed restriction or propose a renewal. The year is run, and every consequence is traced back to the finding that caused it.
game.win: All safety-relevant findings handled by their deadlines, no derailment and no wrong-side failure, few unneeded speed restrictions, the budget kept. A defect at SR_lim that is not acted on ends the round as a serious incident. Repeated audit findings cost the ALV qualification in career mode.
game.knowledge: The limits of Ril 821 and EN 13848, deadlines per defect class, inspection intervals, reading measurement charts and diagnostic logs, uncertainty and the value of an extra inspection.
game.bigGame: Takes inspection results from the inspectors and technicians, and the budget from the asset manager. Gives proposals to the asset manager, speed restrictions to the timetable planner and the operations simulator (journey-time losses), and repair orders to the dispatcher.

roles.name: Maintenance and fault dispatcher
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), maintenance control centre of a production unit
roles.summary: Staffs the maintenance control centre of a district around the clock. Takes fault reports from signallers and train drivers, sends the emergency team, the technician on call or a contractor, asks the signaller for closures, and schedules the day technicians' planned work.
decisions: Rank the open faults by safety and by the number of trains they hold
Send the emergency team on shift, take a day technician off planned work, call the technician on call, or call off the framework contractor
Ask the signaller for a track closure or a possession for the repair
Order an inspection, a drone flight or a measurement after a report
End or extend a shift within the working-time limits
Escalate to the emergency manager or the ALV (major incident, cable theft, storm)
effects: Response time decides how many trains are delayed or cancelled, and how much is paid under the performance regime
Taking day technicians off planned work delays the planned inspections (EBA audit)
Overtime and contractor call-outs use up the maintenance budget
Tired technicians at night make mistakes
resources: One or two emergency teams (vans) per discipline, a technician on call, and framework contractors who need 2–3 h to arrive
SAP work orders, fault reports, the diagnostics of electronic interlockings, and the operations centre's view of the trains
Authority to dispatch staff and order overtime within the tariff and the rota agreed with the works council
limits: ArbZG (§ 3: at most 10 h a day; § 5: 11 h rest; deviations only by tariff, § 7) and the EVG tariff rules on on-call duty (Rufbereitschaft)
Ril 408: closures and written orders are given by the signaller; Ril 132.0118 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78: work in the track needs protection, also when clearing a fault
Framework contracts (call-off conditions, SektVO)
The performance regime under ERegG § 39 and the network statement
risks: Shift work (nights, weekends, public holidays); high stress in major disruptions
Liability when a technician is sent into the track without protection
Blame from operations and the press for long disruptions

career.entry: Apprenticeship in an electrical or construction trade (e.g. Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik), years as a technician, then internal dispatcher training; or a Bachelor in engineering
career.chances: DB tariff (EVG): about €4,000–5,000 a month plus shift allowances, about €55,000–68,000 a year

kpis: Delay minutes caused by infrastructure faults
Faults still open at the end of the shift
Share of planned inspections on time
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Fault Night (Störungsnacht)
game.loop: A live night on the layout. Faults appear through their report paths: an axle counter fault from the interlocking, a train driver reporting a rough ride, a dark signal after cable theft, a broken lift. The player sees the town map with the vans, who is on shift and who is on call, and the trains being held. The player drags a team to a fault, asks the signaller for a closure, and decides whether to wake the technician on call or pay a contractor. The vans drive through the town while the trains wait or run.
game.win: Handover at 06:00 with every safety fault fixed or secured, the fewest delay minutes per euro spent, and no working-time or track-safety rule broken. A team sent into the track without a closure or protection ends the shift as an accident.
game.knowledge: Report paths and priorities, the working-time law and on-call rules, who may close a track, response-time arithmetic (setting off + travel + repair).
game.bigGame: Takes faults from the infrastructure simulation and the control system, and the available staff from the maintenance district managers. Gives repair times and delay minutes to the operations simulator and the railway undertakings, overtime costs to the asset manager, and closure requests to the signaller.

roles.name: Signalling maintenance technician
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), maintenance district
roles.summary: Maintains and repairs the signalling of a district: relay and electronic interlockings, signals, point machines, axle counters, level crossings and balises. Inspects by the plan, clears faults on call, and is the one qualified to declare a repaired safety installation fit for use again.
decisions: Find the fault: which element and which circuit, and what to measure first
Replace the part or module, or call in the specialist or the manufacturer
Run the prescribed tests before handing the installation back to the signaller
Record the fault and the fix in the work and fault log (Arbeits- und Störungsbuch) together with the signaller
Decide whether a temporary fix is allowed or the element stays blocked
Report suspected sabotage or cable theft to the federal police
effects: Until the repair is done, trains run on substitute signals and written orders, which is slow and error-prone
A wrong fix can cause a wrong-side failure, such as a signal showing proceed for an occupied track
Careful diagnosis means fewer repeat faults
resources: A van with tools, measuring instruments and spare parts; a laptop for the diagnostics of electronic interlockings
Circuit diagrams and the documentation of the interlocking
The manufacturer's hotline for electronic interlockings
limits: Ril 892 (maintaining signalling installations) and the documentation and test rules of each interlocking type; a separate qualification for each type
EBA VV BAU-STE: changes to signalling need approval and acceptance tests
EN 50126, EN 50129 and EN 50716 (software, the successor of EN 50128): no unauthorised change to safety logic
Ril 408 (cooperation with the signaller); Ril 132.0118 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 (track safety)
ArbZG and the on-call rules of the EVG tariff
risks: StGB § 315 (dangerous interference with rail traffic) and § 222 when a bridged contact or a skipped test causes an accident
Injury in the track from trains or electricity
Night call-outs, shift and on-call work, often working alone at night

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik (3.5 years, often at DB) or Elektroniker/in für Informations- und Systemtechnik, then DB's signalling qualifications for each interlocking type (several modules over years)
career.chances: DB tariff (EVG): about €3,500–4,500 a month plus on-call and shift allowances. A technician or master craftsman qualification opens the way to ALV, district manager and construction supervision.

roles.timescale: minutes to hours (a fault), a shift

game.title: Dark Signal (Signal dunkel)
game.loop: A fault comes in: signal N2 is dark, a track section shows occupied although it is clear, or a point does not lock. The player gets the panel picture, a simplified circuit diagram, a multimeter, and the signaller on the phone and in the work and fault log. Every measurement costs minutes while the trains on the layout run on substitute signals. The player forms a hypothesis, replaces a part and runs the tests. A shortcut (bridging a contact, skipping a test) is always possible and always faster.
game.win: The fault is fixed with the right tests and log entries in the least time. A skipped test triggers a hidden random roll: often nothing happens, sometimes a wrong-side failure follows later in the big game, is investigated by the BEU, and ends the career with a criminal case.
game.knowledge: The fail-safe principle, relay logic and the diagnostics of electronic interlockings, the rules for resetting axle counters, which tests are prescribed after which repair, reading circuit diagrams.
game.bigGame: Takes faults from the dispatcher. Gives repair times to the operations simulator and to the signaller's game (how long trains run on substitute signals), and risk events (wrong-side failures) to the accident investigator and the safety manager.

roles.name: Track maintenance technician
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), maintenance district
roles.summary: Maintains the permanent way of a district. Walks and checks track and switches, measures gauge and switch dimensions, replaces fastenings, sleepers and insulated joints, lubricates and adjusts switches, and secures a defect with a speed restriction until it is repaired.
decisions: Measure and judge a switch: gauge, check gauge, flangeway widths, blade contact
Fix a defect now under protection, or ask for a closure
Report a defect to the ALV and propose the measure
Ask the signaller to block a switch or impose a speed restriction until the repair
Choose the scope: replace single sleepers or the whole track panel
effects: A missed defect can derail a train; an unneeded restriction costs every train minutes
Small regular care (lubrication, tightening) can double a switch's life
Repairs in gaps between trains need protection by the safety plan; closures need the signaller and cost capacity
resources: A team of 2–6 with a van, small machines (rail saw, drill, hand tamping tools) and gauges
Spare material from the depot; short closures between trains
limits: Ril 821 (inspecting the track), Ril 824 (track works), Ril 820 (fundamentals of the permanent way)
EBO § 2 (safety), § 5 (gauge), § 9 (structure gauge)
Ril 132.0118 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78: no work in the track without a safety plan
ArbZG; EVG tariff
risks: Being hit by a train; injuries from machines and heavy material
Liability for a defect judged wrongly (StGB §§ 222, 315)
Outdoor work in all weathers, at night and at weekends

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Gleisbauer/in (3 years) or Tiefbaufacharbeiter/in, then DB's track maintenance qualification. A technician or master craftsman qualification is needed for supervisory roles.
career.chances: DB tariff (EVG): about €3,200–4,200 a month plus allowances

kpis: Speed restrictions caused by the track
roles.timescale: hours, a shift

game.title: Switch Check (Weichendurchsicht)
game.loop: The player inspects switch W1 on the layout. First the player asks the signaller to block W1 and the tracks over it for 40 minutes, or works in the gaps between trains if the safety plan allows it. The player chooses where to measure (gauge at the blade tip, check gauge, flangeway at the frog, blade contact), reads the values, compares them with the limits, and looks for the hidden defects (a broken fastening, a cracked frog, a worn blade). For each defect the player chooses to fix it now, report it, or keep the switch blocked. Trains keep coming, and the lookout's horn sends the player out of the track.
game.win: All defects found and classified correctly before the block ends, and every safety signal obeyed. A missed critical defect becomes a derailment risk in the operations simulator. Ignoring the horn ends the round.
game.knowledge: Switch geometry (gauge 1,435 mm and its tolerances, check gauge, flangeway), defect types, the limits and measures of Ril 821, how a switch is blocked for work.
game.bigGame: Takes inspection orders from the dispatcher and the ALV. Gives defects to the ALV, and speed restrictions and blocked switches to the operations simulator.

roles.name: Catenary and electrical maintenance technician
roles.name_de: Fachkraft Oberleitung und elektrotechnische Anlagen (50 Hz)
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), maintenance district
roles.summary: Maintains the 15 kV, 16.7 Hz overhead line and, in many districts, the 50 Hz electrical installations (switch heating, lighting, station power). Clears overhead line faults at any hour, and works only on sections that are switched off and earthed.
decisions: Locate the fault from the protection trip, train drivers' reports and the switching centre
Request switching off (Schaltantrag) and confirm that absence of voltage was verified and the section earthed before work starts
Choose a provisional fix (trains pass with lowered pantographs or a speed restriction) or a full repair
Order a tower car (Turmtriebwagen) and a closure of the adjacent track
Hand the section back for switching on
In winter, give switch heater faults priority
effects: Without traction power, every electric train in the section stops; diesel or towed replacements are needed
A provisional fix gets trains running again but can cause a dewirement later
A failed switch heater in frost freezes the switches and blocks the station
resources: An emergency team with a van and earthing equipment; a tower car or a road-rail lifting platform
Spare contact wire, droppers and insulators; support from the switching centre (Zentralschaltstelle)
limits: EN 50110-1 / DIN VDE 0105-100: the five safety rules
DGUV Vorschrift 3, EN 50122-1 (protective provisions), EN 50119, TSI ENE, Ril 997 (overhead lines)
The infrastructure manager's switching and earthing rules (switching requests, railway earthing by an earthing person)
Ril 132.0118 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78; ArbZG
risks: Electrocution at 15 kV; falls from height
Criminal liability when colleagues are hurt by a wrong switching or a missing earth
Call-outs at night and in storms; work in ice and heat

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik, qualified electrician (Elektrofachkraft) with DB's overhead line qualification; a technician or master craftsman qualification for more responsibility
career.chances: DB tariff (EVG): about €3,500–4,600 a month plus on-call, shift and height allowances

roles.timescale: minutes to hours

game.title: Five Rules (Fünf Sicherheitsregeln)
game.loop: A storm drops a tree on the overhead line west of the station, and the trains on the layout stop. To start work, the player requests switching off, waits until the energy controller has switched off and secured the section against reclosing, has the absence of voltage verified, has the earthing person earth and short-circuit both sides of the work site, has adjacent live parts covered or fenced, and only then gets the permission to work. Then the player chooses the repair (provisional or full) and the equipment, against the clock of stopped trains. The interface lets the player do these steps in the wrong order, which is fatal.
game.win: Power back on with every safety step in the right order, in the least time. A provisional fix carries a risk of dewirement into the following days. A step out of order ends the game at once, with an explanation of what would have happened.
game.knowledge: The five safety rules in order (switch off, secure against reclosing, verify absence of voltage, earth and short-circuit, cover adjacent live parts), the switching and earthing roles, the parts of an overhead line, the electrical signals for drivers (El signals).
game.bigGame: Takes outages from the energy controller and the dispatcher. Gives restoration times to the operations simulator and the railway undertakings (cancelled electric trains), and incident risk to the safety manager.

roles.name: Track inspector and measurement engineer
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), maintenance district and measurement services
roles.summary: Inspects the track on foot and by measurement. Plans and evaluates the runs of the track-geometry and ultrasonic measurement trains, reads the charts, classifies exceedances, and sets speed restrictions and deadlines for the ALV.
decisions: Evaluate a measurement run: which exceedances reach SR_A, SR_100 or SR_lim at the line speed
Order an immediate speed restriction or closure at SR_lim
Set the deadline and the measure for each defect (tamping, rail grinding, rail exchange)
Plan the next measurement runs and walking inspections by speed and load
Confirm a defect on site before acting on the chart
effects: Speed restrictions cost every train time (theoretical journey-time loss, an LuFV indicator)
A missed twist fault or rail crack can derail a train
Good data let tamping be planned ahead instead of emergency repairs
resources: Measurement train runs (track geometry, ultrasonic rail testing), several a year per line
Evaluation software, hand-held gauges, a measuring trolley, walking inspectors, drones
limits: Ril 821 (inspecting the track, measurement modules), EN 13848 (track geometry quality), TSI INF
EBO § 2 (safety), § 40 (speeds)
The list of temporary speed restrictions (La) published to the railway undertakings
Track safety for walking inspections (Ril 132.0118, DGUV Vorschrift 77/78)
risks: Liability for a missed exceedance (StGB §§ 222, 315)
Walking in the track, which needs protection
Pressure from operations to lift restrictions early

career.entry: Bachelor in civil engineering or surveying, or an experienced track technician with further training; DB's inspector qualification
career.chances: Upper groups of the DB tariff (EVG): about €4,000–5,500 a month

kpis: Exceedances found and handled on time
roles.timescale: days to months (measurement cycles)

game.title: Reading the Chart (Messschrieb)
game.loop: The player gets the charts of a measurement run over 10 km of line 6250: longitudinal level, alignment, twist, gauge and cant, with the line's speed bands. The player marks each exceedance, classifies it (SR_A, SR_100, SR_lim), computes a twist from the cant values over the measuring base, and sets a measure and a deadline. Then the season runs: the defects grow at uncertain rates, the tamping machine has only a few nights free, and the player's speed restrictions slow the trains in the operations simulator.
game.win: Every SR_lim defect acted on at once, the others planned in time, and the fewest minutes lost to unneeded restrictions. A missed SR_lim causes a derailment event; too many unneeded restrictions bring complaints from the railway undertakings.
game.knowledge: Track geometry parameters and their limits, computing twist (mm per m over a base), how the limits depend on speed, the list of temporary speed restrictions (La).
game.bigGame: Takes measurement runs from the infrastructure simulation. Gives defects to the ALV, tamping orders to the track machine operator, and speed restrictions to the timetable planner and the operations simulator.

roles.name: Lookout
roles.organisation: track safety contractor (Sicherungsunternehmen), prequalified with the infrastructure manager
roles.summary: Watches for approaching trains and warns the workers in the track in time with the horn (signals Ro 1 to Ro 3), so that everyone is out of the danger zone before the train passes. Does nothing else while on duty.
decisions: Take the post the safety plan gives, and check that the required sight distance is really there
Warn: Ro 1 (train on the adjacent track), Ro 2 (clear the working track), Ro 3 (clear the working track at once)
Count heads: confirm that everyone is out of the danger zone
Have the work stopped when sight is lost (fog, curve, noise) and tell the safety supervisor
Refuse a position or task that the safety plan does not cover
effects: A warning given too late can kill; false alarms cost work time and the workers' trust
Stopping the work in fog delays the possession but keeps people alive
resources: A multi-tone horn, a flag or lamp, and a radio; on some sites an automatic track warning system
The safety plan (Sicherungsplan) with the positions and the warning time
limits: DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 (work in the area of tracks), DGUV Regel 101-024; Ril 132.0118
Signal book (Ril 301, ESO): the signals Ro 1, Ro 2 and Ro 3
Warning time = clearing time + a safety margin; required sight distance = line speed × warning time
Lookouts are the last resort in the order of precedence; the safety plan decides whether they are allowed at all
Exclusive duty (no other work while on post); relief for breaks (ArbZG § 4)
Fitness requirements (sight, hearing, colour vision) checked by an occupational physician; minimum wage (MiLoG, €13.90 from 2026)
risks: Being hit by a train; criminal liability (StGB § 222) for a missed warning
Night work, heat and cold, monotonous attention, low pay and short contracts

career.entry: No trade needed: a course of one to three weeks with an exam at a prequalified safety contractor, a fitness examination, and regular refresher courses
career.chances: About €15–20 an hour (minimum wage plus allowances; some firms pay by the security or the construction tariff). With experience, safety supervisor.

roles.timescale: seconds

game.title: Ro 2!
game.loop: First the player computes the sight distance: at 160 km/h and a warning time of 20 s, how far must you see? (889 m). Then the player stands at a lookout point on the layout while a gang works on track G3. Trains from the operations simulator, or from the real control system, approach on both tracks and become visible only at the sight distance. Fog, noise, a curve and a worker's question distract. The player sounds the right signal in time and confirms that everyone is clear.
game.win: For every train: everyone clear before the safety margin, the right signal for the right track, and few false alarms. A late warning with someone still in the track ends the round, and this branch of the career, at once.
game.knowledge: The Ro signals, the arithmetic of warning time and sight distance, when a lookout alone is not enough (an automatic warning system or a closure is needed).
game.bigGame: Takes the train flow from the operations simulator or the control system, and the safety plan from the track safety planner through the safety supervisor. Gives work interruptions (lost productivity) to the site manager, and incidents to the safety chain.

roles.name: Track safety supervisor
roles.organisation: track safety contractor (Sicherungsunternehmen)
roles.summary: Leads the track safety at a worksite for the safety contractor. Checks that the safety plan fits the real site, sets up the protection it prescribes, briefs and places the lookouts, checks them during the shift, and stops the work when the protection no longer holds.
decisions: Check the safety plan against the real site (sight lines, speeds, adjacent tracks, noise) before work starts
Set up and test the protection the plan prescribes (closure confirmed by the signaller, fixed barrier, automatic warning system or lookouts)
Brief every worker and collect their signatures
Relieve lookouts for breaks and to keep their attention
Stop the work when the protection fails (fog, a fault in the warning system, a lookout missing) and demand a change of plan from the planner or the client
Report deviations to the construction supervisor and the client
effects: The quality of the protection on site decides whether people die in the track
More lookouts or a warning system cost money; stopping the work costs possession time
Repeated deviations cost the safety contractor its prequalification
resources: 5–30 lookouts, automatic warning systems, fixed barriers, radios
The safety plan; the authority to stop the work
limits: DGUV Vorschrift 77/78, DGUV Regel 101-024, Ril 132.0118, the signal book (Ril 301, ESO)
The safety plan: changes of the protection only through the planner or the client
ArbSchG § 8 (cooperation of several employers); BaustellV
Prequalification of safety contractors; ArbZG; MiLoG
risks: Criminal (StGB § 222) and civil liability after an accident
Conflict with the site manager, who wants speed
Night work and long shifts

career.entry: Several years as a lookout, then a further course and exam as safety supervisor (Sicherungsaufsicht)
career.chances: About €18–25 an hour, €3,200–4,200 a month

kpis: Incidents and near misses (must be zero)
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Safety on Site (Sicherungsaufsicht)
game.loop: The player receives the safety plan for a gang of 12 on track G3, with traffic on track G2. Before work starts the player walks the site on the layout and checks it: does each post really see far enough, is the warning system's start point where the plan puts it, is the curve in the plan? One error is hidden in the plan. The player briefs the gang, places the lookouts and starts work. Then the shift runs with trains from the operations simulator: fog comes in, a lookout needs a break, the warning system reports a fault, the site manager wants to move the gang to a section the plan does not cover. The player re-places, relieves, demands a change of plan, or stops the work.
game.win: No one in danger, the hidden error in the plan found before work starts, and the least work time lost. A gap in the protection while a train passes ends the round. The results count toward the contractor's prequalification.
game.knowledge: The order of precedence among protection measures, sight distance calculation, the rules for warning systems, working time and relief, who may change a safety plan.
game.bigGame: Takes the safety plan from the track safety planner, the site and the possession from the possession planner and the site manager, and the trains from the operations simulator. Gives protection costs and work interruptions to the site manager, and incidents to the safety manager and the EBA.

roles.name: Track safety planner
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), or a track safety contractor or consultancy commissioned by the client
roles.summary: Plans how the people working in or next to a track are protected from trains. Chooses the protection by the order of precedence (closing the track, a fixed barrier, an automatic warning system, lookouts), computes clearing times, warning times and sight distances, and writes the safety plan (Sicherungsplan) that the safety supervisor and the lookouts carry out.
decisions: Choose the protection by the order of precedence: close the working and adjacent tracks, fence them off with a fixed barrier, warn automatically, or warn with lookouts as the last resort
Compute the clearing time, the warning time and the required sight distance for each track and speed
Place the lookout posts, the warning system's start points and the barriers on the site plan
Request closures of adjacent tracks or lower speeds through the possession planning (Betra)
Rule out lookouts where the sight distance cannot be reached or machine noise drowns the horn
Revise the plan when the site, the timetable or the work changes, and sign it
effects: A plan that does not fit the site leaves people unprotected or forces the supervisor to stop the work
Closing adjacent tracks costs capacity and delay minutes; automatic warning systems cost money; lookouts are cheap but the least safe
A good plan makes the possession productive (fewer warnings, fewer interruptions)
resources: Site plans, line speeds, timetables and the Betra; calculation sheets and planning software
Framework contracts for automatic warning systems, fixed barriers and lookouts
limits: DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 and DGUV Regel 101-024 (protection measures for work in the track area); Ril 132.0118
ArbSchG § 4 (collective protection before individual protection), § 5 (risk assessment)
Ril 406 (Betra) and Ril 408 (closures)
The signal book (Ril 301, ESO): the Ro signals
BaustellV (coordination on construction sites)
risks: Criminal liability (StGB §§ 222, 229) when an accident follows from a wrong plan
Time pressure from the site and the possession planning; plans changed at short notice

career.entry: An experienced safety supervisor, technician or engineer with the infrastructure manager's course and exam for safety planners
career.chances: About €50,000–70,000 a year

kpis: Plans that work on site without changes
Incidents and near misses (must be zero)
Share of collective protection (closures, barriers, automatic systems)
roles.timescale: days to weeks (a plan); hours when a site changes

game.title: Order of Precedence (Rangfolge)
game.loop: The player gets two work requests: a gang of 12 on track G3 for two nights with track G2 in service, and a cable job on the line west of the station in a curve at 160 km/h. For each, the player chooses the protection by the order of precedence, computes clearing time, warning time and sight distance, and places posts, barriers and warning systems on the layout. A check run sends trains from the operations simulator past the sites: every place where the warning would come too late lights up. Costs and the capacity taken from traffic are counted.
game.win: Every worker protected with time to spare, collective protection chosen wherever it is reasonably possible, the plan within the budget and the closures the possession planner granted. A plan that relies on lookouts where the sight distance cannot be reached fails at once.
game.knowledge: The order of precedence, clearing time, warning time and sight distance (s = v × t), when lookouts are not allowed, the Ro signals.
game.bigGame: Takes works and possessions from the possession planner and the site manager. Gives the safety plan to the safety supervisor and the lookouts, closure requests for adjacent tracks to the possession planner, and protection costs to the site manager.

roles.name: Maintenance district manager
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), production unit (Produktionsdurchführung), maintenance district of one discipline
