roles.summary: Leads the maintenance team of one discipline in a district (track, signalling or overhead line): 30–100 technicians, their rosters, on-call duty and qualifications. Answers for inspections done on time, faults cleared and the safety of the own staff, and signs for the district's inspection records.
decisions: Set the shift and on-call rota of the month, and agree it with the works council
Decide who is trained on which interlocking type or machine, and when (qualifications take months)
Balance planned inspections, fault clearing and support for construction projects with too few people
Approve overtime within the working-time law and the tariff, or call off framework contractors
Request new posts and apprentices, and decide on transfers
Sign the district's inspection records, and escalate overdue inspections to the ALV and the asset manager
Carry out the employer's safety duties delegated to the district (risk assessment, instruction, protective equipment)
effects: Qualification gaps mean a fault on an old interlocking waits for the one technician who knows it
Overdue inspections show up in the EBA audit and, after an accident, in court
Overtime and on-call load drive sickness and resignations in an ageing workforce
A fair rota keeps the works council and the staff on side
resources: 30–100 technicians and inspectors of the discipline, 5–15 vans and small machines
A district of about 200–600 km of track
A share of the maintenance budget (several € M a year) and call-offs from framework contracts
limits: ArbZG (§§ 3, 5, 7) and the DB working-time tariff (EVG), including the on-call rules
BetrVG § 87 (1) nos. 2 and 3: the works council co-determines shift plans and overtime
ArbSchG §§ 3, 5, 13 (the employer's duties, risk assessment, delegation); DGUV Vorschrift 1
The inspection periods of Ril 821, Ril 892 or Ril 997, and the qualification rules for each installation type
AEG § 4, EBO § 2
risks: Criminal liability when an accident follows inspections or repairs left undone in the district (compare the charges after Garmisch-Partenkirchen in 2022)
Squeezed between staff shortage and the rules; conflicts with the works council and the staff
On call for major incidents

career.entry: Master craftsman or state-certified technician (Meister/in, Techniker/in) or a Bachelor in engineering, years as a technician or ALV, and DB's leadership training
career.chances: Top groups of the DB tariff (EVG) or above the tariff: about €70,000–95,000 a year

kpis: Faults cleared within their target times
Overtime and on-call hours per head
roles.timescale: a shift to a year (the monthly rota, the yearly inspection and training plan)

game.title: Rota (Dienstplan)
game.loop: The player runs a signalling district for a year in monthly turns. The district has 40 technicians, each with an age, qualifications for some installation types (the relay interlocking of 1979, the electronic interlocking, axle counters, level crossings), overtime on the account and a chance of leaving. Each month the player sets the rota and the on-call plan, sends people to training, calls off contractors and asks for posts, and gets the rota approved by the works council (a computer player or another student). Faults, inspections and construction support then run on the layout and the line map.
game.win: A year with every inspection on time, faults answered within their targets, overtime and on-call within the tariff, and no rota rejected by the works council. If the last technician qualified for the relay interlocking leaves, a fault there lasts for days. Overdue safety inspections before an accident end the round in court in career mode.
game.knowledge: Working-time law and on-call rules, works council co-determination, qualification planning, the queue arithmetic of faults and staff.
game.bigGame: Takes posts and the budget from the asset manager, faults from the dispatcher, and rota approval from the works council member. Gives available technicians and on-call cover to the dispatcher, inspection compliance to the ALV and the EBA, and overtime costs to the asset manager.

roles.name: Project manager of a major project
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), major projects unit (Großprojekte)
roles.summary: Leads a major infrastructure project of DB InfraGO for years: a new or upgraded line, a node, a digital interlocking or a corridor renewal. Secures the financing agreement with the Bund and planning approval from the EBA, steers planners and contractors, and answers for cost, schedule and the commissioning date.
decisions: Fix the scope and the variant to take into planning approval
Negotiate the financing agreement (Finanzierungsvereinbarung) with the Bund and draw down the funds through the EBA
Choose the contract model and procurement procedure with procurement (lots, general contractor, partnering)
Request the possessions years ahead and agree bundled closures with construction-operations planning
Accept, negotiate or dispute contractors' claims
Cut the scope or pay for acceleration when the budget or the date is at risk
Answer objections, lawsuits and the press
effects: Commissioning dates shape the timetable (Deutschlandtakt) and the contracts of the railway undertakings
Overruns cost federal money and trust; scope cuts cost capacity for decades
Long closures hit passengers, freight and whole regions
resources: A project budget of €0.1–10 bn; a team of 20–200 (own staff and consultants)
Funding from the Bund (BSWAG, financing agreement), the Länder or the EU (CEF)
Authority within the project budget and the company's approval limits
limits: AEG § 18 ff. (planning approval by the EBA; exemptions in § 18 (1a)), UVPG, BNatSchG; rail projects are in the overriding public interest since the 2023 AEG amendment
Lawsuits against approvals of the listed projects go straight to the Federal Administrative Court (VwGO § 50 (1) no. 6)
BSWAG and its Bedarfsplan, the financing agreement, BHO § 7 (economy and efficiency)
GWB / SektVO, VOB/A and VOB/B, HOAI
Announcing capacity restrictions in advance (ERegG, EU Delegated Decision 2017/2075)
EIGV and the TSIs for the authorisation to place subsystems in service
risks: Public blame and scrutiny by the Bundestag for overruns; job loss
Liability for compliance breaches in procurement
Very long hours and much travel

career.entry: Master or Diploma in civil or transport engineering, 10–20 years in projects (planning, supervision, construction), project management certification
career.chances: Paid above the tariff (AT): about €100,000–170,000 a year plus a bonus; more for heads of the largest projects

kpis: Claims as a share of the contract value
roles.timescale: months to a decade

game.title: The Big One (Großprojekt)
game.loop: A 10-year upgrade compressed into 20 quarterly turns. Each turn the player sees the risk register, the cash flow, the planning status, the objections and the market prices, and chooses actions: more planning, a change of variant, a dialogue with stakeholders, a procurement model, settling a claim, buying acceleration. Events come from the other roles: a lawsuit from residents, a jump in the construction price index, a protected bird nesting, a possession refused.
game.win: Full success: the subsystems authorised and in service with costs within +10 % of the financing agreement and no more than a year late. Above +30 %, or three years late, the project is taken away from the player (a career setback). The result is reported to the budget committee in the big game.
game.knowledge: The phases and gates of a German rail project (Bedarfsplan, financing agreement, HOAI phases, planning approval, procurement, commissioning), risk and claims management, earned value.
game.bigGame: Takes funding from the federal funding officer and the budget committee MPs, approvals from the EBA, and objections from residents and mayors. Gives new capacity (a line or an interlocking) and closures to the timetable planner and the railway undertakings, contracts to construction companies, and headlines to the press.

roles.name: Planner (HOAI phases 1 to 7)
roles.organisation: engineering consultancy (Ingenieurbüro), working for the infrastructure manager
roles.summary: Plans railway infrastructure measures for the infrastructure manager through the HOAI service phases 1–7: basic evaluation, preliminary design with variants, design, approval planning, execution planning, tender documents and support of the award.
decisions: Choose the planning depth and which surveys and ground investigations to propose to the client
Compare variants and recommend one
Plan the construction phases and the possessions they need
Propose whether to use BIM (employer's information requirements, AIA) and how complete the data must be
Write the tender specification and propose the procurement procedure
Answer the remarks of the plan check (EBA-recognised inspector)
effects: The quality of the planning decides how certain the costs are and how many claims follow
Poor phasing causes long closures
Delays in planning push back the project and its funding
resources: A fee agreed with HOAI §§ 47–48 as guidance (transport installations: roughly 5–15 % of the chargeable costs for all phases, depending on size and difficulty; signalling planning often by the client's own fee rules); a team of 2–15 engineers
The existing asset data (often incomplete), surveys, CAD and BIM software
limits: HOAI 2021 (fees are guidance since the CJEU ruling C-377/17); BGB contract law for works (5-year limitation for building works, § 634a)
The infrastructure manager's design guidelines (Ril 800, Ril 819, Ril 997), EBO, TSIs
EBA VV BAU and VV BAU-STE, and the plan checks
DIN 276 (cost estimate and cost calculation)
The infrastructure manager's prequalification of planning firms
risks: Liability for planning errors (professional indemnity insurance)
Fee pressure and overtime before deadlines

career.entry: Bachelor or Master in civil, transport or electrical engineering; later optionally membership of the chamber of engineers as a consulting engineer (Beratende/r Ingenieur/in); DB's planner qualifications for signalling
career.chances: About €50,000–80,000 a year; as project leader €80,000–110,000; more as partner or owner

roles.timescale: weeks to years

game.title: Lean or Thorough (Planungstiefe)
game.loop: The player plans the renewal of a level crossing, or of a switch connection, on a fee budget. Each HOAI phase offers options (a survey, a ground investigation, more variants, BIM) that cost fee hours but narrow the cost uncertainty, shown as a band. At phase 3 the cost calculation is fixed, at phase 5 the possession is booked, and at phases 6–7 the contractors bid. Then construction runs fast, and the claims reveal the gaps in the planning.
game.win: Final costs within ±10 % of the cost calculation, the possession kept, and a positive fee margin for the consultancy. Large overruns trace back to skipped surveys and cost the firm its next contract.
game.knowledge: HOAI fee calculation (§§ 47–48 and the phase shares), DIN 276, the gates of the infrastructure game, which measures need planning approval, which a plan permission and which neither (AEG § 18 (1a)).
game.bigGame: Takes orders from the asset manager, the major project manager and the crossing-law manager. Gives designs and tender documents to procurement and the contractors, and the possession booking to the possession planner.

roles.name: Construction supervisor
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO) or an engineering consultancy on its behalf
roles.summary: Supervises the works on site for the client (the on-site supervision, örtliche Bauüberwachung, beside HOAI phase 8; DB's qualification 'Bauüberwacher Bahn'). Checks quality, quantities, track safety and the construction-operations instruction (Betra), checks claims, carries out the acceptance inspection and confirms that the works are fit for traffic.
decisions: Choose what to check and how often (sampling, hold points)
Stop the work on a safety breach or a quality defect
Accept, reduce or reject quantities and claims
Recommend acceptance, acceptance with a list of defects, or refusal (or declare it where the client has authorised the supervisor)
Set the speed for the first trains under Ril 824 until the track has settled, and confirm fitness for traffic to the technically authorised person
Demand complete as-built documentation
effects: Defects missed now become faults in the first year
Refusing acceptance delays the reopening
A fair check of claims protects the client's money and the contractor's margin
resources: A supervision fee; 1–3 supervisors per site
Test equipment, the contractor's records, the Betra and the safety plan
limits: VOB/B §§ 2, 4, 6, 12, 13; HOAI phase 8 (Bauoberleitung) and the on-site supervision as a special service for transport installations
Ril 406 (construction and operations, Betra); Ril 824 (track works); Ril 132.0118
EN 13231 (acceptance of track works); EBA VV BAU and VV BAU-STE
The infrastructure manager's supervisor qualification for each discipline
risks: Liability for missed defects; criminal liability when a released track derails a train
Night and weekend shifts in possessions

career.entry: Engineer, technician or master craftsman with field experience, plus DB's qualification 'Bauüberwacher Bahn' for each discipline
career.chances: About €55,000–85,000 a year; freelancers earn about €600–900 a day

roles.timescale: hours to months

game.title: Acceptance (Abnahme)
game.loop: During the renewal of track G3 on the layout, the player has a limited number of checks per shift: ballast depth, sleeper spacing, welding records, tamping geometry, cable laying. Each check may reveal a hidden defect of the contractor. Claims arrive with documents to judge: justified or not (VOB/B § 2). At the end the player recommends acceptance, acceptance with defects or refusal, and sets the speed for the first trains.
game.win: Hidden defects found before acceptance, unjustified claims rejected, and the track reopened on time. Missed defects return as faults in the first year; an unjustified refusal leads to a dispute.
game.knowledge: VOB/B, the acceptance criteria of EN 13231, types of claims, temporary speed restrictions after track works (Ril 824).
game.bigGame: Takes the contractor's work from the site manager. Gives acceptance and as-built data to the ALV and the asset register, and fitness for traffic to the technically authorised person, who reopens the track with the signaller.

roles.name: Railway surveyor
roles.organisation: engineering consultancy or infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO)
roles.summary: Surveys and sets out the railway. Maintains the network of reference points, measures track position and clearances, provides the correction values for tamping, monitors settlement next to works, and delivers as-built data for the asset information model.
decisions: Check the reference points and reject disturbed ones
Compute the track's target position and the correction values for the tamping machine
Check clearances (structure gauge) and the distance between tracks
Apply the alarm thresholds of the monitoring concept in settlement monitoring, and raise the alarm
Accept or reject as-built data
effects: Wrong set-out values put the track in the wrong place: clearance conflicts and a rough ride
A missed settlement can undermine the track while trains run on it
Good as-built data make the asset register reliable
resources: Total stations, GNSS, a track measuring trolley, a laser scanner; teams of 2–4
The reference network (DB_REF) and the line's design alignment data
limits: Ril 883 (railway surveying), DB_REF, ETRS89/UTM
EBO § 9 (structure gauge), § 10 (distance between tracks)
Tolerances of EN 13231; track safety (Ril 132.0118)
risks: Being hit by a train while working in the track; liability for wrong set-out values
Night work in possessions

career.entry: Bachelor or Master in geodesy and surveying (e.g. HTW Dresden), or an apprenticeship as Vermessungstechniker/in
career.chances: About €45,000–75,000 a year

roles.timescale: hours to weeks

game.title: Absolute Track (Absolute Gleislage)
game.loop: The player gets a stretch of track with reference points (one of them disturbed), measured offsets and the design alignment. The player finds the bad point by its misfit, computes versines and correction values, and sends them to the tamping machine. In a second scene the player runs settlement monitoring next to an excavation with live readings, and decides when to raise the alarm (speed restriction or stop).
game.win: The final track within tolerance and clearance, and the right alarm at the right time. Using the disturbed point gives a rough track; a missed settlement leads to a closure.
game.knowledge: Versine f = c²/8R, coordinate geometry, redundancy and blunder detection, the structure gauge of the EBO, ETRS89/UTM.
game.bigGame: Takes orders from the planner and the site manager. Gives correction values to the track machine operator, as-built data to the asset register, and alarms to the dispatcher.

roles.name: Vegetation and winter service coordinator
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), regional unit, with landscaping and winter service contractors
roles.summary: Plans and runs the vegetation control along the lines and the winter service of a region: cutting back trees in the safety zone, weed control on the track, storm readiness, and in winter the switch heaters, snow clearing and platform gritting, with own teams and contractors.
decisions: Choose which lines to cut back and when, within the windows nature protection allows
Apply for permits for herbicides on the track, or use alternatives (hot water, mechanical, electrical)
Raise the winter service readiness level on the weather forecast
Call off contractors' crews for snow clearing and storms
Set priorities in a snowfall: switches, platforms or stations
Negotiate with neighbours and authorities about trees outside the railway land
effects: Fallen trees and snow stop trains for hours; storms close whole networks
Readiness costs standby money even when the storm does not come
Cutting in the breeding season without a safety reason brings fines and bad press
resources: A vegetation budget for the region of €5–25 M a year; framework contracts with landscaping firms
Winter service staff and contractors on call, switch heaters, de-icing equipment
Forecasts of the German weather service (DWD), risk maps
limits: Ril 882 (landscaping and vegetation control)
BNatSchG § 39 (5) (no cutting from 1 March to 30 September, except for traffic safety that cannot wait), § 44 (protection of species)
PflSchG § 12 (2): herbicides on track areas only with a permit, for federal railways from the EBA; the product needs BVL approval
Duty to keep the installations safe (Verkehrssicherungspflicht, BGB § 823) and to clear platforms
SektVO for the contracts; ArbZG for winter shifts
risks: Blame after storm disruptions; conflicts with environmental groups
Liability after falls on icy platforms or trees hitting trains
Seasonal overload, night calls

career.entry: Degree in landscape planning, forestry or civil engineering, or an experienced track technician or foreman
career.chances: DB tariff (EVG): about €4,000–5,500 a month

kpis: Delay minutes caused by weather and vegetation
roles.timescale: days to a season

game.title: Storm and Frost (Sturm und Frost)
game.loop: A year in four seasons on the line map: autumn storms and falling leaves, winter snowfalls with uncertain forecasts, spring and summer with the cutting ban and fire risk. Each week the player sees the forecast (as probabilities) and the risk map, and buys readiness and cutting from a budget. Then the weather comes, and trains on the layout stop where trees fall or switches freeze.
game.win: The fewest weather delay minutes per euro spent, and no fines. A storm on a high-risk day hitting a line that was not cut back closes it. Repeated breaches of nature protection law bring the environmental association to court.
game.knowledge: The expected value of readiness (cost against probability), the nature protection calendar and its safety exception, the rules on herbicides.
game.bigGame: Takes the weather and the budget. Gives line closures and delays to the operations simulator and the railway undertakings, and conflicts to the environmental association and the residents.

roles.name: IT/OT security officer for interlockings
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), information security of the signalling and control systems
roles.summary: Protects the IT and operational technology (OT) of the signalling (electronic and digital interlockings, ETCS, GSM-R and FRMCS, operations centres), a critical infrastructure, against attacks and sabotage: risk analyses, zones and conduits, patch and access management, incident response, and reporting to the BSI.
decisions: Allow or refuse a supplier's remote maintenance access
Patch now (with a safety re-assessment) or compensate with network measures
Isolate a network segment on an alert and accept the impact on operations
Report an incident to the BSI within the deadlines
Set the security levels and requirements for new interlockings in tenders
effects: A successful attack could stop trains in a whole region (compare the physical sabotage of GSM-R cables on 8 October 2022, which stopped trains across northern Germany for hours)
Isolating a segment without need also stops trains
Patches change systems that have a safety approval; assessments and approvals take months
resources: A security team of 5–30 people, a security operations centre, a budget of €1–20 M a year
The asset inventory, network monitoring, supplier contracts
limits: BSIG as amended by the NIS2 implementation act (NIS2UmsuCG, in force since December 2025): risk management (§ 30), reporting (§ 32: early warning within 24 h, notification within 72 h, final report within a month), duties of the management (§ 38)
BSI-KritisV; the KRITIS umbrella act on physical resilience (KRITIS-Dachgesetz, implementing the EU CER Directive)
IEC 62443, DIN VDE V 0831-104, CLC/TS 50701
The safety case under EN 50129, CSM-RA (Regulation (EU) 402/2013), and EBA VV BAU-STE for changes
GDPR for logging
risks: The board is liable under NIS2 and holds the officer to account; dismissal and public exposure after an incident
Stress during incidents; on-call duty

career.entry: Degree in computer science, electrical engineering or information security; certifications (e.g. ISO 27001 lead auditor, IEC 62443); experience in signalling
career.chances: About €80,000–130,000 a year; more as chief information security officer

kpis: Incidents and their impact on operations
Time from advisory to patch or mitigation
roles.timescale: minutes (an incident) to years (a security programme)

game.title: Air Gap (Luftspalt)
game.loop: A queue of alerts, advisories and requests arrives over a simulated week: a supplier asks for remote access to the electronic interlocking, a vulnerability turns up in an interlocking's maintenance PC, a GSM-R site shows odd traffic, a phishing wave hits the office IT. The player maps the assets into zones and conduits, decides which alerts are real and which are false, and acts: block, isolate, patch with an assessment, or compensate. Attacks the player misses spread, and isolations stop trains on the layout through the control-system feed.
game.win: No attacker reaches a safety-relevant zone, the trains keep running, the BSI reports go out in time, and the audit is passed. A compromised interlocking ends the round with a nationwide incident in the big game.
game.knowledge: Zones and conduits and security levels (IEC 62443), patching against the safety approval, the reporting duties and deadlines.
game.bigGame: Takes threat events and the budget. Gives outages to the operations simulator and the network controller, and incidents to the press and to politicians.

roles.name: Level crossing and crossing-law manager
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO), regional unit, negotiating with the road authorities (Bund, Land, district, municipality)
roles.summary: Handles the crossings of the railway with roads under the EKrG: agrees with the road authority whether a level crossing is upgraded, replaced by a bridge or underpass or closed, negotiates the crossing agreement (Kreuzungsvereinbarung) and its cost shares, and settles who maintains what. DB's network still has more than 10,000 level crossings.
decisions: Propose removing a level crossing (an underpass, a bridge, or closure with a detour) or upgrading its protection (EKrG § 3)
Negotiate the crossing agreement with the road authority: scope, who plans and builds, the cost mass and the shares (EKrG §§ 5, 13)
Compute the cost shares and the redemption amount for the future maintenance (Ablösung, ABBV)
Accept a cheaper variant the municipality wants, or insist on grade separation
Apply to the ordering authority for a crossing order when no agreement is reached (EKrG §§ 6, 10)
Agree the closure of a little-used crossing with the municipality, against a detour or a footbridge
effects: Every level crossing removed ends a risk of collisions; level crossing accidents are among the main causes of deaths in German rail operation
Grade separation removes a speed restriction and the crossing's maintenance for good, but takes years and the consent of several payers
A crossing without agreement holds up line upgrades: more trains mean longer barrier closures in the town
Since 2020 municipalities pay no share at crossings of federal railways with municipal roads, which makes removals easier to agree
resources: A portfolio of several hundred level crossings in the region
The railway's share of the crossing budget; planners for the variants; standard cost data
Authority to negotiate and initial agreements up to internal value limits
limits: EKrG § 2 (new crossings must be grade-separated), § 3 (measures for safety or traffic flow), § 5 (crossing agreement), §§ 6, 10 (crossing order; for federal railways the Federal Ministry of Transport decides, § 8)
EKrG § 13: cost thirds (railway, road authority, Bund or Land); at municipal roads Bund 1/2, railway 1/3, Land 1/6; §§ 14–15 (maintenance and its redemption)
1. EKrV (the cost mass) and ABBV (redemption amounts and service lives)
EBO § 11 (level crossings: none on lines above 160 km/h; protection by light signals with or without (half) barriers)
AEG § 18 (planning approval for the new structure); the road law of the road authority
risks: Blame from the town for barrier closure times and from the press after a crossing accident
Shared responsibility when a known hazard at a crossing was not acted on
Slow negotiations that outlast budgets and elections

career.entry: Degree in civil engineering, law or public administration, and years in the infrastructure manager's planning, property or legal departments
career.chances: Upper groups of the DB tariff (EVG) or above the tariff: about €60,000–90,000 a year

kpis: Crossings removed or upgraded per year
Agreements signed and time from proposal to agreement
Accidents at level crossings in the region
The railway's cost share against the budget
roles.timescale: months to years

game.title: Three Payers (Drittelung)
game.loop: The level crossing Talstraße in the town: its accidents, its barrier closure times (growing with every extra train), its condition and the street traffic. The player compares variants (renew the crossing, an underpass, closure with a detour), computes each payer's share under EKrG § 13 and the redemption for the future maintenance, and negotiates with the mayor and the Land, each with a budget and interests of its own (computer players or other students). Without agreement the player can apply for a crossing order, which takes two more years.
game.win: An agreement signed within the railway's budget and the time limit, with the crossing's risk removed or reduced, and the shares computed correctly. Wrong shares void the agreement. A collision at a crossing the player left unchanged despite a known hazard ends the round with an investigation.
game.knowledge: The EKrG cost rules and thirds, the cost mass, redemption amounts (ABBV service lives), the types of protection of EBO § 11, the benefit and cost of grade separation.
game.bigGame: Takes the road authorities' budgets and wishes from the mayor, the district administrator and the state minister, and the crossing's condition from the ALV. Gives grade separation projects to the planner and the major project manager, removed restrictions and fewer accidents to the operations simulator, and changed street traffic to the town.

roles.name: Site manager
roles.organisation: construction company (track construction contractor)
roles.summary: Leads a construction site for the contractor. Plans and runs the works in the possession, manages staff, machines, materials and subcontractors, and is responsible for cost, schedule, safety and the contract with the infrastructure manager.
decisions: Plan the sequence and the shifts of a possession
Order machines, materials and logistics trains
React to breakdowns: wait, rent a backup, or change the sequence
Hand the track back on time, or ask for an extension through the technically authorised person (the operations centre decides)
Notify hindrances (VOB/B § 6) and file claims (§ 2)
Choose subcontractors and check their compliance
effects: An overrun delays the first trains and triggers contractual penalties
Claims and productivity decide the contractor's margin
Safety decisions decide whether people get hurt
resources: A contract value of €0.5–30 M, 20–150 workers, machines worth millions
Possession windows (e.g. a 54-hour weekend)
limits: VOB/B, the contract and its penalty clauses (VOB/B § 11)
The Betra (Ril 406), the safety plan (Ril 132.0118, DGUV Vorschrift 77/78), BaustellV
ArbZG; AEntG § 14 and MiLoG § 13 (liability for subcontractors' wages)
The infrastructure manager's prequalification
risks: Criminal liability for accidents (StGB §§ 222, 319)
Pressure, long hours and weekends; job loss when projects make losses

career.entry: Bachelor in civil engineering (or a technician or foreman with experience), then years as assistant site manager
career.chances: About €60,000–95,000 a year plus a company car and a bonus

roles.timescale: hours (a possession) to months

game.title: Possession Overrun (Sperrpause)
game.loop: A 54-hour weekend possession to renew track G3 and switch W1. The player sets the sequence and the crews on a Gantt chart, then the clock runs on the layout with the construction train, the excavator and the tamping machine. Events hit: the tamping machine breaks down, a material train is late, it rains, a gang hits a cable. The player changes the sequence, rents a backup, extends shifts within the working-time law, or asks for an extension of the possession.
game.win: The track handed back on time, the work accepted, and a positive margin. An overrun costs penalties and delay minutes for every train; a serious injury ends the round.
game.knowledge: The critical path, claims and hindrance notices under VOB/B, working-time limits.
game.bigGame: Takes the contract and the possession. Gives the handback time to the technically authorised person and the operations simulator, costs and claims to the asset manager, and work to the workers.

roles.name: Foreman
roles.organisation: construction company (track construction contractor)
roles.summary: Leads a gang of track workers on site for the contractor. Assigns the tasks, checks the work and safety, coordinates with the machines, the lookouts and the welder, and reports completion to the site manager and the supervisor.
decisions: Assign the workers to tasks by skill
Sequence the work so that the machines do not wait
Check fastenings, sleeper spacing and ballast before the machine runs
Enforce protective equipment and clearing the track on the lookout's signal
Report problems and decide small changes on site
effects: Good sequencing saves hours of the possession
Lax safety leads to accidents
The quality of the work decides the acceptance
resources: A gang of 6–20 workers, small machines, part of the material
limits: The safety plan and the Betra; DGUV Vorschrift 77/78 and DGUV Vorschrift 38 (construction work)
ArbZG and breaks; the construction tariff (IG BAU)
risks: Injury; criminal liability when workers are hurt following the foreman's instructions
Weeks away from home; night shifts

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Gleisbauer/in, years as a worker and charge hand (Vorarbeiter), then the foreman course and exam (geprüfte/r Polier/in)
career.chances: About €4,300–6,000 a month (Werkpolier or Polier under the construction tariff) plus allowances

roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Gang Boss (Rotte)
game.loop: The player has 10 workers, each with skills and fatigue, and a list of tasks with dependencies: unclip the rails, remove sleepers, lay sleepers, fasten, weld, tamp. The machines arrive at fixed times, and the lookout interrupts. The player assigns people section by section on the layout's track G3 and checks the quality points.
game.win: All tasks done before the machine's slot, nobody injured, no rework at acceptance. Mistakes from fatigue appear when breaks are skipped.
game.knowledge: The sequence of a track renewal, breaks under the ArbZG, fastening checks.
game.bigGame: Takes the plan from the site manager. Gives progress to the site manager and work quality to the construction supervisor.

roles.name: Track worker
roles.organisation: construction company (track construction contractor)
roles.summary: Builds and repairs track as part of a gang: removes and lays sleepers and rails, fastens them, works the ballast and the switches, and handles small machines, always ready to clear the track on the lookout's warning.
decisions: Clear the track to the safe side at once on Ro 2
Wear the protective equipment and use the right tool; lift heavy loads with help
Report a defect or an unsafe practice
Refuse work that puts them in immediate danger (ArbSchG § 9)
effects: Clearing quickly saves lives; careful fastening extends the track's life
Reported hazards prevent accidents
resources: Hand tools and small machines (rail saw, sleeper tongs, impact wrench)
limits: DGUV Vorschrift 77/78; protective equipment (fluorescent orange high-visibility clothing, EN ISO 20471)
ArbSchG §§ 9, 15–17; ArbZG; JArbSchG for young apprentices; the construction tariff (IG BAU)
risks: Being hit by a train; crushing; noise and quartz dust from the ballast; heat and cold
Physical wear; seasonal work; long periods away from home

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Gleisbauer/in (3 years) or Tiefbaufacharbeiter/in specialising in track works (2 years); or entry without a trade
career.chances: About €21–27 an hour under the construction tariff (IG BAU) plus travel and night allowances

roles.timescale: seconds to a shift

game.title: Shift in the Track (Schicht im Gleis)
game.loop: Short scenes on track G3. The player does a sleeper change in the right order, chooses protective equipment and tools, reacts to horn signals (which side to clear to, which track the train is on), and spots hazards in pictures of the worksite (a colleague under a raised load, a missing lookout).
game.win: Tasks done correctly, every warning answered in time and to the right side, hazards spotted. A wrong reaction ends the scene. Passed scenes count toward the apprenticeship exam in career mode.
game.knowledge: The Ro signals, the safe area beside the track, protective equipment, the steps of a sleeper change, workers' rights and duties.
game.bigGame: Takes tasks from the foreman. Gives work done and incidents.

roles.name: Track machine operator (tamping machine, road-rail excavator)
roles.organisation: construction company (track construction or machine contractor)
roles.summary: Drives and operates heavy track machines: tamping machines that lift, align and compact the track, ballast regulators, and road-rail excavators. Responsible from the transfer run to the site to the last ramp before the track is handed back.
decisions: Set lift, lining, squeeze time and the number of insertions per section from the design values
Choose the working speed against the time left in the possession
Build the run-out ramp before the possession ends
Set the excavator's slew and height limiter near the adjacent track and the overhead line
Stop when ballast is missing or a cable or obstacle appears
effects: The quality of the tamping decides the track geometry and the next speed restrictions
An unfinished ramp means a speed restriction for the first trains
A slewing excavator can hit a train or the overhead line
resources: A machine worth €2–10 M (tamping machine) or about €0.5 M (road-rail excavator); a crew of 2–3
limits: For transfer runs on the open network a train driver's licence under the TfV (or a licensed driver on board); within the closed track the company's machine licence
EN 14033 (rail-bound machines), EN 15746 (road-rail machines)
The Betra and the closure; Ril 824 (tamping); Ril 132.0118 and DGUV Vorschrift 77/78; ArbZG; EN 13231
risks: Collisions with trains or within the site; electrocution at the overhead line
Night work and noise

career.entry: A construction or mechatronics trade, training on the machine, and a train driver's licence under the TfV
career.chances: About €22–28 an hour plus allowances, often €3,800–4,800 a month

roles.timescale: seconds to a shift

game.title: Tamping Run (Stopfen)
game.loop: The player gets the measured geometry of 300 m of track G3 and the correction values, and drives the tamping machine section by section, setting lift and lining, the insertions and the speed. The result is measured live. The possession is running out, and the ramp must be finished before the handback. A second mode: a road-rail excavator lifts sleepers next to an adjacent track in service, with slew limits.
game.win: Track quality index after tamping within the target, the ramp built, the handback on time. A poor job brings speed restrictions; entering the adjacent track's clearance ends the round.
game.knowledge: Track geometry, tamping parameters, run-out ramps, slew limiting.
game.bigGame: Takes correction values from the surveyor and orders from the site manager. Gives the track geometry to the infrastructure simulation and the handback time to the operations simulator.

roles.name: Rail welder
roles.organisation: construction company (track construction or welding contractor)
roles.summary: Joins rails into continuous welded rail, by aluminothermic (thermite) welding on site or flash-butt welding with a mobile machine. Repairs rail defects and restores the stress-free temperature, so that the rails neither buckle in heat nor break in frost.
decisions: Measure the rail temperature and decide to weld now, tension the rail, or wait
Compute the tension needed to reach the neutral temperature (23 °C ± 3 K)
Set the gap, the preheating time and the mould; pour; trim and grind
Fit a provisional joint (fishplates) with a speed restriction
Have the weld tested by ultrasound after cooling by a certified tester; hand it over or redo it
effects: A wrong neutral temperature leads to track buckling in summer or rail breaks in winter
A bad weld can break under a train
Waiting costs possession time
resources: A welding kit (portions, moulds, preheater), a rail tensor, a mobile flash-butt welding machine; a team of 2–3
limits: EN 14730-1 (aluminothermic welding), EN 14730-2 (qualification of welders, approval of contractors, acceptance of welds), EN 14587 (flash-butt welding)
The infrastructure manager's rules on continuous welded rail and neutral temperature (Ril 824)
Track safety; fire protection (dry vegetation); ArbZG
risks: Burns, fire and fumes
Liability for failed welds

career.entry: Gleisbauer/in with welding courses and the approval as aluminothermic welder (EN 14730-2), renewed by repeated tests
career.chances: About €21–27 an hour plus allowances

kpis: Welds without defects at the ultrasonic test
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Neutral Temperature (Neutraltemperatur)
game.loop: A gap in a 120 m stretch of continuous welded rail at a rail temperature of 8 °C. The player computes the elongation needed (ΔL = α·L·ΔT = 1.15·10⁻⁵ /K × 120 m × 15 K ≈ 21 mm) and sets the tensor, then performs the weld steps in order against timers: gap, mould, preheat, ignite, pour, strip, trim, cool, grind. Then a simulated year follows, in which heat waves and frost test the stress-free temperature.
game.win: The weld passes the ultrasonic test and the stress-free temperature is within the band. Wrong values lead to a buckle in July or a rail break in January in the big game.
game.knowledge: Thermal expansion, neutral temperature, the steps and times of aluminothermic welding.
game.bigGame: Takes tasks from the foreman. Gives weld quality to the infrastructure simulation (fault rates of the track).

roles.name: Catenary fitter
roles.organisation: construction company (catenary contractor)
roles.summary: Builds and repairs overhead lines for a catenary contractor: foundations, masts, cantilevers, messenger and contact wire, droppers and tensioning. Works from tower cars and lifting platforms on sections that are switched off and earthed.
decisions: Confirm switching off and earthing before climbing
Set the contact wire height and the stagger at each mast
Cut the droppers to length for the design geometry
Set the tensioning weights
Stop the work in a thunderstorm or strong wind
effects: The geometry decides the quality of the pantograph contact and the risk of dewirements
A missed earth kills
resources: A tower car or road-rail platform, a wiring train, tools; a team of 4–8
limits: EN 50110-1 / DIN VDE 0105-100, DGUV Vorschrift 3, EN 50119
Ril 997 (DB catenary types such as Re 200, Re 250 and Re 330); rules for work at height; ArbZG
risks: Electrocution, falls, weather
Long periods away from home on installation work

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik or Freileitungsbauer/in, plus the contractor's catenary training; electrically instructed person (elektrotechnisch unterwiesene Person) or qualified electrician (Elektrofachkraft)
career.chances: About €18–26 an hour plus installation and height allowances

roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Re 200 (Kettenwerk)
game.loop: After a dewirement, four spans of overhead line west of the station must be rebuilt in a night possession. The player first checks the switching and earthing sequence, then sets each mast's contact wire height and stagger, computes the dropper lengths from the messenger wire's sag and the design contact wire height, and sets the tension. A virtual pantograph test run at the end shows the contact force and the uplift.
game.win: The test run within limits and the possession ended on time. Poor geometry causes a dewirement in the operations simulator the following week.
game.knowledge: Catenary geometry (contact wire height about 5.50 m, 5.30 m on high-speed types; stagger), sag, tension, the five safety rules.
game.bigGame: Takes repair orders. Gives the state of the overhead line to the operations simulator and the energy controller.

roles.name: Structures inspector (bridges and tunnels)
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO) or engineering consultancy
roles.summary: Inspects the railway's bridges, tunnels, retaining walls and culverts under Ril 804.8001 (close-up inspections at fixed intervals, visual checks in between), grades their condition, and recommends repairs, load or speed restrictions and replacements. DB's network has about 25,000 railway bridges, many of them over 100 years old.
decisions: Choose the access (under-bridge unit, rope access, drone, a possession) and the depth of the inspection
Grade the condition category (Zustandskategorie) of each component
Order an immediate restriction (speed, load or closure) for a critical defect
Recommend repair, monitoring, a load-bearing assessment or replacement
Request a special inspection after a flood, a vehicle impact or a fire
effects: Bridge condition is an LuFV quality indicator; replacements take years to plan and build
A missed crack or scour can bring a bridge down (compare the collapse of the Carolabrücke in Dresden in September 2024, a road and tram bridge, after hidden corrosion of its prestressing steel)
Restrictions slow heavy freight trains and can force diversions
resources: Inspection teams of 2–4; under-bridge inspection units, drones, non-destructive testing
Possessions for access over the track
limits: Ril 804 (railway bridges) and Ril 804.8001 (inspection of structures); Ril 805 (load-bearing capacity of existing bridges); Ril 853 (railway tunnels)
EBO § 2; LuFV quality indicators; EBA supervision (AEG § 5)
Track safety and work at height (Ril 132.0118, DGUV rules)
risks: Criminal and civil liability for a missed defect
Working at height and over traffic

career.entry: Civil engineering degree with structural knowledge, the infrastructure manager's inspector qualification under Ril 804.8001 (the VFIB bridge inspector certificate is common)
career.chances: About €55,000–80,000 a year

roles.timescale: days to years (inspection cycles)

game.title: Under the Bridge (Brückenprüfung)
game.loop: The player inspects a riveted steel bridge of 1912 and a masonry arch within a limited possession time, choosing which components to examine closely. Each choice reveals evidence (corrosion, fatigue cracks at the rivets, scour at the pier). The player grades each component, decides on restrictions and recommends repair or replacement. Then a decade runs in fast mode with traffic and floods.
game.win: Correct grades, every critical defect found, and no unneeded restrictions. A missed critical defect ends the round with a closure or worse.
game.knowledge: Defect types of steel, masonry and concrete bridges, condition categories, inspection intervals, when a load-bearing assessment is needed.
game.bigGame: Takes inspection orders and possessions. Gives the condition of structures to the ALV, the asset manager and the LuFV reporting, restrictions to the operations simulator and freight, and replacement projects to planners.

roles.name: Managing director of a passenger railway undertaking
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Runs a passenger railway undertaking (Eisenbahnverkehrsunternehmen, EVU) as a business. That is either a regional operator that lives on transport contracts with the transport authorities (Aufgabenträger), or a long-distance operator that runs at its own commercial risk (DB Fernverkehr, or an open-access operator such as Flixtrain). Answers for the financial result, the operating licence and safety certificate, the staff, and the relations with the Länder, the unions and the owners.
decisions: Decide whether to bid for a regional network, and sign off the bid price and the risk premium
Negotiate company collective agreements with EVG and GDL (or adopt the sector agreements of an employers' association), and set how many new drivers are trained each year
Choose the maintenance model: own workshop and ECM, full service by the manufacturer, or an ECM contractor
Ask the transport authority to adjust a loss-making contract (index clauses, staff shortage, energy prices) as far as procurement law allows, or carry the losses
Agree an emergency timetable (Notfahrplan) with the authority when drivers are missing, or pay overtime and contract penalties
Approve the operations manager's budget for safety measures and the fleet's budget for spare units
File for insolvency or a protective-shield procedure (Schutzschirmverfahren, as Abellio did in North Rhine-Westphalia in 2021) when the company can no longer pay its debts
effects: The bid price fixes the margin for 10-15 years. A price 2-3 % too low can make the whole contract lose money.
Wage and training decisions settle whether there are enough drivers two or three years later, and so the number of cancellations and penalties
The maintenance model sets who pays penalties along the chain of contracts and how fast failed units come back
If an operator fails, the authority makes an emergency award (Art. 5(5) Reg. 1370/2007, for up to two years), and staff and passengers face months of uncertainty
Cutting safety budgets too far shows up as incidents and EBA findings, and in the worst case as conditions on the safety certificate or its withdrawal
resources: Revenue of a mid-size regional operator: 100-400 M€ a year. Under a gross contract (Bruttovertrag, now the usual form) almost all of it is paid by the authority, which keeps the fares. Under a net contract (Nettovertrag) 60-70 % is contract payment (Bestellerentgelt) and the rest is the RU's share of fares from revenue sharing (Einnahmeaufteilung), with the revenue risk.
500-2,000 staff and 50-150 multiple units (owned, leased from a ROSCO, or provided from the authority's vehicle pool)
EBIT margin of 0-5 % of revenue, and cash for a few weeks of payroll

Total cost of roughly 15-25 € per train-km: track and station charges about a third, vehicles (capital and maintenance) a quarter to a third, staff about a fifth to a quarter, energy and overheads the rest
Authority over the whole company, within approval limits set by the shareholder (a group board or a public owner)
limits: AEG § 6 operating licence (reliability, financial capacity, professional competence; details in the EBZugV) with liability insurance under the EBHaftPflV, and the single safety certificate (Directive (EU) 2016/798, Reg. 2018/763) issued by the EBA or the ERA
Transport contracts under Reg. (EC) 1370/2007 and GWB § 131, with penalty and bonus systems and duties to take over staff; GWB § 132 forbids material changes to a contract without a new tender
Collective agreements with GDL and EVG (Tarifeinheitsgesetz), co-determination under the Betriebsverfassungsgesetz, and the state laws on paying tariff wages (Landestariftreuegesetze)
Track access and station charges set in the IM's network statement; for regional services their yearly rise is capped (ERegG § 37)

GmbHG § 43 (personal liability of directors), InsO § 15a (file for insolvency within three weeks of illiquidity or six weeks of over-indebtedness; a criminal offence if delayed) and StGB § 266a (withheld social security contributions)
Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung (EBV): must appoint an operations manager, give them resources, and may not overrule them on safety
risks: Civil liability for damages, and criminal liability for a delayed insolvency filing, withheld social security contributions, or organisational fault after an accident
Dismissal by the shareholders after losses or a lost re-tender
Public exposure in the regional press and in the state parliament when services collapse
Long hours and constant availability in crises (strikes, storms, accidents)

career.entry: A degree in business, transport engineering or law, then 10-15 years in railway or public transport management (operations, bids, contracts, finance), usually first as head of a region or division
career.chances: Few posts: a few dozen passenger RUs plus the regions of DB Regio. Pay is about 150,000-400,000 € a year at mid-size operators, and higher on the boards of DB Regio or DB Fernverkehr. Contracts run 3-5 years and often end with a lost re-tender or a change of owner.

kpis: EBIT and cash flow against the business plan
Punctuality and cancellations against the contract
Contracts won and kept in re-tenders
Driver vacancies, staff turnover and sickness rate
roles.timescale: Months to years (annual budget, 10-15-year contracts); hours in a crisis

game.title: Ten Years of Contract
game.loop: Each round is one contract year of a regional network on the lab layout. The player sets wages and the training intake, the share of stand-by drivers, the maintenance model (integrated, ECM company, manufacturer full service) and the number of spare units. The operations engine then runs the year fast, as in its Compare view, with shocks drawn from a deck: an energy price jump, a wage settlement, a strike, a flu wave, drivers leaving, lower fare revenue (in a net contract). Each year ends with a profit and loss statement including penalties. Between years the player can ask the authority to adjust the contract (as far as procurement law allows), agree service cuts, or put in equity.
game.win: Finish the contract with positive equity and contract quality above the authority's threshold. Running out of cash forces an insolvency filing within the legal deadline; in the career this means dismissal and a damaged reputation, and a late filing adds a criminal case. Three years in a row below the quality threshold let the authority terminate the contract.
game.knowledge: The cost structure of a regional train-km; gross and net contracts, contract payments, fares and revenue sharing; penalty systems and index clauses; how the staff reserve and the maintenance model affect reliability; the insolvency deadlines and directors' liability
game.bigGame: Takes the contract from the bid manager and the authority's tender manager, the wage settlement from the union official, track access charges from track access sales, and vehicles from the ROSCO. Gives budgets to the operations manager, crew planner and fleet, and quality data and penalties (through the RU's contract manager) to the authority's contract manager. It is the top decision layer of the EVU in the economics simulator, and the place career mode is heading for.

roles.name: Operations manager (by law)
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: The operations manager required by law (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter, EBL; not to be confused with the lab, the Eisenbahnbetriebslabor), personally responsible to the safety authority for the safe running of the undertaking's trains: rules, qualified staff, use of vehicles and handling of incidents. The appointment is confirmed by the EBA (or the state railway authority), and management cannot overrule the EBL on safety.
decisions: Issue and change operating instructions for staff (Betriebsanweisungen), e.g. how trains are dispatched under the technology-based departure procedure (TAV)
Take a driver off duty after a signal passed at danger, and decide on retraining and return to duty
Report an accident or incident to the accident investigation body (BEU) and the EBA without delay, and order immediate measures
Check the route compatibility of an authorised vehicle type before its first use on a line, and set when staff have the route and vehicle knowledge for it
Decide whether a change is significant under CSM-RA and needs an independent assessor
Refuse a roster or timetable change that the safety analysis shows causes fatigue
Order winter or heat measures for the RU's own trains, such as lower top speeds in snow or extra checks of doors and brakes
effects: New instructions change how every driver and conductor works from the next day
Taking drivers off duty protects safety but cancels trains when there is no reserve
Thorough incident analysis lowers repeat incidents. Poor analysis brings EBA audits and conditions on the safety certificate.
The route compatibility check and the staff's knowledge decide whether new vehicles or lines can start on time at the timetable change
resources: A small safety and operations staff (3-15 people), plus instructors and incident investigators
The legal power to give binding instructions on operational safety, and direct access to management
A budget for training and safety measures in the low millions of euros a year at a mid-size RU
On-call duty around the clock, shared with deputies
limits: AEG § 4 (safety duties of railway companies), Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung (EBV) on appointment, confirmation and powers
EBO, ESO, the IM's operating rules (Ril 408) and the RU's own rulebooks; the operation TSI (OPE TSI, Reg. (EU) 2019/773)
Art. 23 Directive (EU) 2016/797: route compatibility check by the RU before using an authorised vehicle
Safety management system under Reg. 2018/762 (CSM SMS), risk assessment under Reg. 402/2013 (CSM-RA), monitoring under Reg. 1078/2012
Eisenbahn-Unfalluntersuchungsverordnung (EUV): immediate reports of serious accidents and incidents
Triebfahrzeugführerscheinverordnung (TfV): driver licences, certificates and periodic checks
risks: Criminal liability (StGB §§ 222, 229, 315a) for organisational failures after an accident
Withdrawal of the confirmation by the EBA
Conflicts with management that wants trains to run; stress of on-call duty and of accident sites

career.entry: A degree in engineering or transport (e.g. Verkehrsingenieurwesen), several years in railway operations, and proof of competence to the authority, which confirms the appointment under the EBV. Often a former dispatcher or safety manager, sometimes a driver who later studied.
career.chances: One post per RU, plus deputies. About 90,000-140,000 € a year; in small RUs often combined with the managing director's post.

kpis: Signals passed at danger and other precursors per million train-km
Share of staff with valid qualifications and periodic training
roles.timescale: Days to months for rules and approvals; minutes when on call for an incident

game.title: The Incident File
game.loop: Incidents arrive from the simulated operations: a signal passed at danger, a passenger trapped in a door, a train run with an overdue unit, a driver whose rest was cut short, a new unit type planned on a line with too-short platforms. For each one the player classifies the event, decides what to report to whom and by when, reads the evidence (the operations log and the control system's record), names the cause, and picks measures from options that have costs. The next simulated month shows whether the measures worked and how many cancellations they cost.
game.win: Correct classification and reporting (the knowledge score), and fewer precursor incidents after a quarter without pushing cancellations above the contract limit. A missed report, or an untreated cause that leads to an accident, ends the round with an EBA investigation; in the career this can cost the confirmation.
game.knowledge: EUV reporting duties; the difference between accident, incident and precursor; root-cause analysis; when a change is significant under CSM-RA; the route compatibility check; TfV rules on licences; the ArbZG and tariff rules behind fatigue
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from drivers, conductors and the dispatcher, return-to-duty proposals from the driver team leader, the roster from the crew planner, and vehicles from the ECM. Gives rules and approvals (a new vehicle on a line, sign-off of a roster) and a safety budget request to the managing director. Its cases feed the EBA supervisor's audits and the BEU investigator's investigations.

roles.name: Train driver (passenger)
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Drives regional or long-distance passenger trains (Triebfahrzeugführer, Tf): prepares the unit, follows signals and written orders, keeps to the timetable, and is the first to act in any emergency on the line.
decisions: Check the unit before service, and decide with the operations control whether a defect still allows it to run (by the RU's defect catalogue)
Brake in time for a restrictive signal or a speed board, under PZB, LZB or ETCS supervision
Pass a signal at danger only on a substitute or caution signal (Zs 1, Zs 7, Zs 8) or a written order (Befehl), after checking it
Make an emergency stop for a person or obstacle on the track, make the GSM-R emergency call when the next track may be blocked, then secure the train and report
Close the doors and depart under the technology-based departure procedure (TAV, door control by the driver) once the platform is clear
Report track defects, faulty level crossings and dark signals to the signaller
Tell the operations control early when a delay will push the shift past its limit, and decline extra work that would break the legal rest
effects: Punctual driving within the limits is the basis of punctuality and of connections in the whole network
A signal passed at danger can cause a collision. Even without one, it stops traffic and takes the driver off duty.
A fast emergency stop reduces the harm but rarely stops the train in time, and the driver lives with the outcome
Running with a defect keeps the service going but can end in a breakdown on the line and a towed unit
resources: One train (a multiple unit with 200-900 seats), its cab systems, and the timetable (Buchfahrplan, or EBuLa on a tablet)
GSM-R radio to the signaller and a phone to the operations control
Authority over the train's technical safety and the decision to stop; none over routes and signals
A shift of 8-10 hours with breaks set by the ArbZG and the tariff
limits: EBO (e.g. § 40 on speeds), ESO signals, Ril 408, and the RU's driving rules (at DB Ril 492)

Triebfahrzeugführerscheinverordnung (TfV, implementing Directive 2007/59/EC): licence from the EBA; certificate from the RU covering vehicle types and routes; medical check every 3 years and yearly from age 55; periodic training and checks
Arbeitszeitgesetz and the GDL/EVG tariffs: maximum shift length, at least 11 hours of rest, breaks; for cross-border work also Directive 2005/47/EC
No alcohol or drugs on duty (0.0 ‰ under company rules); the driver vigilance device (Sifa) needs action about every 30 seconds
risks: Trauma from fatalities on the track: several hundred people a year take their lives on German railways, and many drivers experience one or more in their career
Criminal liability (StGB §§ 315a, 222) after an accident caused by own fault; certificate suspended after a signal passed at danger
Loss of the licence when medical fitness lapses
Shift work, nights and weekends; occasional assaults

career.entry: Either the three-year apprenticeship Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst (Lokführer und Transport) or a conversion course of 9-12 months, often funded by the employment agency. Then psychological and medical aptitude tests, the licence from the EBA and the certificate from the RU.
career.chances: Drivers are in great shortage and jobs are secure. About 45,000-60,000 € a year with allowances under the GDL or EVG tariffs. At DB the GDL agreement of 2024 lowers the reference week step by step to 35 hours by 2029 (drivers may choose to keep a longer week for more pay); private operators have their own agreements.

kpis: Punctuality of own trains (delay caused by driving)
Signals passed at danger and overspeeding (target: none)
Valid certificate and passed check rides
roles.timescale: Seconds (signals, braking), within a shift

game.title: Cab Shift
game.loop: The player drives one rotation of the lab network from a simplified cab. The cab shows the line ahead with signals, speed boards and stations, a combined power and brake lever, PZB with its supervision, the Sifa, GSM-R and a door button. Events come from the simulation: waiting for a late connection, a signal at danger with a written order, a temporary speed restriction, a defect on the unit, a person near the track. Each stop shows the delay, and every rule broken is logged.
game.win: End the shift with all trains run, delays within 3 minutes of the plan, and no rule broken. Passing a signal at danger or a PZB emergency brake ends the shift; in the career this means removal from duty and retraining, and after repeats the loss of the certificate.
game.knowledge: ESO signal aspects, PZB 90 (1000/500/2000 Hz magnets, restrictive supervision), braking distances, written orders, and the order of actions after an emergency stop (GSM-R emergency call, securing the train, report)
game.bigGame: Takes a duty from the crew planner and the dispatcher, a unit from the rotation planner and the fleet, and routes from the signaller. Gives the trains' actual times to the operations (punctuality, penalties, travellers' connections), recorded rides to the driver team leader, and incidents to the operations manager. In career mode it is the classic entry role into operations.

roles.name: Train manager (long distance)
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (long-distance passenger, e.g. DB Fernverkehr)
roles.summary: Leads the on-board team of a long-distance train (Zugchef/in) from departure to the terminus: service, ticket checks, passenger information, safety in the passenger area, and the departure procedure at the platform.
decisions: Divide the team between ticket checks, service and announcements
Declare the train overcrowded and ask passengers without a reservation to leave, or have it partly cleared (Zugräumung) with the federal police if needed
Open first class to second-class passengers when the train is overcrowded or a coach is closed
Ask, through the driver and the operations control, for an unscheduled stop with an ambulance for a medical emergency
Ask the operations control for a connection to be held, and announce whether it is
Exclude an aggressive or ticketless passenger from travel (Beförderungsausschluss) at the next stop
Close a coach with broken air conditioning or toilets and move its passengers
Keep passengers on board a train stranded on the line until an evacuation is organised with the operations control and the IM's emergency manager
effects: Overcrowding blocks aisles and doors. It is a safety risk, and longer dwell times delay the train.
Good information calms passengers and reduces complaints and compensation claims
Each extra stop or held connection costs minutes that spread through the network
Passengers who leave a stranded train on their own put themselves in danger and stop all traffic on the line
Fare revenue and fare evasion depend on the checks done
resources: An ICE with up to about 900 seats (ICE 4), 2-4 train attendants and 2-3 bistro staff
Train radio, a phone to the operations control, and the passenger information app on a tablet
The RU's house rights over passengers, delegated to the train manager
limits: EVO and the conditions of carriage (BB Personenverkehr): validity of tickets, fares charged on board, exclusion from travel

Passenger rights (Reg. (EU) 2021/782): information during the journey, and rerouting or refund once a delay of 60 minutes is expected; DB's conditions of carriage go further and lift train binding (Zugbindung) from 20 minutes of expected delay at the destination
Ril 408 and the RU's rules for closing doors and dispatching the train; the IM's emergency management (Ril 423) for evacuations
ArbZG and the GDL/EVG tariffs on working time
risks: Verbal and physical assault (several thousand attacks on DB staff a year)
Stress from conflicts and long shifts, and nights away from home
Disciplinary action for mistakes in the departure procedure or with cash

career.entry: Several years as a long-distance train attendant (after the apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice or a functional training of a few months), then an internal course for train managers
career.chances: About 40,000-52,000 € a year with allowances (EVG or GDL tariff). A stable job with routes into dispatching, planning or driving.

kpis: Tickets checked and fares collected on board
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift of 8-12 hours

game.title: Full Train to Munich
game.loop: One long-distance run in fast time, shown on a map of the train's coaches. Passengers board with and without reservations, some without tickets. The player assigns the team, chooses announcements and answers events: overcrowding at a big station, broken air conditioning in one coach, a medical emergency, a delay that breaks connections, an aggressive passenger, a stop on the line after a failure. Passengers also ask questions that have a right answer (is my saver fare valid on the next train, what compensation will I get). Passenger mood (the colour in the passenger simulation) and the train's delay respond to every choice.
game.win: Reach the terminus with average mood above a threshold, no blocked doors at any departure, no passenger leaving the train on the line, and no more delay than the network caused; wrong answers to passengers return as claims and complaints. A dangerous overcrowding or an escalated conflict ends the round; in the career it counts as a serious complaint.
game.knowledge: Ticket validity, passenger rights (train binding, rerouting, compensation), the rules for excluding passengers, first-aid steps, evacuation rules, and how dwell time turns into delay
game.bigGame: Takes demand and reservations from the revenue manager, the delay from operations and the network, and the team from the crew planner. Gives delay minutes, complaints and compensation claims to the passenger rights desk, and fares collected on board to the RU's economics.

roles.name: Conductor and ticket inspector (regional)
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (regional passenger)
roles.summary: Works on regional trains as conductor and ticket inspector (Zugbegleiter/in; at DB Regio, Kundenbetreuer/in im Nahverkehr, KiN): checks tickets, informs and helps passengers, assists at the doors and with boarding, keeps order on board, and has duties in an emergency.
decisions: Judge within seconds whether a ticket is valid (zones, Deutschlandticket with photo ID, discounts, bicycles)
Charge the increased fare (erhöhtes Beförderungsentgelt, 60 € under the EVO) or accept a credible excuse
Call security or the federal police, or step back from a conflict
Set up the ramp for a wheelchair user and hold the train for it
Where the conductor dispatches the train, check the platform and give the driver the order to depart
Inform passengers about connections and cancellations and suggest alternatives
Keep passengers in a stranded train, and help evacuate it only when the operations control confirms that the neighbouring track is closed
Report defects (doors, toilets, heating) to the operations control
effects: Visible checks reduce fare evasion (often a few per cent of passengers) and protect revenue: in a net contract the RU's, in a gross contract the authority's
Without a conductor the operator pays contract penalties on lines that require staff on board
A well-handled conflict keeps the train on time; a badly handled one injures staff or passengers
Helping at the doors adds seconds of dwell time but keeps boarding safe and accessible
resources: A handheld ticket device, and a small cash float or card terminal where tickets are sold on board
Phone or radio to the driver and the operations control; a bodycam where introduced
House rights delegated by the RU, but no police powers
limits: EVO, the tariff rules of the transport association (Tarifbestimmungen), the Deutschlandtarif and the Deutschlandticket conditions
Only the rights every citizen has (Jedermannrechte): StPO § 127 (holding a person caught in the act), StGB § 32 (self-defence)
Fare evasion is a criminal offence (StGB § 265a), which RUs usually report only for repeat cases
Data protection when checking ID (GDPR, DSGVO)
Ril 408 and the RU's rules for dispatching trains and for emergencies; ArbZG and the GDL/EVG tariffs
risks: Verbal and physical assault, especially on late-evening trains
Stress from conflicts, and shift work
Disciplinary action after a wrongful charge or an escalated conflict

career.entry: The three-year apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice or a conversion course of 3-6 months; many career changers
career.chances: About 36,000-45,000 € a year with allowances. Demand is high, and moving on to driver training is common.

kpis: Tickets checked per hour and fare evasion found
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Tickets, Please
game.loop: The player walks through a regional train between stops of the lab network. The passengers are travellers of the journeys module and the town, each with a real start and aim, and each shows a ticket. Between two stations (a short real-time window) the player checks as many as possible, judges each one (valid, wrong zone, expired, missing ID, child fare), and decides on fares and excuses. Some passengers react badly; the player can call security or step back. Now and then the train stops on the line and the player must keep passengers on board until the operations control gives the word.
game.win: The score counts correct judgements, revenue and passengers checked, minus wrong charges and escalations. The round ends at the terminus. Three escalations, a wrongful charge that turns into a complaint, or passengers let out onto an open track cost reputation in the career.
game.knowledge: Zones and tariff rules of a transport association, the Deutschlandticket conditions, the increased fare and its reduction to a fee when a forgotten personal season ticket is shown later, the limits of the rights every citizen has, and the conductor's emergency duties
game.bigGame: Takes duties from the crew planner and travellers from the journeys and town modules. Gives fare revenue and evasion rates to revenue sharing, the trains covered with a conductor to the contract (penalties), and incidents to security and the operations manager.

roles.name: Dispatcher in the operations control
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Runs the undertaking's daily production from its operations control centre (Transportleitung), around the clock: vehicles, crews and passenger information when trains are late, units fail or staff are missing. Negotiates with the infrastructure manager's controllers, who decide the order of trains.
decisions: Cancel a train, turn it short, or let it run late when its unit or crew is missing
Bring a spare unit out of the depot or swap units between rotations
Find a replacement driver among the stand-by drivers or ask someone on a free day
Decide which connections to hold, and agree the waiting time with the IM's dispatcher
Order rail replacement buses (SEV) and taxis for stranded passengers
Give the passenger information for each disrupted train (in larger RUs through an information dispatcher)
Ask the IM's network controller for a different order of trains or an extra stop
effects: A cancellation can save the trains later in the day, but costs penalties (12 € per train-km in the lab contract) and passenger compensation
Holding one connection makes the waiting train late and can break its own connections
Fast replacement of drivers keeps the timetable; too much overtime breaks rest times on the next day
Good information reduces crowding at platforms and complaints
resources: The day's rotations and rosters, 1-3 spare units and a few stand-by drivers per region
Framework contracts with bus and taxi companies
Dispatching tools and the passenger information system
Authority over the RU's own resources only: the IM decides the order of trains on the network
limits: The IM's dispatching rules and priorities in the network statement (SNB); DB InfraGO's rules for operations control (Ril 420) and emergency management (Ril 423)
ArbZG and tariff rest times when reassigning crews
Contract rules on cancellations, short turns and replacement services
Passenger rights (Reg. 2021/782): information, rerouting, help with taxis and hotels
risks: Shift work around the clock, with high stress during disruptions
Disciplinary or safety consequences when a decision breaks rest times or sends out a defective unit
Public anger after large disruptions

career.entry: Usually a former driver, conductor or train manager with internal dispatcher training; some have a transport degree
career.chances: About 45,000-60,000 € a year with shift allowances; a good route into planning or operations management

kpis: Punctuality and cancellations of the day
Time until passenger information is published
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a 12-hour shift

game.title: Transportleitung
game.loop: For one morning peak on the lab network, the player takes over the decisions of the operations engine's built-in dispatcher. Every departure without a unit or driver, every sick call and every breakdown asks for a choice: wait, run short, cancel, turn short, send a spare unit, pick a stand-by driver, hold a connection, order buses. The layout shows the trains and the travellers, and the Today view counts penalties and delays.
game.win: Beat the built-in dispatcher on penalties and passenger delay minutes with the same seed and stress test. A broken rest time, or a defective unit sent out, ends the round with a safety warning; in the career this is a written warning.
game.knowledge: What each penalty costs, rest-time rules, how delays pass along rotations and duties, and passenger rights duties
game.bigGame: Takes the roster from the crew planner, rotations from the rotation planner, units from the fleet, and disruptions from the IM (network controller, faults). Its decisions set the day's penalties for the contract managers, the messages for the information dispatcher, the claims for the passenger rights desk, and the reports for the operations manager.

roles.name: Crew planner and rosterer
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Turns the timetable and the rotations into duties and rosters for drivers and conductors (Dienstplanung, Personaldisposition), so that every train has its crew within working-time law, the tariff rules and with the works council's consent.
decisions: Cut the timetable's work into duties: where crews change, where breaks fall, where staff sign on
Set the number of stand-by duties and the staffing margin
Assign duties to people, considering route and vehicle knowledge, wishes and rest days
Approve or refuse vacation in busy weeks
Order overtime, or propose service cuts when sickness rises
Plan training days for route learning and periodic instruction
effects: Productive duties lower the cost per train-km; very tight ones turn every delay into overtime and rest-time problems
Stand-by drivers cost money every day, but with too few every sick call becomes a cancellation
Fair rosters reduce sickness and staff turnover
resources: 50-1,500 drivers and conductors per region; rostering software (e.g. IVU.rail)
A personnel budget in which a driver costs the company about 70,000-90,000 € a year
A planning horizon from the annual rest-day plan down to the next day
limits: Arbeitszeitgesetz (8 hours a day, at most 10 if averaged out; 11 hours of rest; breaks after 6 hours) and the GDL and EVG tariffs (at DB the GDL week falling to 35 hours by 2029, rest days planned for the year ahead, limits on consecutive shifts)
Directive 2005/47/EC for drivers in cross-border services (at most 9 hours' driving on a day shift, 8 on a night shift)
BetrVG § 87(1) Nos. 2 and 3: the works council co-decides duty schedules and overtime
TfV: only drivers with valid route and vehicle knowledge may be assigned
The transport contract's duties on staffing (e.g. conductors on certain lines)
risks: Blame from colleagues and the works council for unfair rosters
Pressure when sickness cancels trains; tight deadlines at every timetable change
Rest-time errors that lead to authority findings

career.entry: A former driver or conductor with internal training, the apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice, or a transport degree
career.chances: About 45,000-65,000 € a year, mostly office hours; leads to team leadership in production planning

kpis: Productivity (share of driving time in paid time)
roles.timescale: Days to weeks (monthly rosters, daily corrections, the annual rest-day plan)

game.title: The Roster
