game.loop: The player gets a week of duties on the lab network and its 51 drivers, each with a contract, a home, route knowledge and vacation wishes. The player sets the stand-by duties and assigns drivers, while a checker flags every ArbZG or tariff rule broken and every point the works council will object to. The week then runs in the operations engine with a stress test (flu wave, drivers leaving). The result shows cancellations, overtime and costs.
game.win: A roster with no rule broken that the works council accepts, and after the week fewer cancellations and lower cost than the reference setup. A roster the works council rejects must be redone; repeated rest-time violations cost reputation in the career.
game.knowledge: ArbZG and tariff rules, co-determination, qualification rules for drivers, and the trade-off between reserve and cancellations
game.bigGame: Takes rotations from the rotation planner, staff numbers from HR, available drivers from the driver team leader, and the wage settlement from the union. Gives duties to drivers and conductors, the reserve to the dispatcher, and personnel costs to the managing director's budget.

roles.name: Rotation and vehicle planner
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Plans which vehicle runs which trips (Umlaufplanung, Fahrzeugeinsatzplanung): chains the timetable into rotations, couples units for the peaks, fits in maintenance and cleaning windows, and keeps the fleet as small as the contract allows.
decisions: Chain trips into rotations and set the turn times at the ends of the lines
Decide where units stand overnight and which empty runs this requires
Couple or split units for peak capacity (Verstärker)
Set the number of spare units
Place maintenance and cleaning windows in the rotations
Request train paths for empty runs and transfers to the workshop
effects: Every unit saved is about 0.5-1 M€ a year of lease or capital cost
Tight turns save units but pass delays from one trip to the next
Missing maintenance windows produce overdue units that may not run
Trains too short in the peak bring overcrowding and penalties for missing seats
resources: A fleet of 20-150 units, each costing about 6-15 M€ new depending on length and drive (often from the authority's vehicle pool or a ROSCO)
Stabling and depot capacity; planning software
Time: the annual timetable and its weekly changes for construction works
limits: The contract's capacity requirements (seats per train and time band)
Vehicle authorisation and route compatibility (platform lengths, ETCS, power systems)
The ECM's maintenance programme (intervals in km and days)
Path allocation for empty runs (ERegG, network statement)
risks: Low personal risk; stress before timetable changes and in the construction season
Blame when overcrowding or failures follow from a tight plan

career.entry: A degree in transport engineering or logistics, or experience as a dispatcher with internal training
career.chances: About 50,000-70,000 € a year; specialists are sought after for bids

kpis: Units short at the morning pull-out
roles.timescale: Weeks to a timetable year

game.title: Rotation Puzzle
game.loop: On a time-distance chart of the lab network's lines, the player links trips into rotations, couples units in the peaks and places the maintenance nights. The game counts units, empty km, and seats against demand. A test week in the operations engine, with failures, then shows which rotations break and how many units end up short.
game.win: The fewest units and empty km with all capacity rules met, and fewer shortages in the test week than a set limit. Invalid rotations (impossible turns, units missing their maintenance) do not count.
game.knowledge: Minimum turn times, maintenance intervals, coupling rules, and the cost of a unit and of an empty km
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable from the service planner and the maintenance rules from the ECM. Gives rotations to the crew planner and the dispatcher, and the fleet size to the managing director and to the bid manager's calculation.

roles.name: Service and timetable planner
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Designs the service: lines, stopping patterns, frequencies and the timetable with its connections, and requests the train paths from the infrastructure manager. In long distance this is the RU's own commercial decision; in regional traffic it works within the authority's specification, and often the authority plans the timetable itself and the RU fills in the details.
decisions: Choose the lines and the stopping policy (fast trains or all stops)
Set the frequency and the times at the hubs for connections (integrated clock-face timetable, ITF)
Request train paths for the annual timetable by the deadline, and react to conflicts with other requests
Adapt the timetable to construction works and possessions
Propose extra services to the authority, or drop weak ones in long distance
effects: A clock-face timetable with well-timed hubs raises ridership across the whole network
More stops serve more places but slow down through travellers
Every train-km costs track charges, energy, staff and vehicle time
Losing a path conflict can break the hub concept for a whole year
resources: A train-km budget agreed with the authority (1-15 million train-km a year per contract)
Fleet and staff limits from rotation and crew planning
Timetabling software, passenger counts and demand models
limits: ERegG and the network statement (SNB): requests for the annual timetable by the second Monday in April for the change in December; conflicting requests are coordinated and then decided by priority rules (ERegG § 52)
The authority's specification in the transport contract (Leistungsbeschreibung); authorities may request paths themselves as access applicants
Framework agreements (Rahmenverträge) on capacity, and the federal target timetable of the Deutschlandtakt that shapes hub times
Infrastructure capacity: single-track sections, junctions, platform tracks
risks: Low personal risk; public criticism of timetable changes from mayors and passengers
Deadlines at the yearly path request

career.entry: A degree in transport engineering (Verkehrsingenieurwesen) or in transport planning or geography
career.chances: About 50,000-75,000 € a year; moves between RUs, the IM, authorities and consultancies are common

roles.timescale: Months to years (the yearly timetable, plans 2-5 years ahead)

game.title: Hub Builder
game.loop: The player designs the timetable of the lab network: frequencies, stops, and the minutes at which each line is at the station, aiming for connections between the RE, the RB, the S-Bahn and the town's buses. Each design is checked for conflicts at the platforms and on single-track sections. Then the journeys module plans the travellers' trips, and the town module counts how many people take the train.
game.win: The most passengers and connections within a fixed budget of train-km and units, with no path conflicts. A design that needs more units than the fleet has fails.
game.knowledge: Clock-face timetables and hub symmetry, running and turn times, path request rules and deadlines
game.bigGame: Takes the specification and the budget from the authority's planner, and the available capacity from the IM's timetable planner. Gives the timetable to the rotation planner, the crew planner and the revenue manager, and the path requests to track access sales.

roles.name: Pricing and revenue manager
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (long-distance passenger)
roles.summary: Sets and steers the fares of long-distance trains (Preis- und Erlösmanagement): price levels, quotas of discount fares per train and day, BahnCard and promotions, so that trains fill up and earn as much as possible. Regional fares are not set here but in the transport associations' tariffs and by Bund and Länder.
decisions: Set the quotas of saver fares (Sparpreis, Super Sparpreis) per train and day, and when to close them
Propose the level of the flexible fare (Flexpreis) for the next timetable change
Launch promotions for weak trains and periods
React to competitors (e.g. Flixtrain, long-distance buses) and to events (trade fairs, holidays, strikes)
Decide on mandatory reservations or sales limits for trains that will be overcrowded
effects: The quotas decide the load factor and the revenue of every train
Fares that are too cheap fill trains until they overflow and must be cleared; fares that are too high lose passengers to cars and buses
Fare increases bring political and press reactions
resources: Booking data, demand forecasts and a revenue management system
Revenue base of DB Fernverkehr of the order of 5-6 bn € a year; one ICE run brings in some 10,000-50,000 €
Authority to open and close quotas within the pricing policy set by the board
limits: Conditions of carriage and Reg. 2021/782: refund or rerouting from 60 minutes of expected delay; DB's own rule lifts train binding from 20 minutes
Competition law (GWB § 19, Art. 102 TFEU) for a dominant operator; price display rules (PAngV)
VAT of 7 % on long-distance tickets since 2020
Long-distance fares need no approval; regional fares follow the association tariffs and the Deutschlandtarif, and the Deutschlandticket price (63 € a month from 2026) is set by Bund and Länder
Seat capacity and the safety limits for standing passengers
risks: Low personal risk; public criticism of fare increases
Targets tied to bonuses

career.entry: A degree in economics, business or transport, often with operations research or data analysis
career.chances: About 55,000-90,000 € a year, above tariff. Few posts, mostly at DB Fernverkehr and a few open-access operators.

kpis: Revenue per train-km and per seat-km
roles.timescale: Days, across a booking horizon of about six months per train

game.title: Booking Curve
game.loop: The player steers the fares of a few long-distance trains over their booking horizon in fast time. Each simulated day, bookings arrive by fare level, and the player opens or closes quotas. Events shift demand: a trade fair, an announced strike, a competitor's promotion. On the day of travel the train runs; overcrowded trains must be cleared and lose goodwill.
game.win: The most revenue with every load factor below the safety limit. A train over capacity counts heavily against the score, and a strike day with refunds tests the forecast.
game.knowledge: Price elasticity, booking curves, quota control, and passenger rights after delays (refunds, lifted train binding)
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable and seats from the service and rotation planners and the delays from operations. Gives revenue to the RU's economics and passenger loads to the train manager's game.

roles.name: Travel centre sales agent
roles.organisation: railway undertaking's sales (at DB, DB Vertrieb for DB Fernverkehr and DB Regio), a regional operator's own sales, or an agency
roles.summary: Advises customers and sells tickets at the counter of a travel centre (Reisezentrum): travel plans, single tickets and season tickets, refunds, and help during disruptions, for long-distance, regional and transport association fares.
decisions: Find the best connection and fare for the customer (a saver fare with train binding or a flexible fare)
Grant a refund or exchange under the conditions of carriage, or a goodwill gesture
Recommend a BahnCard or a season ticket
Confirm a delay for a passenger rights claim, or rebook passengers during a disruption
Book assistance for a disabled traveller
effects: Correct advice prevents increased-fare charges and claims later
Long queues during disruptions bring complaints and missed trains
Sales revenue for the RU, or commission for an agency
resources: The sales system, a cash drawer and a few colleagues per shift
Authority for goodwill gestures up to small limits
limits: Conditions of carriage (BB Personenverkehr), EVO, the transport association tariffs and the Deutschlandtarif for regional trips across associations
Reg. 2021/782: passenger rights and accessibility duties
Cash handling rules and liability for shortfalls (Mankohaftung)
risks: Angry customers, especially during disruptions
Liability for cash shortfalls
Travel centres closing as sales move online

career.entry: The three-year apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice (or one in tourism), or a conversion course
career.chances: About 34,000-42,000 € a year. Counters are shrinking, but moves into on-board service or station roles are open.

roles.timescale: Minutes per customer, within a shift

game.title: Counter Rush
game.loop: Customers queue in the station building, each with a question drawn from the journeys module: from a house to a station beyond the layout at a given time, perhaps with a BahnCard, a bicycle or a wheelchair. The player answers and sells using the travel planner and a fare table. When a disruption starts, the queue grows and the requests change to rebooking and refunds.
game.win: Correct sales and refunds while the queue's waiting time stays under a limit. Wrong fares come back later as increased-fare charges for the customer and as claims; a long queue makes travellers miss their trains.
game.knowledge: Fare rules, train binding, refund rules, passenger rights, and how to book assistance
game.bigGame: Takes fares from the revenue manager and the day's disruptions from operations. Gives ticket revenue, assistance bookings to the mobility service, and delay confirmations to the passenger rights desk.

roles.name: Passenger rights and compensation agent
roles.organisation: Servicecenter Fahrgastrechte (run by Deutsche Bahn in Frankfurt am Main, also for many other railway undertakings), or an RU's own customer service
roles.summary: Handles claims for delay compensation and refunds: checks the journey, the delay and the rules, pays or refuses, and answers complaints. Most claims now arrive online and are checked automatically; the agents handle the paper claims, the exceptions and the disputes.
decisions: Check whether a claim is valid (delay at the destination, ticket, deadlines)
Calculate the compensation: 25 % of the fare from 60 minutes, 50 % from 120 minutes, flat amounts for season tickets and the Deutschlandticket (1.50 € a case in second class), nothing under 4 €
Accept or refuse extra costs (a taxi up to 120 € at night or after the last train, a hotel, other transport after 100 minutes without information)
Apply the force majeure exception (extreme weather, persons on the track) or not
Flag suspected fraud
effects: DB pays well over 100 M€ of compensation a year. Errors either waste money or lead to arbitration cases.
Slow processing misses the one-month deadline and brings action by the EBA as national enforcement body
Fair handling keeps customers
resources: A claims system with delay data, and a team of dozens to hundreds of agents
Authority for small goodwill payments
limits: Reg. (EU) 2021/782 (compensation, rerouting, force majeure exception since June 2023), EVO and the conditions of carriage
Payment within one month of a complete claim
Arbitration by the söp (Schlichtungsstelle für den öffentlichen Personenverkehr); the EBA as national enforcement body for passenger rights
Data protection (GDPR, DSGVO)
risks: Low physical risk; high volumes and stress after large disruptions
Pressure from performance targets

career.entry: The apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice or in office management, or experience in sales
career.chances: About 34,000-42,000 € a year; team leader posts

roles.timescale: Days (the queue of claims)

game.title: Claims Desk
game.loop: After a simulated day with disruptions, the travellers of the journeys module send claims with their ticket and their story. The player checks each one against the operations log (actual delay and its cause) and decides on compensation, extra costs or refusal. Some claims are false or exaggerated.
game.win: Correct decisions within the time limit. The score drops for every wrong payment, every wrongful refusal (which goes to arbitration) and every missed deadline.
game.knowledge: The thresholds and exceptions of Reg. 2021/782 (60 and 120 minutes, force majeure, the 100-minute rule for other transport), the flat amounts for season tickets, the rules for taxis and hotels, and the 4 € minimum
game.bigGame: Takes delays and their causes from operations and tickets from sales. Gives compensation costs to the RU's economics, which the RU can pass on to the IM or ECM where contracts allow.

roles.name: Mobility service agent for disabled passengers
roles.organisation: Deutsche Bahn's Mobilitätsservice-Zentrale (MSZ), working for the station operator DB InfraGO and for DB and many other railway undertakings
roles.summary: Plans and coordinates help for travellers with reduced mobility at the Mobilitätsservice-Zentrale (MSZ): bookings, ramps and lifts, and staff to help with boarding and changes, for all RUs at DB stations.
decisions: Accept a booking and plan the help at each station (boarding, change, arrival)
Assign station staff, a ramp or a platform lift (Hublift) to each step
Re-plan when an elevator is out of order or a train is cancelled
Advise an alternative route via step-free stations
Tell the train crew that the passenger is on board and where they get off
effects: Each missed assistance leaves a traveller stranded and brings complaints and press coverage
Good planning makes rail travel possible for wheelchair users and older people
Station staff time is limited: overbooking a time slot forces refusals
resources: A booking system, and the station service staff at several hundred stations that offer help with boarding
Ramps and platform lifts, and live data on elevator status
limits: Reg. 2021/782 (assistance; at most 24 hours' advance notice may be required; DB asks for bookings by 20:00 the day before) and TSI PRM (Reg. 1300/2014)
Platform heights (mostly 55 or 76 cm, 96 cm at S-Bahn stations, some old 38 cm) against vehicle floor heights
Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz (BGG)
risks: Low physical risk; stress during disruptions
Public criticism when help does not come

career.entry: The apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice or Kaufmann/-frau für Dialogmarketing, or station experience
career.chances: About 34,000-42,000 € a year; few posts

roles.timescale: Minutes to a day

game.title: Step-Free
game.loop: Bookings arrive from travellers using a wheelchair or a walking frame, and from blind travellers; the journeys module gives their travel plans. The player plans who helps each of them at each station and with which ramp, and checks step-free access and elevators. During the day elevators fail and trains are cancelled; the player re-plans and informs the train crew.
game.win: All travellers reach their aim with help on time; a missed assistance counts heavily. Overbooking the staff in a time slot forces refusals.
game.knowledge: Accessibility rules, platform and vehicle floor heights, booking deadlines, step-free routes
game.bigGame: Takes bookings from the travel centre and the wheelchair user role, and disruptions from operations and the IM (elevator faults). Gives tasks to station staff and conductors, and complaints to the station manager.

roles.name: On-board catering staff
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (long-distance passenger; DB Fernverkehr runs its own) or a catering contractor
roles.summary: Runs the bistro or restaurant car of a long-distance train (Bordgastronomie): checks the loaded stock, prepares and sells food and drinks, serves first class at the seat, and is responsible for hygiene and cash.
decisions: Check the loaded stock against the list, and order supplies at a supply point on the way
Close the bistro or take products off sale when the cooling fails
Choose between service at the seat and at the counter as the train fills
Refuse alcohol to minors or drunk passengers
Report a broken coffee machine or till, and decide on a cash-only service
effects: Revenue on board and customer satisfaction, in the train manager's score too
Hygiene failures can make passengers ill and bring fines
Shortages lose sales; overstock becomes waste
resources: A bistro car, stock worth a few thousand euros per trip, a till, and one to three staff
limits: Food hygiene (Reg. (EC) 852/2004, LMHV, HACCP; chilled food at no more than 7 °C) and allergen labelling (LMIV, Reg. 1169/2011)
Infection protection law: IfSG § 43 instruction before working with food
Youth protection law (JuSchG) on alcohol
ArbZG and the tariff
risks: Burns, cuts and heavy loads in a moving train
Liability for cash shortfalls
Shift work and nights away from home

career.entry: Training in hospitality or a functional training of a few weeks; a health instruction under IfSG
career.chances: About 30,000-38,000 € a year plus tips; moves into the train attendant career are common

roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift

game.title: Bistro Run
game.loop: A four-hour long-distance run in fast time. The player sees the bistro's stock, the train's load and the passengers' mood. Before departure they check the loading list; during the trip they choose between counter and seat service and react to events: a cooling failure (with a temperature log), the till going offline, the coffee machine failing, a delay that makes people hungry, a group of drunk football fans.
game.win: Revenue minus waste and fines. Any hygiene breach (food above 7 °C sold) or alcohol sold to a minor ends the round; in the career this means a warning.
game.knowledge: HACCP temperatures, allergen rules, youth protection, stock planning
game.bigGame: Takes the passengers and the delay from the train manager's run and from operations. Gives revenue and waste to the RU's economics and customer satisfaction to the train's score.

roles.name: Train cleaner
roles.organisation: cleaning contractor or railway undertaking (at DB, DB Services)
roles.summary: Cleans trains during the turn at the terminus and in the depot at night (Zugreinigung): litter, toilets, seats, windows and graffiti. Often employed by a cleaning contractor whose contract with the RU sets quality checks and penalties.
decisions: Choose the order of tasks in a short turn (toilets first, then litter and spills)
Report vandalism, graffiti and defects (toilet out of order, broken seat)
Refuse to handle needles or body fluids without protective equipment, and call for special cleaning
Wait for the track to be protected before working around stabled units
Mark a coach as not clean enough to use and inform the dispatcher
effects: Cleanliness is a quality item in most transport contracts, checked by testers and penalised when it falls short
Defects reported early get repaired; unreported ones become comfort defects that are fined per day
Unsafe work on the tracks can be fatal
resources: A team of 2-6 per train, cleaning trolleys and chemicals
A turn of 5-20 minutes at the terminus, or a night shift in the depot
limits: The building-cleaning sector minimum wage and tariff, above the statutory minimum wage (13.90 € an hour in 2026)
Occupational safety: DGUV rules, Biostoffverordnung (needles, faeces, toilet tanks), Gefahrstoffverordnung (cleaning chemicals)
Railway safety in depots: work only on protected tracks, never climb on roofs under the 15 kV overhead line
The service levels and quality checks of the cleaning contract
risks: Injury from needles, chemicals or slipping; electric shock, or being hit by a moving vehicle
Low pay, night work, and changing employers when the cleaning contract is re-tendered

career.entry: No formal training required: an induction and a safety briefing. The apprenticeship Gebäudereiniger/in is possible.
career.chances: About 14-16 € an hour, or 25,000-32,000 € a year full time; team leader posts. RUs welcome career changers into on-board service.

kpis: Quality points in the contract's checks
roles.timescale: Minutes per turn, within a shift

game.title: Turnaround Clean
game.loop: A unit arrives at the terminus with litter that depends on its load in the passenger simulation. In the 10-15 minutes of its turn, the player sends two or three cleaners through the coaches. Tasks appear: toilets, litter, spills, a needle, graffiti. Departure ends the turn, and a contract tester checks random coaches. A night round in the depot adds deep cleaning on protected tracks.
game.win: Quality points above the contract's threshold and no unsafe action. Touching a needle without gloves, or stepping onto a track that is not protected, ends the round; in the career this is an accident or a warning.
game.knowledge: Cleaning priorities, protection rules (biological hazards, chemicals, track safety), how to report defects
game.bigGame: Takes turn times from the rotation planner and passenger loads from the simulation. Gives cleanliness (which feeds contract penalties) to the contract manager, and defect reports to the fleet.

roles.name: Security officer on trains and in stations
roles.organisation: DB Sicherheit or a private security contractor
roles.summary: Patrols stations and rides on trains in shifts for DB Sicherheit or a private security contractor: prevention, help for staff and passengers, enforcement of the house rules, and handing offenders over to the federal police.
decisions: Choose, within the shift plan of the security control centre, which trains and platforms to cover (known hot spots)
De-escalate, issue a station ban (Hausverbot), or remove a person under house rights
Hold a person caught in the act (StPO § 127) until the federal police arrive
Cordon off an abandoned bag and call the federal police
Give first aid and call the rescue services
Start recording with the bodycam
effects: Visible presence reduces assaults on staff and passengers
Excessive force leads to criminal charges and press coverage
How fast an abandoned bag is handled decides whether a station closes for hours
resources: Teams of two (some with a dog), radio to the security control centre and the federal police, a bodycam
The rights every citizen has, plus delegated house rights; no police powers
DB Sicherheit employs several thousand staff and also uses contractors
limits: GewO § 34a (security trade; the IHK competence exam for patrols in public transport) and DGUV Vorschrift 23
StPO § 127, StGB §§ 32 and 34 (self-defence, necessity), BGB § 229
House rules of DB stations; the federal police have police powers on railway premises (BPolG § 3)
ArbZG and the tariff
risks: Injury from violence, and criminal charges for excessive force
Night work and stress

career.entry: The competence exam under GewO § 34a (IHK) or training as Fachkraft für Schutz und Sicherheit, then DB's internal training
career.chances: About 32,000-42,000 € a year with allowances at DB Sicherheit; less at private contractors

kpis: Incidents and assaults in the patrol area
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, within a shift

game.title: Night Patrol
game.loop: An evening at the lab station and on its trains. The player plans the patrol (which trains, which platforms); then incidents arise from the passenger simulation: a fare dodger threatening a conductor, a drunk group after a football match (a crowd surge), a person in the track area, an abandoned bag. For each one the player chooses an action and must stay within their legal powers.
game.win: The fewest incidents with harm and no unlawful action. An unlawful action ends the round with a complaint; in the career it brings the risk of a criminal investigation.
game.knowledge: The rights every citizen has, house rights, when to call the federal police, the procedure for abandoned luggage
game.bigGame: Takes calls for help from conductors and the 3-S centre, and crowd events from disruptions. Gives safer trains (less sick leave for staff, better passenger mood) and hands incidents over to the federal police.

roles.name: Bid manager for regional rail tenders
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Prepares the undertaking's bids in tenders for regional rail services (SPNV-Ausschreibungen): reads the tender, calculates the costs over 10-15 years, proposes the price, and writes the operating concept with the team.
decisions: Recommend whether to bid for a network (bid or no bid)
Calculate staff, vehicles, energy, track access and overheads over the contract term
Choose the vehicles: new from a manufacturer, leased, or from the authority's pool
Set the risk premium and the profit margin
Send questions to the authority (Bieterfragen) and object to unfair clauses (Rüge)
Plan the strategy for the negotiation rounds
effects: A price too high loses the bid; one too low wins 10-15 years of losses (several regional operators got into trouble around 2020)
The concept decides the jobs of hundreds of staff and the vehicles the region gets
A successful objection can change the tender for all bidders
resources: A bid team of 3-10 people for 3-9 months, and a bid budget of 0.3-1.5 M€
Cost models, and offers from manufacturers and ROSCOs
Authority to propose only; management and owners sign off the price
limits: GWB § 131 and the VgV (procedure), Reg. (EC) 1370/2007, the Landestariftreuegesetze, and the staff transfer clause (GWB § 131(3))
Tender deadlines; an objection must reach the authority within 10 days of spotting the breach (GWB § 160(3)) before the public procurement tribunal (Vergabekammer) can review it
The index clauses for cost changes that the authority sets
risks: Career damage when a bid is lost, or won at a loss
Long hours before deadlines

career.entry: A degree in transport, economics or engineering, and several years in planning or finance
career.chances: About 70,000-110,000 € a year plus bonus; a small, well-connected community in the sector

kpis: Margin of won contracts after a few years
roles.timescale: Months for a bid; consequences for 10-15 years

game.title: The Tender
game.loop: The player reads a short tender for the lab network (train-km, years, vehicles, quality system) and builds the calculation: staff from the duties of the operations engine, units from its rotations, energy and track charges per train-km, overheads and a risk premium. Computer competitors bid as well. If the player wins, the contract runs for years in fast time with shocks, and the outcome shows whether the price was right.
game.win: Win the contract and stay profitable through its term. A lost bid scores by how close the price came to the winner's. A won contract that turns loss-making counts as a failure; in the career the next role inherits the blame.
game.knowledge: The cost structure of regional rail, procurement rules and deadlines, index clauses, and risk
game.bigGame: Takes the tender from the authority's tender manager, and offers from industry and the ROSCO. Gives the contract to the managing director (its start point in the economics simulator) and the operating concept to the planners.

roles.name: Rail replacement service coordinator
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Plans and runs rail replacement bus services (Schienenersatzverkehr, SEV) for construction works and disruptions: buses, routes, stops, guides at the stops and information. The RU's link between the bus companies, the IM's construction planning and the municipalities.
decisions: Order buses (number, size, low-floor) from contracted bus companies for a possession
Plan routes and replacement stops with the municipalities and road authorities
Time the buses to keep connections, and decide between express and all-stops buses
Place guides (SEV-Lotsen) and signs at the stations
Order buses at short notice when a line is blocked, and release them when trains run again
effects: A good replacement service keeps passengers; a bad one loses them for years
Bus costs (about 60-90 € per bus-hour) are paid by the RU or the authority, depending on the contract
Buses make journeys 20-50 % longer and break connections
resources: Framework contracts with bus companies; a budget of hundreds of thousands to several million euros per major possession

Construction schedules from the IM, 12-24 months ahead for planned works; for the general refurbishments of corridors (Generalsanierungen) a replacement concept agreed with DB InfraGO and the authorities
limits: PBefG and the bus companies' licences; StVO and road traffic orders (StVO § 45) for stops
The transport contract's rules on replacement services, and accessibility duties
Driving and working time of bus drivers: Reg. (EC) 561/2006 does not apply to regular services on routes up to 50 km, so most replacement buses fall under the ArbZG and the Fahrpersonalverordnung
risks: Public criticism and complaints
Stress during large disruptions

career.entry: A former dispatcher or bus operations staff member, or a transport degree
career.chances: About 45,000-60,000 € a year; in high demand during the Generalsanierungen

roles.timescale: Months for planned works; minutes in a disruption

game.title: Bus Bridge
game.loop: A track closure on the lab network is announced (the maintenance story's renewal). The player lays out replacement bus routes on the town's streets, orders buses and sets their times. Then the closure runs, and the travellers of the journeys module take the buses.
game.win: Most travellers arrive within a target delay, at a cost within budget. Stranded travellers and missed connections count heavily.
game.knowledge: Bus capacity and running times, connection planning, accessibility, and the PBefG and working-time rules
game.bigGame: Takes possessions from the IM's possession planner and disruptions from the dispatcher. Gives bus times to the information dispatcher, costs to the RU's economics, and complaints and ridership effects to the contract manager.

roles.name: Transport contract manager (railway undertaking)
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (regional passenger)
roles.summary: Manages the transport contract with the authority from the RU's side: quality reports, penalties and bonuses, disputes about the causes of incidents, amendments and yearly index adjustments. Passes claims on to subcontractors.
decisions: Check the monthly penalty statement, and dispute items caused by the infrastructure or third parties
Pass claims on to the ECM, the workshop or the cleaning contractor along the chain of contracts
Negotiate amendments for extra services, construction works or changed costs
Apply the index clause each year
Prepare the quality reports and passenger counts
effects: Every disputed penalty that is won goes straight to profit
Fair amendments keep a contract viable
Good evidence (delay codes) shifts costs to whoever caused them
resources: A contract worth hundreds of millions of euros over its term, with penalties of about 0.5-3 % of the yearly payments
Delay data from operations and from the IM
limits: The transport contract and its quality annex; BGB contract law
GWB § 132: amendments must not change the contract materially, or the authority has to tender again
The IM's delay attribution rules (delay codes) and its performance scheme (Anreizsystem) in the network statement
risks: Low personal risk; pressure from management and from the authority

career.entry: A degree in business, law or transport, and experience in controlling or planning
career.chances: About 60,000-90,000 € a year

roles.timescale: Monthly (penalty statements) to yearly (index, amendments)

game.title: Penalty Ledger
game.loop: After a simulated month of operations, the player gets the penalty statement from the operations module's Penalties view. They check each incident's cause, dispute the items that are exempt (infrastructure, external causes) with evidence, and claim from the ECM and the workshop along the contracts. A final negotiation with the authority settles the open points.
game.win: The lowest net penalties with no unfounded dispute. Unfounded disputes cost credibility, which makes the next negotiation harder.
game.knowledge: Contract penalty rules, delay attribution, the limits on amendments, and how penalties pass along the chain of contracts
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from operations and the IM. Gives net penalties to the managing director's result, and claims to the ECM and the workshop.

roles.name: Passenger information dispatcher
roles.organisation: railway undertaking's operations control (Transportleitung), working with the station operator's passenger information
roles.summary: Turns the operations control's decisions and the IM's forecasts into what passengers are told: delay forecasts, cancellations, platform changes, alternative routes and replacement buses, in the apps, on station displays, in announcements and on the trains. Decides when uncertain information is good enough to publish.
decisions: Publish a delay forecast now or wait for a better one, knowing that every correction costs trust
Announce a cancellation early so passengers can re-plan, or keep the train as delayed while a spare unit or driver may still be found
Recommend alternative routes and connections, and announce whether a connection is held
Announce replacement buses with their stops and times, together with the replacement coordinator
Propose a general goodwill rule (Sonderkulanz: tickets valid on other trains or days) to the duty manager before a storm or a strike
Word the messages: cause, expected duration, and what passengers should do
effects: Early, honest information spreads passengers over the alternatives and keeps platforms from overcrowding
Wrong forecasts make passengers miss trains or wait for trains that never come, and raise claims and complaints
A general goodwill rule moves demand away from the disruption but costs revenue and fills the next trains
Messages that are not accessible (audio only, no step-free alternative) leave some passengers stranded
resources: The RU's dispatching system linked to the IM's real-time data, and the channels to apps, station displays and train displays
Message templates, texts in several languages, social media channels
Authority over the RU's own messages; displays and announcements at stations belong to the station operator, which takes the RU's input
limits: Reg. (EU) 2021/782 Art. 9 and 20: information before and during the journey, and on delays as soon as it is available
TSI TAP (telematics for passenger services) and Reg. (EU) 2017/1926 on multimodal travel information
Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG, since June 2025) and TSI PRM: information in visual and audible form, accessible apps
The transport contract's quality rules for passenger information, checked by the authority's testers
risks: Low physical risk; shift work around the clock
Public anger and press coverage when information comes late or the app shows trains that do not run
Pressure to soften messages about the causes

career.entry: Usually former train staff or travel centre agents with internal training; some come from customer service or communication
career.chances: About 40,000-55,000 € a year with shift allowances; a few posts per RU, more in large operations centres

kpis: Time from the event to the first message
Share of cancellations announced before the planned departure
Quality points in the authority's checks
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift

game.title: What Do We Tell Them?
game.loop: During a disruption on the lab network (the failed signal of the maintenance story, a broken-down unit), the operations engine produces forecasts that become more certain over time. The player decides when to publish a delay, declare a cancellation, or point to the bus. The travellers of the journeys module read the messages and re-plan, wait, or walk to the bus stop; the station boards and the passengers' mood show the result.
game.win: The fewest passenger delay minutes and stranded travellers with few corrected messages. A train announced as running that is then cancelled with passengers waiting counts heavily, and so does a crowded platform left without information for more than 10 minutes. The round ends with the disruption; in the career, repeated false forecasts cost reputation.
game.knowledge: Information duties under passenger rights, how forecasts behave (delays grow more often than they shrink), alternative routes in the network, and accessible messages
game.bigGame: Takes decisions from the RU's dispatcher, forecasts and faults from the IM's network controller, and buses from the rail replacement coordinator. Gives travellers' re-planned journeys (crowding, missed connections) back to operations, and complaints and claims to the passenger rights desk.

roles.name: Train driver team leader
roles.organisation: railway undertaking (passenger)
roles.summary: Line manager of a group of 30-80 drivers at a depot: rides with them and checks them in the cab, keeps their certificates and route and vehicle knowledge valid, handles the return to duty after incidents and fatalities, and is the first person drivers turn to. The link between the drivers, the crew planner and the operations manager.
decisions: Ride along with drivers for the periodic checks (Begleitfahrten) and decide whether a driver needs extra training
Interview a driver after a signal passed at danger or a PZB emergency brake, and propose to the operations manager whether and when they return to duty
Arrange care after a fatality on the track: time off, the railway psychologist, a gradual return with a colleague in the cab
Plan refreshers for route knowledge that has lapsed and training for new vehicle types
Approve leave and shift swaps within the roster and the works council agreements
Start disciplinary steps, or treat a mistake as a learning case under a just culture
effects: Good checks find bad habits before they cause a signal passed at danger
Every driver kept off duty is a duty the crew planner has to cover; returning a driver too early risks a repeat
Fair and caring leadership keeps drivers in the company in times of shortage
Lapsed route knowledge makes a driver unusable on that line, and can cancel trains
resources: 30-80 drivers, a share of the training budget, and a few days a month in the cab
The RU's records of certificates, route and vehicle knowledge and checks
Authority to instruct drivers and to stand them down for safety reasons until the operations manager decides
limits: TfV and Directive 2007/59/EC: certificates, the RU's register, periodic checks and training
The RU's rules for drivers (at DB Ril 492) and the competence management of its safety management system (Reg. 2018/762)
Arbeitsschutzgesetz and the statutory accident insurer (Unfallversicherung Bund und Bahn for DB, VBG for most private operators) on care after traumatic events
BetrVG (co-determination on rules of conduct, § 87(1) No. 1) and the GDL/EVG tariffs
risks: Responsibility, and in the worst case a criminal investigation, if a driver they cleared causes an accident
Being caught between loyalty to former colleagues and safety duties
Emotional strain from caring for drivers after fatalities

career.entry: An experienced driver (usually five years or more) with a leadership course, often also qualified as an examiner or instructor
career.chances: About 55,000-75,000 € a year; several posts in every mid-size RU, a common step up for drivers who want to lead

kpis: Checks and refreshers done on time
Signals passed at danger and other precursors in the team
Sickness and turnover in the team
roles.timescale: Days to weeks; hours after an incident

game.title: Back in the Cab?
game.loop: The player leads a team of drivers from the operations module's crew. Each week brings cases: a recorded ride from Cab Shift to assess, a driver after a PZB emergency brake, a driver back after a fatality, lapsed route knowledge, leave requests during a flu wave. For each case the player picks a measure (check ride, training, care, time off, return to duty); the following simulated weeks show cancellations, repeat incidents and the team's sickness rate.
game.win: Keep precursor incidents and cancellations below their limits without returning any driver before they are fit. A repeat incident by a driver returned too early ends the round with an inquiry by the operations manager; in the career it costs reputation.
game.knowledge: TfV certificates and checks, what a recorded ride shows (PZB, speeds, signals), care after traumatic events, co-determination
game.bigGame: Takes rides and incidents from the train driver's game and the roster from the crew planner. Gives available drivers to the crew planner, return-to-duty proposals to the operations manager, and training needs to the instructors.

roles.name: Managing director of a freight railway undertaking
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (Güterverkehrs-EVU): a private EVU such as Captrain Deutschland, TX Logistik or RheinCargo, or DB Cargo AG, where the top level is a management board (Vorstand) instead of managing directors
roles.summary: Leads a freight railway undertaking (Eisenbahnverkehrsunternehmen, EVU) with tens to thousands of staff. Decides which markets and customers it serves and which locomotives and staff it has. Carries the legal responsibility for the operating licence, the safety certificate and the company's solvency, in a market where trucks set the price and track access charges keep rising.
decisions: Bid for a multi-year block-train contract, or walk away from it
Buy, lease or rent locomotives (multi-system, with or without ETCS)
Fit ETCS onboard units now, with EU (CEF) or federal funding where available, or wait and risk losing access to ETCS-only lines
Set the hiring and training plan for train drivers: own school, lateral entrants, or drivers hired from personnel service providers
Close or keep a loss-making single-wagonload (Einzelwagenverkehr) or regional production
Negotiate the company tariff agreement with GDL or EVG, directly or through an employers' association, or ride out a strike
Apply for federal funding: the subsidy on freight track access charges (Trassenpreisförderung), single-wagonload and combined-transport funding
Appoint the operations manager (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter) and sign off the safety management system
effects: Contracts won or lost shift tonnage between rail and road (one block train carries the load of roughly 40–50 trucks)
Fleet decisions tie up tens of millions of euros for 20–30 years and decide which corridors the company can serve
Too few drivers means cancelled trains and contract penalties; too many means idle cost
Saving on safety (SMS, maintenance) raises the risk of incidents and can cost the safety certificate
Losses drain liquidity: a few bad quarters can push a mid-sized EVU into insolvency
resources: Revenue of €10–300 million a year in a private EVU (DB Cargo: about €5–6 billion, with losses in the hundreds of millions a year for many years)
20 to over 1,000 staff, most of them train drivers (DB Cargo: tens of thousands)
10–150 locomotives (a new multi-system locomotive costs about €4–5 million; a full-service lease €25–40k a month)
Wagons mostly hired from wagon keepers (about €20–60 per wagon-day)
Investment budget of a few million euros a year; credit lines from banks or the parent group
Authority over hiring, contracts and prices; reports to the shareholders or the supervisory board
limits: AEG §6 with the Eisenbahnunternehmer-Berufszugangsverordnung (EBZugV): operating licence (Unternehmensgenehmigung) with proof of reliability, financial fitness and professional competence
Single safety certificate (Directive (EU) 2016/798, transposed in the AEG), issued by ERA or, for operation only in Germany, by the EBA
Common safety methods for the safety management system (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762) and for monitoring (Regulation (EU) 1078/2012)
Regulation (EU) 2019/779: every vehicle needs a certified entity in charge of maintenance (ECM)
ERegG: track access charges approved by BNetzA, path allocation and framework agreements
Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung (EBV): an operations manager must be appointed and confirmed by the supervisory authority
GmbHG §43 liability of directors; InsO §15a duty to file for insolvency within three weeks of illiquidity (six weeks of over-indebtedness)
EU state aid law: the Commission's case on DB Cargo (opened 2022) was closed on condition that DB AG stops covering DB Cargo's losses and DB Cargo becomes profitable after a short restructuring
GDL/EVG tariff agreements (e.g. the 2024 GDL agreement with DB that cuts the reference week in steps from 38 to 35 hours by 2029) and the Working Hours Act (ArbZG)
TSI CCS (ETCS), TSI OPE, TSI Noise and the Schienenlärmschutzgesetz (loud freight wagons banned on German lines since the timetable change of December 2020)
risks: Civil liability to the company (§43 GmbHG) and criminal liability for filing for insolvency too late (§15a InsO)
Prosecution for negligent homicide after an accident if safety duties were neglected (Organisationsverschulden)
Dismissal by the shareholders after losses; fixed-term contract not renewed
Public exposure after accidents, strikes or job cuts
Long hours and constant availability

career.entry: Degree in business, transport engineering or law; 10–15 years in rail freight sales, production or controlling, often first as head of a business unit or a subsidiary
career.chances: €150–300k a year plus bonus in a mid-sized private EVU; €400k to over €1 million on the board of DB Cargo; few posts, fixed-term contracts of 3–5 years

roles.timescale: months to years (business year, contracts of 3–5 years, vehicles for 20–30 years)

game.title: Cargo turnaround
game.loop: The player runs a mid-sized freight EVU for five business years in about 25 minutes; each quarter is one turn. The board shows the contracts on offer (block trains, intermodal shuttles, single wagonload), the fleet, the drivers in training, liquidity and the safety record. The player bids, buys or leases locomotives, hires driver cohorts (ready 9–12 months later), sets the safety budget and reacts to events: a rise in track access charges, a GDL strike, a corridor closed for weeks (like Rastatt 2017), an energy price spike. The operations engine runs each quarter and returns punctuality, penalties, incidents and the result.
game.win: Survive five years with positive cash and the safety certificate intact; the score is cumulative EBIT, market share and safety. When the cash runs out the player must decide on insolvency (filing late is a criminal offence), and a serious accident with a poor SMS record ends the round with the certificate suspended. In career mode a failed company stains the CV; a turnaround opens the board of a larger group.
game.knowledge: Cost structure of a freight train (traction, driver, energy, track access per train-km, wagon hire), contribution margin, liquidity versus profit, the AEG licence and the safety certificate, the duties of an SMS and an ECM, the funding schemes, and how long it takes to get drivers and vehicles.
game.bigGame: Takes tenders from the shipper, forwarder and intermodal operator games, path prices from track-access-sales, funding from federal-rail-funding-officer and strikes from union-official. Gives budgets and staffing limits to the dispatcher, planner, sales and train driver games, and orders for locomotives and wagons to rosco-manager and wagon-keeper. In the economics simulator it is the EVU's top-level turn.

roles.name: Key account and sales manager (rail freight)
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking
roles.summary: Wins and keeps transport business with industrial shippers, forwarders and intermodal operators. Calculates the price of a train or wagon offer, negotiates framework contracts, and is the customer's contact for the business relationship when trains run late or volumes change.
decisions: Calculate a price per train, wagon or tonne from the production cost
Decide how low to go against a truck offer or a rival EVU
Offer guaranteed capacity (take-or-pay) or flexible volumes
Agree escalation clauses that pass on rises in energy prices and track access charges
Quote for a customer's extra train at short notice, once production confirms a locomotive, a driver and a path
Agree service levels, penalty clauses and the liability limits of the contract
Escalate a quality problem to production, or offer the customer a credit note
effects: A won contract keeps locomotives and drivers busy for years; a mispriced one loses money on every train
Penalty clauses turn operational unreliability into lost revenue
Lost customers move freight to the motorway (one block train is about 40–50 trucks)
Promises to customers set the workload of the planner, the dispatcher and the yard
resources: A portfolio of 10–40 key accounts worth €5–50 million of revenue a year
A costing tool (Kalkulation) with production costs per train-km and per hour
Authority to give discounts up to a limit; larger deals go to the head of sales or the managing director
Production planning and pricing teams for support
limits: HGB §§407 ff (freight contract): liability for loss and damage limited to 8.33 SDR per kg (§431), which standard terms may set between 2 and 40 SDR (§449); delay liability up to three times the freight
CIM (COTIF Appendix B) for international traffic: 17 SDR per kg, delay up to four times the carriage charge
The EVU's general terms (e.g. DB Cargo's Allgemeine Leistungsbedingungen, ALB) and the GCU for the use of wagons
Competition law (GWB, Art. 101/102 TFEU): no price agreements with competitors
Track access charges (DB InfraGO's price system, approved by BNetzA under the ERegG) and path availability
Production capacity: locomotives, drivers, yard slots
risks: Revenue targets and a bonus tied to volumes; job loss when key accounts leave
Little personal legal liability, but a badly mispriced contract ends a sales career
Much travel; pressure from customers and from production at once

career.entry: Degree in business, logistics or transport, or an apprenticeship as freight forwarder (Kaufmann/-frau für Spedition und Logistikdienstleistung) plus experience; usually 3–5 years in sales, customer service or production first
career.chances: €60–100k a year plus a bonus of 10–20 %; head of sales €100–150k

roles.timescale: weeks to years (tenders, annual price rounds, contracts of 1–5 years)

game.title: Price the train
game.loop: A shipper invites tenders for a weekly flow, e.g. three block trains of steel coils of 1,800 t each over 450 km. The player builds up the cost: locomotive hours, driver shifts, energy, track access per train-km, wagon hire, shunting for the first and last mile, and then adds risk and margin and chooses the contract terms (take-or-pay, escalation, liability). The shipper compares the offer with a truck price and a rival bid; a contract year is then simulated with disruptions, delays and penalties.
game.win: Win the tender at a price that still earns a positive contribution after the contract year. A round is one tender (10–15 minutes) or a portfolio of three. Winning below cost, or losing every bid, ends the round with a poor rating; in career mode a profitable portfolio leads to head of sales.
game.knowledge: Freight cost components and their orders of magnitude (about €15–35 per train-km all in; track access about €3–5 per train-km before the federal subsidy, more for heavy trains), truck cost and toll (about €1.6–2.2 per truck-km including the CO2 toll), payload per wagon, empty return runs, contribution margin, take-or-pay, escalation clauses, liability limits under HGB and CIM.
game.bigGame: Takes demand from the shipper, forwarder and intermodal operator games, cost rates from the managing director's company and path prices from track-access-sales. Gives contracts (trains per week, service levels) to the production planner, the dispatcher and the yard master, and revenue to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Freight train driver
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking, or a personnel service provider that hires drivers out to EVUs
roles.summary: Drives freight trains of up to 740 m and usually 1,000–2,500 t (heavy ore and coal trains up to about 6,000 t with two locomotives) over the main lines, often at night and across borders. Checks the locomotive and the brake slip (Bremszettel) before departure, drives to the signals and the timetable, and deals with faults alone out on the line.
decisions: Accept the train after checking the brake slip and the brake test, or refuse it
Check that the brake percentage (Bremshundertstel) reaches the minimum in the timetable, and run slower as the rules require if it does not
Choose when to brake and when to coast with a heavy train on a gradient, using the electric brake as far as allowed
React to a restrictive signal, a PZB enforcement or an ETCS intervention, and report every enforced braking
Stop and inspect after a hot-box alarm from the signaller or an unusual noise, and agree with the signaller whether and how fast the train may continue
Tell the dispatcher in time when the working time will run out before the crew change
Secure a stopped train on a gradient with hand brakes when the rules require it
effects: Safe and punctual running keeps the path; a missed path can cost hours waiting for the next one
Energy-aware driving cuts the traction energy bill by 10–20 %
A signal passed at danger (SPAD) or a runaway can cause collisions and derailments
Lateness passes on to the yard, the terminal and the customer
resources: A locomotive of 5.6–6.4 MW (e.g. class 185, 187 or 193 Vectron) with PZB, LZB or ETCS on board
The timetable (Buchfahrplan or EBuLa), the brake slip and the list of temporary speed restrictions (La)
GSM-R radio to the signaller and the company's dispatch
A shift of up to about 12 hours under the tariff, with breaks
limits: Train driver licence (Fahrerlaubnis, issued by the EBA) and the company's certificate (Zusatzbescheinigung) under the Triebfahrzeugführerscheinverordnung (TfV, Directive 2007/59/EC): category B, with route knowledge (Streckenkunde) and vehicle knowledge

EBO (freight trains mostly 100 km/h, some 120 km/h), the Signalbuch (Ril 301, based on the ESO), Ril 408 (running trains and shunting), Ril 915 (operating and testing brakes), Ril 492 (driving traction units), or a private EVU's equivalent rules
Working Hours Act (ArbZG) and the GDL/EVG tariff (shift length, rest at home and away from home); Directive 2005/47/EC for cross-border drivers (at most 9 hours of driving in a day shift, 8 at night)
Medical fitness checked every 3 years and every year from age 55; psychological aptitude test at entry (TfV)
Criminal law: §315a StGB (endangering rail traffic by driving unfit or in gross breach of duty), §§222 and 229 StGB (negligent homicide and injury)
risks: Criminal and disciplinary consequences after a SPAD or an accident; certificate suspended
Trauma after collisions with people (suicides, trespassers), with care by railway psychologists
Night and weekend shifts, nights away from home, irregular rosters
Injury when walking along the train on the track
Job loss when the company loses contracts, although drivers are in high demand

career.entry: Three-year apprenticeship as Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst (Lokführer und Transport), or 9–12 months of lateral-entry training with a recognised training provider; licence exam with an EBA-recognised examiner; at least 20 years old
career.chances: €3,300–4,300 gross a month plus allowances for nights, Sundays and overnight stays (about €45–60k a year); private EVUs often pay more because drivers are scarce; instructor or dispatcher posts pay similar or slightly more

kpis: Handovers to the yard and the customer on time
roles.timescale: seconds to a shift

game.title: The 740-metre train
game.loop: First the player reads the brake slip of a 1,900 t train and works out whether its brake percentage reaches the minimum given in the timetable; if it does not, they look up the lower permitted speed. Then they drive a 40 km section with gradients, temporary speed restrictions and signals. They must brake early, because the air brake takes many seconds to act along a 740 m train (in brake position G up to about 30 s to full force), and must stop in a passing loop at the exit signal, clear of the fouling point, while an ICE overtakes. The shift clock runs all the time: the train must reach the crew change before the working time ends.
game.win: Arrive at the crew change within the path and the working time, without a PZB enforcement, a SPAD or overrunning the loop; the score adds punctuality and energy. A SPAD ends the round and in career mode suspends the certificate until retraining. Running out of working time on the line strands the train, and the company pays a relief driver by taxi.
game.knowledge: Brake percentage and brake positions G and P, train length versus the usable length of a track, signal aspects (H/V, Hl, Ks, Zs 1 substitute signal), PZB monitoring with 1000/500/2000 Hz, working-time limits, energy-saving driving.
game.bigGame: Takes a train, a path and a shift from the production dispatcher and the timetable planner, and signals from the signaller games. Gives delays, energy use and incidents to the dispatcher, the yard master and the managing director, and a driving record to career mode.

roles.name: Locomotive, crew and wagon dispatcher
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (dispatch or transport control centre)
roles.summary: Works in the dispatch centre (Disposition, Transportsteuerung) of a freight EVU and matches locomotives, drivers and wagons to the day's trains: who drives what from where, which locomotive is due for maintenance, which customer gets which empty wagons. Decides what to do when a train is four hours late or a driver calls in sick.
decisions: Assign locomotives to trains, taking train protection (PZB, LZB, ETCS), voltage systems and maintenance due dates into account
Assign drivers who have the route and vehicle knowledge and enough working time left
Order an ad-hoc path (Gelegenheitsverkehr) from DB InfraGO for an extra, late or rerouted train
Hire a driver from a personnel service provider, or a locomotive from another EVU
Cancel, merge or hold back a train, and tell customer service which customers are hit
Send empty wagons to the customer who needs them most
Send drivers to their relief point by train or taxi, or book them a hotel
effects: Good dispatching keeps the trains running with few spare locomotives and drivers
Breaches of working time bring fines and union complaints
Hired staff and taxis cost money; cancelled trains cost penalties and customers
Postponed locomotive maintenance raises the risk of failures
resources: A pool of 20–200 locomotives and 50–500 drivers (split by region in a large EVU)
Circulation and crew dispatch software, and DB InfraGO's path ordering portal
Authority to spend up to a few thousand euros per case on hires and taxis
Round-the-clock shifts of 2–10 dispatchers
limits: Working Hours Act (ArbZG) and the GDL/EVG tariff on shift length and rest
Route knowledge (Streckenkunde) and vehicle knowledge of each driver (TfV)
Locomotive maintenance intervals set by the entity in charge of maintenance (ECM, Regulation (EU) 2019/779)
ERegG and DB InfraGO's network statement (Schienennetz-Nutzungsbedingungen, SNB) for ad-hoc paths
Train protection and voltage compatibility of each locomotive with the route
risks: Stress from constant disruptions; shift work
Blamed for cancelled trains and overtime costs
Little personal legal liability, but knowingly ignoring rest times leads to disciplinary action and fines

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst or as freight forwarder, or experience as a train driver; internal training of a few months
career.chances: €3,500–5,000 a month (€45–65k a year); head of dispatch €70–90k

kpis: Locomotive and driver productivity (hours driven per shift)
roles.timescale: minutes to a day

game.title: 24 hours at the dispatch desk
game.loop: The player sees a day of 15–30 freight trains on a Gantt board, with locomotives, drivers (home base, route knowledge, hours left) and wagon groups. Events arrive in compressed time: a train four hours late from the border, a driver off sick, a locomotive failing its ETCS check, a customer asking for an extra train. The player swaps, hires, orders paths, cancels or sends drivers by taxi, and the operations engine plays out the consequences.
game.win: Run as many trains as possible at the lowest extra cost and without a working-time breach in a 20-minute session (one day). Cancelled trains, breaches and missed connections lower the score; in career mode a breach brings a formal warning, and repeated breaches cost the job.
game.knowledge: Working-time rules, route and vehicle knowledge, locomotive compatibility (voltage, train protection), lead times for ordering paths, the cost of each alternative.
game.bigGame: Takes the yearly plan from the production planner, contracts from sales, locomotives from the fleet and workshop games, and paths from track-access-sales. Gives trains with drivers to the train driver game, arrival times to the yard, terminal and customer service games, and costs to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Shunter and shunting locomotive driver
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (or a siding owner's or terminal's shunting service)
roles.summary: Moves wagons in yards, terminals and sidings: couples and uncouples them, connects brake hoses, gives hand signals or radio commands, sets hand-operated points and secures wagons against rolling away. The shunting locomotive driver drives the locomotive, often by radio remote control. It is one of the most dangerous jobs on the railway.
decisions: Plan the moves that sort the wagons into the order the train needs
Give the commands (shunting signals Ra 1 to Ra 5, radio phrases) to the locomotive driver
Decide when it is safe to step between the wagons to couple them
Secure standing wagons with hand brakes or skids (Hemmschuhe)
Refuse a move when visibility, the track or a wagon is unsafe
Check that the points are set and the route is clear, and get the signaller's consent, before a move
Never kick (Ra 4) or hump wagons with RID label 15, and handle those with label 13 with care
At the hump crest, uncouple the cuts as the humping list says (Entkuppler)
effects: Efficient sorting makes outbound trains ready on time
A wagon left unsecured can run away onto the main line
Hard coupling damages wagons and loads (costs, leaks of dangerous goods)
Accidents injure or kill shunters
resources: A shunting locomotive (e.g. class 261 Gravita, 294, 363 or a hybrid), radio, hand lamp, skids
A team of 2–3 per shift (locomotive driver and 1–2 shunters)
The shunting plan for the shift
limits: EBO, Ril 408 (shunting), Signalbuch (Ril 301: Ra and Sh signals), Ril 915 (brake tests)
Shunting at no more than 25 km/h, and at walking pace when approaching vehicles to couple
Train driver licence and certificate category A for shunting locomotive drivers (TfV)
RID: shunting labels 13 (shunt with care) and 15 (do not hump or kick), protective distances
Occupational safety: Arbeitsschutzgesetz, DGUV rules, protective equipment
Working Hours Act and EVG/GDL tariffs
risks: Crushing between the buffers, falls from the footstep, being run over; fatal accidents happen every year
Night shifts in all weather
Disciplinary action and criminal investigation after accidents
Strain on joints and back

career.entry: Training of 3–6 months as shunter (Rangierbegleiter), open to lateral entrants, or part of the apprenticeship Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst; shunting locomotive driver with a category A licence
career.chances: €2,800–3,500 gross a month plus shift allowances (about €35–45k a year); as shunting locomotive driver up to about €4,000

roles.timescale: seconds to a shift

game.title: Shunting puzzle
game.loop: On a small yard of the EBL layout with three sidings of limited length (a puzzle of the Inglenook kind), the player must form an outbound train of five wagons in a given order, with model wagons tracked by their tags or virtual ones. Every move is a command to the locomotive (Ra 1 move away, Ra 2 come here, Ra 3 close up, Ra 5 stop), and every coupling needs the right steps: stop, wait for standstill, couple, connect the hose, open the cocks, release the hand brake. Hazards appear: a wagon with RID label 15, a wagon left without a hand brake on a gradient, a colleague in the track.
game.win: Form the train in the fewest moves within the time and without a safety violation. A violation (stepping in while wagons move, a wagon left unsecured, a label ignored) costs heavily, and a serious one ends the round with an accident report. In career mode safe rounds unlock the shunting locomotive licence and then the train driver training.
game.knowledge: Shunting signals and radio phrases, the coupling procedure, the rules for securing wagons, RID shunting labels, speed limits for shunting.
game.bigGame: Takes the shunting plan from the yard master or the siding owner. Gives formed trains, with the time they are ready, to the wagon inspector, the train driver and the dispatcher, and incidents to the safety manager.

roles.name: Carriage and wagon inspector
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking
roles.summary: Inspects freight trains before departure and at handovers between EVUs (wagentechnische Untersuchung, WTU): wheels, springs, brakes, couplings, loads and load securing, and labels, and performs the brake test. Decides whether a wagon may run, may run only to the workshop, or must stay.
decisions: Pass a wagon, or label it as damaged under GCU Annex 9 and set it aside
Decide under the damage catalogue whether a damaged wagon may run on loaded, must be unloaded, may run empty to the workshop or must be repaired on site
Perform the full or the simplified brake test and sign the brake slip
Set the brake positions (G/P, empty/loaded) and compute the brake percentage
Reject a load whose securing does not meet the UIC Loading Guidelines
Report leaks of dangerous goods or wrong labelling
effects: Defects that are found prevent derailments, hot axle boxes and lost loads
Wagons set aside delay or shorten the train and annoy the customer
A wrong brake percentage can leave the train unable to stop in time
The findings feed the wagon keeper's maintenance (ECM)
resources: 30–60 minutes for a train of 20–35 wagons
Hand tools, a lamp, a gauge for wheel flats, the brake test equipment
Damage labels and the damage catalogue; a tablet with the wagon data
limits: GCU (General Contract of Use for Wagons), Annex 9: technical transfer inspection, with its damage catalogue and labels
Ril 915 (brake tests), the brake rules of the EBO, UIC Loading Guidelines (Verladerichtlinien)
RID (labels, placards, checks of tank wagons)
TSI WAG and the keeper's maintenance plan as ECM (Regulation (EU) 2019/779)
Working Hours Act
risks: Being struck by moving trains while walking along the tracks
Criminal liability for negligence after an accident caused by an overlooked defect
Night work and weather; pressure from production to pass trains

career.entry: Apprenticeship in a metal or mechatronic trade (e.g. Mechatroniker/in, Industriemechaniker/in) plus 6–9 months of training as Wagenmeister with an exam; private EVUs often use shorter Wagenprüfer training for the WTU
career.chances: €3,200–4,000 gross a month plus shift allowances (about €40–50k a year)

kpis: Defects found (and those found later by others)
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Fit to run?
game.loop: A train of 22 wagons must leave in 40 game minutes. The player walks along it, on screen or in AR along model wagons with deck cards, inspects wheels, springs, couplings, brakes, loads and labels, and labels the defects. Then they set the brake positions, compute the brake percentage from the brake weights and decide which wagons run, which run empty to the workshop and which stay.
game.win: Find every safety-critical defect, set no sound wagon aside, and have the train ready before its path; safety weighs far more than speed in the score. A missed critical defect plays out later in the big game as a hot-box stop or a derailment, and in career mode it triggers an investigation.
game.knowledge: Damage catalogue and wagon types (Sgns, Sggrss, Lgns, Shimmns, tank and flat wagons), brake weights, brake percentage and the minimum for the line, load securing, RID labels and placards.
game.bigGame: Takes formed trains from the shunter and the yard master, and loaded wagons from the loading supervisor. Gives a ready train with its brake slip to the train driver, damaged wagons to the keeper's ECM and the workshop games, and delays to the dispatcher.

roles.name: Marshalling yard production manager
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (e.g. DB Cargo) working in a marshalling yard (Zugbildungsanlage) that DB InfraGO owns as a service facility, such as Maschen, Seelze or Köln-Gremberg
roles.summary: Leads a shift in a marshalling yard, where single wagons from many trains are sorted into new trains. Decides the humping order, the use of the classification tracks, and which outbound trains are formed when and with which staff, so that wagons make their connections in the single-wagonload network.
decisions: Set the order in which arriving trains are humped
Allocate destinations to classification tracks; merge or split groups
Close an outbound train at its cut-off, or hold it for a late connection
Deploy shunters, wagon inspectors and shunting locomotives across the shift
Order overtime or call in reserve staff
Ask the network to hold trains back, or divert wagons to another yard, when this one is full
effects: Wagon connections (Anschlusssicherung) decide the transit time of thousands of wagons
A full yard backs arriving trains up onto the main line
Late outbound trains lose their paths and reach the customers late
Overtime costs money and wears out the team
resources: A large yard handles one to several thousand wagons a day (Maschen, the largest in Germany, the most) on 30 to over 60 classification tracks
A shift of 20–80 staff and 3–10 shunting locomotives
Train lists and wagon data (destinations, RID, weights)
limits: Ril 408 (shunting and train preparation), Ril 915 (brake tests), the local yard instructions
Lengths of the classification and departure tracks, maximum train length of 740 m, weight limits of the locomotive and the line
RID: shunting labels 13 and 15, protective distances in trains (RID 7.5.3)
Working Hours Act, tariffs, co-determination of the works council on rosters (BetrVG §87)
DB InfraGO's conditions of use for service facilities (Nutzungsbedingungen Serviceeinrichtungen, NBS) under the ERegG
risks: Responsibility for accidents in the yard
Shift work; heavy stress when trains back up
Cost cuts and yard closures in the single-wagonload network

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst and years as shunter or dispatcher, or a degree in transport engineering; internal leadership training
career.chances: €4,500–6,500 a month (about €55–80k a year)

roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Night shift in the marshalling yard
game.loop: Twelve trains arrive in the night, each a list of wagons with destinations. The yard has 20 classification tracks of limited length and 10 outbound trains with cut-off times. The player orders the humping, assigns destinations to tracks, decides which outbound trains wait for late connections, and moves staff between the hump, the inspections and the departure tracks. The yard runs in compressed time while full tracks, late arrivals and a broken retarder test the plan.
game.win: Get as many wagons as possible onto their connections and the outbound trains away on time in a shift of 20–30 minutes. A yard so full that trains back up onto the main line ends the round. In career mode a strong record leads to production management.
game.knowledge: Logic of the single-wagonload network, track capacity in metres, limits on train length and weight, RID protective distances, staff deployment.
game.bigGame: Takes arriving trains from the train driver and dispatcher games and wagons booked by sales and customer service. Gives formed trains to the inspector and driver games, a humping programme to the hump operator, and dwell times to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Hump operator
roles.organisation: infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, which owns and operates the marshalling yards as service facilities); in some yards and private systems the freight EVU's own staff
roles.summary: Works the hump interlocking (Ablaufstellwerk) of a marshalling yard: wagons roll down the hump into the classification tracks, the points are set for each cut and the retarders (Gleisbremsen) brake it so that it reaches its track and couples gently. In modern yards a process computer sets the points and controls the retarders; the operator watches and steps in.
decisions: Set or confirm the pushing speed of the hump locomotive
Override the computer's retarder setting for a cut, or brake it by hand when the automation fails
Stop humping when a cut runs wrong, stalls or catches up with the one ahead
Refuse to hump wagons with RID label 15 and have them moved by locomotive
Call a shunting team to close gaps on the classification tracks (Beidrücken)
Report faults of retarders and points to the maintenance dispatcher
effects: Too fast: impacts damage wagons and loads and can make dangerous goods leak
Too slow: gaps that need extra shunting, or wagons that stop in the points
A misrouted cut spoils the formation of an outbound train
The hump's rate sets the capacity of the whole yard
resources: A hump interlocking with process control (e.g. at Maschen, Seelze, Nürnberg), retarders, points and track occupancy detection
A humping rate of up to about 200 wagons an hour at peak
Radio to the hump locomotive and the shunters
limits: Ril 408 and the local yard instructions (örtliche Richtlinien)
Coupling speed of at most about 1.5 m/s (about 5 km/h), lower under the local rules for wagons with RID label 13
RID label 15: do not hump or kick
EBO, Working Hours Act, DB InfraGO tariff (EVG)
risks: Damage claims and investigations after collisions or leaks
Monotony broken by sudden stress; shift work
Fewer posts as yards close and automation grows

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst (Fahrweg) at DB InfraGO, then local qualification for the hump interlocking
career.chances: €3,300–4,200 a month plus shift allowances (EVG tariff at DB InfraGO)

roles.timescale: seconds to minutes

game.title: Over the hump
game.loop: The process computer has failed and the player humps by hand. Cuts of 1–4 wagons roll off the hump one after another: an empty flat wagon, a loaded tank wagon, a covered wagon in a head wind, each with its own rolling resistance. The player sets the points and the exit speed at two retarders so that each cut reaches the wagons already on its track and couples at no more than 1.5 m/s. Fog, frost and a failed retarder raise the difficulty, and wagons with RID label 15 must be stopped and taken round by locomotive.
game.win: Hump a train of 40–60 wagons in time with no impact above the limit, no misrouted cut and few gaps. A hard impact on a tank wagon ends the round with an incident report. In career mode the score counts towards promotion to an electronic interlocking.
game.knowledge: Rolling resistance and gradients (the basic physics of a rolling wagon), coupling speed limits, RID shunting labels, the logic of points and retarders.
