game.bigGame: Takes the humping programme from the yard master and loaded wagons from the loading supervisor's game (a badly secured load can shift in a hard impact). Gives sorted tracks, damage and delays back to the yard master, and faults to the maintenance dispatcher.

roles.name: Combined-transport terminal manager
roles.organisation: terminal operator (e.g. DUSS, Contargo, duisport or a port terminal)
roles.summary: Runs a combined-transport terminal (KV-Terminal) where containers, swap bodies and semi-trailers move between trains, trucks and barges. Sets the slots, opening hours, prices, staffing and investments, and as operator of a service facility must give all railway undertakings and operators fair access.
decisions: Allocate train slots on the loading tracks across the week
Set opening hours and shift plans
Set prices per lift and storage fees, including the free storage time
Invest in a crane, reach stackers or longer tracks, with federal funding
Decide on access requests from a new operator under the conditions of use, and justify any refusal
Clear a backlog: extra shifts, refusing trains, or pushing containers out
effects: Slots and crane capacity decide whether trains leave on time
High yard occupancy slows every move and blocks deliveries
Funded investments extend capacity for decades
Unfair access decisions can be challenged at BNetzA
resources: 2–8 loading tracks of up to 700 m, 1–4 gantry cranes (€5–10 million each), several reach stackers (€0.5–0.8 million each)
20–150 staff; 50,000–500,000 lifts a year
Federal funding for private terminals covering up to 80 % of eligible investment costs
An operating budget of €5–30 million a year
limits: ERegG on service facilities and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/2177 on access to them; the terminal's conditions of use (Nutzungsbedingungen für Serviceeinrichtungen), supervised by BNetzA
Conditions of the federal funding guideline for combined-transport terminals: open access and minimum use over the funding period
Occupational safety: DGUV rules on cranes, Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV)
RID and ADR for dangerous goods in storage; emission and noise permits (BImSchG)
Customs rules for temporary storage (Union Customs Code)
risks: Responsibility for occupational accidents
Losses when volumes fall; repayment of funding when its conditions are breached
Pressure from operators, forwarders and neighbours (noise, trucks)

career.entry: Degree in logistics, transport engineering or business; years in terminal operations or forwarding
career.chances: €60–90k a year at a small terminal, €90–130k at a large one

kpis: Lifts per year and per crane hour
Train dwell time and slot adherence
roles.timescale: days to years

game.title: Terminal week
game.loop: The player plans a week at a terminal on the ARail layout: assigns train slots to the operators' requests, sets the shift plans and the storage fee, and then watches the terminal simulation run the week in fast motion. Late trains bunch, a crane fails, a strike in the port fills the yard. Between days the player can add shifts, refuse trains or change fees, and each quarter decides on an investment, with or without funding.
game.win: Keep trains within their slots, trucks under 45 minutes in the terminal and the yard below 85 % occupancy while covering costs. A yard that overflows, so that no more moves are possible, ends the round early. In career mode good results lead to a larger terminal or to the operator.
game.knowledge: Capacity calculation (lifts per hour times hours), yard occupancy and dwell time, cost per lift, open access rules, funding conditions.
game.bigGame: Takes trains from the intermodal operator and the port railway, and trucks from the forwarders and truck drivers. Gives slots to the dispatcher and the operator, workload to the terminal dispatcher and the crane operator, and costs and revenue to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Terminal dispatcher
roles.organisation: terminal operator
roles.summary: Plans the shift in a combined-transport terminal: which unit goes onto which wagon and where (the loading plan), the order of the crane moves, the truck slots and the yard positions, so that trains leave full and on time and trucks are served quickly.
decisions: Draw up the loading plan: which unit goes on which wagon and position, within the weight and length limits
Sequence the crane moves to avoid reshuffles
Choose yard positions for arriving units according to when they will be picked up
Accept or reject units that arrive after the cut-off or without documents
Place dangerous goods units according to the rules
Assign cranes and reach stackers to trains, trucks and barges
effects: A good plan saves crane moves and fills the train
Overweight or wrongly placed units endanger the train and are rejected by the wagon inspector
Bad yard positions cause reshuffles and long waits for trucks
Units left behind miss the train and the customer's deadline
resources: Terminal operating system (TOS) with booking data from operators and forwarders
1–4 cranes, reach stackers and a crew per shift
A shift of 8 hours with 2–6 trains to work
limits: Load limit grids of the wagons by line category (e.g. D4), length and position rules of the wagon types
UIC Loading Guidelines and the codification of intermodal units and lines (UIC leaflet 596-6, profile codes P and C)
RID and ADR placement and segregation of dangerous goods
Customs status of units (Union Customs Code)
Working Hours Act; crane safety rules
risks: Stress at peaks; shift work
Blamed for units left behind
Responsibility for overloading if the plan was wrong

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Kaufmann/-frau für Spedition und Logistikdienstleistung, Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik or Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst
career.chances: €3,200–4,500 a month (about €40–55k a year)

roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Load plan
game.loop: A train of Sgns, Sggrss and Lgns wagons stands on the loading track, and 30 units wait in the yard and on trucks, each with a size, weight, destination and in some cases dangerous goods. The player places each unit on a wagon bay: 40 ft only on the allowed bays, weight within the limits per wagon and line category, dangerous goods kept apart. Then the ARail terminal runs the crane moves: blocked stacks cost reshuffles, and trucks queue at the gate.
game.win: Load as many units as possible within all limits before the train's departure; the score is units loaded minus crane moves and truck waiting time. An overloaded wagon or a wrongly placed dangerous good is caught by the wagon inspector as a penalty, or becomes an incident if it is missed.
game.knowledge: Wagon types and their bays, payloads and line categories, container sizes (20, 40 and 45 ft, high cube), segregation of dangerous goods, stacking rules.
game.bigGame: Takes trains from the intermodal operator and the port railway, trucks from the forwarders and truck drivers, and customs holds from the customs officer. Gives the move list to the crane operator and loaded trains to the wagon inspector and the dispatcher.

roles.name: Crane operator
roles.organisation: terminal operator
roles.summary: Drives the gantry crane or reach stacker of a terminal, lifting containers, swap bodies and trailers between wagons, trucks, barges and the yard quickly and precisely. Stops when wind, people in the danger zone or a lock that has not released make a lift unsafe.
decisions: Follow the TOS move sequence, or ask the dispatcher to swap a move when a unit is blocked or a truck is waiting
Stop a lift when a truck chassis or a wagon rises with the unit because a twist lock or a lockable spigot was not released
Stop work when the wind exceeds the crane's limit
Refuse a lift while a person is in the danger zone
Report an overweight or damaged unit
Choose the path that keeps sway and time low
effects: Moves per hour set the terminal's capacity
Damaged units or wagons cost money and can leak dangerous goods
A lifted chassis or wagon, or a dropped unit, can kill
resources: A gantry crane with a spreader (safe working load about 40 t) or a reach stacker
Radio and a TOS screen in the cab
A shift of 8 hours with breaks
limits: DGUV regulation 52 (cranes) and DGUV principle 309-003 (selection, instruction and certification of crane operators); DGUV principle 308-001 for reach stackers
Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV), the crane's wind limit and safe working load
Occupational medical check for driving, control and monitoring work (formerly G 25)
Working Hours Act; the terminal's rules for people and trucks in the crane area
risks: Fatal accidents in the crane area; criminal investigation afterwards
Back and neck strain from the cab position; shift work
Fewer posts as cranes are automated or remote-controlled

career.entry: Usually a trade apprenticeship plus crane operator training of several weeks with a certificate under DGUV principle 309-003; many lateral entrants
career.chances: €3,000–3,800 a month plus shift allowances

kpis: Lifts per hour (20–30 for a gantry crane)
roles.timescale: seconds to minutes

game.title: Twenty lifts an hour
game.loop: The player drives the gantry crane of the ARail terminal through a move list, on screen or in AR over the lab's model crane: hoist, trolley and gantry, with a swinging spreader that must settle before it lands. Random events demand a stop: a truck driver walks into the danger zone, a truck chassis rises with its container because a twist lock was left closed, a gust pushes the wind gauge over the limit.
game.win: Work the move list in time with no damage and no safety violation; lifts per hour make the score. A lift over a person or a lifted chassis ends the round with an accident report, and in career mode leads to retraining or dismissal.
game.knowledge: Crane controls and sway, signals and radio, the danger zone, wind limits, twist locks and spigots, safe working load.
game.bigGame: Takes the move list from the terminal dispatcher. Gives completed moves, damage and delays back to the terminal, truck turnaround times to the truck driver game, and the trains' departure times to the dispatcher.

roles.name: Freight forwarder
roles.organisation: forwarding company (Spedition)
roles.summary: Organises transport for customers without owning the trains. Chooses the mode (truck, combined transport, rail wagon, barge), books capacity with intermodal operators and hauliers, prepares the documents and deals with problems on the way. Decides every day whether a load goes by rail or by road.
decisions: Choose truck or combined transport for each order
Book slots on intermodal trains and plan the trucks for pre- and on-carriage
Re-route loads during a rail strike or a line closure
Negotiate prices with hauliers and operators
Prepare the consignment notes (CMR, CIM) and customs documents (T1 transit)
Decide whether to re-book a missed train or switch to a truck
effects: Each container moved by rail saves truck-km and CO2 on the motorway
Reliable bookings fill intermodal trains; cancellations leave slots empty
Switching modes during disruptions costs money and customers
resources: A desk with 30–100 orders a day and a pool of hauliers (own or subcontracted trucks)
Budget per order, with a margin of a few percent
Booking portals of the intermodal operators; a transport management system
limits: HGB §§453 ff (forwarding contract) and §§407 ff (freight contract), ADSp 2017
CMR convention for international road transport, CIM for rail
Truck toll (LKW-Maut with CO2 surcharge since December 2023) and EU driving and rest times (Regulation (EC) 561/2006)
Benefits of combined transport: 44 t gross weight in pre- and on-carriage (StVZO §34), exemption from the Sunday driving ban (StVO §30(3)), motor vehicle tax exemption (KraftStG)
Customs (Union Customs Code, NCTS transit) and ADR/RID for dangerous goods
risks: Liability for damage and delay within the limits of ADSp and HGB
Losing customers; thin margins
Stress from daily disruptions

career.entry: Three-year apprenticeship as Kaufmann/-frau für Spedition und Logistikdienstleistung, or a degree in logistics
career.chances: €2,800–4,500 a month; branch manager €70–100k a year

roles.timescale: hours to days

game.title: Rail or road?
game.loop: Each game day brings 10–20 orders (origin, destination, weight, deadline, dangerous goods, customs status). The player books each one on a truck or on an intermodal train with pre- and on-carriage, weighing price, transit time, cut-off times and CO2. During the week disruptions hit: a strike, a closed line, a late train, a shortage of truck drivers. The player re-books or lets the shipment ride.
game.win: Deliver every order by its deadline with the highest margin over a week (15–20 minutes), with a bonus for rail share and CO2 saved. Missed deadlines cost penalties and customers; in career mode a strong week leads to rail sales or to an intermodal operator.
game.knowledge: Cost of truck and rail (toll, the 44 t rule, the Sunday ban exemption), cut-off and availability times, documents, liability limits.
game.bigGame: Takes prices and slots from the intermodal operator and from sales, and delays from the disruptions. Gives bookings (units and trucks) to the terminal and truck driver games, and demand to the operator and the economics simulator.

roles.name: Shipper's logistics manager
roles.organisation: shipper (industrial company in e.g. chemicals, steel, automotive or building materials)
roles.summary: Decides how the company's raw materials and products move: by rail, road or waterway, with which carriers, and how much stock to hold. Large shippers in chemicals, steel and cars are the backbone of German rail freight, and their choices set volumes for years.
decisions: Put the transport volumes out to tender and choose the carriers
Set modal split targets (e.g. a rail share for the CO2 goals)
Set safety stocks against transport failures
Keep, extend or close the plant's siding
Lease wagons from a keeper, or use the carrier's
Switch to backup modes during a strike or low water on the Rhine
effects: Volumes and contract length decide which EVU invests in locomotives and staff
Closing the siding puts thousands of trucks a year onto the roads
Too little stock stops the plant when trains fail
The rail share shows up in the company's greenhouse gas reporting
resources: A logistics budget of €10–500 million a year
A team of planners and buyers; plant sidings and loading equipment
Authority over carriers and modes within company policy
limits: HGB freight law and the contracts; the GCU for wagons; the consignor's duties for loading and dangerous goods (HGB §§412 and 414, RID/ADR, GGVSEB)
Greenhouse gas reporting (CSRD where it applies, scope 3 of the GHG Protocol)
Siding rules of the Land (BOA or EBOA) and the siding contract (Infrastrukturanschlussvertrag) with DB InfraGO
Störfall-Verordnung (Seveso III) for chemical plants
risks: Blamed for plant stoppages caused by logistics; job loss
Fines for the company as consignor for breaches of dangerous goods rules (GGVSEB)
Public criticism when freight moves to the roads

career.entry: Degree in logistics, industrial engineering or business; years in purchasing or supply chain
career.chances: €80–150k a year; head of logistics in a large group over €150k

roles.timescale: weeks to years

game.title: Keep the plant running
game.loop: The player runs the logistics of a chemical plant for one year in monthly turns: tenders the inbound and outbound flows (block trains, single wagons, trucks, barges), sets safety stocks and decides on the siding. Real-world events hit: low water on the Rhine (as in 2018 and 2022), a rail strike, a line closed for several weeks, a price spike. The simulation answers with costs, CO2 and the days the plant had to cut production.
game.win: Keep the plant supplied at the lowest total cost while meeting a CO2 target; one round is a year (about 20 minutes). A plant stoppage is a heavy loss, and in career mode two stoppages cost the job.
game.knowledge: Costs and capacities of the modes, stock and safety-stock logic, contract terms, CO2 per mode (rail emits roughly a fifth of road per tonne-km), the economics of a siding.
game.bigGame: Gives tenders and volumes to sales, the forwarder and the intermodal operator, loading orders to the loading supervisor and siding decisions to the siding owner; takes prices and reliability back. In the economics simulator it is the demand side.

roles.name: Siding owner (operations manager of a private siding)
roles.organisation: industrial company with a private siding (Anschlussbahn); often a side duty of the plant's logistics or technical manager
roles.summary: Is responsible, as operations manager (Betriebsleiter), for a company's private siding under the Land's railway supervision: its tracks, points and level crossings and the shunting on it. Prepares the decision whether the siding is maintained, extended with federal funding, or closed.
decisions: Plan inspections and maintenance of tracks, points and crossings
Apply to the EBA for federal siding funding to build, extend or reactivate the siding
Shunt with own staff and locomotive, or order the EVU's last-mile service
Close a track or limit the speed after a defect
Recommend to management whether to keep or close the siding
Issue the siding's operating instructions and appoint and instruct the shunting staff
effects: A siding in good condition keeps freight on rail (each wagon replaces 2–3 trucks)
Neglected tracks lead to derailments inside the plant
Closure ends rail access for good, and reactivation is expensive
resources: 1–20 km of track, some points, a shunting locomotive or a contract with an EVU
A maintenance budget of €50k–1 million a year
Federal siding funding (Gleisanschlussförderung) of up to 50 % of eligible investment
A small team of 2–20 staff
limits: Land law on sidings: the BOA or EBOA under the Land's railway act, supervised by the state railway authority (Landeseisenbahnaufsicht, or the EBA where a Land has delegated it); the EBO applies only to public railways
VDV-Schrift 600 (track guidelines for non-federal railways) for track maintenance
Siding contract (Infrastrukturanschlussvertrag) with DB InfraGO
Conditions of the federal siding funding guideline (Gleisanschlussförderrichtlinie), with a duty to keep the traffic for the funding period
RID and the Störfall-Verordnung on chemical sites
risks: Personal responsibility as Betriebsleiter after accidents
Investments refused by management; closure of the siding ends the role
On-call duty

career.entry: Engineering degree, or master craftsman (Meister) with railway experience; appointment as Betriebsleiter confirmed by the state railway authority after proof of qualification
career.chances: €55–85k a year

roles.timescale: days to years

game.title: Keep the siding
game.loop: Five budget years for a plant siding with 3 km of track, 8 points and a level crossing, built from ARail's infrastructure assets with condition and faults. Each year the player inspects, repairs or renews, applies for funding (with deadlines and a share of own funds) and chooses the shunting model. Traffic and faults run in between, and a derailment or a closed point stops wagons.
game.win: Keep the siding available and safe within the budget for five years; the score is wagons handled per euro. A derailment caused by ignored defects, or closure of the siding by the state authority after an inspection, ends the round, and in career mode bars the player from the Betriebsleiter role for a while.
game.knowledge: Siding law (BOA/EBOA, state supervision), inspection intervals, condition and failures of track and points, funding rules, cost per wagon compared with a truck.
game.bigGame: Takes volumes and investment decisions from the shipper, funding from the federal funding officer and last-mile service from the EVU. Gives availability (wagons that can be loaded) to sales, customer service, the dispatcher and the shipper.

roles.name: Dangerous goods safety adviser
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking, shipper, terminal or wagon keeper (employee or external adviser)
roles.summary: Every company that carries, loads, fills, packs or ships dangerous goods must appoint a dangerous goods safety adviser (Gefahrgutbeauftragte/r), with exemptions for small quantities. The adviser monitors compliance with RID and GGVSEB, checks procedures and training, writes the annual report and the accident reports, and advises management, which stays responsible and decides.
decisions: Check procedures for loading, labelling, documents and train formation, and record the deficiencies
Recommend stopping a consignment with wrong documents, missing labels or a leak, or stop it where management has delegated that authority
Define and check the training of all staff involved (RID 1.3)
Write an accident report after every serious incident (RID 1.8.3.6) and propose measures
Advise on segregation and protective distances in trains (RID 7.5.3)
Write the annual report to management (GbV) within half a year after the business year
effects: Correct procedures prevent leaks, fires and explosions
Stopped consignments cost time and customers
Gaps in compliance lead to fines and to accidents
resources: A certificate (IHK) and the right to inspect and advise, without command over operations
Part-time or full-time, depending on the volume of dangerous goods
Budget for documentation and training
limits: RID (1.8.3 safety adviser, 5.3 placards and labels, 5.4 documents, 7.5 loading and protective distances), GGVSEB, Gefahrgutbeauftragtenverordnung (GbV)
ADR and ADN for the road and waterway legs
Störfall-Verordnung for plants; emergency information for fire brigades
risks: Fines (Ordnungswidrigkeiten) for breaches of the adviser's own duties; criminal investigation after accidents
Conflict with production when recommending stops
Exposure during investigations of incidents

career.entry: IHK training and exam (certificate valid for five years), usually after a technical or chemical apprenticeship or degree
career.chances: €50–80k a year as an employee; external advisers charge €80–150 an hour

kpis: Findings in inspections by the authorities
roles.timescale: days to months; minutes in an incident

game.title: Placarded
game.loop: A train of 20 wagons with tank wagons and containers arrives at the yard with its documents. The player compares the documents, the orange plates (hazard identification number over UN number, e.g. 33/1203 for petrol), the labels and each wagon's position in the train, and marks the errors, such as wagons with explosives next to a tank of flammable liquid without the protective distance of 18 m required by RID 7.5.3, or a missing shunting label 13. In the second phase a tank wagon leaks; the player identifies the substance from its plate and gives the fire brigade the right emergency information within minutes, calling the chemical industry's TUIS help if needed.
game.win: Find all breaches with few false alarms in 15 minutes, and give the correct emergency information in the incident. Missed breaches become fines, or accidents in the big game; in career mode they put the certificate in question.
game.knowledge: RID classes, UN numbers and hazard identification numbers (Kemler numbers), labels and placards, shunting labels, segregation and protective distances, transport documents, emergency procedures and TUIS.
game.bigGame: Takes consignments from the shipper, the loading supervisor, the forwarder and the terminal. Gives cleared or stopped units to the terminal and yard games, and incidents to the rescue incident commander and the safety manager.

roles.name: Customs officer
roles.organisation: German customs administration (Zoll): Generalzolldirektion and main customs offices (Hauptzollämter)
roles.summary: Clears and controls goods that cross the EU's external border, including by rail. Container trains from China usually enter the EU in Poland under transit (T1) and are cleared at the destination customs office, e.g. in Duisburg or Hamburg. Checks declarations in ATLAS and NCTS, selects containers for inspection by risk, X-rays or opens them, and enforces duties, sanctions and bans on drugs and weapons. Each check holds up a container or a train.
decisions: Select consignments for a document check, an X-ray or a physical inspection
Release, hold or seize goods
Accept or reject a transit declaration or a guarantee
Check declarations against sanctions lists and dual-use rules
Call in specialists (drug dogs, a chemist) or the police
Impose duties and fines, or open criminal proceedings
effects: Hits against smuggling and sanctions evasion
Each inspection delays a container or wagon by hours or days
Missed checks let contraband through
Fast clearance keeps terminals and trains moving
resources: A team of 5–30 officers at a port or terminal; container X-ray scanners
IT systems ATLAS and NCTS, risk profiles
Sovereign powers (search, seizure) under customs law
limits: Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) 952/2013) with its delegated and implementing acts
Customs Administration Act (ZollVG), Abgabenordnung, Code of Criminal Procedure (StPO)
EU sanctions regulations (e.g. 833/2014), dual-use regulation (EU) 2021/821
Federal civil service law and the working time ordinance for federal civil servants
risks: Confrontation with organised crime; bribery attempts
Disciplinary and criminal liability for misconduct
Shift work; exposure to hazardous goods

career.entry: Civil service: middle grade (two-year training as Zollsekretäranwärter/in, grades A6–A9) or upper grade (three-year dual study as Diplom-Finanzwirt/in at the Federal University of Applied Administrative Sciences, grades A9–A13)
career.chances: Federal civil servant pay of about €3,000–4,700 a month in the middle grade and about €3,700–7,000 in the upper grade; a job for life with a pension; promotion within customs, e.g. to the customs investigation service (Zollfahndung)

roles.timescale: minutes to days

game.title: Risk at the gate
game.loop: A container train from China arrives at a terminal with 40 declarations (consignor, consignee, goods code, weight, route). The player has 6 X-ray slots and 2 physical inspections per shift, and chooses what to check by spotting inconsistencies: a declared weight 20 % off, a goods code that does not fit the shipper, a consignee on a sanctions list. Each check delays the container, and the ARail terminal keeps working around it.
game.win: Find the most contraband and sanctions breaches with the limited checks while keeping the train's units moving; one shift takes 15 minutes. Letting a flagged shipment through is a miss, and holding many clean ones costs the terminal and the forwarders. In career mode a strong hit rate leads to the customs investigation service.
game.knowledge: Customs procedures (transit, release for free circulation), risk indicators, goods codes, the logic of sanctions, documents.
game.bigGame: Takes declarations from the forwarders and shippers, and units from the terminal and the port railway. Gives holds and releases to the terminal dispatcher, and delays to the forwarder and the economics simulator.

roles.name: Port railway dispatcher
roles.organisation: port railway (port authority as infrastructure manager, e.g. Hamburg Port Authority or duisport)
roles.summary: Controls the traffic of a port railway (Hafenbahn) between the main line and the quay terminals. Assigns arrival and departure tracks, lets trains into the terminals within their slots, coordinates the shunting locomotives of many railway undertakings, and keeps the port's rail network from clogging. Hamburg's port railway handles around 200 trains a day.
decisions: Assign arrival and departure tracks to incoming trains
Sequence trains into the terminals by their slots and their actual arrival
Re-plan when a train arrives hours late or a terminal is full
Grant or refuse requests for track use at short notice
Close tracks for works or faults and route around them
Agree handover times with the main-line train dispatcher, and ask for trains to be held back when the port is full
effects: Smooth handovers keep ships loaded and trains on their paths
Congestion backs trains up onto the main line and delays the hinterland
Late decisions leave terminal cranes idle
resources: A network of about 300 km of track (Hamburg) with several arrival yards
The port's rail control and information system, and radio
A team of dispatchers per shift
limits: AEG and EBO (the port railway is a public, non-federal infrastructure manager under state railway supervision)
ERegG: non-discriminatory access, the port railway's network statement and its infrastructure charges
The port railway's own operating rules
Slot agreements with the terminals; Working Hours Act
risks: Responsibility for operational safety in the port network
Stress when ships and trains bunch; shift work
Complaints by railway undertakings to BNetzA about discrimination

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst (Fahrweg) or experience as a signaller; local qualification
career.chances: €3,800–5,500 a month under a public-sector or company tariff

kpis: Waiting time at the port entry
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Feed the quay
game.loop: On a port network of the ARail layout with two arrival groups and three terminals, 12–20 trains arrive in a shift with random delays, and each terminal has slot windows and a limited number of loading tracks. The player assigns arrival tracks, decides who enters which terminal next, sends shunting locomotives, and holds trains at the main-line handover when the port is full. A ship arrives early or a terminal's crane fails, and the plan must change.
game.win: Keep the terminals busy, waiting at the port entry under 60 minutes and no train backed up onto the main line in a 20-minute shift. Gridlock, with no free track left to move to, ends the round. In career mode good shifts lead to network control.
game.knowledge: Track capacity in metres, slot logic, non-discriminatory access, the operating rules of the port network.
game.bigGame: Takes trains from the main line (train dispatcher, freight dispatcher, train driver) and slots from the terminal games. Gives arrivals to the terminals, departures back to the main line, and delays to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Intermodal operator's product manager
roles.organisation: intermodal operator (KV-Operateur, e.g. Kombiverkehr, Hupac or Metrans)
roles.summary: Buys whole trains (traction) from freight railway undertakings and sells their capacity to forwarders unit by unit. Designs the network of intermodal shuttles (which terminals, how many departures, which cut-off and availability times), sets the price per unit, and carries the risk of trains running half empty.
decisions: Open, cut or change a shuttle between two terminals
Set the departures per week and the cut-off and availability times
Buy traction from an EVU and slots from terminals
Set prices per unit and discounts for regular customers
Decide whether to run a train that is only 60 % booked
Re-route trains during a line closure
effects: Each new shuttle gives forwarders a rail option, and good cut-off times win loads from trucks
Low utilisation means losses for the operator
Cancelled trains push forwarders back onto the road
resources: A network of 10–100 shuttles; a train trip costs €10–30k
Trains of 30–40 units, with utilisation targets above 80 %
Federal funding for terminals and the federal subsidy that lowers freight track access charges
limits: Contracts with EVUs (traction), terminals (slots) and forwarders (HGB, the operator's general terms)
Combined Transport Directive 92/106/EEC and the German rules for combined transport (44 t, Sunday ban exemption)
ERegG path ordering and framework agreements (where the operator orders paths itself as an applicant)
Competition law (GWB)
risks: Revenue risk from empty slots; job loss in downturns
Pressure from forwarders and EVUs at once

career.entry: Degree in logistics or business, or an apprenticeship as freight forwarder with experience
career.chances: €60–100k a year; head of network or sales director €100–150k

roles.timescale: weeks to a timetable year

game.title: Fill the train
game.loop: The player designs a weekly network of intermodal shuttles between four terminals (departures, cut-off times, prices) and buys traction and slots. A demand model of forwarders books units by price and transit time against the truck. Week by week the player adjusts the network, decides whether to run or cancel half-empty trains, and deals with a line closure.
game.win: Reach a positive contribution and over 80 % utilisation over a simulated quarter (about 20 minutes). Losses in three quarters in a row end the round; in career mode success leads to sales director or managing director.
game.knowledge: Economics of an intermodal train (fixed cost per trip against the price per unit), utilisation, the truck as competitor, cut-off and availability times.
game.bigGame: Takes traction offers from the EVU's sales, slots from the terminals and bookings from the forwarders. Gives trains to the production planner, the dispatcher and the terminals, and revenue to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Production and path planner (rail freight)
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (production planning)
roles.summary: Turns contracts into a production plan for the timetable year: which trains run on which days, the locomotive circulation (Lokumlauf) and the crew duties, and the paths ordered from the infrastructure manager for the annual timetable (Netzfahrplan). Re-plans when the path offer comes back with conflicts or when a long closure for construction work breaks the plan.
decisions: Order annual paths by the deadline (the second Monday in April, eight months before the timetable change in December), or rely on ad-hoc paths
Comment on the draft network timetable, then accept or reject the final path offer within the deadlines of the network statement
Choose between a faster path at a higher price and a slower one with long waits in loops
Book pre-arranged paths on the rail freight corridors through the corridor one-stop shop
Design the locomotive circulation and crew duties so that each locomotive runs as many hours as possible
Plan diversions, extra drivers with route knowledge and extra locomotives for long closures such as the corridor renovations (Generalsanierungen)
Apply for framework capacity (Rahmenvertrag) for multi-year flows
effects: Good annual paths give fast, reliable trains; a plan built on ad-hoc paths risks finding no capacity at busy times
A tight circulation saves locomotives (each €4–5 million) but passes every delay on
Long closures add train-km, drivers and energy, and some customers switch to road
The plan sets the daily work of the dispatcher and the yard
resources: DB InfraGO's path ordering portal and the corridor one-stop-shop tools
Circulation and crew planning software
A team of 3–20 planners; track access charges of tens of millions of euros a year in a large EVU
limits: ERegG rules on the annual timetable, ad-hoc paths, framework agreements and congested infrastructure; DB InfraGO's network statement (SNB) and price system
Regulation (EU) 913/2010 on rail freight corridors (pre-arranged paths, corridor one-stop shop)
Construction closures announced under the infrastructure manager's rules for works planning
Working Hours Act and tariffs for crew duties; route and vehicle knowledge (TfV)
ECM maintenance intervals of the locomotives (Regulation (EU) 2019/779)
risks: Little personal legal liability
Peaks of stress around the timetable deadlines
Blamed when a plan looks lean on paper and collapses in operation

career.entry: Degree in transport engineering, railway operations or logistics (e.g. Verkehrsingenieurwesen at TU Dresden), or an apprenticeship plus years in dispatch
career.chances: €50–75k a year; head of production planning €80–110k

kpis: Share of trains on annual paths
Locomotive productivity (hours or km per day)
roles.timescale: months to a timetable year

game.title: Paths for the year
game.loop: The player gets eight customer flows for the next timetable year and an ARail network whose passenger trains already run in a fixed pattern. In a time-distance diagram (Bildfahrplan) they draw freight paths between the passenger trains, respecting the running times for the train's weight and braking, and order them by the April deadline. The infrastructure manager's draft comes back in July with some paths shifted or refused; the player comments, re-plans and builds the locomotive and crew circulation. Then a five-month closure for a corridor renovation is announced, and the plan must be rebuilt around a diversion.
game.win: Run every flow within the customer's time window with the fewest locomotives and drivers and the lowest path cost; a round is one timetable year (about 25 minutes). Flows left without a path must go as ad-hoc trains in the big game, with a risk of finding no capacity; in career mode a lean and robust plan leads to head of production.
game.knowledge: Time-distance diagrams, running times and headways, the timetable calendar (requests by the second Monday in April, draft in early July, change in mid-December), framework agreements, pre-arranged corridor paths, priority rules on congested lines, circulation planning.
game.bigGame: Takes contracts from sales and the intermodal operator, path offers from track-access-sales and the timetable planner, and closures from the possession planner. Gives the yearly production plan to the production dispatcher, locomotive and driver numbers to the managing director, and path costs to the economics simulator.

roles.name: Customer service and order management agent (rail freight)
roles.organisation: freight railway undertaking (customer service centre)
roles.summary: Takes the customers' orders for empty wagons and trains, checks the consignment notes, tracks the wagons and tells the customer when they will arrive, and handles claims for delay, loss and damage first. The daily link between the shipper's siding and the EVU's production.
decisions: Accept a wagon order, or offer another wagon type or date when none is free
Check consignment notes and send back incomplete or wrong ones (missing UN number, weight above the load limit, wrong destination code)
Give the customer an honest new arrival time when a wagon is delayed
Carry out a customer's instruction to change the destination or consignee on the way (subsequent modification, CIM Art. 18)
Charge demurrage (Standgeld) when a customer keeps wagons beyond the free time
Assess a claim against the contract and the liability limits, settle small ones, and pass larger ones to legal
effects: Correct documents keep wagons from being held in yards
Early information lets customers adjust production and stock
Demurrage pushes customers to release wagons, which improves fleet use
Poor service drives customers to trucks
resources: The order, tracking and telematics systems of the EVU
30–80 customer contacts a day
Authority for goodwill payments up to a few hundred euros
limits: CIM (COTIF Appendix B) and the CIM consignment note; HGB §§407 ff for domestic traffic
The EVU's general terms (e.g. DB Cargo's ALB) and the GCU
RID rules on transport documents (RID 5.4.1)
Customs transit documents for international traffic
Liability limits: HGB 8.33 SDR per kg and three times the freight for delay; CIM 17 SDR per kg and up to four times the carriage charge for delay
risks: Stress from complaints
Low personal liability
Jobs cut as booking and tracking are digitised

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Kaufmann/-frau für Spedition und Logistikdienstleistung or another commercial apprenticeship; internal training of a few weeks
career.chances: €2,800–3,800 a month; team leader up to about €4,800

roles.timescale: minutes to days

game.title: Where is my wagon?
game.loop: The player works a customer service inbox for one shift: wagon orders, consignment notes, tracking requests and claims. Some notes have errors (a missing UN number, a weight above the wagon's load limit, a wrong destination station code, a missing transit document), and wagons move or stall in the yard simulation, so the player must give customers honest arrival times. Claims arrive for damage and delay, and the player assesses them against the contract and the HGB or CIM limits.
game.win: Clear the inbox with no faulty consignment note passed on, arrival times close to the actual ones, and claims settled within the legal and contractual limits. A wrongly accepted dangerous goods note becomes a fine or an incident in the big game; in career mode a strong record leads to sales or dispatch.
game.knowledge: Fields of the CIM consignment note, wagon types and load limits, RID document rules, demurrage and free time, liability limits under HGB and CIM, subsequent modification of the contract.
game.bigGame: Takes orders from the shipper, the loading supervisor and the siding owner, wagon positions from the yard and dispatcher games, and delays from the disruptions. Gives booked wagons to production, demurrage and claim costs to the economics simulator, and customer satisfaction to the sales and shipper games.

roles.name: Truck driver in combined-transport pre- and on-carriage
roles.organisation: haulier (Fuhrunternehmen) working for a forwarder or an intermodal operator
roles.summary: Collects containers, swap bodies and trailers from customers and brings them to the terminal before the train's cut-off, or takes them from the terminal to the customer after the train: the first and last mile of every combined-transport chain. Works to gate slots, cut-off times and driving-time limits.
decisions: Plan the tour to meet the cut-off and the gate slot
Check the unit's seal, damage and weight before taking it
Refuse a unit that is overweight, damaged or badly secured
Decide when to take the break within the driving-time rules
Use the 44 t limit and the Sunday-ban exemption only on a real combined-transport trip
At a congested gate, wait, re-book the slot or tell the dispatcher that the cut-off will be missed
Open the twist locks before the lift and stay out of the crane's danger zone
effects: A missed cut-off means the unit misses the train and the customer's deadline
Queues at the gate cost tours per day and make the truck look like the better option
An overweight unit endangers the wagon and is caught at the gate or by the wagon inspector
resources: A tractor with a container chassis (about €100–150k), a digital tachograph
Up to 44 t gross weight in combined transport
A slot booking app and phone contact with the forwarder's dispatcher
limits: Regulation (EC) 561/2006: 45 min break after 4.5 h, 9 h of driving a day (10 h twice a week), 56 h a week, 90 h in two weeks; tachograph under Regulation (EU) 165/2014
Fahrpersonalgesetz and the Working Hours Act
StVZO §34 (44 t in combined transport), StVO §30(3) (Sunday-ban exemption), truck toll
Berufskraftfahrerqualifikationsgesetz: initial qualification and 35 hours of training every 5 years; ADR certificate for dangerous goods
The terminal's rules for drivers in the crane area
risks: Road accidents and fatigue
Fines for driving-time breaches, for driver and company (roadside checks by BALM and the police)
Being crushed or struck in the crane area
Low pay and long days

career.entry: Driving licence class CE with the initial qualification (Grundqualifikation), or a three-year apprenticeship as Berufskraftfahrer/in
career.chances: €2,600–3,500 gross a month plus daily allowances

roles.timescale: minutes to a day

game.title: Before the cut-off
game.loop: The player drives one working day of 4–6 container jobs between customers in the ARail town and the terminal: book a gate slot, collect a unit, check seal and weight, and reach the terminal before the train's cut-off. A driving-time clock runs all the time, and traffic, a unit not ready at the warehouse, a broken seal, an overweight box or a queue at the gate force choices: wait, refuse, re-book, or take the break now.
game.win: Deliver all units before their cut-offs and collect the import units within their free time, with no driving-time breach and no unsafe load. A roadside check fines breaches, and a missed cut-off pushes the unit to the next train in the big game. In career mode a clean record opens terminal dispatch or train driver training.
game.knowledge: Driving and rest times, the 44 t rule and the Sunday-ban exemption, gate procedure, twist locks and the crane danger zone, basics of ADR.
game.bigGame: Takes bookings from the forwarder and slots from the terminal. Gives units at the gate to the terminal dispatcher and crane operator, and delivery times to the forwarder and the shipper.

roles.name: Loading supervisor at a shipper's plant
roles.organisation: shipper (the plant's dispatch department)
roles.summary: Leads the loading of wagons at the plant: decides how goods are placed and secured on each wagon, loads each wagon up to its load limit, weighs, seals and labels, and hands the loaded wagons with their documents to the EVU. Under freight law the consignor normally loads, so a load that shifts on the way is the plant's fault.
decisions: Choose the wagon type and the loading pattern from the UIC Loading Guidelines
Choose the securing: wedges, lashings, anti-slip mats, bulkheads
Spread the weight so the centre of gravity stays within the allowed offsets
Load up to the load limit for the line category, never beyond
Refuse to load a damaged wagon and report it to the EVU or the keeper
Hold back dispatch to fix a doubtful load, even if the train is waiting
Seal the wagon and apply RID labels and placards
effects: A shifted load can derail the train or block the line
An overloaded wagon is set aside by the wagon inspector or damages the track
Fully and correctly loaded wagons lower the cost per tonne
resources: A loading crew of 3–15, forklifts or cranes, a track scale
Lashing material and the loading guideline sheets
1–3 loading tracks in the plant
limits: HGB §§412 and 414 and CIM Art. 13 and 14: the consignor's duty to load and package safely and its liability
UIC Loading Guidelines (Verladerichtlinien) and the load limit grid on each wagon
RID 7.5 (loading of dangerous goods) and the consignor's duties under the GGVSEB
GCU (use of wagons, reporting damage)
Occupational safety: work at height on wagons, DGUV rules
risks: Falls from wagons and crushing by loads
Criminal investigation after an accident caused by a shifted load; the company liable to the carrier
Pressure to load fast

career.entry: Apprenticeship as Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik or in a metal trade, years in dispatch, internal training in load securing; often master craftsman (Meister) later
career.chances: €3,000–4,200 a month; as Meister up to about €4,800

kpis: Wagons rejected by the wagon inspector
roles.timescale: minutes to a shift

game.title: Lash it down
game.loop: The player loads a shift's wagons at a steel plant: coils on a Shimmns coil wagon, plates on an open wagon, timber on a stake wagon. For each wagon they choose the loading pattern and the securing from the loading guideline sheets, keep within the load limit for the line category and keep the centre of gravity within the allowed offsets. The wagon inspector checks a sample, and the wagons then run through the hump and a hard braking in the simulation, where a badly secured load shifts.
game.win: Load all wagons fully and safely within the shift; the score is tonnes loaded minus wagons rejected. A load that shifts on the way stops the train in the big game or derails it; in career mode it triggers an investigation of the consignor.
game.knowledge: UIC Loading Guidelines, load limit grids (line categories A to D), weight distribution, friction and lashing, the consignor's duties under HGB and CIM, RID loading rules.
game.bigGame: Takes orders from the shipper and empty wagons from customer service and the wagon keeper. Gives loaded wagons and their documents to the shunter, the wagon inspector and customer service, and shifted-load incidents to the disruptions.

roles.name: ECM manager (management function)
roles.name_de: Leiter/in der für die Instandhaltung zuständigen Stelle (ECM, Managementfunktion)
roles.organisation: Entity in charge of maintenance (ECM): the ECM unit of an RU (e.g. DB Regio, DB Cargo, a private RU), of a wagon keeper or leasing company, or a manufacturer acting as ECM under a full-service contract
roles.summary: Heads the management function of the entity in charge of maintenance (ECM) under Regulation (EU) 2019/779. Answers for the safe state of maintenance of every vehicle for which this ECM is entered in the European Vehicle Register (EVR), runs the maintenance system that ties the other three functions together (maintenance development, fleet maintenance management, maintenance delivery), whether in-house or contracted, and keeps the ECM certificate.
decisions: Decide which ECM functions stay in-house and which are contracted out (own depot, ECM company, workshop company, manufacturer full service)
Ground a fleet type or order an inspection campaign after a safety alert in ERA's Safety Alert IT tool (SAIT) on cracked axles or brake parts
Issue a safety alert in SAIT when a defect found in the own fleet may affect other ECMs' vehicles
Decide whether a change to the maintenance system is a significant change under CSM-RA and needs an assessment body
Select, audit and, if needed, drop a workshop or parts supplier
Set competence requirements and the yearly internal audit plan; close the certification body's non-conformities
Refuse the return to operation of a unit with a safety-relevant defect, even when the RU wants it in service tomorrow
Split the maintenance budget between preventive work, corrective work and modifications
effects: Grounding a fleet type removes 10-30 % of capacity overnight: cancellations, replacement buses and penalties from the transport authority
The outsourcing model adds handovers, data delays and penalty chains between parties (exactly what ARail's ECM setups compare: integrated, distributed, full service)
A suspended ECM certificate stops every vehicle registered with this ECM: no return to operation, no service
Supplier audits and competence rules decide whether failures repeat after workshop visits
Passing on safety information through SAIT protects other ECMs across Europe; a missed alert can end like Viareggio 2009 (axle fracture of an LPG tank wagon, 32 dead)
resources: Maintenance budget of the fleet: about EUR 10-150 million a year (roughly EUR 1-3 per unit-km for regional multiple units, EUR 1,500-3,000 a year per freight wagon)
Fleet of 50-2,000 multiple units or locomotives, or 1,000-90,000 freight wagons
ECM organisation of 10-100 engineers and planners; contracted workshops with hundreds of staff
Authority to withdraw vehicles from service and to stop a supplier
Maintenance IT (SAP PM, fleet diagnostics), the vehicle register entries, access to SAIT
limits: Regulation (EU) 2019/779 (ECM certification for all vehicles since 16 June 2022, for freight wagons since 2011 under the former Regulation (EU) 445/2011; requirements of the management function in Annex II)
Directive (EU) 2016/798 Art. 14 and AEG § 4 (safety duties of RUs, keepers and ECMs); railway supervision by the EBA (AEG § 5)
Implementing Regulation (EU) 402/2013 (CSM-RA): the ECM is a proposer for changes to its maintenance system
EBO vehicle provisions (§§ 18 ff., incl. the examination and monitoring of vehicles in § 32) and the maintenance file required by the TSIs
Availability contract with the RU, workshop and full-service contracts, the GCU for freight wagons
Surveillance by the certification body (the EBA or a DAkkS-accredited body) at least once a year; certificate valid for at most 5 years
risks: Criminal liability after an accident caused by poor maintenance (StGB § 222 negligent homicide, § 315 dangerous interference with rail traffic)
Suspension of the ECM certificate and loss of the post after a failed audit
Permanent tension between availability and safety, pushed by the RU's managing director and the transport authority
Public exposure after a fleet grounding or an accident (press, BEU investigation)
On-call duty for safety alerts and incidents

career.entry: Degree in mechanical, electrical or railway vehicle engineering (e.g. TU Dresden, TU Berlin, RWTH Aachen, KIT), 10+ years in fleet, workshop or maintenance engineering, solid knowledge of 2019/779 and the CSMs, often an auditor course (ISO 19011)
career.chances: Senior management, out of tariff (AT): about EUR 110,000-180,000 a year plus bonus. Few such posts (one per ECM), so the next step is usually technical director (Leiter Technik), managing director or consulting

kpis: Safety-relevant incidents attributable to maintenance (per million vehicle-km)
ECM certificate kept; audit findings closed on time
Fleet availability against the availability contract (typically 90-95 %)
Safety alerts handled within their deadlines
roles.timescale: Months to years for the maintenance system and contracts; hours to days during a safety alert

game.title: Who Maintains the Train? (certificate and crisis)
game.loop: Act 1: the player assigns the four ECM functions to parties (RU, ECM company, workshop company, manufacturer), sets the penalty pass-through of the availability and workshop contracts and runs ARail's operations comparison for four weeks under a stress test. Act 2: a certification audit as a quiz: find the gaps in a mock maintenance system description against Annex II of 2019/779. Act 3: a SAIT alert reports axle cracks in part of the fleet; the player chooses between grounding, an ultrasonic inspection campaign within N days, or a speed restriction, decides whether to pass the finding on to other ECMs, and sees cancellations, penalties and the simulated risk of a derailment.
game.win: Score from availability, the ECM party's net penalties, audit findings and safety (no derailment, no overdue unit in service). A derailment or an ignored alert ends the round with the certificate suspended; in career mode it brings a BEU investigation, possible prosecution and a career setback, while a clean audit and a well-handled alert add reputation and open the step to technical director.
game.knowledge: The four ECM functions and who answers for what; Annex II requirements (leadership, risk assessment, monitoring, competence, contracted activities, documentation); SAIT; the significance criteria of CSM-RA Art. 4; availability contracts and penalty chains
game.bigGame: Takes the availability demand and the maintenance budget from the RU's managing director and the transport contract; gives available units per day to fleet and rotation planning, penalties to finance, safety events to the safety manager and the EBA. In the economics simulator its ECM model sets the RU's maintenance cost structure.

roles.name: Maintenance development engineer
roles.organisation: Entity in charge of maintenance (ECM), maintenance development function; similar posts in manufacturers' service engineering
roles.summary: Runs the maintenance development function of the ECM: writes and keeps the maintenance programme (levels, intervals in km and days, tolerances, wear limits, non-destructive test intervals) from the manufacturer's maintenance file, analyses failure and wear data, decides on interval extensions and modifications, and manages each vehicle's configuration.
decisions: Set the interval of each maintenance level (e.g. inspections every 7,500 km or 21 days and every 30,000 km, a yearly level, heavy overhaul at about 1.2-1.6 million km)
Grant or refuse a one-off interval extension that fleet planning asks for
Set method and interval of non-destructive tests of axles and wheels (e.g. ultrasonic testing of hollow axles every N thousand km)
Move a component from fixed intervals to condition-based maintenance using diagnostic or sensor data
Release a modification (retrofit, software update, fix of a series defect) into the maintenance documents
Set wear limits and measuring tasks (wheel profiles, brake pads, pantograph carbon strips)
Decide whether a programme change is significant under CSM-RA and needs an assessment body
Start a root-cause analysis with the manufacturer and claim warranty for a series defect
effects: Longer intervals cut workshop hours and raise availability, but beyond the knee of the wear curve failures rise steeply
Shorter intervals raise cost and take units out more often, leaving rotations without units
Good condition-based maintenance lowers failures and cost together; a bad one hides wear until a breakdown
Modifications and software updates change the reliability of a fleet type for years

Wrong wear limits or test intervals on wheelsets or brakes are a direct accident risk: Eschede 1998 (fatigue fracture of a resilient wheel tyre, 101 dead) and the ICE 3 axle fracture at Köln Hbf in 2008 led to new limits and shorter ultrasonic test intervals
resources: Fleet data: failure records, mileage, diagnostic codes (TCMS), workshop findings for hundreds of units over years
Engineering budget of EUR 0.5-5 million a year; modification campaigns EUR 1-50 million
A team of 3-20 engineers per fleet type; the manufacturer's maintenance manual and support
Authority over the maintenance documents (Instandhaltungsunterlagen) and their release
limits: Regulation (EU) 2019/779 Annex II (maintenance development: maintenance file, configuration management)
Maintenance file and operating limits required by TSI LOC&PAS and TSI WAG

EN 17023 (creation and modification of the maintenance plan), DIN 27200 and DIN 27201 (state of railway vehicles), EN 15313 (in-service wheelset limits), EVIC and the VPI maintenance guide (VPI-EMG) for freight wagon wheelsets
CSM-RA (Implementing Regulation (EU) 402/2013) for significant changes
Warranty and availability clauses of the supply contract
risks: Shared responsibility and possible criminal investigation if an extended interval or a wide wear limit contributes to an accident
Blamed by operations for units in the workshop and by safety for rising failures
Disputes with the manufacturer over series defects
Office hours, on call during series defects

career.entry: Engineering degree (mechanical, electrical, vehicle or railway systems), 2-5 years in a workshop, fleet engineering or at a manufacturer, reliability methods (RAMS, Weibull analysis, FMECA, RCM)
career.chances: EVG-tariff engineer at DB or out of tariff: about EUR 60,000-95,000 a year; team lead up to about EUR 110,000. Good demand: few engineers know maintenance engineering

kpis: Mean distance between failures (MDBF) per fleet type
Programme changes approved and implemented on time
roles.timescale: Weeks to years (programme revisions, modification campaigns); hours for an extension request

game.title: Interval (write the maintenance programme)
game.loop: The player sees the fleet's failure history (a Weibull plot per component, the bathtub curve over age, workshop findings) and sets the interval and tolerance of each maintenance level of ARail's programme (IS1, IS2, IS3). The operations simulation runs eight weeks with those intervals, using its age and wear failure model. Between rounds, extension requests and a series defect (a door controller) arrive; the player answers and may switch a component to condition-based maintenance at a sensor cost.
game.win: Lowest maintenance cost plus penalties under a fixed safety floor: no unit beyond its limit plus tolerance, hard failures per 100,000 km below a cap. Breaking the floor ends the round with a safety finding; in career mode it costs reputation and blocks promotion for a while.
game.knowledge: Weibull shape (early failures, random failures, wear-out), RCM logic (EN 60300-3-11), preventive vs condition-based vs run-to-failure, tolerance rules, safety-critical components, the CSM-RA significance test
game.bigGame: Takes failure data and extension requests from fleet management and the workshops, series-defect input from the manufacturer's engineer; gives the maintenance programme that sets workshop load, parts demand and fleet reliability in the economics simulator.

roles.name: Fleet manager (fleet maintenance management)
roles.organisation: Railway undertaking (e.g. DB Regio, Go-Ahead, National Express, Transdev) or the ECM company: fleet maintenance management function
roles.summary: Runs fleet maintenance management, the third ECM function: decides every day which unit goes to the workshop when and which defects may wait, agrees with the RU's vehicle dispatch which unit takes which rotation, and issues the return to operation, so that tomorrow's pull-out is covered and no unit runs past its maintenance limit.
decisions: Book the units due for maintenance into tonight's workshop slots
Agree with the RU's vehicle dispatch which unit takes which rotation, giving the unit with the most km left to the longest rotation
Let a unit run with a comfort defect (air conditioning, toilet, a door out of order) or take it out
Ask maintenance development for an interval extension when no slot is free
Order a transfer run to a workshop elsewhere or bring a spare unit
Issue the return to operation (Wiederinbetriebnahme) after the workshop's maintenance release
Plan a modification campaign (ETCS retrofit, new door software) around the timetable
Claim penalties from the workshop or warranty from the manufacturer for late releases and repeat failures
effects: Units missing at the morning pull-out mean short-formed or cancelled trains and penalties per train-km
Comfort defects in service cost penalties per unit and day and annoy passengers
Booking too early wastes interval kilometres; booking too late grounds units as overdue
A good plan smooths the workshop's load and its overtime
resources: Fleet of 20-300 multiple units with a reserve of 10-15 %
Workshop slots per night (2-10 tracks), transfer runs, spare units
Mileage and diagnostic data, live or as daily reports
Maintenance contracts of EUR 5-80 million a year; penalty exposure EUR 0.1-5 million a year
limits: Regulation (EU) 2019/779 Annex II (fleet maintenance management: scheduling, release to service, return to operation)
Limits and tolerances of the maintenance programme; EBO vehicle provisions
Transport contract (Verkehrsvertrag) with availability and comfort penalties
Workshop contract, the parties' working hours, works agreements on night work
risks: Responsibility if a unit runs overdue or with a safety-relevant defect returned to operation by mistake
Daily pressure from operations control and the transport authority's quality monitoring
Stress and weekend on-call, worst in winter and heat waves
Career risk after repeated penalties; low criminal risk if the rules are kept

career.entry: Degree in engineering or industrial engineering, or a state-certified technician (staatlich geprüfte/r Techniker/in) with workshop experience; a few years as workshop planner or rotation planner
career.chances: EVG tariff or out of tariff at DB, about EUR 55,000-90,000 a year; head of fleet EUR 90,000-120,000

kpis: Units available at the first pull-out against plan
Train-km lost and penalties for missing or short-formed units
Unit-days with comfort defects in service
Workshop slot use and transfer runs
roles.timescale: A day (the plan for tomorrow, made around noon), with minutes when a unit fails

game.title: Pull-out (plan tomorrow's fleet)
game.loop: Every game day at 13:00 the player sees the fleet board of ARail's operations module: each unit's km and days to its next level, its defects, tonight's workshop slots and tomorrow's rotations. They drag units to slots and rotations, decide which defects may wait and ask for extensions. The day then runs with failures, breakdowns and a parts delay, and the transport contract's penalties come in. A round is one week.
game.win: Every rotation covered at the first pull-out with no unit overdue; the score is penalties avoided minus workshop and transfer cost. An overdue unit in service is a safety violation that ends the round; in career mode repeated misses stall promotion and a clean week adds reputation.
game.knowledge: Maintenance levels and tolerances, rotation lengths, penalty items of the transport contract, the value of the night window, data latency between parties
game.bigGame: Takes timetable and rotations from service and rotation planning and the programme from maintenance development; gives the workshop plan to the workshop planner and units per rotation to operations; its penalties flow into the RU's accounts in the economics simulator.

roles.name: Workshop manager (maintenance delivery)
roles.organisation: Maintenance workshop: an RU's depot (e.g. a DB Regio or DB Fernverkehr depot), a workshop company, a manufacturer's service depot (e.g. Siemens' RRX depot in Dortmund-Eving), or a heavy-overhaul works (DB Fahrzeuginstandhaltung)
roles.summary: Runs maintenance delivery, the fourth ECM function: leads a depot of 50-500 staff in shifts, delivers the booked inspections, repairs and overhauls on time and to quality, issues the maintenance release through authorised staff, and keeps people safe in a hall with pits, lifting jacks, 15 kV catenary and heavy parts.
decisions: Choose the shift model (24/7 in three shifts or two shifts Mon-Sat) and agree it with the works council
Hire, train and qualify staff (electrically skilled persons, EN 15085 welders, wheel lathe operators, NDT inspectors)
Accept or refuse an extra job tonight when the hall is full
Invest in equipment: underfloor wheel lathe, lifting jacks, roof platforms, diagnostics
Subcontract work (bogie overhaul, HVAC repair) or keep it in-house
Stop work after a safety incident and change procedures
Contest late-release and repeat-failure penalties with the ECM
effects: Shift model and staffing decide on-time releases and the units at tomorrow's pull-out
Workmanship decides repeat failures and safety in service
Labour is 50-70 % of the workshop's cost; overtime and agency staff eat the margin
Work accidents (falls from roofs, electric shock, crushing) injure staff and stop the depot
resources: Staff of 50-500 (mechatronics technicians, electricians, mechanics, planners, master craftsmen)
2-20 workshop tracks with pits, a wheel lathe, a wash plant, a parts store
Budget of EUR 10-80 million a year; investments EUR 1-10 million (a wheel lathe EUR 2-5 million; a new depot EUR 50-200 million)
Authority to issue the maintenance release after work (Instandhaltungsfreigabe)
limits: Regulation (EU) 2019/779 (maintenance delivery), the workshop contract with the ECM
Arbeitsschutzgesetz, BetrSichV (lifting equipment, pits), DGUV Vorschrift 3 (electrical safety), DGUV rules for work on roofs and near catenary, GefStoffV
Arbeitszeitgesetz, EVG or IG Metall tariff, BetrVG § 87 (works council co-determination on shift plans and overtime)
EN 15085 welding certification, ISO 9001 or ISO/TS 22163 (IRIS) quality system
Environmental law for washing, oils and paints (WHG, BImSchG)
risks: Criminal and civil liability for work accidents and faulty releases
Shift and on-call duty; stress around the morning pull-out
Losing the workshop contract in a re-tender; site closures
Conflicts with works council and union over shifts and staffing

career.entry: Engineer (B.Eng./M.Eng./Dipl.-Ing.) or master craftsman / technician with 5-10 years in a workshop and leadership training
career.chances: Out of tariff at DB or manufacturers: about EUR 80,000-130,000 a year; heads of heavy-overhaul works more

kpis: Turnaround time per job and level
Repeat failures within N days after a visit
Penalties paid under the workshop contract
roles.timescale: A shift (the night window) to months (staffing, investment)

game.title: The Depot (a month at the workshop)
game.loop: The player runs the workshop company of ARail's distributed or full-service setup: sets the shift model, headcount, training and overtime rules, picks one investment (a second lathe track, diagnostics, more staff) and negotiates the shift plan with the works council in a short dialogue. The operations simulation runs four weeks; workshop speed, quality and parts delays follow the choices, while stress tests hit (staff shortage, heat wave, a work accident).
game.win: Profit of the workshop company: contract revenue minus labour, overtime, investment and penalties for late releases and repeat failures, without a serious accident. A serious accident or a lost contract ends the round; in career mode it costs the post.
game.knowledge: Shift models under the Arbeitszeitgesetz, co-determination under BetrVG § 87, workshop contract penalties, what drives quality and repeat failures, safety rules for pits, roofs and catenary
game.bigGame: Takes booked jobs from fleet planning and the contract price from the ECM; gives released units and penalties to the ECM and RU, labour demand to HR and the unions.

roles.name: Workshop planner
roles.organisation: Maintenance workshop (depot of an RU, workshop company or manufacturer's service)
roles.summary: Prepares the work (Arbeitsvorbereitung) in the depot: turns booked maintenance and repair jobs into a shift plan with tracks, qualified staff, tools, parts kits and documents, so that every unit is back for its pull-out.
decisions: Slot tonight's jobs onto workshop tracks (pit, roof platform, wheel lathe, wash plant)
Assign technicians by qualification (electrically skilled person, welder, lathe operator, NDT inspector)
Order parts kits and special tools for each job in time
Re-plan when a broken-down unit is towed in or a finding extends a job
Decide which job to defer when the night is too short and tell fleet planning
Plan switching off and earthing the workshop catenary for roof work
effects: A tight plan releases units for the morning pull-out; a bad one leaves rotations without units
Missing qualifications or parts stop the work and delay releases
Over-planned nights cost overtime and raise the risk of mistakes
resources: 2-20 tracks and a night window of about 4-6 hours between pull-in and pull-out, plus day slots
10-60 technicians per shift with recorded qualifications
Parts store, maintenance IT (SAP PM work orders, digital job cards)
limits: Maintenance programme and work instructions; releases only by qualified staff
Arbeitszeitgesetz (11 hours rest, breaks), tariff shift rules, works agreements
DGUV Vorschrift 3 and depot safety rules: catenary off and earthed before roof work
BetrSichV: only inspected lifting jacks and cranes
risks: Shift and night work
Blamed for late releases; shared responsibility if the plan forces shortcuts
Low criminal risk

career.entry: Master craftsman (Industriemeister Metall or Elektrotechnik) or state-certified technician after vocational training and several years in the workshop; sometimes a B.Eng.
career.chances: EVG tariff at DB or IG Metall at manufacturers: about EUR 45,000-65,000 a year plus shift allowances

roles.timescale: A shift: the night plan, re-planned within minutes

game.title: Night Shift (the workshop plan)
game.loop: At 22:00 the player gets tonight's jobs from fleet planning in ARail's operations and a crew with qualifications. They drag jobs onto tracks and people onto jobs in a Gantt chart until 04:30, order parts kits and plan the earthing for roof jobs. During the night events arrive: a broken-down unit is towed in, an inspection finds a cracked damper, a technician calls in sick, a part is missing, and the player re-plans.
game.win: Units released before their pull-out: points per rotation covered, minus overtime and penalties. Roof work without earthing or a release by an unqualified person is a rule breach that ends the round. In career mode good nights lead to the workshop manager's post.
game.knowledge: Job durations by level, who may release what, working-time rules, the safe order of work (earthing, lifting, testing), parts lead times
game.bigGame: Takes jobs from fleet management and staff from the workshop manager; gives release times to fleet planning and operations, parts demand to parts supply.

roles.name: Rolling stock mechatronics technician
roles.organisation: Maintenance workshop (depot of an RU, workshop company or manufacturer's service)
roles.summary: Inspects, diagnoses and repairs the mechanical, pneumatic and electrical systems of trains in the depot (doors, brakes, pantographs, traction converters, air conditioning, the train control and diagnostic system, wheelsets) and signs off the work done.
decisions: Read the diagnostic log and choose the next test to find the fault
Repair a component or swap a line-replaceable unit
Measure a wheel profile and decide whether the unit goes to the wheel lathe
Refuse to start roof work until the workshop catenary is off and earthed
Record a finding beyond the job (a cracked bracket) and stop the release
Sign off the job card for the work done
effects: A right diagnosis fixes the fault first time; a wrong one brings the unit back as a repeat failure
A missed finding on brakes or wheelsets is a direct safety risk in service
Working speed decides whether the unit makes its pull-out
resources: Tools and measuring equipment (wheel profile gauge, multimeter, laptop with diagnostic software), job card and work instructions
Planned time per job: minutes to a few hours
Parts from the store
limits: Work instructions and maintenance documents; wheel limits per EN 15313 and TSI LOC&PAS (for wheels of 840 mm and more: flange thickness Sd at least 22 mm, flange height Sh at most 36 mm, flange slope qR at least 6.5 mm)
DGUV Vorschrift 3 (electrically skilled person, the five safety rules), catenary off and earthed, high-voltage qualification for traction batteries
Fall protection on roofs, lock-out tag-out, BetrSichV for lifting jacks
Arbeitszeitgesetz, EVG or IG Metall tariff, shift plans
risks: Injury: electric shock (15 kV, traction batteries), falls from roofs, crushing under lifted vehicles
Night and weekend shifts
Criminal investigation after an accident if a release was signed falsely
Noise, dust, hazardous substances

career.entry: Three-and-a-half-year dual vocational training (Mechatroniker/in or Elektroniker/in für Betriebstechnik, IHK exam), e.g. at DB, a manufacturer or a private workshop; career changers through a two-year retraining (Umschulung)
career.chances: EVG tariff at DB roughly EUR 3,200-4,100 gross a month plus shift and night allowances; IG Metall at manufacturers about EUR 3,500-4,500; a master craftsman or technician qualification adds EUR 500-1,000 a month. A shortage profession with safe jobs

kpis: Repeat failures traced to own work
roles.timescale: Minutes to hours per job, within a shift

game.title: Fault Finder (in the pit)
game.loop: A unit from ARail's operations arrives with a defect (door out of order, air conditioning, restricted traction, a brake fault, a flat spot). The player first secures the workplace in the right order (catenary off and earthed, lock-out, chocks), then reads diagnostic codes, picks tests from a fault tree (each costs minutes) and chooses the repair; for wheels they read a profile gauge and decide on the lathe against the limits. Release time and quality go back into the simulation.
game.win: Fault fixed within the planned time without a repeat failure in the following simulated week, with the safety steps in order. Skipping earthing or a false release ends the round at once (and in career mode can end the career); fast, correct diagnoses earn the master craftsman qualification.
game.knowledge: The five electrical safety rules, catenary earthing, wheel profile limits (Sd, Sh, qR), how door control, brakes and HVAC work, reading fault codes
game.bigGame: Takes jobs from the workshop planner; gives the real job duration and quality (repeat-failure probability) to the workshop and the fleet.

roles.name: Parts and supply chain manager
roles.organisation: Maintenance workshop, the ECM, or a central materials unit (e.g. DB's materials management); sometimes the manufacturer's spare-parts service
roles.summary: Keeps the spare parts flowing for a fleet: what to stock, how much, from whom, and how to run the loop of repairable exchange parts; fights long lead times, obsolete electronics and failing suppliers.
decisions: Set reorder points and safety stock per part (wheelsets, brake pads, door drives, converter modules)
Choose the source: the manufacturer, an independent supplier or a reverse-engineered part (needs release by maintenance development)
Place a last-time buy for an electronic part going obsolete
Allow cannibalising a grounded unit to keep others running
Organise the overhaul loop of repairables (bogies, couplers, pantographs) and its turnaround
Tender framework contracts for consumables (under SektVO when the buyer is a sector contracting entity such as a DB company)
effects: Missing parts keep units out of service and cost penalties
Too much stock binds capital and turns obsolete
Cannibalisation keeps trains running but grounds one unit and doubles the work
Parts outside the maintenance file's configuration can void the vehicle's conformity and the ECM's release
resources: Stock of EUR 2-50 million per fleet, 5,000-50,000 part numbers
Purchasing budget of EUR 5-60 million a year
Lead times: brake pads weeks, wheelsets 6-12 months, bogie frames and converters up to 12-18 months
ERP system (SAP MM/PM) and framework contracts
limits: GWB part 4 and SektVO for purchases above the EU thresholds (several hundred thousand euros for supplies) by sector contracting entities such as DB companies; private RUs and workshop companies buy freely
Configuration rules of the maintenance file: only approved parts; changes via maintenance development
Traceability of safety-critical parts (wheelsets, axles) required for ECMs and by EVIC
REACH and export control for some materials
risks: Blamed for grounded units; job risk after large write-offs of obsolete stock
Compliance risk: bribery in purchasing (StGB § 299), procurement law breaches
Office work, little physical risk

career.entry: Vocational training (Industriekaufmann/-frau, Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik) or a degree in logistics, business or industrial engineering
career.chances: About EUR 45,000-80,000 a year; head of materials management EUR 80,000-120,000

roles.timescale: Days to months (orders); years (last-time buys)

game.title: Waiting for Parts
game.loop: The player manages 12 critical part families of the fleet in ARail's operations: reorder points, safety stock and the source (cheap and slow, manufacturer and fast, or a reverse-engineered part pending release). Repairs in the simulation wait for parts whenever stock runs out. Over 26 simulated weeks events hit: a supplier insolvency, a chip shortage, a series defect that drains brake controllers, an obsolescence notice with a last-time-buy offer.
game.win: Lowest total of capital cost, write-offs and penalties for units waiting for parts after 26 weeks. Running out of a safety-critical part or fitting an unreleased part is a violation; in career mode a strong round opens head of materials or procurement.
game.knowledge: Reorder point and safety stock under demand and lead-time variation, ABC/XYZ analysis, repairable loops, obsolescence management (EN 62402), procurement thresholds and who is bound by them
game.bigGame: Takes parts demand from the maintenance programme and failures; gives part availability (repair delays) to the workshop and stock cost to the economics simulator; buys from the manufacturer's sales manager.
