roles.name: Vehicle procurement manager
roles.organisation: Railway undertaking (e.g. DB Regio, DB Fernverkehr) or a transport authority's vehicle pool (e.g. Landesanstalt Schienenfahrzeuge Baden-Württemberg, the LNVG pool in Lower Saxony, VRR)
roles.summary: Leads the purchase of new trains from the first requirements to the last accepted unit: writes the specification, runs the EU-wide procurement, chooses the manufacturer, steers design reviews, authorisation, delivery and acceptance, and claims liquidated damages for delays.
decisions: Fix the specification: length, seats, doors, platform height (550 or 760 mm, 960 mm on S-Bahn lines), traction (electric, battery, hydrogen, diesel), ETCS, top speed
Choose the procedure (negotiated procedure with a call for competition under SektVO or VgV) and the award criteria (price vs life-cycle cost vs quality)
Set the size of the framework and options (e.g. 20 firm plus 40 optional units)
Agree delivery dates, liquidated damages and availability guarantees
Accept or reject units at acceptance and withhold payments for defects
Bridge delays with leased or old trains
effects: The chosen train shapes capacity, energy and maintenance cost and comfort for 30 years
Late authorisation or delivery forces old trains or replacement concepts, penalties and bad press
A flawed tender can be stopped by the review chamber (Vergabekammer) for months
Battery or hydrogen trains decide whether a non-electrified line runs without diesel
resources: Budgets of EUR 100 million to several billion (regional EMU about EUR 7-12 million, double-deck unit EUR 12-18 million, high-speed train EUR 30-50 million, locomotive EUR 3-5 million)
Project team of 5-30 (engineers, lawyers, buyers) plus consultants
3-6 years from tender to first unit in service
limits: GWB part 4, SektVO (sector entity) or VgV (classic contracting authority), review procedure (GWB §§ 155 ff.)
Regulation (EC) 1370/2007 and the transport contract's vehicle requirements
TSIs (LOC&PAS, PRM, NOI, CCS), Directive (EU) 2016/797 and authorisation via ERA's one-stop shop
Budget and funding law of the Land for pools (funded from regionalisation funds under the Regionalisierungsgesetz)
risks: Career damage when trains arrive years late (e.g. Talent 2 units stood unauthorised for up to two years around 2011-2013)
Compliance: bribery (StGB § 299; §§ 331 ff. for public officials), procurement breaches
Political and press exposure

career.entry: Degree in engineering, industrial engineering or business; years in fleet management, at a manufacturer or in procurement; project management certificate (IPMA, PMP)
career.chances: Project lead at DB or a pool company about EUR 80,000-130,000 a year; at authorities TVöD/TV-L E 13-15, about EUR 60,000-95,000

kpis: Delivery on time and within budget
Reliability and availability in the first years
roles.timescale: Months to years (a procurement runs 4-8 years)

game.title: Buy a Train
game.loop: The player writes a specification for the lab's RE 1 and RB 33 services (seats, doors, platform heights, battery range for an assumed non-electrified branch beyond Bf Neustadt, ETCS), sets award criteria and runs the tender: three AI bidders answer with prices, delivery dates and LCC guarantees whose risk is hidden. After the award, a fast-forward of the delivery years throws design-review issues, authorisation delays and a review-chamber complaint; then the trains run in ARail's operations and passenger simulation with their capacity, dwell times and reliability.
game.win: Score from life-cycle cost per seat-km over 30 years, punctuality and crowding in the simulated service, delay to service start, and legal soundness. A lost review or a train that cannot be authorised ends the round; in career mode success opens managing director or leasing posts.
game.knowledge: Procurement procedures, thresholds, award criteria and review; LCC with discounting; the authorisation process; TSI PRM and German platform heights; battery multiple unit basics
game.bigGame: Takes service requirements from the transport authority and money from the economics simulator; gives a fleet (capacity, reliability, cost) to the RU and orders to the manufacturer's sales manager; delays become disruption scenarios.

roles.name: Leasing company asset manager
roles.organisation: Rolling stock leasing company (ROSCO), e.g. Alpha Trains, Akiem, Railpool, Beacon Rail, Northrail, European Loc Pool
roles.summary: Manages a portfolio of leased locomotives and multiple units as long-lived assets: buys vehicles, leases them to railway undertakings (dry or full-service), keeps their value through maintenance and upgrades, and re-leases them when a transport contract ends.
decisions: Buy vehicles on speculation or only against a signed lease
Set lease rate, term, return conditions and maintenance reserves
Offer a dry lease or a full-service lease with the ROSCO as ECM
Invest in an upgrade (ETCS retrofit, country package, refurbishment) to keep a fleet leasable
Re-market a fleet returned after a lost tender, move it abroad or scrap it
Repossess vehicles from a defaulting lessee
effects: Leasing lets small RUs bid in tenders without capital and keeps vehicles in use across contracts
Idle vehicles destroy value; a type without ETCS or a country package cannot be re-leased
Lease rates enter the RU's bid and so the price per train-km the transport authority pays
resources: Portfolio of hundreds of locomotives and multiple units worth EUR 1-5 billion
Capital from banks and investors; interest rates drive lease rates
Lease rates: a multi-system locomotive about EUR 20,000-35,000 a month, a regional EMU about EUR 50,000-120,000 a month
Technical team acting as ECM for full-service leases
limits: Lease contracts under civil law (BGB) and their return conditions
Keeper duties under AEG and EBO, registration in the European Vehicle Register, ECM under 2019/779
Authorisations per area of use (Directive (EU) 2016/797, Regulation (EU) 2018/545), ETCS requirements of TSI CCS
Re-use guarantees (Wiedereinsatzgarantie) of some transport authorities; IFRS 16 on the lessee side
risks: Residual value and job risk when fleets stand idle
Counterparty risk: insolvent lessees
Little physical risk; office and travel

career.entry: Degree in engineering, business or finance; experience in fleet management, at a manufacturer or in asset finance
career.chances: About EUR 80,000-150,000 a year plus bonus; heads of asset management more

kpis: Utilisation (share of the portfolio on lease)
roles.timescale: Years to decades (vehicle life 30-40 years, leases 1-15 years)

game.title: Residual Value
game.loop: Over 30 game years in one-year turns the player orders vehicle types and leases them to AI railway undertakings that bid in transport authorities' regional tenders (10-15 year contracts) and to freight operators. Each turn: set lease rates and terms, choose upgrades (ETCS, country packages, refurbishment), react to interest rates, lost tenders that return fleets, defaults and new rules (ETCS deadlines, noise rules).
game.win: Net present value of the portfolio at the end; when debt service is not covered the company fails and the round ends. In career mode a strong portfolio leads to managing director posts.
game.knowledge: Annuity, NPV and residual value, lease types, re-use guarantees, why ETCS and country packages decide re-leasing
game.bigGame: Takes tender outcomes from transport authorities and bid managers; gives vehicles and lease rates to RUs in the economics simulator; orders vehicles from the manufacturer's sales manager.

roles.name: Wagon keeper's fleet manager
roles.organisation: Wagon keeper (Wagenhalter), e.g. VTG, GATX Rail Europe, Ermewa, Wascosa, On Rail, or DB Cargo as keeper of its own wagons
roles.summary: Manages a fleet of freight wagons let to shippers and freight railway undertakings: fleet mix and investment, leases, maintenance through the (often own) ECM, damage claims under the GCU, and the big conversions such as quiet brake blocks and the digital automatic coupling.
decisions: Decide the fleet mix: tank wagons for chemicals, pocket and container wagons for intermodal, flat and coil wagons for steel
Set lease rates and terms with shippers and RUs
Send a wagon to revision now, park it or scrap it
Convert wagons to composite brake blocks and plan the move to the digital automatic coupling (DAC)
Claim damage from the RU under the GCU when a wagon comes back damaged
Stop and inspect affected wagons after a safety alert on axles or wheelsets
effects: The right wagons in the right place win freight for rail; idle wagons cost parking and capital
Loud wagons have been banned on German tracks since December 2020 (Schienenlärmschutzgesetz)
Badly maintained wagons derail (Viareggio 2009)
DAC could transform freight productivity but costs billions across Europe
resources: Fleet of 1,000-90,000 wagons; a new wagon costs EUR 100,000-250,000
Lease rates of about EUR 15-60 per wagon and day, depending on type
Own or contracted workshops; the ECM function
Investor capital
limits: GCU (General Contract of Use for Wagons) between keepers and RUs, with its annexes on technical inspection and damage
Regulation (EU) 2019/779 (ECM certification, required for freight wagons since 2011)
Schienenlärmschutzgesetz, TSI NOI (quieter routes from December 2024)
TSI WAG, COTIF (CUV, ATMF), RID for dangerous goods wagons (periodic tank inspections)
risks: Liability as keeper and ECM after accidents
Market risk: wagons idle in a downturn
Little physical risk

career.entry: Degree in engineering, logistics or business; experience in freight sales, wagon maintenance or leasing
career.chances: About EUR 60,000-110,000 a year; heads of fleet more

roles.timescale: Weeks (leases, damage cases) to decades (wagon life 30-40 years)

game.title: Wagon Pool
game.loop: Monthly turns over ten years. The player sees demand by wagon type from shippers (chemicals, steel, intermodal at ARail's container terminal, grain), places wagons on leases, sends wagons to revision, buys or scraps. Events: a market slump, a damage dispute under the GCU, the 2020 noise ban for unconverted wagons, an axle safety alert, the choice of when to join the DAC migration.
game.win: Return on capital at the end; unconverted wagons after the noise ban or an ignored safety alert cost heavily. In career mode it feeds the move to freight management.
game.knowledge: Wagon types (Zacns, Sgns, Sdggmrss, Shimmns, Eanos), GCU basics, ECM rules, the noise law, RID, DAC
game.bigGame: Takes freight demand from shippers and forwarders; gives wagons and their cost to freight RUs and the terminal; safety alerts to ECMs.

roles.name: Manufacturer's vehicle engineer
roles.organisation: Rolling stock manufacturer, e.g. Siemens Mobility (Krefeld, Erlangen), Alstom (Salzgitter, Hennigsdorf, Bautzen), Stadler (Berlin-Pankow), CAF, Škoda, Talgo
roles.summary: Designs a train or one of its systems (car body, bogie, traction, brakes, doors, HVAC, interior, train control) to meet the customer's specification, the TSIs and the EN standards within mass, cost and schedule, and supports authorisation and series production.
decisions: Trade seats against standing room, doors and toilets in the layout
Choose the car body structure (aluminium or steel) against mass, crash and cost
Size traction and battery for the route (range on a non-electrified branch)
Specify sub-suppliers' components and interfaces
Decide on a design change after a failed test or a series defect
Sign the design verification evidence for the authorisation file
effects: Mass and axle load drive energy use, track wear and the lines the train may run on (line categories of EN 15528)
Doors and layout decide dwell times and punctuality on busy lines
A flaw found late costs months of delay and millions in retrofits
Good design lowers life-cycle cost for 30 years
resources: Teams of 10-300 per project; development budgets of EUR 10-200 million per platform
CAD/CAE (FEM, multibody simulation), test benches
3-5 years from order to first delivery
limits: TSI LOC&PAS, TSI PRM, TSI NOI, TSI SRT, TSI CCS and notified national rules for Germany

EN 12663 (car body strength), EN 15227 (crashworthiness), EN 45545 (fire protection), EN 13749 (bogie frames), EN 14363 (running dynamics), EN 50155 (electronics), EN 15085 (welding), EN 50126 (RAMS) and EN 50657, now merged into EN 50716 (software)
Customer specification and contract penalties
Arbeitszeitgesetz, IG Metall tariff
risks: Professional liability; criminal investigation if a design flaw causes an accident
Deadline pressure and overtime near milestones
Job risk when orders fall or plants are restructured

career.entry: Master's degree in mechanical, electrical or vehicle engineering (e.g. TU Dresden, TU Berlin, KIT, RWTH Aachen, TU Braunschweig), often after an internship or a master thesis at the manufacturer
career.chances: IG Metall tariff about EUR 58,000-75,000 to start, EUR 85,000-120,000 as senior or system lead; chief engineers out of tariff

kpis: First-time pass rate in tests and assessments
roles.timescale: Months to years (a design project)

game.title: Design a Train
game.loop: The player configures a regional multiple unit in a builder: cars and length, doors per side, seating, floor height for 550 or 760 mm platforms, traction and battery size, car body material. Each choice moves mass, cost, capacity, energy and dwell time; a check panel flags TSI and EN limits (axle load, PRM step and gap, crash zones, fire category). Then the train runs on the lab's lines for a simulated week in ARail's operations and passenger simulation: dwell times, crowding, battery range on the branch, energy cost.
game.win: Meet the customer's specification and every hard limit (a design that cannot be authorised loses the round) at the lowest life-cycle cost, with bonuses for punctuality and passenger satisfaction. In career mode good designs lead to system lead and chief engineer.
game.knowledge: TSI PRM and German platform heights, axle load limits and line categories, the crash scenarios of EN 15227, mass budgets, doors and dwell time, battery range
game.bigGame: Takes the specification from procurement via sales; gives a vehicle type (capacity, reliability, cost, delivery date) to procurement and testing; hidden design flaws become series defects for maintenance development.

roles.name: Manufacturer's sales and bid manager
roles.organisation: Rolling stock or signalling manufacturer (e.g. Siemens Mobility, Alstom, Stadler, CAF, Hitachi Rail) or a major supplier (e.g. Knorr-Bremse)
roles.summary: Wins orders: watches the tenders of railway undertakings, transport authorities and DB InfraGO, decides with management whether to bid, builds price and risk position with engineering, operations and legal, negotiates, and hands over to the contract project manager a contract the company can deliver.
decisions: Bid or no-bid
Set price and margin, balancing win chance against risk
Commit to delivery dates, availability guarantees and LCC values
Accept or negotiate penalty and liability caps
Offer full-service maintenance with the trains
File a complaint (Rüge) against tender conditions or an award, and a review application if it is rejected
effects: A won order fills a plant for years and keeps jobs; an underpriced one loses money for years
Over-promised dates lead to late trains and penalties
Prices and guarantees end up in the cost of rail transport
resources: Bid team of 5-50, bid budget EUR 0.5-5 million for a large tender
Order values from EUR 100 million to several billion with margins of a few per cent
Pricing authority within limits set by a deal approval board
limits: GWB, SektVO and VgV as bidder (complaint and review rules, GWB § 160)

Competition law (GWB § 1, Art. 101 TFEU; e.g. the Bundeskartellamt's rail cartel fines of 2012-2013 and the European Commission's 2018 fine on rail brake suppliers), anti-bribery (StGB § 299), bid rigging (StGB § 298), company compliance
Export control for some markets
Plant capacity and realistic authorisation timelines
risks: Bonus and job tied to orders; criminal risk for cartel agreements, bid rigging or bribery
Travel and deadline pressure
Career damage after a loss-making contract

career.entry: Engineering or business degree, experience in engineering, project management or on the customer side; MBA common
career.chances: About EUR 90,000-160,000 a year with a variable part of 15-30 %; sales directors more

kpis: Claims and penalties in executed contracts
roles.timescale: Months (a bid takes 3-12 months); years for customer relations

game.title: Bid or No Bid
game.loop: A pipeline of tenders arrives (regional EMUs, locomotives, an interlocking). For each the player decides whether to bid, then sets price, delivery date, availability guarantee and a full-service offer; free plant capacity, engineering risk and likely authorisation time are shown with uncertainty. AI competitors bid and the buyer scores price and quality. Won contracts play out in fast-forward with delays, penalties and warranty claims.
game.win: Cumulative profit over ten years with the plant kept busy. A competitor's offer to share the market is a trap: accepting it brings a Bundeskartellamt fine and ends the career.
game.knowledge: Award criteria and scoring, LCC, liquidated damages, capacity planning, competition and compliance rules
game.bigGame: Takes tenders from vehicle procurement, transport authorities and DB InfraGO; gives prices and delivery dates to buyers and work to the project manager, the design and the test engineers.

roles.name: Signalling industry engineer (interlocking and ETCS)
roles.name_de: Projektierungs- und Inbetriebnahmeingenieur/in Stellwerks- und ETCS-Technik (LST)
roles.organisation: Signalling manufacturer, e.g. Siemens Mobility, Alstom, Hitachi Rail (formerly Thales), Scheidt & Bachmann; axle counter makers such as Frauscher
roles.summary: Turns the infrastructure manager's signalling plans into a working interlocking and ETCS for DB InfraGO and other infrastructure managers: the manufacturer-specific project data (route tables, overlaps, flank protection, ETCS data) built on the planner's neutral plans, factory and site tests, and commissioning in a weekend possession.
decisions: Turn the planner's manufacturer-neutral signalling plans (PT 1) into manufacturer-specific project data (PT 2): routes, overlaps, flank protection, speeds, balises and ETCS route data
Write the test cases for the factory acceptance test and the site tests
Decide whether an error needs a new software version or a data correction
Plan the cut-over weekend with a fall-back plan
Give go or no-go for commissioning together with the infrastructure manager
Answer the findings of the independent assessor and the EBA-recognised inspector
effects: Correct data makes the interlocking safe; one wrong flank protection entry is a hidden hazard
A late commissioning keeps the line closed longer and delays digitalisation
Each ETCS project changes capacity and which trains may run
resources: Project budgets of EUR 10-500 million (an electronic interlocking for a mid-sized station roughly EUR 20-60 million; digital nodes much more)
Test labs and simulators, teams of 5-50 engineers
Possessions for tests and cut-over, mostly nights and weekends
limits: EN 50126, EN 50129 (SIL 4 for interlocking functions), EN 50128 now merged into EN 50716 (software), EN 50159 (safe communication)

TSI CCS and the ETCS specifications (Baseline 3); ERA's prior approval of ETCS trackside tender specifications (Directive (EU) 2016/797 Art. 19) and the EBA's authorisation for placing in service of the trackside subsystem (Art. 18)
DB InfraGO rules for signalling planning (Ril 819) and operation (Ril 408), the EBA's product approvals
EBA VV BAU-STE (supervision of signalling, telecommunication and electrical works), acceptance by an EBA-recognised inspector
IT security: IEC 62443, CLC/TS 50701
risks: Criminal liability for safety errors in data or software
Night and weekend work at commissioning; site work next to running trains
High pressure in cut-over weekends

career.entry: Degree in electrical engineering, computer science or railway systems engineering; product training at the manufacturer; DB qualifications for data and test roles
career.chances: IG Metall tariff about EUR 60,000-90,000; senior or project lead EUR 90,000-130,000; strong demand from the digitalisation of the network

kpis: Data errors found in tests vs in service (target zero in service)
Open findings of assessor and inspector
roles.timescale: Months to years (a project); hours during the cut-over weekend

game.title: Route Table (project an interlocking)
game.loop: Bf Neustadt, the station of ARail's signaller game, gets an electronic interlocking in place of its relay interlocking. The player gets the track plan and fills the route table: for each route the points and their positions, the sections that must be clear, the overlap, the flank protection and the conflicting routes. A test bench runs scripted test cases and then the signaller game itself on the player's data, while an AI tester tries to set conflicting routes. Errors found in tests cost time; errors that reach service are hazards that a seeded disruption may turn into an incident.
game.win: All routes correct and complete and commissioned before the possession ends. Data that lets two conflicting routes be set at commissioning is a safety failure that ends the round; in career mode it closes the path to approved inspector.
game.knowledge: Interlocking principles (route locking, flank protection, overlap, conflict matrix), EN 50129 safety logic, test case design, ETCS basics
game.bigGame: Takes the signalling plan from the HOAI planner and possessions from the possession planner; gives an interlocking (capacity, reliability) to the infrastructure manager and the signallers; delays shift the digital rail programme.

roles.name: Conformity assessor (NoBo, DeBo)
roles.name_de: Prüfer/in einer benannten oder bestimmten Stelle (NoBo, DeBo)
roles.organisation: Notified body (NoBo) for TSIs and designated body (DeBo) for national rules, e.g. EISENBAHN-CERT (EBC, at the EBA), TÜV SÜD, TÜV Rheinland, DEKRA, Bureau Veritas; accredited by DAkkS. Many of these bodies also certify ECMs under Regulation (EU) 2019/779
roles.summary: Checks independently that a vehicle, subsystem or interoperability constituent meets the TSIs (as NoBo) and the notified national rules (as DeBo): reviews design and test evidence, witnesses tests and issues the EC certificate of verification that the applicant needs for authorisation. Does not authorise: that is ERA's or the EBA's decision.
decisions: Agree the assessment plan and the conformity modules (e.g. SB type examination with SD or SF for production, or SH1)
Accept or reject design calculations and test reports
Demand or witness additional tests
Issue a certificate, an intermediate statement of verification, or a certificate with conditions
Refuse a certificate while a non-conformity remains
Raise an interpretation question in the NoBo coordination group (NB-Rail)
As ECM certification body: issue, suspend or withdraw an ECM certificate after an audit
effects: Without the certificate the vehicle cannot be authorised: months of delay
A lenient certificate can let a non-compliant vehicle into service
Consistent assessment builds trust in the European authorisation system
resources: Assessment fees of EUR 100,000-2 million per vehicle project; teams of 2-15 experts
Accreditation scope, the TSIs and ERA application guides, time to witness tests
limits: Directive (EU) 2016/797, Decision 2010/713/EU (modules), Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/545
TSI LOC&PAS, WAG, PRM, NOI, SRT, CCS; notified national rules for Germany
Accreditation under ISO/IEC 17065 or 17020 by DAkkS; independence and impartiality
NB-Rail recommendations for use
risks: Professional liability and loss of accreditation for errors
Pressure from applicants who pay the fee
Travel to plants and test sites

career.entry: Engineering degree and several years at a manufacturer, test centre or ECM; qualified within the body's accreditation scope
career.chances: About EUR 60,000-100,000 a year; senior assessors and heads of a NoBo more

roles.timescale: Weeks to months (an assessment)

game.title: Certificate (TSI check)
game.loop: The player receives a new vehicle's technical file as cards: drawings with dimensions (step heights, door widths, handrails), test reports (pass-by noise, braking, crash test) and constituent declarations. With the TSI clauses at hand they mark each item conforming, non-conforming or needing more evidence, and may order tests at a cost in time. Some items are subtly wrong, e.g. noise measured at the wrong speed or a step outside the gap limit.
game.win: Correct decisions within the time limit: points for each non-conformity found, a heavy penalty for certifying a non-conforming vehicle (it later fails in service; in career mode accreditation is lost). Unneeded tests cost the client time and reputation.
game.knowledge: TSI structure and key values (PRM step and gap, noise limits, crash scenarios), conformity modules, the roles of NoBo, DeBo and AsBo and who authorises
game.bigGame: Takes evidence from the manufacturer's engineers and the test engineer; gives certificates or delays to the homologation manager and the authorisation officer and so the delivery date to procurement; as ECM certification body it audits the ECMs.

roles.name: Independent safety assessor (AsBo, CSM-RA)
roles.name_de: Gutachter/in einer Bewertungsstelle (AsBo) bzw. unabhängige/r Sicherheitsgutachter/in (ISA)
roles.organisation: Assessment body (AsBo) under CSM-RA, accredited by DAkkS or recognised by the EBA (e.g. TÜV SÜD, TÜV Rheinland, DEKRA, EBC, independent consultancies); also independent safety assessor (ISA) under EN 50129
roles.summary: Assesses independently whether the risk management process for a significant change (new vehicle, interlocking, operating rule, outsourced maintenance) was applied correctly under CSM-RA and whether its results support safe integration, and writes the safety assessment report. The proposer, not the AsBo, accepts the risk; the report is the evidence it relies on.
decisions: Agree scope and assessment plan with the proposer
Check system definition, hazard identification and hazard log
Judge whether each hazard is controlled by a code of practice, a reference system or explicit risk estimation
Accept or challenge safety requirements (SIL, tolerable hazard rates) and their evidence
Raise findings and decide when they are closed
Issue the safety assessment report, with or without restrictions
effects: Weak assessment lets hazards into service; strong assessment prevents accidents
Many findings delay projects at the proposer's cost
Mutual recognition: an AsBo report must be accepted elsewhere in the EU
resources: Fees of EUR 50,000-1 million per project; small teams of 1-10
Freelance day rates of about EUR 1,000-1,600
limits: Implementing Regulation (EU) 402/2013 (CSM-RA), Annex II for the criteria for assessment bodies
EN 50126, EN 50129 (ISA role), EN 50128 and EN 50657 now merged into EN 50716 (software); ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation
Independence from the proposer; professional liability
risks: Professional and possibly criminal liability after an accident in an assessed system
Commercial pressure from the client; loss of reputation

career.entry: Engineering degree and many years in RAMS, signalling or vehicle engineering; training in CSM-RA and EN 5012x; qualified within an accredited AsBo
career.chances: About EUR 70,000-120,000 a year employed; more as freelancer

kpis: No accident in an assessed system
roles.timescale: Weeks to months

game.title: Hazard Log
game.loop: A proposer presents a change in ARail's world: a new workshop company takes over maintenance, ETCS on the branch line, or driver-only operation with door cameras. The player reads the system definition and hazard log, adds missing hazards, judges each control (code of practice, reference system, explicit estimation) and writes findings. A Monte Carlo run of the disruptions and operations simulation then shows how often uncontrolled hazards became incidents over a year.
game.win: Score from hazards found, correct principles and incidents avoided. Signing off a change with an unmitigated catastrophic hazard ends the round; over-demanding findings cost the proposer time and lower the client score.
game.knowledge: CSM-RA process and principles, significance criteria, risk matrices, SIL and tolerable hazard rates, the AsBo's role next to NoBo and approved inspector, and who accepts the risk
game.bigGame: Takes changes from ECMs, manufacturers and the infrastructure manager; gives safety assessment reports needed for authorisation and go-live; misses become incidents for investigators.

roles.name: Test engineer
roles.organisation: Manufacturer or test centre, e.g. Siemens Mobility Test and Validation Center Wegberg-Wildenrath, DB Systemtechnik (Minden, Kirchmöser), the Velim test ring (CZ), the Rail Tec Arsenal climatic wind tunnel (Vienna)
roles.summary: Plans and runs the tests that prove a new vehicle meets its requirements and the TSIs (running dynamics, braking, pantograph-catenary interaction, compatibility with train detection, noise, climate, ETCS) on test rings and on the open network at night, and writes the test reports for authorisation.
decisions: Plan the test campaign: which tests, where, in which order, on which prototype
Request test paths and possessions (runs up to 10 % above top speed)
Stop a run when measured values exceed limits (derailment quotient, temperatures, contact force)
Decide whether a failed test needs a design change or a retest
Set up and validate the instrumentation
Agree witnessing with the NoBo
effects: A smooth campaign brings authorisation on time; failures cost months
Unsafe test runs endanger staff and the network
Test data become the evidence that millions of journeys rely on
resources: 1-3 prototypes, measuring wheelsets, instrumentation
Test ring days (roughly EUR 20,000-100,000 a day) and test paths on DB InfraGO's network
Test teams of 5-30; campaign budgets of EUR 5-50 million
limits: EN 14363 (running dynamics), EN 50317 and EN 50367 (pantograph-catenary), EN 50121 and ERA's interface document for compatibility with train detection, TSI NOI with ISO 3095 measurements, EN 14531 (braking)
Temporary authorisation for test runs on the network from the EBA (Directive (EU) 2016/797 Art. 21) and test paths from DB InfraGO; operation under Ril 408 with a qualified test train driver
Arbeitszeitgesetz for long night campaigns
risks: Injury on test runs or at the trackside
Night work, travel, weeks away from home
Responsibility for safety decisions during tests

career.entry: Engineering degree (mechanical, electrical, vehicle), measurement and test experience, often from a thesis at a test centre
career.chances: IG Metall or DB tariff, about EUR 55,000-90,000 a year plus travel and night allowances

kpis: Data quality accepted by the NoBo
roles.timescale: Hours (a test run) to months (a campaign)

game.title: Test Campaign
game.loop: The player has 12 weeks to authorisation, two prototypes and a list of required tests. They book test ring days and night paths, order tests with dependencies (braking before high-speed runs) and react to results: a failed compatibility test against axle counters, an overheating converter in the climate chamber, a cancelled path. During a run they watch live values (speed, derailment quotient, contact force) and must stop when a limit is crossed.
game.win: All tests passed with accepted reports before the deadline and within budget; running on past a safety limit causes an incident that ends the round. In career mode success leads to a NoBo or the EBA.
game.knowledge: Which tests the TSIs and EN standards require, test sequencing, limits (Y/Q, contact force), booking test paths
game.bigGame: Takes prototypes from the design engineer and paths from track access sales; gives test reports to the conformity assessor and the homologation manager, delays to procurement.

roles.name: Homologation manager (vehicle authorisation)
roles.organisation: Rolling stock manufacturer; also RUs, keepers and leasing companies for modifications and extensions of the area of use
roles.summary: Plans and drives the authorisation of a vehicle type: chooses the authorisation case and the area of use, runs the optional pre-engagement with ERA and the EBA through the one-stop shop, gathers NoBo, DeBo, AsBo and test evidence into the file, and answers the authorities' issues until the authorisation is granted. The industry counterpart of the EBA's authorisation officer.
decisions: Choose the authorisation case (first authorisation, renewed authorisation, extended area of use, new authorisation after a change, authorisation in conformity to type for series units)
Choose the authorising entity: ERA when the area of use covers several countries; ERA or the EBA for Germany only
Ask for pre-engagement and freeze the requirements and applicable TSI versions at the right moment
Sequence assessments and tests on the critical path
Answer the issues raised by ERA or the EBA in the one-stop shop's issue log; accept conditions and limits of use
Authorise a reduced configuration first to start service earlier
effects: The authorisation date decides when passengers get the new trains and when liquidated damages start
Conditions limit where and how the train may run
A clean file speeds the next type and the next country
resources: Team of 2-15; budget for assessments and tests of EUR 5-30 million per platform
Access to ERA's one-stop shop; contracts with NoBo, DeBo and AsBo
limits: Directive (EU) 2016/797 Art. 21, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/545 (authorisation cases, pre-engagement; decision within four months of a complete file)
TSIs, notified national rules for Germany, CSM-RA
Contract delivery dates and liquidated damages
risks: Career risk when finished trains stand unauthorised; public pressure
Little physical risk; travel

career.entry: Engineering degree and years in design, testing or assessment; knowledge of EU authorisation law
career.chances: About EUR 75,000-120,000 a year; heads of homologation more; scarce specialists

kpis: Conditions and limits in the authorisation
roles.timescale: Months to years

game.title: Authorisation Route
game.loop: A network puzzle: the player places the steps of an authorisation (requirements capture, pre-engagement, design reviews, NoBo, DeBo and AsBo assessments, test campaign, intermediate statements, submission) on a timeline with dependencies and durations. Issues arrive (a revised TSI, an EMC finding, an ERA issue log entry) and the player chooses a response: argue, retest, accept a condition, split configurations.
game.win: Authorisation before the contract delivery date with as few conditions as possible; a missing mandatory step makes the file incomplete and restarts the clock. In career mode it decides the bonus and a move to an authority.
game.knowledge: Authorisation cases and steps of 2018/545, the roles of ERA, EBA, NoBo, DeBo and AsBo, decision deadlines
game.bigGame: Takes reports from the test engineer and assessors; gives the authorisation date to the project manager, procurement and sales; the gate between industry and operation.

roles.name: Manufacturer's contract project manager
roles.organisation: Rolling stock manufacturer (e.g. Siemens Mobility, Alstom, Stadler, CAF, Škoda, Talgo); similar posts at signalling manufacturers
roles.summary: Delivers a won train order: owns schedule, cost and margin of the contract from kick-off to the end of warranty, steers engineering, purchasing, the plant, testing and homologation, and manages the customer, change requests, claims and liquidated damages.
decisions: Re-baseline the delivery schedule and tell the customer when authorisation slips
Accept, price or reject a customer change request (more seats, a new passenger information system)
Hand over units with open items under a concession or hold them until fixed
Expedite or replace a late sub-supplier (bogies, doors, converters)
Offer interim vehicles or a reduced first configuration to cut liquidated damages
Raise claims against the customer for late information or changes, and against suppliers for their delays
Release contingency within the project budget
effects: Late delivery forces the RU to run old trains or replacement buses and to pay the transport authority's penalties
Liquidated damages, often capped at 5-15 % of the contract value, can wipe out the project's margin
Units handed over with open items lower availability in the first years and burden the fleet manager
The project's result decides the plant's year and its jobs
resources: Contract value of EUR 100 million to several billion
Project team of 20-200 across engineering, purchasing, quality, plant and service
Contingency of a few per cent of the contract value
3-6 years to the first delivery, 2-5 years of warranty
limits: The contract: delivery dates, liquidated damages and their caps, availability guarantees, acceptance procedure, warranty
BGB § 650 (contract for the supply of goods to be produced: sales law) and the warranty rules
Directive (EU) 2016/797 and Regulation (EU) 2018/545 (authorisation), the TSIs, CSM-RA for design changes
ISO/TS 22163 quality system; IG Metall tariff and working time in the plant
risks: Career damage after a loss-making or late project; a task force takes over
Public exposure when trains arrive late
Travel and constant deadline pressure
Low criminal risk; compliance risk in claims and supplier dealings

career.entry: Engineering or industrial engineering degree, 5-10 years in engineering, testing or sub-project management, project management certificate (IPMA, PMP)
career.chances: Upper IG Metall tariff or out of tariff: about EUR 90,000-150,000 a year with a bonus tied to the project margin

kpis: Units delivered on the contract dates
Claims recovered from customer and suppliers
roles.timescale: Weeks to years (a project runs 4-8 years including warranty)

game.title: Late Train (deliver the order)
game.loop: Monthly turns over four to six years from contract to the last unit, on a critical-path network of design, supplier deliveries, car body production, tests and authorisation. Each month risks hit (a supplier insolvency, a failed test, a TSI revision, a customer change request); the player spends contingency, adds shifts, accepts or rejects changes and negotiates with the buyer. Delivered units enter ARail's operations fleet: units handed over with open items have more failures and comfort defects, and liquidated damages run per day and unit.
game.win: Project margin at the end of warranty after liquidated damages and warranty cost. A margin below a floor ends the round with the project taken over by a task force; in career mode a project on time and in budget leads to sales director or a customer-side post.
game.knowledge: Critical path and earned value, liquidated damages and caps, change and claim management (Nachtragsmanagement), authorisation timelines, the cost of open items
game.bigGame: Takes the contract from the sales manager and requirements from vehicle procurement; gives delivery dates and unit quality to procurement and the fleet, liquidated damages to the RU's and manufacturer's accounts, workload to the plant.

roles.name: Rolling stock assembly worker and welder
roles.organisation: Rolling stock manufacturer's plant (e.g. Alstom in Bautzen, Hennigsdorf and Salzgitter, Siemens Mobility in Krefeld-Uerdingen, Stadler in Berlin-Pankow)
roles.summary: Builds trains in the plant: welds car bodies, fits bogies, cables, doors, interiors and equipment along the assembly line and tests the finished unit's functions, working to drawings and instructions in a takt.
decisions: Stop the line when a part does not fit or a weld fails inspection
Choose the welding sequence within the welding procedure specification to limit distortion
Report a deviation (non-conformance report) instead of improvising
Check and record torque values
Make improvement proposals (KVP)
effects: Weld and assembly quality decides fatigue life and series defects years later
Line speed decides whether delivery dates hold
Plant jobs and closures are a political issue in the regions
resources: Workstation, tools and welding equipment; a takt of hours to days per station
Drawings and work instructions
limits: EN 15085 (welding of railway vehicles), welders certified to EN ISO 9606
Arbeitsschutzgesetz, DGUV rules (welding fumes, work at height), GefStoffV
IG Metall tariff, Arbeitszeitgesetz, shift agreements
Quality system ISO/TS 22163
risks: Injury, welding fumes, noise
Shift work
Job loss when orders fall or plants close

career.entry: Vocational training (Konstruktionsmechaniker/in, Mechatroniker/in, Elektroniker/in) plus welder certificates to EN ISO 9606
career.chances: IG Metall tariff, about EUR 3,200-4,200 gross a month plus shift allowances; foreman or master craftsman more

roles.timescale: Minutes to a shift

game.title: Car Body Line
game.loop: On a stylised assembly line the player welds and fits a car body in takt: chooses welding sequences (distortion is shown), reads weld symbols, checks parts and torques. Deviations appear (a misfitting bracket, a porous weld); stopping the line costs takt, hiding a deviation creates a hidden defect that may surface years later as a series defect in ARail's operations fleet.
game.win: Quality and takt over a shift; hidden defects found later reduce the score. In career mode it leads to master craftsman or works council paths.
game.knowledge: Weld symbols, EN 15085 basics, distortion, torque, quality reporting
game.bigGame: Takes orders and takt from the project manager and the plant; gives built units and hidden defects to the fleet; plant employment matters to politics and unions.

roles.name: Non-destructive testing inspector (wheelsets and axles)
roles.name_de: Prüfer/in für zerstörungsfreie Prüfung (ZfP) an Radsätzen
roles.organisation: Wheelset shops and heavy-maintenance works (e.g. DB Fahrzeuginstandhaltung), depots, private wagon workshops, NDT service companies; also manufacturers' and wheelset makers' quality departments
roles.summary: Tests axles, wheels and safety-critical welds for cracks with ultrasonic, magnetic particle and eddy-current methods, at the intervals and with the procedures set by maintenance development, and decides as a certified inspector whether a wheelset passes, needs confirmation or is rejected.
decisions: Calibrate the instrument and probes on the reference block before testing
Judge an ultrasonic indication: geometric echo from a transition, corrosion pit or crack
Reject an axle with an indication above the recording or rejection limit
Call for magnetic particle testing to confirm a surface indication after removing the paint
Stop and notify the ECM when the same indication appears on several axles of a series
Refuse to sign when the test conditions (coupling, surface, time per axle) were not met
effects: A missed crack can end in an axle fracture and derailment (Viareggio 2009; the ICE 3 axle fracture at Köln Hbf in 2008)
False rejections scrap axles and wheelsets worth thousands of euros each and drain a stock with lead times of months
Findings feed maintenance development's test intervals and limits
A series finding triggers grounding and a safety alert to other ECMs
resources: Ultrasonic flaw detector with angle probes or a phased-array or automated test bench; magnetic particle equipment
About 20-60 minutes per axle; reference blocks and test procedures
Test records in the maintenance IT
limits: EN ISO 9712 (qualification and certification of NDT personnel, levels 1-3, eyesight tests, renewal after 5 years)

DIN 27201-7 (non-destructive testing in the maintenance of railway vehicles), EN 15313 (in-service wheelset maintenance), EVIC and the VPI maintenance guide for freight wagon axles, EN 13261 (axles) and EN 13262 (wheels)
The ECM's maintenance programme and test procedures; only certified staff may sign
Arbeitsschutzgesetz, Arbeitszeitgesetz, EVG or IG Metall tariff
risks: Criminal investigation (StGB § 222, § 315) if a crack is missed through a test not done to procedure
Loss of certification after failed audits or blind tests
Concentration fatigue in repetitive work; shift work
Pressure to pass wheelsets when stock is short

career.entry: Vocational training as mechanic, mechatronics technician or materials tester (Werkstoffprüfer/in), NDT courses (e.g. at DGZfP) and certification to EN ISO 9712 level 2 in UT and MT; level 3 needs further training and years of practice
career.chances: EVG or IG Metall tariff about EUR 3,300-4,500 gross a month plus allowances; level 3 experts about EUR 60,000-85,000 a year

kpis: Indications correctly classified (audits, blind tests on reference axles)
roles.timescale: Minutes per axle, within a shift

game.title: Echo (find the crack)
game.loop: The player sees the A-scan of an ultrasonic test of an axle and a schematic with the probe position. After calibrating on the reference block, they scan the axle zone by zone; geometric echoes from transitions and the wheel seat appear on every axle, crack echoes only on some. For each indication they decide: ignore, confirm by magnetic particle testing (costs time) or reject. A shift has a quota of axles.
game.win: Correct classifications within the shift. Missed cracks go into ARail's operations fleet as hidden defects with a chance of an axle fracture; a fracture ends the round and in career mode brings an investigation and loss of certification. False rejections drain the wheelset stock of the parts game. High accuracy leads to level 3.
game.knowledge: Ultrasound basics (sound velocity, time of flight, angle probes, near field), axle geometry and crack-prone zones (wheel seat, transitions), recording and rejection limits, EN ISO 9712 levels
game.bigGame: Takes wheelsets from the workshop planner and test intervals from maintenance development; gives pass or reject (wheelset demand) to parts supply, hidden-crack risk to the fleet, series findings to the ECM's safety alerts.

roles.name: Rail construction contractor's estimator and claims manager
roles.organisation: Rail construction company (e.g. Spitzke, Leonhard Weiss, Max Bögl, Strabag Rail, Swietelsky, Hering, Eiffage Rail) bidding for track, catenary and civil works of DB InfraGO and other infrastructure managers
roles.summary: Prices the contractor's bids from the bill of quantities and, during execution, prices and pursues change orders and obstruction claims (Nachträge) under VOB/B when quantities, possessions or the design change. The supply side of the infrastructure manager's tenders.
decisions: Bid or not for a tender, given the crews, machines and possessions already booked
Price each item of the bill of quantities (Leistungsverzeichnis): labour, machines (tamping machine, ballast cleaner, track renewal train), material, overhead, risk and profit
Spot errors in the tender documents and decide whether to ask a bidder question, complain (Rüge) or price them speculatively
Submit a change order when the client orders changed or extra work (VOB/B § 2 (5) and (6))
Notify obstruction in writing (Behinderungsanzeige, VOB/B § 6) when a possession is cancelled or plans arrive late
Settle a claim in negotiation or take it to an expert, conciliation or court
effects: Low bids win work but can turn into losses that end in claims disputes
Claims shift cost to the infrastructure manager and so to the federal funds behind it (LuFV, BSWAG)
A cancelled possession (Sperrpause) leaves crews and machines idle at tens of thousands of euros per shift
Disputes delay the final account by years
resources: Tenders of EUR 1-100 million with margins of a few per cent
Estimating software, unit costs from past jobs, machine hourly rates
A team of 2-15 estimators and claims managers
limits: GWB part 4 and SektVO (DB InfraGO as sector contracting entity) with DB's tender conditions; VOB/A for public clients outside the sector rules
VOB/B as contract terms (§ 2 remuneration and quantity changes over 10 %, § 6 obstruction, § 13 defects), BGB §§ 650a ff. (construction contract law since 2018)
DB's prequalification of contractors, the construction tariffs and the posting rules for foreign crews
GWB § 1 and StGB § 298 (bid rigging), StGB § 299 (bribery)
risks: Job risk after loss-making jobs
Criminal risk for bid rigging and bribery
Stress near bid deadlines and in disputes

career.entry: Civil engineering degree (Bauingenieurwesen) or state-certified technician, years as site engineer or site manager
career.chances: About EUR 55,000-95,000 a year; head of estimating or commercial manager EUR 100,000 and more

kpis: Margin of won jobs against the estimate
roles.timescale: Weeks (a bid) to years (claims)

game.title: Unit Price (bid and claim)
game.loop: Act 1: the player prices a track renewal at Bf Neustadt from a bill of quantities of about 15 items (with a hidden quantity error) against AI bidders. Act 2: during execution in ARail's infrastructure module, possessions are cancelled, the client changes the design and quantities differ; the player writes change orders and obstruction notices with the right VOB/B basis and within the deadlines, and the client's construction supervisor (AI) accepts or contests them.
game.win: Final margin of the job. Claims without timely notice are lost; a competitor's call proposing to split the tenders is bid rigging that ends the career.
game.knowledge: Unit price calculation, VOB/B §§ 2 and 6 (quantity deviations over 10 %, changed and extra work, obstruction), tender questions and complaints, bid rigging
game.bigGame: Takes tenders from the infrastructure manager's procurement and budget; gives prices to the IM's budget years, crews and machines to possessions, claims to the IM's accounts.

roles.name: Station service staff
roles.organisation: Station operator: DB InfraGO AG, business unit passenger stations (Personenbahnhöfe, until 2023 DB Station&Service AG), regional station management (Bahnhofsmanagement)
roles.summary: The face of the station: answers travellers at the information desk (DB Information) and on the platforms, guides them when trains change platform or are cancelled, gives the boarding assistance (ramp or mobile lift) booked through the Mobility Service Centre (Mobilitätsservice-Zentrale), and reports faults, dirt and dangers to the 3-S centre. Informs about passenger rights but does not decide claims; that is the railway undertaking's job.
decisions: Announce and guide a short-notice platform change
Choose whom to help first when a queue forms at the information desk
Send stranded travellers to the rail replacement bus (SEV), the next train or another route
Fetch the ramp or the mobile lift (Hublift) and help a booked wheelchair user board within the dwell time
Report a broken lift, a dark display or a dangerous spot to the 3-S centre
Call security or the Federal Police when a conflict escalates
Tell a traveller what their ticket and their passenger rights allow after a delay (the claim itself is decided by the railway undertaking)
Close off an overcrowded or icy platform access under house rights and report it to the 3-S centre
effects: Travellers catch or miss their trains after platform changes: departure delays, broken connections
Assistance on time keeps the train's dwell time; a late ramp or lift delays it by minutes
Wrong information turns into complaints and compensation claims at the railway undertaking's passenger rights centre (Servicecenter Fahrgastrechte)
Fault reports start repairs (lifts, displays) through the 3-S centre and facility management
Calm guidance prevents crowding on narrow platforms and accidents at the platform edge
resources: 1-4 staff per shift at a mid-size station, dozens around the clock at a main station (Hauptbahnhof); most small stations are unstaffed
Radio to the 3-S centre; the passenger information system (RIS) app with live train data, platform changes and coach orders
A portable ramp or a mobile lift (Hublift) and the day's list of assistance bookings from the Mobility Service Centre
The station operator's house rights (Hausrecht), no police powers
Small goodwill (water in a heatwave, snack vouchers in long disruptions) as the station management or the railway undertaking provides it
limits: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 on rail passenger rights: information (Art. 9), assistance to persons with reduced mobility at stations by the station manager (Art. 23), on notice of at least 24 h (Art. 24)
EBO § 2 (3) (railways' programmes for barrier-free use) and § 13 (platform heights)
Ril 813 of the station operator (passenger stations): the danger zone along the platform edge, marked by the white line, wider where trains pass at high speed
TSI PRM (Regulation (EU) 1300/2014): platform heights, boarding aids designed for 300 kg
Station infrastructure use conditions (INBP) and the station house rules (Hausordnung)
Working-time law (ArbZG) and the EVG collective agreements at DB (shift lengths, rest periods, allowances)
GDPR for lost property and the health data in assistance bookings (Art. 9 GDPR)
risks: Verbal and physical assaults by angry travellers
Shift work at nights, weekends and holidays, outdoors in heat and cold
Injury at the platform edge, back strain from ramps, lifts and luggage
Stress in major disruptions with hundreds of travellers asking at once
Disciplinary consequences for misconduct or for leaving a booked traveller behind

career.entry: Apprenticeship Kaufmann/-frau für Verkehrsservice (3 years, IHK, focus Sicherheit und Service) or lateral entry with a few weeks of internal training; customer service and foreign languages count
career.chances: About 2,800-3,500 € gross a month (EVG tariff at DB) plus shift, night and Sunday allowances; apprentices about 1,100-1,400 €. Team leader after a few years, station manager with further training (business economist course or a degree); lateral moves into train dispatch, train crew or signalling with paid retraining.

kpis: Travellers served and waiting time at the desk
roles.timescale: Minutes, within a shift

game.title: Platform change!
game.loop: A busy morning on the lab station: the scenario moves trains to other platforms, cancels them or replaces them by buses. The player is one service worker with a radio and chooses where to stand, whom to answer (each question has a right answer: the next train, ticket validity, passenger rights) and when to fetch the ramp or lift for a booked assistance. The passenger and journey simulations show who reaches their train and how long trains stand.
game.win: Score from travellers who catch their train or the right alternative, assistance served before departure, correct answers, and dwell-time delays caused. A round lasts 30 simulated minutes (about 15 real ones). It fails if a booked wheelchair user is left behind or a traveller falls at the edge of a platform the player should have closed off. In the career mode a failed round means a talk with the station manager and a refresher course; passed rounds count towards the platform dispatcher, the 3-S centre or the station manager.
game.knowledge: Passenger rights after delays (compensation 25 % from 60 min and 50 % from 120 min, paid by the railway undertaking; refreshments from 60 min; another train when 20 min of delay at the destination are expected; a taxi up to 120 € when an arrival between 0:00 and 5:00 is expected 60 min late or the last connection of the day fails); force majeure (persons on the track, storms) excludes compensation but not information, rerouting or refreshments; the Deutschlandticket is not valid on IC/ICE apart from a few IC sections opened to local tickets; the saver-fare tie (Zugbindung) is lifted at an expected 20 min delay; platform sectors and the white line; the assistance procedure; reading live train data.
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable, delays and platform changes from the signallers and train dispatchers via the passenger information dispatcher, and the assistance bookings from the mobility service agent; gives dwell-time effects to the trains and the platform dispatcher, complaints and goodwill to the passenger rights agent, fault reports to the 3-S centre and the station facility technician.

roles.name: 3-S centre operator (service, security, cleanliness)
roles.organisation: Station operator (DB InfraGO, business unit passenger stations), regional 3-S centre (3-S-Zentrale), working hand in hand with the Federal Police and DB Sicherheit
roles.summary: Watches the stations of a region from a control room: video, help and emergency call points (Info- und Notrufsäulen), the status of lifts and escalators; dispatches service, security and cleaning staff and is the first point of contact for the Federal Police, the fire brigade and the railway's emergency control centre (Notfallleitstelle) when something happens at a station.
decisions: Answer an emergency call point and decide whom to send
Dispatch security, cleaning or service staff to an incident
Hand an unattended item over to the Federal Police and prepare closing a station area (the police decide)
Report a lift or escalator fault to facility management and warn the Mobility Service Centre
Order extra cleaning, security or winter service before a football match or a frost
Report a person on the track at once to the signaller or the emergency control centre so that trains are stopped
Release video footage only on a lawful request from police or prosecutors
Make a station announcement or change a display text when the central passenger information cannot
effects: Response time decides injuries, damage and the feeling of safety
Closing a platform or a station holds trains and passengers: delays, broken connections
A late lift report strands wheelchair users and produces complaints
Staff sent to the wrong place leave other stations unattended
Mistakes with video become data protection cases
resources: A control room with 3-8 operators per shift for a region of dozens to a few hundred stations
Hundreds of cameras, help and emergency call points, the facility status of lifts and escalators (FaSta)
Dispatchable staff: DB Sicherheit patrols, service staff, the cleaning contractor's on-call team, lift and facility technicians
Direct lines to the Federal Police, the DB emergency control centre (Notfallleitstelle), the signallers, fire brigade and ambulance
limits: GDPR: video by a private-law operator such as DB InfraGO rests on Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (since the Federal Administrative Court's ruling of 2019, § 4 BDSG binds only public bodies), with signs and deletion after a few days
House rights only; the Federal Police (railway police, § 3 BPolG) decides on unattended items, evacuations and closures for danger

Ril 408 (Fahrdienstvorschrift): a danger in the track goes at once to the signaller, who stops the trains; Ril 123 of DB InfraGO (emergency management): the reporting chain to the emergency control centre and the emergency manager
Regulation (EU) 2021/782 (information and assistance to passengers)
Service levels and response times in the security and cleaning contracts
Working-time law (ArbZG), the EVG shift agreements, screen work rules (ArbStättV Annex 6)
risks: Wrong triage in an emergency, with disciplinary and in extreme cases criminal consequences (negligent bodily harm, failure to render assistance, § 323c StGB)
Stress from simultaneous incidents and distressing images (suicides, assaults)
Night shifts and screen fatigue
Personal responsibility for data protection breaches

career.entry: Experience as station service or security staff, or an apprenticeship as Fachkraft für Schutz und Sicherheit or in a commercial job, plus internal training (radio procedure, video rules, emergency management)
career.chances: About 3,000-4,000 € gross a month (EVG tariff) plus shift allowances; shift leader, then station management, or with operational training the emergency management of the infrastructure manager.

kpis: Time from call to someone at the scene
Lift and escalator availability reported and followed up
Cleanliness and security grades in station quality checks
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, a shift

game.title: Eyes on the station
game.loop: The player sees the lab station through cameras (views of the passenger simulation) and a queue of calls: a stuck lift, vomit on the stairs, an unattended suitcase, a crowd surge after a match, a person reported near the track. With two security patrols, one service worker and one cleaning team the player dispatches, escalates to the Federal Police, the signaller or the emergency control centre, closes areas and makes announcements; each choice changes the crowd, the trains and the passengers' mood.
game.win: Score from response times weighted by severity, the passengers' mood, train delays caused by closures, and lawful handling of video. A round has 6-10 incidents in about 20 minutes. It fails if a danger to people is not escalated in time (a person on the track not reported to the signaller or emergency control centre within a minute, a trapped person in a lift left without a technician) or footage is released unlawfully. In the career mode a failed round leads to an incident review with the station manager.
game.knowledge: Who decides what: house rights against police powers (BPolG); the danger report to the signaller and the reporting chain of Ril 123; video rules under the GDPR; priorities of incidents; the meaning of the facility status.
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from the passenger and infrastructure simulations (lift and display faults) and the crowds that the timetable and events bring; gives danger reports and closures to the signaller and the emergency manager, jobs to cleaners, security and the station facility technician, reports to the station manager, footage to the Federal Police.

roles.name: Station cleaner
roles.organisation: A facility services company (DB's own facility subsidiary or an external contractor) under a cleaning contract with DB InfraGO, business unit passenger stations
roles.summary: Keeps platforms, stairs, underpasses, waiting areas and toilets clean on a timed route, removes litter, graffiti and hazardous waste, and in winter clears and grits platforms and stairs: what travellers see first of the railway's quality.
decisions: Choose the order of the route when the shift's tasks do not fit the time
Deal with an urgent mess first (vomit, broken glass, spilt drinks on stairs) or keep to the route
Put up a wet-floor sign and block the area while it dries
Pick up a used syringe by the sharps procedure or call for help
Clear and grit the platforms before the first train in frost
Step back behind the white line when a through train is announced
Report graffiti, damage and a broken lift or light to the 3-S centre
Refuse an unsafe task, such as cleaning at the platform edge while trains pass
effects: Cleanliness grades in the station quality checks, which decide the contractor's bonus or penalty
Slips and falls prevented or caused (the operator's duty of care, Verkehrssicherungspflicht, and liability under § 823 BGB)
Travellers' satisfaction and the station's image
Short platform closures for incidents, which can hold trains
The cleaner's own health (cuts, chemicals, back)
resources: A shift of 6-8 hours with a route plan; 1-3 cleaners at a mid-size station, teams of 10-30 around the clock at a main station
Cleaning trolley, scrubber-drier, sharps container, gritting material and snow shovels
Contract volume of a few hundred thousand to several million euros a year per group of stations
No authority over travellers; can only report to the 3-S centre
limits: Wage agreement of the building cleaning trade (Lohntarifvertrag Gebäudereinigerhandwerk, IG BAU), as a rule declared generally binding: lowest pay group about 14-15 € an hour in 2026, above the statutory minimum wage of 13.90 € (MiLoG)
Framework agreement of the trade (Rahmentarifvertrag: working time, night and Sunday allowances)
Hazardous substances ordinance (GefStoffV), safety data sheets, skin protection
Biological agents ordinance (BioStoffV, risk assessment under TRBA 400) for sharps and body fluids; hepatitis B vaccination offered under the ArbMedVV
Platform work: stay behind the white line when trains pass (Ril 813 and the operator's safety instructions); work in the track area only under DGUV Vorschrift 78 with safety staff
ArbSchG § 9 (3): the right to leave the workplace in immediate danger; ArbZG, night work (§ 6 ArbZG)
Service specification and penalties of the cleaning contract (Leistungsverzeichnis, quality audits)
risks: Needle-stick injuries (hepatitis, HIV), cuts, chemical burns
Slips, falls, and danger from passing trains at the platform edge
Abuse and assaults, especially at night
Low pay, part-time and fixed-term contracts; job loss when the cleaning contract is re-tendered
Night and weekend work

career.entry: No formal training needed: a few days on the job and a safety briefing for platforms; for skilled posts the apprenticeship Gebäudereiniger/in (3 years)
career.chances: About 2,300-2,600 € gross a month full-time at the tariff; foreman (Vorarbeiter/in) about 16-19 € an hour; site manager of the contract (Objektleiter/in) 3,500-4,500 €. Moves into station service or train cleaning at a railway company.

kpis: Cleanliness grade in quality audits (penalties below the contract's threshold)
Route tasks done in the shift
Response time to urgent cleaning requests
Accidents of travellers and of the cleaner
roles.timescale: Minutes; the route of a shift

game.title: Clean sweep
game.loop: A shift on the lab station: where the passenger simulation crowds people, litter builds up; rain brings mud and frost brings ice; the 3-S centre radios urgent jobs. The player moves the cleaner along a route (platforms, underpass, stairs, toilets) and chooses what to do next and how thoroughly, while trains pass at the platform edge and an inspector checks areas at random times.
game.win: Score from the inspector's grades, urgent jobs done in time, no traveller slipping, and the shift's time kept. One shift takes 15-20 minutes. It fails with a needle-stick injury (sharps procedure skipped), a traveller's fall on an unmarked wet floor, or the cleaner in front of the white line when a through train passes. In the career mode a bad audit costs the contractor a penalty and the cleaner a warning; good shifts lead to foreman.
game.knowledge: GHS hazard pictograms and mixing bans, the sharps procedure, marking wet floors, the winter duty of care (clear before the first train), the white line and the announcement of through trains.
game.bigGame: Takes passenger volumes from the timetable, crowds from disruptions and jobs from the 3-S centre; gives cleanliness grades to the station manager (station quality, the contract's penalties) and to the transport authority's station quality reports, accident reports to the 3-S centre.

roles.name: Station retail tenant
roles.organisation: Tenant of the station operator (DB InfraGO, letting of station space): a shop, kiosk, bakery or restaurant, often a franchise of a chain
roles.summary: Runs a shop or restaurant in the station on a lease with the station operator and lives off the footfall the trains bring; the rent, often a share of turnover, helps finance the station.
decisions: Set opening hours within the lease's operating obligation and the shop-opening rules for stations
Order tomorrow's fresh goods from the expected footfall
Plan staff per hour (part-time, mini-jobs) around the rush hours
Fit the assortment to travel needs (Reisebedarf), in many Länder the only goods allowed on Sundays
Negotiate the lease: turnover rent, minimum rent, service charges, fit-out
React to a disruption with extra staff and stock when travellers are stranded
Claim a rent reduction (§ 536 BGB) when station works block the access for months
effects: The station operator's letting income and the station's attractiveness
Wasted fresh food or lost sales
Travellers' comfort (food, drinks, warmth) in disruptions
Jobs at the station and social control (more people, fewer dark corners)
resources: A shop of 20-300 m² with 2-30 staff
Turnover from about 300,000 € (kiosk) to several million € a year (large restaurant in a main station)
Rent of roughly 8-20 % of turnover with a minimum rent, plus service charges
Footfall data from the station operator: tens of thousands to over 500,000 people a day at the largest stations
limits: Shop-opening law: § 8 Ladenschlussgesetz (where a Land has not legislated) and the Länder shop-opening laws let station shops open longer and on Sundays, limited to travel needs (Reisebedarf)
Food hygiene: Regulation (EC) 852/2004, LMHV, HACCP; instruction of food staff under § 43 IfSG
The commercial lease with the station operator (operating obligation, opening hours, branding, deliveries; rent reduction under § 536 BGB)
Minimum wage (MiLoG, 13.90 € an hour in 2026), working-time law (ArbZG), Sunday work rules
Station house rules and fire protection
Youth protection act (JuSchG) for alcohol and tobacco
risks: Insolvency when footfall drops (works, pandemics, competition)
Personal liability as sole trader, or as managing director of a GmbH
Theft, robbery, assaults at night
Long hours, Sunday and holiday work
Fines after food hygiene inspections

career.entry: No licence; capital for fit-out and franchise fee (50,000-500,000 €), experience in retail or catering
career.chances: Owner's income very variable, from a loss to 3,000-8,000 € a month; staff at minimum wage to retail and catering tariffs (about 13.90-17 € an hour). A successful franchisee grows to several stores; some move into the station operator's letting and station management.

kpis: Turnover per day and spend per passer-by
Rent as a share of turnover
roles.timescale: Hours (staffing), days (ordering), years (lease)

game.title: Footfall
game.loop: The player runs a bakery kiosk in the lab station for a simulated week. Each evening they order fresh goods and plan staff hours for tomorrow; during the day the passenger simulation brings customers with the timetable, and disruptions (cancellations, a crowd surge, a track closed for works) change the footfall. Each evening shows sales, waste, wages, rent and profit.
game.win: Profit over the week with waste under 10 % and no hygiene breach; five days in about 20 minutes. Bankruptcy (cash below zero) ends the round. In the career mode the profit is the player's income; in the big game the rent is the station operator's letting income.
game.knowledge: The newsvendor problem (the best order quantity at the critical ratio of margin to the cost of waste), turnover-rent arithmetic, the shop-opening rules for stations, hygiene basics.
game.bigGame: Takes footfall from the timetable and the railway undertakings' trains, closures and works from the infrastructure manager; gives rent to the station operator (letting income that offsets station charges), comfort for stranded travellers in disruptions, complaints to the station manager.

roles.name: Bus and tram operations controller
roles.organisation: Municipal bus and tram operator (kommunaler Verkehrsbetrieb), operations control centre (Leitstelle)
roles.summary: Watches every bus and tram of a city in the computer-aided dispatch system (ITCS, rechnergestütztes Betriebsleitsystem RBL), keeps headways and connections, holds buses at the station for late trains, sends spare vehicles, sets up diversions and provides buses for rail replacement services.
decisions: Hold a bus at the station for passengers of a late train, or let it leave on time
Send a spare bus into a gap or onto an overcrowded line
Short-turn a tram to restore the headway
Set up a diversion when a street or a tram track is blocked
Provide buses and drivers for a rail replacement service ordered by a railway undertaking
Ask the railway undertaking's dispatcher to hold the last train for a late bus (the railway decides)
Inform passengers on the stop displays and by announcement
Call police and ambulance for an incident on a vehicle and relieve the driver
effects: Connections made or broken at the interchange (passengers' travel time, complaints)
Delays propagating along a line and buses bunching
Drivers' working time and the cost of extra vehicles
Penalties or bonuses in the public service contract with the transport authority (punctuality, reliability)
resources: A control room with 2-10 dispatchers for a fleet of about 100 to over 1,000 buses and trams
ITCS with live positions, voice and data radio to every vehicle, displays at stops (DFI)
A few spare vehicles and drivers on standby per shift
Live delays of trains through a data interface with the railway
limits: PBefG (passenger transport act), BOKraft (buses), BOStrab (trams)
Public service contract under Regulation (EC) 1370/2007 with the municipal transport authority (Aufgabenträger), the local transport plan (Nahverkehrsplan)
Connection rules of the transport association (e.g. waiting at most 3-5 minutes)
Drivers' working and break times: ArbZG, FPersV, Regulation (EC) 561/2006 for lines over 50 km; TV-N collective agreement of the Land (ver.di)
StVO and the road authority's orders for diversions
risks: Stress from simultaneous incidents, shift work
Responsibility after an accident caused by an instruction
Public criticism for missed connections and gaps in service

career.entry: Experience as bus or tram driver plus internal training, or the apprenticeship Fachkraft im Fahrbetrieb (3 years); further training to Verkehrsmeister/in (IHK)
career.chances: About 3,500-4,500 € gross a month (TV-N, plus shift allowances); shift leader, head of operations, or planning at the transport authority.

kpis: Cost of spare vehicles and overtime
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes, a shift

game.title: Hold or go
game.loop: The lab town's bus lines 62 and 85 meet the trains at the bus station Bahnhof. The player sees the buses on the streets and the trains' live delays; for each bus about to leave the station they decide to hold it for a late train (shown: how many want to change) or keep the headway, and they can send a spare bus or short-turn one. The journeys show who reaches their aim and how long others waited.
game.win: Score from the passengers' total lost time, connections kept, regularity of the lines and the cost of spare buses. A morning peak takes 20-30 minutes. It fails if a driver's break is cut below the rules or a chain of held buses breaks the following connections for many. In the career mode good shifts lead to shift leader.
game.knowledge: Connection rules, headway control and bunching, the trade-off between waiting at the stop and delay on board, drivers' break rules.
game.bigGame: Takes train delays from the railway undertakings' dispatchers and the signallers, orders for replacement buses from the replacement service coordinator; gives connections to travellers, punctuality to the transport authority's contract, buses for rail replacement.

roles.name: Bus or tram driver at the interchange
roles.organisation: Municipal bus and tram operator, or a private bus company working as its subcontractor
roles.summary: Drives a bus or tram on a line through the town to the station: keeps to the timetable, lets people on and off safely, helps wheelchair users and prams aboard, checks or sells tickets, and waits for connections when the control centre says so.
decisions: Leave on time or wait for people running from a late train
Kneel the bus or lay the ramp for a wheelchair user or a pram
Refuse boarding when the bus is full
Check a ticket, or let it go to avoid a conflict
Brake hard for a hazard, knowing standing passengers may fall
Report a dangerous passenger or an incident to the control centre
Take the break at the terminus even when running late
effects: Punctuality and regularity of the line
Connections at the station
Safety of passengers (falls on board) and of cyclists and pedestrians
Fare revenue and fare evasion
The driver's own health and working time
resources: A bus (12-18 m, 70-150 passengers, 300,000-800,000 €) or a tram (2-4 million €)
Radio to the control centre, the on-board computer showing the deviation from the timetable
Layover time at the terminus in the timetable
The transport conditions (Beförderungsbedingungen) and house rules, no further powers
limits: Driving licence class D (FeV) and the professional driver qualification (BKrFQG: initial qualification, 35 hours of further training every 5 years); tram drivers trained and licensed by the company under BOStrab
StVO, BOKraft, BOStrab, PBefG (obligation to carry, § 22)
Working and break times: ArbZG, FPersV (in urban line service up to 50 km breaks may be taken as layovers totalling one sixth of the driving time), Regulation (EC) 561/2006 for lines over 50 km
TV-N collective agreement (ver.di) or the private bus sector's agreements
Fares and conditions of the transport association (increased fare, usually 60 €, for riding without a valid ticket, § 9 VO-ABB)
risks: Road accidents with criminal liability (negligent bodily harm, § 229 StGB) and loss of licence
Assaults by passengers
Split shifts, back problems, stress
Medical checks for class D (FeV Annexes 5 and 6) can end the career

career.entry: Licence class D with the professional driver qualification (often paid by the employer or the employment agency, 6-12 months), or tram driver training of about 3 months at the operator; apprenticeship Fachkraft im Fahrbetrieb (3 years)
career.chances: About 2,800-3,500 € gross a month under TV-N, less at private subcontractors; the driver shortage gives job security; moves into the control centre, to instructor, or to train driver by lateral entry.

roles.timescale: Seconds (driving), minutes (stops), a shift

game.title: Line 62
game.loop: The player drives a bus of line 62 round the lab town on ARail's streets: at each stop they decide how long to wait, whether to kneel or lay the ramp, whether to check tickets; at the bus station they see trains arriving late and the control centre's instruction. Traffic, a crowd of pupils at the school and a wheelchair user at a stop create the dilemmas.
game.win: Score from punctuality, passengers carried, connections kept, no falls on board and a break taken. A round trip takes 15-25 minutes. It fails with an accident (too fast at a junction, harsh braking with people standing) or a passenger refused against the obligation to carry. In the career mode failures mean a test drive with the instructor.
game.knowledge: StVO at stops (§ 20: hazard lights, passing buses at walking speed), the obligation to carry, break rules, ticket types (Deutschlandticket, school tickets).
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable and holding instructions from the control centre and train arrivals from the operations; gives connections and delays to travellers and the control centre, fare revenue to the bus operator.

roles.name: Taxi driver
roles.organisation: Taxi company or self-employed taxi operator, licensed by the municipality
roles.summary: Waits at the station's taxi rank and drives travellers the last mile, above all at night and when trains fail; the link between the railway and places without buses, and the railway's fallback when passenger rights promise a taxi.
decisions: Wait in the queue at the station rank or take app orders elsewhere
Head for the station when the board shows cancellations or a late last train
