Accept a railway taxi voucher (Taxigutschein) or ask for cash and give a receipt for the claim
Take a short trip from the rank (it may not be refused)
Drive another hour or stop at the working-time limit
Drive as a replacement taxi for a railway undertaking on a contract
effects: Stranded travellers get home at night (passenger rights fulfilled)
The railway undertaking's cost for taxis
The driver's income and empty kilometres
Traffic and parking pressure on the station forecourt
resources: One car (30,000-60,000 €) with taximeter, and a licence per vehicle (Konzession) from the municipality
A place in the station rank shared with 5-50 taxis, a dispatch radio or app
A fixed tariff set by the municipality
limits: PBefG: licence (§ 13), operating obligation (§ 21), obligation to carry (§ 22, for taxis § 47 (4) within the compulsory area), taxi tariffs (§ 51)
Permit for passenger transport (Fahrerlaubnis zur Fahrgastbeförderung, § 48 FeV: medical check, police record), a local knowledge test only where the municipality still requires it
The local taxi regulations (Taxenordnung: order at the rank)
Minimum wage (MiLoG, 13.90 € an hour in 2026) for employed drivers; ArbZG
Fiscal rules for taximeters (KassenSichV)
Rail passenger rights (EVO): the railway pays a taxi up to 120 € when an arrival between 0:00 and 5:00 is expected 60 minutes late or the last connection of the day fails
risks: Robbery and assaults at night
Road accidents and loss of licence
Low, volatile income; competition from ride-hailing with hire cars (Mietwagen, § 49 PBefG)
Long hours sitting, night work

career.entry: Driving licence class B held for 2 years, the permit for passenger transport; as operator the professional competence test at the IHK
career.chances: Employed drivers about minimum wage up to 2,500 € gross a month; self-employed 1,800-3,500 € after costs; growth into a taxi company with several cars.

roles.timescale: Minutes (trips), a shift

game.title: Last train
game.loop: A night shift in the lab town: the player sees the station's departure board, their place in the rank and app orders from the town. Every arriving train brings travellers of whom some want a taxi (more at night and after cancellations, when the railway pays); the player chooses to queue, cruise or take an app order, and when to stop.
game.win: Net income of the night after fuel and hours, without refusing an obligatory trip and within the working-time limit; 10-15 minutes. A refused short trip costs a fine; driving on past the limit raises the risk of an accident that ends the round. In the career mode income and reputation carry over.
game.knowledge: Tariff calculation, the obligation to carry, the passenger-rights taxi rule (120 €, arrivals between 0:00 and 5:00, last connection).
game.bigGame: Takes arrivals, cancellations and night delays from the railway undertakings; gives the transport of stranded travellers (passenger rights fulfilled) and its cost to the passenger rights agent, road traffic to the town.

roles.name: Commuter
roles.organisation: Public: an employee or self-employed person travelling to work
roles.summary: Travels to work every day by train, bus, bike or car: the railway's most regular customer, whose choice of mode, ticket and connection decides ridership and whose complaints reach the media and politics.
decisions: Choose the mode: train, bus, bike and ride, park and ride or car
Buy the Deutschlandticket or a job ticket, or pay per trip
Choose a train with a safe transfer or a faster one with a tight change
Leave earlier when works or a strike are announced
Claim compensation for delays
Complain, join the passenger association, or go back to the car
Ask the employer for flexible hours or working from home
effects: Ridership and fare revenue (shared out through the Deutschlandticket's revenue distribution)
Peak crowding and dwell times on platforms and trains
Road traffic and emissions when switching to the car
Pressure on politics and the railway through complaints and the media
Compensation costs for the railway undertaking
resources: Time: 30-90 minutes a day
Money: Deutschlandticket 63 € a month (2026), job ticket with employer subsidy; commuting allowance of 0.38 € per km in the income tax from 2026
Information: DB Navigator, the transport association's app, live delays
limits: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 and the EVO: compensation 25 % from 60 minutes, 50 % from 120 minutes, paid by the railway undertaking; with the Deutschlandticket a flat 1.50 € per delay of 60 minutes; nothing paid below 4 € (claims can be collected); no compensation for force majeure such as extreme weather or persons on the track (since June 2023)
With an expected delay of 20 minutes at the destination, other trains may be taken; with the Deutschlandticket only local ones, not IC/ICE
Buses and trams: no EU compensation on local lines (Regulation (EU) 181/2011 only from 250 km), only the transport association's own guarantees (e.g. the RMV 10-minute guarantee)
Conditions of the transport association (validity, bikes)
Working hours agreed with the employer (core hours, ArbZG)
risks: Late to work, warnings from the employer
Stress, long days, crowding
The cost of a second car

career.entry: Anyone with a job; in the career mode every railway worker also commutes
career.chances: No pay as a role: its currency is time, money and nerves saved. Railway companies recruit commuters as lateral entrants (Quereinsteiger) with paid retraining to train driver, signaller or conductor.

roles.timescale: Days (a working month)

game.title: Twenty days to work
game.loop: Twenty working days compressed: each morning the player's traveller in the lab town gets the day's outlook (works, weather, a strike warning) and picks mode, departure time and transfer time from ARail's journey planner; then the journey runs through the operations with their delays. In the evening the player can claim compensation, change the ticket or switch to the car.
game.win: Score from punctual arrivals (the boss tolerates three late days), total time, money and stress; 20 days in 10-15 minutes. More than five late days ends with a warning from the employer (round failed). Correct claims add money, wrong ones are rejected.
game.knowledge: Passenger rights (thresholds, the Deutschlandticket rules, force majeure, no EU rights on local buses), reading a travel plan, the transfer-time trade-off.
game.bigGame: Takes the timetable, delays and disruptions from the railway undertakings and the infrastructure manager, fares from the transport authority; gives demand and mode choice to the transport authority's planner and the revenue manager, claims to the passenger rights agent, satisfaction (votes) to politicians.

roles.name: Leisure traveller (tourist or family with children)
roles.organisation: Public
roles.summary: Travels for holidays, family visits or day trips, often with luggage, children, a bike or a pram, on long-distance trains with saver fares: price-sensitive, less practised with the system and hit hardest by a missed connection.
decisions: Book a saver fare tied to one train (Super Sparpreis or Sparpreis, Zugbindung) or a flexible fare
Buy a BahnCard 25 or 50, or not
Reserve seats and bike spaces for the family
Choose a connection with enough transfer time
Find the coach on the platform by the coach order (Wagenreihung)
After a missed connection: take the next train, claim refreshments or a hotel, or give up the trip
Claim compensation
effects: Revenue of long-distance services and the yield of saver fares
Luggage and crowds on platforms, longer dwell times
Compensation, hotel and taxi costs of the railway undertaking
The railway's image in social media
resources: A budget of 50-500 € per trip for a family
Children under 6 free; children of 6 to 14 free with parents or grandparents when entered on the ticket
Apps and the information staff at stations
limits: Regulation (EU) 2021/782: rerouting (Art. 18), compensation (Art. 19), refreshments from 60 minutes of delay and a hotel when an overnight stay becomes necessary (Art. 20); under DB's conditions the tie to a train is lifted when 20 minutes of delay at the destination are expected
DB's conditions of carriage (BB Personenverkehr): luggage, bikes, reservations
A reservation is lost (and its fee refunded) when a train runs with a different coach set
risks: A missed holiday, extra costs, being stranded at night
Stress with children
Falls with luggage on stairs and at the platform edge

career.entry: Anyone
career.chances: No pay; budget, time and the family's mood are the currency. Frequent travellers become passenger advocates (Pro Bahn) or travel writers.

roles.timescale: Hours (a journey)

game.title: Holiday with three children
game.loop: A family travels from the lab town to the sea with two changes. The player books (saver or flexible fare, BahnCard, reservations) and packs (luggage, pram), then plays the day: a platform change, a reversed coach order, a missed connection at a station beyond the layout. At every snag they choose an action (next train, ask staff, refreshments, hotel, taxi) and the family's mood reacts.
game.win: Arrive within budget with the family's mood above zero and the claims correctly filed; 15-20 minutes with short questions at each snag. Failure: stranded overnight without using the rights (hotel paid themselves), or a child left behind at a platform change.
game.knowledge: Ticket types and the tie to a train, children's fares, passenger rights (refreshments, hotel, compensation), coach order and platform sectors.
game.bigGame: Takes fares from the revenue manager and trains with delays from the operations; gives demand for saver fares, compensation claims and reviews (reputation) to the railway undertaking and the press.

roles.name: Wheelchair user
roles.organisation: Public
roles.summary: Travels in a wheelchair and depends on step-free stations, working lifts, the right platform height and booked boarding help; every broken lift or missing ramp turns a journey into a dead end.
decisions: Plan a route through step-free stations only
Book boarding help with the Mobility Service Centre (by law at least 24 hours ahead), or travel spontaneously and hope for staff
Check the lift status before leaving
Choose a train with level boarding or a ramp
Wait for help, or ask other passengers when assistance does not come
Complain to the railway, the arbitration body (söp) or the EBA as enforcement body, or go to court
Join the station operator's accessibility advisory group or a disability association
effects: Demand for assistance and staff time at stations
Delays when boarding takes longer than the dwell time
Pressure on the priorities of station modernisation (lifts, raising platforms)
Complaints that test the railway's legal duties
resources: A manual or electric wheelchair (TSI PRM boarding aids are designed for 300 kg with the user)
Severely disabled person's card: with mark 'G' or 'aG' free local transport with a token (Wertmarke, § 228 SGB IX); with mark 'B' a companion travels free, also on DB long-distance trains
The Mobility Service Centre's booking line, apps showing lift status
limits: Regulation (EU) 2021/782 Arts. 21-25: accessibility, information, assistance free of charge on notice of at least 24 h, compensation for lost or damaged mobility equipment; the EBA enforces it in Germany
TSI PRM (Regulation (EU) 1300/2014): wheelchair spaces, boarding aids; platform heights 55 or 76 cm, 96 cm on some S-Bahn networks (EBO § 13)
EBO § 2 (3): railways' programmes for barrier-free use
Disability equality act (BGG); PBefG § 8 (3): local transport plans had to aim at full accessibility by 1 January 2022, a deadline widely missed
UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
risks: Stranded on a platform or in a train
Falls at gaps and ramps
Damage to the wheelchair
Stress, exclusion, dependence on others

career.entry: Anyone; a role for teaching accessibility, and for players of other roles to feel the consequences of their decisions
career.chances: No pay; time, independence and trust in the system are the currency. Experts by experience work as accessibility advisers for railways and authorities.

roles.timescale: Hours (a journey), a day ahead (booking)

game.title: Step-free
game.loop: The player plans and makes a journey through the lab network in a wheelchair: only step-free paths count, lifts are infrastructure assets that can fail, and platform heights and train types decide whether a ramp is needed. The player books assistance or not, checks the lift status, and reacts when a lift fails on the way: wait, reroute through another station, call the 3-S centre.
game.win: Arrive within the time window; score from arrival time, waiting time, independence and rights used; 10-20 minutes. The round fails if the traveller is stranded with no step-free way left and no help called, or tries an unsafe way (stairs, the track). The debrief shows where the system failed; the station manager in the career mode sees the same journey as a complaint.
game.knowledge: Assistance rules (24 hours, free of charge), platform heights and boarding aids, compensation for mobility equipment, the marks on the disability card, the complaint routes (railway, söp, EBA).
game.bigGame: Takes lift faults and repairs from the infrastructure simulation and the station facility technician, assistance capacity from the mobility service, trains from the operations; gives complaints and demands for lifts and platform works to the station manager, the asset manager and politics, assistance requests to the mobility service agent.

roles.name: Pupil or student traveller
roles.organisation: Public
roles.summary: Pupils ride to school by bus and train; students commute to university and travel home at weekends: a large, price-sensitive group with sharp peaks at school times, the group most at risk of trespassing on the tracks, and the railway's future workforce.
decisions: Catch the school bus or the earlier train
Use the school ticket or the student Deutschlandticket
Take the short cut across the tracks or the underpass
Ride without a ticket or not
Push to the platform edge with the crowd or wait back
Find a cheap weekend trip home (saver fare, long-distance coach)
Apply for a railway apprenticeship or a transport degree
effects: Peak loads at school times: extra buses, longer dwell times
Trespassing and accidents on the tracks
Fare evasion losses
The railway's future workforce
resources: School transport paid by the district under the Land's school law (school ticket)
Student Deutschlandticket (Deutschlandsemesterticket) at 60 % of the full price (37.80 € a month in 2026) where the university has it
Little money, much time, a smartphone
limits: EBO § 62: entering the railway premises outside the places meant for it is forbidden (a fine under § 64b EBO)
The overhead line carries 15 kV: an arc can jump over 1.5 m; never climb onto wagons or masts
Transport conditions: an increased fare (usually 60 €) when caught without a ticket; fare evasion is still an offence (§ 265a StGB)
School transport rules of the Land and the district (Schülerbeförderung)
Youth protection and parents' responsibility for minors
risks: Death or injury at the tracks (trespassing, train surfing, the overhead line)
Fines and a criminal record for fare evasion
Late for school or exams

career.entry: Anyone of school or university age
career.chances: Railway apprenticeships (Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst, Mechatroniker/in) pay about 1,100-1,400 € gross a month and lead to secure jobs; dual study programmes; students work part-time in stations and as trainees.

roles.timescale: Days (a school week)

game.title: School run
game.loop: A school week in the lab town: each morning the player gets a pupil from home to school by bus 85 or the S-Bahn, choosing when to leave and which way. Short cuts tempt (across the tracks, riding without a ticket); the Federal Police and the conductor check; a safety quiz (overhead line, platform edge, level crossing) unlocks the shortest safe way.
game.win: On time on five days, no trespassing, the quiz passed; about 10 minutes. Trespassing that meets a train ends the round at once, with a debrief on a real accident pattern. In the career mode a passed school week opens the apprenticeship or a place at university.
game.knowledge: Safety at the railway (EBO § 62, the overhead line, the white line, level crossings), tickets for pupils and students.
game.bigGame: Takes school times and bus lines from the transport authority and the bus operator; gives peak demand and fare revenue, and in the career mode the start of a railway career through apprenticeship or study.

roles.name: Resident near the line and citizens' initiative
roles.organisation: Public: a resident, or a citizens' initiative (often a registered association)
roles.summary: Lives next to a line, a station or a construction site and bears its noise, vibration and night works; can object in the planning approval of new tracks, go to court or campaign with a citizens' initiative, and can be the strongest ally for reopening a line or a station.
decisions: File an objection in the planning approval procedure before the deadline
Demand noise barriers or soundproof windows (noise protection for new lines, the federal noise remediation programme for existing ones)
Found a citizens' initiative, collect signatures, approach the mayor and the press
Sue against the planning approval decision, or settle with the project
Complain about night works and demand information
Support a station reopening or the replacement of a level crossing
effects: Delays and extra costs of projects (months to years, millions of euros)
Better protection (noise barriers, quieter brakes) and acceptance
Changes to the project: route, barrier heights, works by day instead of night
Political pressure on the mayor, the Land and the Bund
resources: Time, and a few hundred to tens of thousands of euros for lawyers and noise experts, often shared in the initiative
Participation rights in planning approval (§ 18 AEG with §§ 72-78 VwVfG)
Local media and the municipal council
limits: AEG §§ 18-18e: planning approval of railway lines; for listed projects the Federal Administrative Court decides in first and last instance, and the grounds of an action are due within 10 weeks (§ 18e AEG)
VwVfG § 73: plans on display for a month, objections until two weeks after; late objections are excluded from the procedure

16. BImSchV: noise limits for new or substantially changed lines (residential areas 59 dB(A) by day, 49 dB(A) at night), without the old 5 dB rail bonus (abolished in 2015); 24. BImSchV for soundproof windows

The federal noise remediation programme for existing lines (voluntary, within its budget, from 64 dB(A) by day and 54 dB(A) at night in residential areas); the Rail Noise Protection Act banning loud freight wagons since December 2020
DIN 4150 (vibration), AVV Baulärm (construction noise)

The overriding public interest in rail infrastructure written into the AEG in 2023, which weighs against objections; for a few projects approval by act of parliament under the Maßnahmengesetzvorbereitungsgesetz (2020)
risks: Legal costs when losing in court
Stress and conflicts with neighbours
Health effects of noise (sleep)
Loss of property value, or expropriation of land the project needs (§ 22 AEG)

career.entry: Anyone living near a line; leaders of initiatives are often retirees, lawyers or engineers
career.chances: No pay; a successful initiative can start a local political career (council, mayor).

kpis: Noise level at home in dB(A)
roles.timescale: Months to years (a planning approval, a lawsuit)

game.title: Objection!
game.loop: The planning approval file for a third track through the lab town is on display: plans, a noise report, a schedule of works. The player reads the file, marks what affects their house and street, chooses which objections to file before the deadline (each needs an admissible ground) and how to mobilise (signatures, the press, the mayor). The project side (the computer, or a player as project manager) answers with changes, a settlement or the approval; the player may sue.
game.win: Score from the protection won (dB less at the house, works by day), money spent and neighbours' support; 20-30 minutes over the steps of the procedure. The round fails if the deadline is missed or no objection has an admissible ground. In the big game the project's delay and extra cost are the counterpart's loss.
game.knowledge: The steps and deadlines of planning approval, the noise limits of the 16. BImSchV and the remediation values, what makes an objection admissible, court deadlines, cost sharing for level crossings (EKrG).
game.bigGame: Takes projects (HOAI phases, planning approval) from the infrastructure manager and the planner; gives objections, lawsuits and delays to the planning approval officer and the project manager, pressure to the mayor and MPs, stories to the journalist.

roles.name: Environmental association representative
roles.name_de: Vertreter/in eines Umweltverbands (z. B. BUND, NABU)
roles.organisation: Recognised environmental association (anerkannte Umweltvereinigung, e.g. BUND or NABU), at Land or federal level
roles.summary: Speaks for nature in railway projects: comments on environmental impact assessments, demands protection for species and habitats, may sue against planning approvals without own rights being affected, and at the same time campaigns for more rail as climate protection.
decisions: Choose which projects to comment on with few staff
Demand surveys and protection for protected species (sand lizards, bats, breeding birds)
Sue against a planning approval, or settle for better compensation measures
Campaign for a line reopening, or against a new line through a protected area
Demand limits on vegetation cutting and herbicide use on the track
Build coalitions with residents, the rail lobby or the unions
effects: Better environmental measures: compensation habitats, works outside the breeding season
Project delays and extra costs (surveys, relocating animals at up to thousands of euros each)
Whether the public sees rail as green or as destructive
Court precedents
resources: A handful of paid officers per Land and hundreds of volunteers; 10,000-100,000 € for a lawsuit
The right of action of recognised associations (UmwRG § 2)
Participation rights in planning approval (BNatSchG § 63)
limits: UmwRG (Environmental Appeals Act: recognition under § 3, right of action under § 2, grounds of an action within 10 weeks under § 6)

BNatSchG: § 44 (protection of species), § 15 (impact mitigation and compensation), § 34 (habitats assessment), § 39 (5) (no cutting of trees and bushes from 1 March to 30 September, with exceptions for traffic safety)
UVPG (environmental impact assessment)
AEG §§ 18 ff. (planning approval) and its deadlines
Aarhus Convention
Non-profit and association law (AO)
risks: Losing a lawsuit and its costs
Public criticism for obstructing climate-friendly rail
Burnout of volunteers
Loss of members and donors

career.entry: A degree in biology, landscape planning, geography or law, often after years as a volunteer
career.chances: About 3,500-5,000 € gross a month as officer (often part-time or fixed-term); managing directors of large associations 80,000-120,000 € a year; moves into politics, authorities or consulting.

roles.timescale: Months to years

game.title: Lizards and lines
game.loop: The association has one officer, ten volunteers and 50,000 € for the year. Four railway projects come up: a line reopening, an electrification, a freight bypass through a protected area, a vegetation cut along a line. The player chooses where to engage, what to demand (surveys, relocation, construction windows) and whether to sue or settle; each project's planner reacts, and the outcome shows habitat saved, delays caused, and the CO2 of road traffic that rail did or did not take over.
game.win: Score balances nature protected against the climate benefit of the rail projects (a delayed reopening costs CO2), members' support and the budget; a year in about 20 minutes. The round fails if a lawsuit is filed without standing or out of time, or the money runs out.
game.knowledge: Species protection law, impact mitigation and compensation, the ban on cutting in spring and summer, the associations' right of action and its deadlines, the climate effect of rail against road.
game.bigGame: Takes projects and vegetation plans from the infrastructure manager; gives demands, lawsuits, delays and extra costs to the project managers and the planning approval officer, campaigns to politics.

roles.name: Journalist
roles.organisation: Media: a regional daily, a public broadcaster, an online outlet, or freelance
roles.summary: Reports on the railway: delays and chaos, accidents, strikes, construction projects and politics; chooses the stories, checks the sources and decides how the public sees the railway.
decisions: Choose the story of the day: the signal failure, the strike, the cost overrun
Check a claim with a second source before publishing
Ask the press office, the union, the Federal Police and passengers
Request documents under the freedom of information act or the press laws
Publish now or wait for confirmation
Protect a whistleblower
Report on a fatal accident with restraint
Correct an error in public
effects: Public opinion and political pressure on the railway and on ministers
Reputation of the railway undertakings and the infrastructure manager
Changes in projects or management after investigative stories
Harm from careless reporting (copycat suicides, wrong blame)
resources: A few hours to weeks per story; a newsroom of 5-200 people
Press card; information rights against authorities and publicly controlled companies
Freelance fees of about 100-500 € per article
limits: Press laws of the Länder (Landespressegesetze: right to information against Land authorities, duty of care, right of reply); against federal authorities the right follows from Art. 5 GG (Federal Administrative Court); companies controlled by the state can be bound too (Federal Court of Justice, 2017)
Press code of the German Press Council (Pressekodex: truth, sources, privacy, restraint on suicides, guideline 8.7)
Freedom of information acts (IFG of the Bund for the EBA and the ministry; DB AG as a private-law company is not covered), Länder transparency laws
Personal rights: images (KUG § 22), defamation (§§ 186-187 StGB)
Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG)
The station operator's permission for filming in stations (house rights)
risks: Injunctions and damages for false or defamatory reports
Loss of credibility after errors
Precarious freelance work, deadline stress
Hostility online

career.entry: Usually a degree and a 1-2 year traineeship (Volontariat), or a school of journalism
career.chances: Trainee 2,000-2,600 € gross a month, editor 3,900-6,000 € under the newspaper editors' tariff; freelancers often less. Moves to press offices (better paid) or into politics.

roles.timescale: Hours (a deadline) to weeks (an investigation)

game.title: Deadline at six
game.loop: Something happens on the lab line, from ARail's disruptions or the maintenance story: a signal failure, a track closure, a person on the track. The player has two simulated hours to file a story; they question sources (press office, union, passengers, Federal Police, a leaked document), each with its own interest, and write claims. The game checks every claim against the simulation's real event log.
game.win: Score from accuracy (claims the log confirms), speed, reach and fairness (both sides heard, privacy respected); 15-20 minutes. A false claim triggers a right of reply or a complaint to the Press Council; a defamatory claim or naming a suicide victim fails the round. In the career mode reputation is the journalist's capital.
game.knowledge: Railway terms (signal failure, overhead line damage, person accident, replacement bus), how punctuality is counted (a train is on time below 6 minutes of delay; cancelled trains are not counted), press law and the press code.
game.bigGame: Takes events from every role (incidents, delays, budgets, strikes); gives public pressure (reputation) to the press officer, the railway managers and the politicians, and information to commuters and residents.

roles.name: Trade union official
roles.organisation: Trade union: EVG (railway and transport union in the DGB, about 180,000 members) or GDL (train drivers' union in the dbb, about 40,000 members); in municipal bus and tram companies ver.di
roles.summary: Negotiates the collective agreements on pay and working time with the railway companies, organises warning strikes and strikes, advises works councils and members, and represents railway workers in politics.
decisions: Set the demands of the bargaining round: pay, working time, shift rules
Call a warning strike, or a full strike after a ballot of members (Urabstimmung)
Accept arbitration (Schlichtung) or a settlement
Agree emergency-work arrangements (Notdienst) for safety-critical work; the emergency timetable itself is the employer's decision
Fight for the majority in a business under the collective bargaining unity act
Support a member after an accident (legal protection, care)
Lobby for staff transfer rules in regional tenders
effects: Labour costs of the railway undertakings (each percent of pay costs DB in Germany roughly 100-150 million euros a year)
Strike days: cancelled trains, freight backlogs, losses of tens of millions of euros a day for DB and more for the economy
Working conditions, recruitment and retention of staff
Public opinion of the union and the railway
resources: Strike fund and members' dues (about 1 % of gross pay)
Bargaining commission, works councils, members in key jobs (train drivers, signallers)
Lawyers and a press office
limits: GG Art. 9 (3): freedom of association and the right to strike, shaped by case law

Collective Agreements Act (TVG) and the Collective Bargaining Unity Act (Tarifeinheitsgesetz 2015, § 4a TVG: in a business only the majority union's agreement applies; upheld in essence by the Federal Constitutional Court in 2017)
Peace obligation while an agreement runs (Friedenspflicht)
Proportionality of strikes; injunctions by labour courts (ArbGG)
Arbitration agreements between DB and the unions
The union's statutes (a ballot with a qualified majority, usually 75 %, before an indefinite strike)
risks: Public hostility during strikes
Damages and injunctions if a strike is unlawful
Losing members or the majority in a business
Long hours and travel

career.entry: Mostly from the railway workforce (train driver, signaller, conductor) through works council and union functions; some with a degree in law, economics or social science and a union trainee programme
career.chances: Union secretary about 4,500-6,500 € gross a month; national leaders about 10,000 € and more; former union leaders have become DB board members (labour director) and politicians.

kpis: Pay and working time achieved in the round
roles.timescale: Months (a bargaining round), years (the term of an agreement)

game.title: Bargaining round
game.loop: The player leads the union's bargaining commission against the railway undertaking's HR director (the computer, or another player). Each round they present demands, read the offer, and decide to call a warning strike (the operations simulation turns it into cancelled trains and costs), go to arbitration or settle. Members' support, the strike fund and public opinion move with every step.
game.win: A settlement members accept in the final ballot (pay and working time above their threshold), with the strike fund intact and public support above a minimum; 20-30 minutes. Failure: an injunction (a strike without a ballot or during the peace obligation), losing the majority in a business, or members rejecting the deal. The result sets the pay tables of the career mode and the undertaking's labour costs.
game.knowledge: The right to strike and its limits, the peace obligation, the majority rule of the Tarifeinheitsgesetz, arbitration, emergency work during strikes, the cost arithmetic of pay rises and shorter hours.
game.bigGame: Takes the undertaking's finances and staff numbers from the railway undertaking simulator; gives pay tables and working-time rules to the career mode and the crew planners, strike days to the operations, pressure to politics.

roles.name: Works council member
roles.organisation: Works council of a railway company (e.g. a regional DB company, DB InfraGO, a private railway undertaking or a workshop)
roles.summary: Elected by the staff, co-determines rosters, shift systems, overtime, monitoring technology, hiring and transfers, and negotiates the social plan when a business changes or a tender is lost.
decisions: Consent to or refuse next month's rosters and shift plans
Agree to overtime and extra shifts in a staff shortage, or not
Approve or block monitoring technology (apps, cameras, telematics, body cams)
Consent to a hiring or transfer, or refuse with reasons within one week
Object to a dismissal
Negotiate a reconciliation of interests and a social plan after a lost tender or a restructuring
Call the conciliation board (Einigungsstelle) when no agreement is reached
effects: Rosters that respect health and family, or cancelled trains when rosters are not agreed
Staff satisfaction, sickness and retention
Costs and flexibility of the company
Protection of staff who move to a new operator after a tender
resources: Release from work (§ 38 BetrVG: one fully released member from 200 employees, more in large businesses)
Information rights, experts paid by the employer by agreement (§ 80 (3) BetrVG), training (§ 37 (6))
The council's costs borne by the employer
limits: BetrVG: § 87 (working time, monitoring, health), § 99 (hiring and transfers, one week to refuse), § 102 (dismissals), §§ 111-112 (business changes, social plan), § 76 (conciliation board)

Working-time law (ArbZG: 8 hours a day, up to 10 if averaged; 11 hours of rest, which collective agreements may change under § 7; at least 15 free Sundays a year) and the EVG and GDL agreements (rest days, shift lengths, rostering rules)
Ban on favouring or disadvantaging council members (§ 78 BetrVG; criminal offence under § 119)
Transfer of undertakings (§ 613a BGB) and staff transfer in rail tenders (§ 131 (3) GWB)
risks: Conflicts with management and colleagues
Criminal risk in accepting benefits (§ 119 BetrVG)
Re-election every four years
Falling behind in the original job

career.entry: Elected by the employees every four years (1 March to 31 May; last in 2026); any employee with six months in the business can stand
career.chances: Keeps the pay of the original job (about 3,000-5,000 €) and the career of comparable colleagues; chairs of large councils sit on supervisory boards as employee representatives (Mitbestimmungsgesetz).

kpis: Rosters agreed on time with the rules kept
roles.timescale: Weeks (rosters), months (agreements)

game.title: Roster veto
game.loop: Each round the crew planner (ARail's crew desk, or another player) presents next month's rosters for the lab network's drivers and conductors. The player checks them against the working-time law and the tariff (rest periods, longest shift, weekends off, wishes) and decides: consent, consent with conditions, or refuse. The operations simulation then runs with the agreed roster and shows cancellations from too few staff or sickness from overload.
game.win: Score from violations found, staff sickness and overtime, trains run, and relations with management; a month in 15-20 minutes. Failure: consenting to a roster that breaks the working-time law, or blocking so long that trains are cancelled and the company calls the conciliation board. In the career mode the next election is the result.
game.knowledge: ArbZG (daily maximum, 11 hours of rest, Sunday rest and its exceptions for transport), tariff rostering rules, the works council's co-determination rights and deadlines.
game.bigGame: Takes rosters from the crew planner and staff numbers from HR; gives agreed rosters (or delays) to the operations, demands and conflicts to management, agreements that change the undertaking's costs.

roles.name: Association and lobby representative
roles.name_de: Referent/in eines Verbands (Allianz pro Schiene, VDV, Pro Bahn)
roles.organisation: Industry or passenger association: Allianz pro Schiene, VDV (transport companies), VDB (rail industry), mofair or Die Güterbahnen (DB's competitors), Pro Bahn (passengers)
roles.summary: Makes the case for rail in Berlin and Brussels: analyses budgets and draft laws, writes position papers, talks to MPs, ministries and the press, and builds coalitions; Pro Bahn speaks for passengers, mostly with volunteers.
decisions: Choose the year's priorities: infrastructure budget, track access charges, funding of the Deutschlandticket
Write a position paper or commission a study
Meet the budget committee's rail rapporteur before the final budget session (Bereinigungssitzung)
Comment on a draft law in the ministry's consultation
Build a coalition with unions, environmental groups or business
Go public with a campaign, or work quietly
effects: Budget lines for rail (billions of euros a year), subsidies for track access charges, funding of the Deutschlandticket
Details of laws changed by amendments
The public image of rail
Members' interests served, or not
resources: Association budgets from about 100,000 € (Pro Bahn) to tens of millions of euros (VDV)
5-150 staff; access to MPs, ministries and the media
Data and studies, e.g. rail investment per inhabitant compared with Switzerland and Austria
limits: Lobby Register Act (LobbyRG): registration and code of conduct for contacts with the Bundestag and the federal government; breaches are fined
The federal budget procedure (BHO, Haushaltsgrundsätzegesetz), the debt brake (Art. 115 GG) and the infrastructure special fund (Art. 143h GG)
Joint rules of procedure of the federal ministries (GGO § 47: consultation of associations)
Competition law for associations (GWB: no agreements between competitors)
Association and non-profit law
risks: Loss of credibility as a paid voice
Revolving-door scandals
Dependence on members' money
Long hours in the budget season

career.entry: A degree in economics, political science, law or transport engineering, often after work in an MP's office or a ministry
career.chances: Policy officer about 4,500-7,000 € gross a month; managing directors 120,000-250,000 € a year; a revolving door to politics and companies.

roles.timescale: Months (a budget cycle), a legislature

game.title: Budget season
game.loop: From the government's draft budget in summer to the budget committee's final session in November the player has a limited number of meetings, studies and press releases. They pick arguments (each a fact with a source; a wrong fact costs credibility), target MPs by committee and party, and time a campaign. The computer MPs move budget lines by arguments, coalitions and public opinion.
game.win: Budget lines for rail moved in the members' favour, credibility above a minimum, the lobby register rules kept; 20-30 minutes. Failure: an unregistered contact, or a false fact exposed by the press. In the big game the result changes next year's budgets of the infrastructure manager and the Länder.
game.knowledge: The federal budget procedure; how rail is financed (LuFV III for maintaining the existing network, the Bundesschienenwegeausbaugesetz for new lines, Regionalisierungsmittel for regional services, the infrastructure special fund of 500 billion € over 12 years); key rail statistics; the lobby register rules.
game.bigGame: Takes budgets and reports from every role (delays, the investment backlog); gives arguments and pressure to MPs and the minister, which change budgets for the infrastructure manager and the Länder.

roles.name: Federal police officer
roles.organisation: Bundespolizei (railway police tasks under § 3 BPolG), a federal police station at a main station
roles.summary: Protects passengers and the premises of the federal railways: patrols stations and trains, deals with crimes and dangers (assaults, theft, unattended items, persons on the track, football fans, cable theft) and investigates on the railway after accidents and suicides.
decisions: Assess an unattended suitcase and decide to clear an area and have trains stopped
Order a person to leave (Platzverweis) or take them into custody
Check identities in a weapons ban zone
Escort a train with football fans
Have trains stopped through the signaller or the emergency control centre for persons on the track
Release the scene after a fatal accident once the evidence is secured, so the emergency manager can hand the line back
Use force (handcuffs, pepper spray) within proportionality
effects: Safety, and the feeling of safety, in stations
Delays and closures: clearing a station area for 1-3 hours hits thousands of travellers
Prosecution of offenders
Trust or distrust of minorities (the racial profiling debate)
resources: A federal police station with 20-200 officers at a main station; patrols of 2-4
Powers under the BPolG (questioning, identity checks, orders to leave, custody) and access to the joint station video
Explosive detection dogs, bomb disposal, support units for events
limits: BPolG: railway police tasks (§ 3), prosecution (§ 12), suspicion-independent questioning in trains and stations (§ 22 (1a)), identity checks, orders to leave and custody; StPO for investigations; UZwG for the use of force
Weapons Act (WaffG): knife and weapons bans in stations and trains, also by general orders of the Federal Police
Fundamental rights, proportionality, non-discrimination
Entering the track only after the trains are confirmed stopped (and the overhead line switched off and earthed where needed), Ril 123 procedures
Working time ordinance for federal civil servants (AZV), duty rosters
risks: Injury and assault, knife attacks
Being hit by a train or the overhead line on the track
Criminal and disciplinary proceedings after using force
Trauma after suicides and accidents
Shift work, mass events

career.entry: 2.5 years of training for the middle service (Polizeimeister/in), or a 3-year bachelor at the federal university of applied administrative sciences (HS Bund) for the higher intermediate service (Polizeikommissar/in); age, fitness and aptitude tests
career.chances: Federal civil servant pay: A7-A9 (about 3,000-4,200 € gross a month) in the middle service, A9-A13 (about 3,600-6,500 €) in the higher intermediate service, plus the police allowance; employment for life. Later moves into DB's corporate security or a 3-S centre.

kpis: Crimes per 100,000 travellers at the station
Minutes trains were stopped for police reasons
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes (incidents), a shift

game.title: Match day at the station
game.loop: A match day on the lab station: fans arrive, the passenger simulation fills the platforms, the 3-S centre reports an unattended bag and a person walking along the track. The player commands a patrol of four: talk, check, order to leave, clear an area (which closes platforms and holds trains), call the bomb squad. Every measure costs trains and travellers' time; doing too little risks harm.
game.win: Score from incidents handled, nobody harmed, delays caused and proportionality (the measure fits the danger); about 20 minutes. The round fails if officers or travellers go onto the track before the trains are stopped, or a danger is ignored. In the career mode a disproportionate use of force starts a disciplinary review.
game.knowledge: The powers of the BPolG and their limits, the procedure for unattended items, stopping trains (and earthing the overhead line) before entering the track, proportionality.
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from the 3-S centre and the security staff, crowds from the timetable and events; gives closures and stops to the emergency manager and the signallers (delays for the railway undertakings), cases to prosecutors, crime figures to politics and the press.

roles.name: Fire and rescue incident commander
roles.organisation: Municipal fire brigade (professional or volunteer) and rescue service, under the Land's fire and rescue law
roles.summary: Commands fire brigade and rescue service at railway accidents: collisions at level crossings, train fires, persons hit by a train, derailments with dangerous goods, evacuating a train on the open line; works with the railway's emergency manager (Notfallmanager), who has the line blocked and the overhead line switched off and earthed.
decisions: Choose the access point and the assembly area near the line
Demand the line blocked and the overhead line switched off and earthed before anyone enters
Evacuate the passengers or keep them in the train
Set up triage for many casualties (MANV)
Call dangerous goods experts (the chemical industry's TUIS) and keep the area clear
Request the railway's rescue train for a tunnel through the emergency manager
Hand the site over to the Federal Police and the accident investigators
effects: Lives saved or lost; injuries to rescuers
Hours of closure and delays across the network
Damage to the environment with dangerous goods
Evidence kept or lost for the investigation
resources: Fire engines and crews (a platoon of about 22, more by alarm level), ambulances and emergency doctors
Hydraulic rescue tools; earthing only by authorised railway staff; tunnel equipment
The DB emergency control centre and the emergency manager, who arrives typically within 30-60 minutes
limits: Fire and rescue laws of the Länder (e.g. SächsBRKG); FwDV 100 (command and control)
Ril 123 of DB InfraGO (emergency management) and the agreements with fire services: nobody near the overhead line before the earthing is confirmed (Bahnerdung)
EBA guideline on fire and disaster protection in railway tunnels and TSI SRT (Regulation (EU) 1303/2014): rescue concepts
RID and ADR (dangerous goods): hazard identification and UN numbers
Occupational safety of rescuers (DGUV)
risks: Electrocution (15 kV overhead line), being hit by a train on the neighbouring track
Trauma (fatal accidents, children)
Criminal liability for wrong decisions (negligent homicide in extreme cases)
Public and media scrutiny

career.entry: Professional: a completed vocational training plus about 18-24 months of fire service training (Brandmeister/in) for the middle service; an engineering bachelor plus about 18-24 months of preparatory service (Brandinspektor/in) for the higher intermediate service; a master plus 2 years (Brandreferendar/in) for the higher service; volunteers: courses up to group, platoon or unit leader at the Land's fire service school
career.chances: Civil servant pay of the Land or municipality: about A7-A9 for firefighters, A9-A13 for officers (about 3,300-6,000 € gross a month), A13-A16 for heads of large brigades; volunteers unpaid apart from expense allowances.

kpis: Time until the line is handed back
roles.timescale: Seconds to hours (an incident)

game.title: Line live?
game.loop: Alarm: a regional train has hit a car at a level crossing of the lab line, the engine room is on fire, the neighbouring track is still in use. The player commands the units on a map of the layout: where to approach, whom to send, when to ask for the line to be blocked and the overhead line earthed, when to evacuate and how to triage. The railway side (emergency manager, signaller, energy controller) answers with realistic delays.
game.win: Score from time to rescue, casualties, rescuers' safety and the time until the line is handed back; 10-20 minutes. The round fails at once if a rescuer enters the danger zone of the overhead line before the earthing is confirmed, or the neighbouring track is not blocked (a danger to people). In the career mode the accident investigation interviews the player.
game.knowledge: Dangers of the overhead line and the earthing procedure, the roles of emergency manager and incident commander, triage, dangerous goods plates (hazard identification and UN numbers).
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from the operations and the infrastructure (level crossing, overhead line) and the emergency manager's earthing; gives closure times to the network controller and the railway undertakings, cases to the accident investigator, casualties to politics.

roles.name: Lift and escalator technician at stations
roles.name_de: Techniker/in für Aufzüge und Fahrtreppen (Facility Management im Bahnhof)
roles.organisation: Station operator (DB InfraGO, passenger stations, facility management) or a lift manufacturer's service under contract
roles.summary: Keeps the lifts, escalators, doors and passenger displays of stations running: answers fault calls, frees trapped passengers, does preventive maintenance and prepares the statutory inspections. For a wheelchair user a broken lift means the station is closed.
decisions: Rank fault calls when two lifts fail at once
Free a trapped passenger first, then find the cause
Order a spare part, or patch the lift for now
Shut down an unsafe escalator
Schedule maintenance at night, away from the crowds
Book the approved inspection body (ZÜS) for the periodic inspection
Report a lift that needs renewing to the asset manager
effects: Availability of lifts and escalators: step-free access to the platforms
Journeys of wheelchair users, families with prams and travellers with luggage
Repair and renewal costs (a new station lift costs a few hundred thousand euros to over 1 million €)
Safety of passengers on escalators
resources: A van, tools and common spare parts; a region of 20-80 lifts and escalators
Remote monitoring of lift status and the lifts' emergency call system
Service contracts with manufacturers for parts
limits: Industrial Safety Ordinance (BetrSichV): lifts are installations subject to monitoring; an approved inspection body (ZÜS) inspects them every 2 years (main inspection) with an intermediate inspection in between
Escalators are work equipment: inspected by a competent person (TRBS 1201), often by a ZÜS as well
TRBS 3121 (operating lifts: two-way emergency call, a rescue service that frees trapped people in reasonable time, 30 minutes being the usual target)
EN 81-20/50 (lifts), EN 115-1 (escalators), electrical safety (DGUV Vorschrift 3)
TSI PRM and the operator's accessibility programme (EBO § 2 (3))
Working-time law for on-call duty
risks: Electric shock, crushing in the machinery
Liability after an accident caused by poor maintenance
On-call nights
Public complaints

career.entry: Apprenticeship as mechatronics or electronics technician (3.5 years), with the manufacturer's lift training
career.chances: About 3,200-4,300 € gross a month (metal and electrical trade tariffs or the EVG tariff) plus on-call allowances; master craftsperson or engineer for promotion.

kpis: Availability of lifts and escalators (target above 95 %)
roles.timescale: Minutes to hours (faults), months (maintenance plan)

game.title: Lift down
game.loop: The lifts of the lab network's stations are infrastructure assets with condition and faults. The player gets fault calls from the 3-S centre and drives between stations, deciding whom to serve first, whether to repair now or patch and order a part, and when to do preventive maintenance at night. Wheelchair users from the journeys are stranded while a lift is down.
game.win: Availability above 95 %, nobody trapped longer than 30 minutes, costs within budget; a month in 15-20 minutes. The round fails with an accident after skipped maintenance or an overdue statutory inspection.
game.knowledge: Inspection intervals under the BetrSichV, the rescue procedure, condition grades, preventive against corrective maintenance costs.
game.bigGame: Takes fault reports from the 3-S centre and the infrastructure simulation and budgets from the asset manager; gives availability to the station manager, to wheelchair users and to the station quality figures, renewal needs to the asset manager.

roles.name: Station mission social worker or volunteer
roles.organisation: Bahnhofsmission, run ecumenically by the churches' welfare organisations (Diakonie, Caritas and IN VIA) at about 100 stations in Germany
roles.summary: Helps anyone in need at the station, without conditions: lost or stranded travellers, people with disabilities changing trains, children travelling alone, homeless people and people in crisis; the station's social safety net between the 3-S centre, the police and social services.
decisions: Decide whom to help first when several people are waiting
Accompany an elderly or disabled traveller to the next train
Call the social psychiatric service, an emergency doctor or the police for a person in crisis
Refer a homeless person to a shelter or emergency accommodation
Take over a child travelling alone (Kids on Tour) and hand it over safely
Report a risk to a child's welfare to the youth office
Calm a conflict instead of calling the police, when that is safe
effects: Fewer conflicts and police operations at the station
Stranded travellers continue their journey
People in crisis reach help (suicide prevention)
The station's social image
resources: A room in the station provided by the station operator, 1-3 paid social workers and 10-50 volunteers
A budget of about 50,000-300,000 € a year per mission from churches, municipalities and donations
A network of social services, shelters and counselling
limits: The station house rules and the cooperation agreement with the station operator
Referrals under social law (SGB II, SGB XII); child protection (§ 8a SGB VIII)
Confidentiality (§ 203 StGB for state-recognised social workers) and GDPR
Duty to help in emergencies (§ 323c StGB)
The welfare organisation's rules for training and supervising volunteers
risks: Aggression and violence by clients
Emotional strain, secondary trauma
Low pay, or unpaid work
Infections

career.entry: Social workers: a bachelor in social work with state recognition; volunteers: a short course by the welfare organisation
career.chances: Social workers about 3,700-5,000 € gross a month (TVöD SuE or church tariffs); volunteers unpaid; head of a mission or of a regional office.

roles.timescale: Minutes to hours, a shift

game.title: Open door
game.loop: A late shift in the station mission of the lab station with two volunteers: people come in from the passenger simulation (a family stranded after the last train was cancelled, a confused elderly man, a child travelling alone whose connection broke, a person in crisis on the platform). The player decides whom to help first, whom to accompany to a train, and when to call the police, a doctor or social services.
game.win: People helped and safely handed over, conflicts calmed, volunteers not overloaded; a shift in about 15 minutes. The round fails if a child is left alone or a person in acute danger is not handed to the emergency services.
game.knowledge: Who helps with what (social services, emergency services, police), child protection, the rights of stranded travellers.
game.bigGame: Takes stranded travellers from disruptions and the town's people; gives fewer police operations and complaints to the station manager and the 3-S centre, help to travellers.

roles.name: Safety manager (safety management system)
roles.organisation: Railway undertaking (EVU) or infrastructure manager (EIU), e.g. DB InfraGO, DB Regio, a private regional or freight railway. In a small company the operations manager by law (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter) often holds the role as well.
roles.summary: Runs the safety management system (SMS) on which the single safety certificate (EVU) or the safety authorisation (EIU) depends. Collects and analyses events, prepares the CSM-RA decision on whether a change is significant, steers investigations, audits and corrective actions, and watches the trends. Reports to the board and answers to the EBA in supervision. The role advises, audits and escalates; the line responsibility for safe operation stays with the operations manager by law (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter) and the line managers.
decisions: Classify each reported event (accident, incident, or a precursor such as a SPAD or a wrong-side failure) for the statistics and the Common Safety Indicators, and check that reportable events reached the BEU and the EBA in time (operations makes the immediate notification)

Prepare the proposer's decision on whether a change (a new vehicle type, timetable concept, contractor, ETCS) is significant under CSM-RA and needs the full risk management process with an independent assessor (AsBo); the operations manager or the board signs it
Commission an investigation and set its depth: a short check, a root-cause analysis or human-factors interviews
Propose corrective and preventive actions with owners and deadlines, technical (e.g. a train protection upgrade), organisational (briefings, rosters) or training, and chase them until they are closed
Set the audit programme: which departments, contractors, ECMs and staffing agencies are audited this year
Escalate to the board, or recommend stopping an operation (a vehicle series, a contractor) until the risk is under control
Write the annual safety report for the EBA (due by 31 May for the previous year) and the CSM monitoring report
effects: Fewer precursors (SPADs, wrong-side failures, shunting irregularities) and accidents. If a trend is missed, a serious accident and a BEU investigation follow.
Measures cost money and capacity: speed restrictions, extra briefings in crew time, vehicles withdrawn

The safety certificate (valid up to 5 years, issued by the ERA, or by the EBA if the railway undertaking operates only in Germany and chooses it) is renewed smoothly or with findings and conditions; in the worst case it is restricted or revoked
Reporting culture: a just culture raises the number of reports and with it what is known; blame lowers it and hides risk
Contractors and ECMs that fail audits must improve or lose work
resources: A team of 1-5 in a regional railway, 20-100 in a large group, plus safety officers in the operating units
A budget for audits, assessments and studies of about 0.1-2 m € a year; measures come out of line budgets that the safety manager must win over
Event data: incident reports, train data recorder downloads, CSM monitoring records, BEU reports on other companies
Authority: a direct line to the board, the right to audit everyone and to demand action plans; no command over trains or staff
limits: AEG and the Safety Directive (EU) 2016/798: an SMS is a condition of the single safety certificate (procedure: Implementing Reg. (EU) 2018/763) or of the infrastructure manager's safety authorisation

CSM on SMS requirements (Delegated Reg. (EU) 2018/762), CSM-RA (Implementing Reg. (EU) 402/2013), CSM monitoring (Reg. (EU) 1078/2012); the Common Safety Indicators and their definitions in Annex I of Directive 2016/798
Eisenbahnbetriebsleiterverordnung (EBV): the operational responsibility of the operations manager by law
Eisenbahn-Unfalluntersuchungsverordnung (EUV): immediate notification of serious accidents, accidents and certain incidents to the BEU
ECM Regulation (EU) 2019/779: every vehicle needs an entity in charge of maintenance, and the railway undertaking must make sure it has one
ArbSchG and DGUV regulations where worker safety overlaps; works council co-determination (BetrVG § 87(1) no. 6) for measures that can monitor staff, such as analysing train data recorder downloads
risks: Criminal investigation after a fatal accident if known risks were ignored (StGB § 222 negligent homicide, § 315a endangering rail traffic), as witness or suspect
Public exposure in BEU reports, the press and parliamentary questions
Conflict with management over cost and punctuality; job loss after a major accident
Stress from on-call duty after serious events

career.entry: An engineering degree (transport, electrical or mechanical) or an operational career (train driver or signaller, then master craftsman or Fachwirt). 5-10 years in operations or maintenance, plus training in CSM, risk assessment and auditing (ISO 19011)
career.chances: Out of tariff (AT) about 75,000-130,000 € a year; head of safety in a large group 130,000-200,000 €. Demand is steady, and moves to operations manager by law or to the authorities are common.

kpis: Precursors per million train-km (SPADs, wrong-side failures)
Common Safety Indicators (fatalities and weighted serious injuries)
Open audit findings and overdue corrective actions
EBA supervision findings; certificate renewed without conditions
roles.timescale: Days to years: events daily, investigations over weeks, audits and the safety report yearly, the certificate every 5 years

game.title: Precursors (Vorboten)
game.loop: One railway year, played week by week. The inbox fills with event reports drawn from the operations and infrastructure simulations: SPADs, doors released on the wrong side, a missed brake test, a contractor on the track without a lookout. The player classifies each report, decides what to investigate and how deeply, and spends a limited budget and the line managers' goodwill on measures. A hidden risk model raises the chance of a serious accident wherever precursors are left alone. Proposed changes (a new vehicle type, a staffing agency) come with a CSM-RA significance question that the player must prepare for the board.
game.win: Passed after a year if the risk index is below its starting value, the EBA audit finds nothing major and no serious accident happened. A serious accident ends the round with a BEU investigation that shows which ignored report pointed to it. Misclassified reportable events count as findings. In the career mode a failed round means a reprimand or a move back to the line; a passed one counts towards operations manager by law.
game.knowledge: Event classes and reporting duties (EUV); the CSI definitions (a significant accident has at least one person killed or seriously injured, damage of 150,000 € or more, or a disruption of 6 hours or more; seriously injured means in hospital for more than 24 hours); the six CSM-RA significance criteria (failure consequence, novelty, complexity, monitoring, reversibility, additionality); root cause versus symptom; just culture; the order of measures (eliminate or substitute, technical, organisational, personal)
game.bigGame: Takes events from the signaller, driver, ECM and maintenance games and from BEU reports. Gives measures that change other games' rules (speed restrictions, briefings that cost crew time, withdrawn vehicles, contractor bans), costs to the finance controller, and the safety certificate status that the railway undertaking's simulator needs in order to run at all.

roles.name: HR manager and recruiter
roles.organisation: HR department of a railway company (railway undertaking or infrastructure manager)
roles.summary: Finds, selects and keeps the staff the timetable needs, above all scarce train drivers and signallers. Plans vacancies against retirements, runs campaigns and selection, makes offers within the tariff agreements, organises the retraining of career changers and obtains the works council's consent.
decisions: Forecast vacancies per depot and signal box from retirements, attrition and the next timetable
Choose channels and spending: job boards, referral bonuses, campaigns, recruitment abroad, the employment agency's training vouchers (Bildungsgutschein)
Select candidates (pre-screening, interviews, assessment centre) and send them to the medical and psychological fitness checks
Make offers within the tariff group (EVG or GDL agreement) and decide on extras: relocation, housing, preferred shifts
Start a retraining course for career changers (9-12 months) or poach licensed drivers from competitors

Bind a company-funded retrained driver with a training cost repayment clause, within the limits of labour court case law (for a course of 6-12 months a binding of up to about 3 years, reduced pro rata)
Agree retention measures with the works council: roster preferences, part-time models, the working-time options of the GDL agreement
effects: Crews and signallers on duty or posts vacant, so trains run or are cancelled and penalties go to the transport authority
Staff costs and cost per hire; poaching between railway undertakings drives wages up
Training capacity is tied up for a year before a hire becomes a driver
The workforce's age structure and diversity, morale, and early attrition
resources: A recruiting budget of about 3,000-8,000 € per external hire; retraining a career changer as train driver costs 30,000-50,000 € and takes 9-12 months
A team of 2-10 recruiters in a regional company; the DB group has hired around 20,000 people or more a year in recent years
Applicant tracking system, employer brand, tariff tables; partnerships with the employment agency and training providers
limits: General Equal Treatment Act (AGG): no discrimination in job ads or selection; claims must be made in writing within 2 months (§ 15(4))
Works Constitution Act (BetrVG) § 99: in companies with more than 20 employees the works council must consent to each hire and grading; § 95 selection guidelines
Train driver licence ordinance (TfV) and Directive 2007/59/EC: minimum age, medical and psychological fitness, language skills at level B1

EVG and GDL tariff agreements (pay groups, working time; under the GDL's 2024 agreement the week falls stepwise from 38 to 35 hours by 2029, with options to work more for more pay); the Collective Agreement Unity Act (TarifEinhG) decides which union's agreement applies in each unit

Working Hours Act (ArbZG), GDPR for applicant data, SGB IX for severely disabled applicants, Skilled Immigration Act for recruitment outside the EU (licences from outside the EU are not recognised, the full training is needed)
risks: AGG claims by rejected applicants (up to three months' pay if the applicant would not have been hired anyway, more otherwise)
Data protection fines; blamed for cancellations while vacancies persist
Target pressure, caught between line managers, the works council and the budget

career.entry: A degree in business, psychology or law, or a commercial apprenticeship with a Fachwirt or HR qualification; some recruiters come from operations
career.chances: About 45,000-75,000 € a year (tariff or AT); head of HR 90,000-150,000 €; more as HR director (Arbeitsdirektor) on a board. Demand is high because of the staff shortage.

kpis: Vacancy rate for drivers and signallers
Time to hire and cost per hire
Share of candidates passing the fitness checks and the course
Early attrition in the probation period
Trains cancelled for lack of staff
roles.timescale: Weeks to years: campaigns monthly, a course takes a year, the workforce plan covers several years

game.title: Drivers for December (Lokführer für Dezember)
game.loop: Monthly turns over the two to three years before a new transport contract starts at the December timetable change. The player sees the driver need (from the duties in the operations module) and the forecast leavers, and spends money on channels. Candidates arrive as cards with traits (licence, language, age, motivation) and pass a funnel: interview, fitness checks (a fixed share fails), retraining course, route and vehicle knowledge. A rival undertaking competes with its own offers and poaches graduates who are not bound by a repayment clause; the works council must consent to each hire, and the tariff and morale limit what can be offered.
game.win: Passed if, on the start day, vacancies are below 3 % and the budget held; the operations simulation then runs the first months with the crews actually hired. Too few drivers means cancellations and contract penalties. A discriminatory selection triggers an AGG claim and fails the round, as does a repayment clause that a labour court would strike down. In the career mode: promotion to head of HR, or a move to a consultancy.
game.knowledge: Lead times of the training pipeline, base rates of the fitness checks, tariff groups and working-time rules, works council co-determination, the AGG, the limits on repayment clauses
game.bigGame: Takes the staff need from the crew planner and the timetable, training places from the driver instructor, fitness results from the physician and the psychologist, and the budget from the finance controller. Gives staff (the crews' vacancies setting) to the railway undertaking's simulator and costs to its accounts.

roles.name: Train driver instructor
roles.organisation: Training provider (Bildungsträger) or the training department of a railway undertaking; the exams are held by examiners recognised by the EBA
roles.summary: Turns career changers and apprentices into licensed train drivers and keeps licensed drivers competent. Teaches rules, signals, brakes and vehicles in the classroom and simulator, rides in the cab with trainees as the driver in charge, decides when a trainee is ready for the exam, and gives periodic training as well as route and vehicle familiarisation.
decisions: Plan the course: theory blocks (signals, Ril 408, brakes, vehicle), simulator hours, practical cab hours
In the cab: let the trainee correct a mistake, or take over, and decide how close to a stop signal to intervene
Release a trainee to the exam, prescribe extra training, or recommend ending the course
Choose scenarios for simulator and periodic training (failures, Zs 1 and written orders, degraded ETCS modes)
Confirm route and vehicle-type knowledge for the driver's complementary certificate (Zusatzbescheinigung)
Report human-factor patterns seen in training to the safety manager
effects: Drivers ready in time for the timetable or not, so trains run or are cancelled
The graduates' future rate of SPADs and irregularities
Course costs, dropouts, and the training provider's standing with the employment agency and the EBA
resources: Groups of 8-15 trainees; 9-12 months per career changer at about 30,000-50,000 € a head, often funded by the employment agency's voucher
A driving simulator (0.5-2 m €), classrooms, training rides on service trains with the instructor in charge
Exam slots with EBA-recognised examiners
limits: Train driver licence ordinance (TfV) and Directive 2007/59/EC: content of the licence and the complementary certificate, recognised trainers and examiners, periodic checks
Signal rules (ESO, DB Ril 301), train operation (Ril 408), driving traction units (Ril 492), brakes in operation (Ril 915), the undertaking's own operating instructions
AZAV approval for courses funded by the employment agency; trainer aptitude (AEVO) when training apprentices
Working Hours Act and the tariff for training rides
risks: The instructor is the driver in charge while the trainee drives: a SPAD or overspeed is the instructor's responsibility (StGB § 315a, § 229 if someone is hurt) and can cost the licence
Management pressure to pass trainees faster because of the driver shortage
Shift work and nights on training rides

career.entry: A licensed train driver with several years' experience and instructor training (didactics, AEVO); examining also needs recognition by the EBA
career.chances: On the tariff (EVG or GDL) about 3,800-5,200 € a month plus allowances; self-employed trainers 400-800 € a day. Demand is strong; next steps are team leader of drivers, operations manager by law, or safety.

kpis: SPADs and irregularities of graduates in their first years
Course on time and within budget
Periodic training completed for all drivers
roles.timescale: Seconds in the cab, days per course module, a year per course

game.title: The Second Seat (Lehrfahrt)
game.loop: The player sits beside a computer-played trainee who drives a train over the lab's line (Bergheim to Talsee via Bf Neustadt), with signals, speed boards and a signal failure. The trainee makes mistakes according to a skill profile: braking late for a caution aspect, missing a speed board, mishandling the conversation with the signaller about Zs 1. The player can coach, wait or take over, and each choice changes both the trainee's learning and the risk. Between rides the player picks the next lesson (classroom, simulator or cab) and finally decides whether the trainee goes to the exam.
game.win: Passed if the trainee passes the exam within the course time and nobody was put in danger; a SPAD or a dangerous overspeed that the player did not prevent fails the round. The learning curve is scored: intervening too much slows learning, too little risks a SPAD. In the career mode the instructor's graduates later appear as drivers whose error rates come from this round.
game.knowledge: German signals (Hp, Ks, Vr, Zs 1, Zs 7, Lf), braking distances and the distant signal spacing (usually 1000 m on main lines, shorter on slower lines), the Ril 408 procedure for passing a failed signal (Zs 1 or a written order), the TfV licence and complementary certificate
game.bigGame: Takes trainees from the HR recruiter and apprentices. Gives licensed drivers, each with an error profile, to the crews of the railway undertaking's simulator, and training findings to the safety manager.

roles.name: Signaller instructor (railway operations lab)
roles.organisation: Training centre of the infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO with DB's training company) or a university lab such as the EBL at TU Dresden
roles.summary: Trains signallers and students on real interlockings in the lab. Designs exercises with regular and irregular operation (failed signals, written orders, closures for works), runs the session from the instructor's desk, injects faults, stops dangerous moves and leads the debrief. In a training centre the instructor also judges whether trainees are ready for the qualification exam.
decisions: Choose the scenario and its difficulty: timetable, interlocking type (mechanical, relay, electronic), which irregularities happen and when
Assign participants to the desks: signallers of neighbouring stations, drivers of the model trains, the dispatcher
Inject a fault (a failed signal, a section that does not clear) or hold it back for a struggling group
Intervene or freeze the session when a move would be unsafe, or let the mistake happen and debrief it
Grade participants and decide whether they qualify or repeat
Report lab defects and propose lab investments (a new interlocking type, the control-system interface)
effects: Signallers and graduates who know the rules for irregular operation and later make fewer dangerous mistakes
Lab time used well or wasted; the confidence of students and trainees
Feedback into the rules when exercises expose unclear procedures
resources: The lab: several real interlocking types on a model railway with an instructor's desk; sessions of 90-180 minutes
Groups of 10-20, with 1-3 staff; a maintenance and upgrade budget of tens of thousands of euros a year (much more for a new interlocking)
Scenarios and the ARail control-system interface for trains and disruptions
limits: Train operation rules (Ril 408), signal rules (ESO, Ril 301), operating signalling installations (Ril 482), and for non-federal railways the FV-NE
EBO §§ 47-48 on operating staff (Betriebsbeamte): qualification and fitness
The infrastructure manager's qualification rules for operating staff, or the university's study and examination regulations
Electrical safety of the lab (DGUV Regulation 3)
risks: Little physical risk; reputational risk if a training gap shows up in an accident
Fixed-term contracts at a university (WissZeitVG)

career.entry: An experienced signaller with instructor training or, at a university, a transport engineering graduate (Diplom) working as research associate or lab engineer
career.chances: At a university TV-L E11-E13 (about 3,800-6,500 € a month); at a DB training centre about the same on the EVG tariff. Leads on to operations management, safety or research.

kpis: Learning outcomes reached (exam or test results)
roles.timescale: Seconds to minutes in the session; a semester or a course for the programme

game.title: Instructor's Desk (Ausbilderpult)
game.loop: The player runs a 30-minute lab session in which computer players (or classmates) work as signallers at the signaller game's Bf Neustadt and its neighbours, each with a hidden skill profile. The player picks the scenario, decides which fault to inject and when, watches the panels and the log, and can freeze the session. Rule breaks happen, such as Zs 1 without the checks or a track reopened with the team still on it. The player must spot them and decide whether to intervene now or debrief later.
game.win: Scored on the participants' learning gain (questions before and after), rule breaks noticed (missed dangerous ones weigh heavily), keeping to the session time, and the debrief (matching each mistake to its rule). A dangerous move that was not stopped fails the round. Passing leads in the career mode to training manager or operations management.
game.knowledge: Ril 408 for irregular operation: substitute signal, written orders, closures and their release; teaching skills: difficulty curve, feedback
game.bigGame: Takes trainees and students. Gives qualified signallers, each with a skill profile, to the infrastructure manager's operations, and findings on the rules to the safety manager.

roles.name: Finance controller
roles.organisation: Controlling department of a railway undertaking or the infrastructure manager
roles.summary: Plans and steers the money: budgets, monthly forecasts and variance analyses for the board, cost calculations for bids and investment cases. At the infrastructure manager the controller also watches the line between maintenance (largely paid from its own money) and replacement investment (paid mainly by the Bund under the LuFV), a line that shapes how assets are treated.
decisions: Set the yearly budget per cost centre and agree it with the managers
Forecast the year each month and explain variances: energy prices, track access charges, penalties, overtime, unit failures
Propose countermeasures to the board: hiring freeze, deferred maintenance, renegotiation, claims against contractors
Decide with accounting how a measure is classified, as maintenance (opex) or as replacement investment (capex, LuFV-funded), under the accounting rules and the LuFV definitions
Calculate the cost per train-km and the price of a tender bid with the bid manager
Judge investment cases (a new depot, an ETCS retrofit) by net present value and payback
effects: The board's decisions on staff, maintenance and investment
Bids won or lost, and contracts that make or lose money for 10-15 years
Assets renewed or patched, depending on which money is available
Liquidity and the company's rating; findings by auditors, the EBA's check of how federal funds were used, and the BNetzA
resources: ERP (SAP) data and the management report; a team of 2-30

Orders of magnitude: a regional railway undertaking has 50-500 m € revenue a year; LuFV III provides about 86 bn € for 2020-2029 (federal funds plus DB's own contribution), roughly 8-9 bn € a year for the existing network, plus money from the 2025 special fund for infrastructure
Authority: no budget of its own, but the board's ear and the right to demand figures
limits: German Commercial Code (HGB), IFRS in the group, the external audit
ERegG: separate accounts for the infrastructure manager, track access charges approved by the BNetzA, no cross-subsidies
LuFV: quality indicators, a minimum maintenance spend, proof of how the federal funds were used (checked by the EBA)
