BSWAG funding agreements and their proof of use; since the 2023 amendment of the BSWAG the Bund may also fund some maintenance, e.g. in the Generalsanierungen
Regulation (EC) 1370/2007: public service compensation without overcompensation; the transport contract's indexation and penalties
risks: Pressure to make the numbers look good; criminal liability for false accounts (HGB § 331), fraud (StGB § 263) or subsidy fraud (StGB § 264)
Blamed for wrong forecasts; workload peaks at every closing

career.entry: A degree in business, industrial engineering (Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen) or transport economics; a trainee programme or 2-5 years in a consultancy
career.chances: About 55,000-95,000 € a year; head of controlling 100,000-160,000 €; much more as CFO of a railway company. A good route into general management.

kpis: Closing on time; audit without findings
roles.timescale: Months to years: monthly closing, yearly budget, multi-year business plan

game.title: Month End (Monatsabschluss)
game.loop: Each month the player receives the figures from the railway undertaking's simulator (train-km, penalties, overtime, workshop hours from operations) or from the asset management game (maintenance and replacement money). For each variance the player finds the cause in the data and chooses a countermeasure; a full-year forecast is due every quarter. In the infrastructure manager variant the player classifies measures as maintenance or replacement investment, with the temptation to shift costs onto federal money.
game.win: Passed after a year if the forecast error is small, the result is on target, liquidity never went negative and the audit finds nothing. Maintenance passed off as replacement investment is found when the use of the LuFV money is checked, and fails the round with a repayment. In the career mode this is the path to CFO.
game.knowledge: Contribution margin; fixed and variable cost per train-km; opex versus capex; net present value; PSO compensation and overcompensation; LuFV and ERegG basics
game.bigGame: Takes costs and revenues from every department of the railway undertaking's simulator and from the asset management budget years. Gives budgets to fleet, crews, maintenance and HR, and the bid price to the bid manager.

roles.name: Procurement and tendering manager (SektVO)
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager or railway undertaking acting as a sector contracting entity (e.g. DB InfraGO, municipal railways)
roles.summary: Buys works, supplies and services for a sector contracting entity under procurement law, from tamping frameworks to signalling and vehicles. Chooses the procedure, writes the award criteria, runs a fair competition, deals with bidders' complaints and awards the contracts.
decisions: Choose the procedure: open, restricted or negotiated with a call for competition (a free choice in the sector), competitive dialogue or innovation partnership
Split the contract into lots for small and medium firms or bundle it; decide on a framework agreement (up to 8 years in the sector)
Set suitability requirements, award criteria and their weights (price, quality, delivery time, life-cycle cost)
Answer bidders' questions equally for all and decide whether to extend time limits
Query the competition register, exclude bidders on the exclusion grounds or accept their self-cleaning, and check abnormally low tenders
Respond to a complaint (Rüge) or a review application, then award, cancel or re-tender
effects: Contracts at a price and quality the projects must live with; delays when a review stops the award
Market capacity locked into frameworks (e.g. tamping, signalling installation) or left to competitors
A contract awarded without a required EU procedure can be declared ineffective (GWB § 135); bidders can claim damages
resources: Contract values from 0.1 m € to several 100 m € per procedure; the DB group buys for tens of billions of euros a year
E-procurement platform, qualification systems (prequalification), templates; a team of buyers and lawyers
Time: a procurement above the EU thresholds takes 3-9 months
limits: GWB Part 4 (§§ 97 ff.: competition, transparency, equal treatment, lots; §§ 123-126 exclusion and self-cleaning) and the SektVO for sector entities
EU thresholds (2026-2027: about 5.4 m € for works, about 0.43 m € for supplies and services in the sector); below them the company's own rules apply

Minimum time limits, the standstill period (GWB § 134: 15 days, 10 if sent electronically), complaint within 10 days (GWB § 160(3)) and review at the federal procurement tribunal (Vergabekammer des Bundes), then the procurement senate of the Higher Regional Court of Düsseldorf
Competition Register Act (WRegG): query before awards from 30,000 €; VOB/B as contract terms for works; Supply Chain Act (LkSG); tariff compliance laws where they apply
Criminal law on bid rigging (StGB § 298) and commercial bribery (StGB § 299); the company's compliance rules
risks: A review that stops a project for months, with the blame landing on procurement
Corruption allegations; criminal liability for taking bribes or manipulating a procedure
Damages claims by bidders who were treated unequally

career.entry: A degree in law, business, engineering or industrial engineering; procurement training (e.g. certified public procurement specialist); experience in construction or purchasing
career.chances: About 55,000-95,000 € a year; head of procurement 110,000-160,000 €. Demand is strong with the investment boom.

kpis: Share of contracts to small and medium firms
roles.timescale: Weeks to months per procurement; frameworks run for years

game.title: Award Day (Zuschlag)
game.loop: The player procures one contract from the asset management game's projects: a track renewal, a level crossing or a tamping framework. Step by step the player estimates the value and checks it against the threshold, chooses the procedure and the lots, sets criteria and weights, and sets the time limits. Computer-played bidders, each with capacity, a price strategy and an appetite for complaints, respond. Questions arrive, one bid is suspiciously low, and a losing bidder files a Rüge. The player evaluates the bids and decides.
game.win: Passed if the contract is awarded before the booked possession, within the estimate, and survives review. A wrong procedure or unequal treatment makes the Vergabekammer order the evaluation or the whole procedure to be repeated; the project slips a year and the possession is lost. In the career mode: head of procurement, or a move to the transport authority.
game.knowledge: Thresholds, procedures and time limits under GWB and SektVO; award criteria and scoring formulas; abnormally low tenders; exclusion grounds and self-cleaning; the standstill period and complaint deadlines
game.bigGame: Takes procurement needs from the asset manager, the planner and the vehicle procurement manager. Gives contractors, prices and dates to the projects and possessions, and costs to the finance controller.

roles.name: Legal counsel (contracts, procurement, liability)
roles.organisation: Legal department of a railway company
roles.summary: The in-house lawyer of a railway company. Drafts and negotiates contracts and defends or settles claims: contractors' supplementary claims, passenger claims, accident liability, penalties. Advises on procurement and regulation, and guides the company and its staff through investigations after accidents.
decisions: Assess a contractor's supplementary claim (VOB/B § 2) and recommend paying, negotiating or litigating
Draft contract clauses: liability caps, penalties and bonus-malus, change rules, warranty
Defend an accident claim under strict liability (HPflG) or settle it
Advise on a bidder's complaint and whether to defend at the Vergabekammer
After an accident: secure documents (legal hold), arrange counsel for involved staff, advise the board and the press office on what may be said publicly
Lodge a complaint with the BNetzA about access conditions or charges (ERegG), or challenge a BNetzA or EBA decision at the administrative court
effects: Money paid or saved; years of litigation or a settlement
Contracts that allocate risk sensibly, or become traps in the next dispute
Staff protected in criminal investigations; the company's credibility with authorities and courts
resources: A department of 3-50 lawyers; a budget for outside law firms from hundreds of thousands to millions of euros a year
The documents: contracts, logs, train data recorder data, correspondence
Signing authority only within delegated limits; larger settlements need the board
limits: Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO §§ 46-46c): the professional independence of in-house counsel
BGB (contracts; 3-year limitation period, §§ 195, 199), VOB/B (warranty 4 years unless agreed otherwise), GWB and SektVO
AEG, ERegG, EBO; Liability Act (HPflG § 1: strict liability for operating a railway, excluded only by force majeure; caps in §§ 9-10)
Passenger rights Regulation (EU) 2021/782 (25 % compensation from 60 minutes' delay, 50 % from 120; none for force majeure such as extreme weather or persons on the track), EVO, CIM for freight
Criminal law (StGB §§ 315, 315a, 222, 229) and the StPO; GDPR; competition law
risks: Professional liability for wrong advice or missed deadlines
Conflict between loyalty to the company and the law (assisting offenders to evade prosecution, StGB § 258)
High stress in big disputes; public exposure in court

career.entry: A law degree with both state examinations (Volljurist) and admission as Syndikusrechtsanwalt; often first a few years in a law firm
career.chances: About 80,000-150,000 € a year; general counsel 180,000-300,000 €. Moves between company, authority, law firm and the bench are possible.

kpis: Cases won, or settled below the reserve
roles.timescale: Days to years: opinions in days, contracts in weeks, litigation over years

game.title: Claim or Settle (Klagen oder vergleichen)
game.loop: Over one simulated year a docket of 5-8 cases arrives, each with documents drawn from ARail runs. Examples: a contractor claims extra pay after the possession overran (maintenance story, infrastructure projects); the transport authority's penalties are disputed because the infrastructure may have caused the delays (operations); a passenger claims compensation after a disruption (journeys); a level crossing accident leads to a liability claim. The player reads the evidence, finds the applicable rule, estimates the chances, and chooses to pay, negotiate (with offers), litigate or counterclaim, all within deadlines.
game.win: Scored on money saved against the fair value, deadlines kept, and correct legal reasoning (questions on the applicable norm). A missed limitation period or a settlement above the signing limit fails that case; a pattern of reckless litigation costs reputation. In the career mode: general counsel, or a move to the regulator.
game.knowledge: VOB/B supplementary claims and notices; strict liability under the HPflG and its limits; passenger compensation thresholds and the force majeure exemption; how penalties are allocated by cause; limitation periods and complaint deadlines
game.bigGame: Takes disputes from all roles: contractors' claims, penalties, passenger claims, accidents. Gives payments and reserves to the finance controller, contract templates to procurement and the bid manager, and precedents that change future claims.

roles.name: Press officer
roles.organisation: Communications department of a railway company (e.g. a DB regional press office or a private railway)
roles.summary: Speaks to the media for the company: answers journalists, writes press releases and briefs the board for interviews. In a crisis (an accident, a long disruption, a strike, a closure for works) decides within minutes what can be said, by whom and when.
decisions: Issue a holding statement within the first 30 minutes of an incident, or wait for verified facts
Decide which facts to confirm (number of injured, cause, duration) and which to leave to the police, fire service, prosecutor or BEU
Choose the spokesperson (press office, regional manager or the board) and whether to go on camera
Announce bad news proactively (a closure for works, a timetable cut) or react only when it leaks
Answer false reports, and decide whether to demand a right of reply (Gegendarstellung) under the press laws
Coordinate with passenger information so that the press and the stations say the same thing
effects: The company's reputation and trust; political pressure on the board and the ministry
Passengers informed and replanning in time, or stranded and angry
Investigations left unprejudiced; the privacy of staff and victims protected or violated
resources: A team of 2-20 with an around-the-clock on-call roster
Facts from the operations centre, the emergency manager and the incident commander
Channels: press releases, social media, website, interviews; campaign budgets of tens to hundreds of thousands of euros
limits: The Länder press laws (the press's right to information, which courts have extended to companies controlled by the state)
Personality rights and the right to one's own image (KUG §§ 22-23), GDPR: no naming of victims or staff
Police and fire service lead at an incident and speak about victims; no statements on causes while the BEU and the prosecutor investigate (practice and legal advice)
Defamation and damage to credit (StGB §§ 186-187, BGB § 824): no false claims about unions, contractors or other railways, also during a strike
risks: Public exposure: one wrong statement can go viral and end a career
24/7 availability, high stress, burnout
Conflicts with the legal department and the board

career.entry: A degree (journalism, communications, political science, sometimes engineering) and a traineeship in journalism or PR; often several years as a journalist
career.chances: About 55,000-100,000 € a year; head of communications 120,000-200,000 €. Moves to ministries, associations and politics are common.

kpis: Share of positive or neutral coverage
roles.timescale: Minutes in a crisis; days for campaigns

game.title: The First Hour (Die erste Stunde)
game.loop: A disruption from ARail's scenarios unfolds: the maintenance story's signal failure and track closure, a person struck by a train, or a storm. Facts arrive one at a time, each with a confidence level from the simulation, while journalists' questions and social media posts appear in the town's news feed. Every few minutes the player picks statement cards (confirm, deny, no comment, refer to the police), a speaker and a channel. The journeys module shows travellers reacting to what was said.
game.win: Passed if, after the hour, trust (from simulated coverage) is high, nothing false was said, no privacy was breached, nobody speculated on causes, and travellers were informed (the share who replanned in time). A wrong casualty figure or a named victim fails the round. In the career mode: head of communications, or a move into politics.
game.knowledge: Who speaks on what at an incident (police, fire service, BEU, prosecutor, company); press law basics; personality rights; how a holding statement is built
game.bigGame: Takes incidents from the emergency manager and network control, and questions from journalists. Gives reputation, which affects ridership in the simulator and the attention of politicians, and the quality of passenger information.

roles.name: Digital rail programme manager (ETCS, digital interlockings)
roles.organisation: Infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO, the Digitale Schiene Deutschland programme), funded by the Bund
roles.summary: Leads a programme that equips lines and nodes with ETCS and digital interlockings (DSTW). Sequences the rollout and coordinates the signalling industry, the railway undertakings' vehicle retrofits, funding, approvals and possessions, and decides, once the authorisations are in place, when a section goes live.
decisions: Prioritise sections and nodes (e.g. a TEN-T corridor or a digital node) and sequence them with the corridor renewals
Choose and freeze technical baselines: ETCS Level 2 with or without lineside signals (L2mS, L2oS), Baseline 3 or the Baseline 4 of the 2023 TSI CCS, ATO, FRMCS
Set the contract strategy: frameworks with the signalling industry, standard interfaces (EULYNX), lots
Agree the retrofit timeline with railway undertakings and vehicle keepers, and propose a federal funding scheme for onboard units to the ministry (the Bund decides)
Accept or reject a change (software release, scope) with its cost and delay
Decide on commissioning once the safety case, the assessors' reports and the EBA's authorisation for placing into service are in, or postpone it
effects: Capacity and punctuality gains from shorter headways, or delays and cost overruns
Vehicles without ETCS are locked out of equipped lines once the class B systems (PZB, LZB) are switched off
Industry capacity tied up; legacy interlockings kept alive longer
Political pressure and federal budget decisions
resources: Programme budgets in billions of euros: a digital node about 1 to several bn €, one digital interlocking area tens of millions; a vehicle retrofit several hundred thousand euros per vehicle
A team of 50-500, including consultants and industry staff
Funding: the federal budget (BSWAG, LuFV, the 2025 special fund for infrastructure) and EU co-funding (CEF)
limits: TSI CCS (Reg. (EU) 2023/1695), Interoperability Directive (EU) 2016/797 (including the ERA's prior approval of ETCS trackside specifications, Art. 19), TEN-T Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 with its ETCS deadlines (core network 2030, extended core 2040, comprehensive 2050)
CSM-RA with an assessor (AsBo), conformity assessment (NoBo, DeBo), the EBA's authorisation for placing into service
CENELEC EN 50126, EN 50716 (successor of EN 50128) and EN 50129 (safety integrity); IT security (BSI Act and KRITIS rules, NIS2, IEC 62443, CLC/TS 50701)
Procurement law (GWB, SektVO), the funding agreements and proof of use, possessions planned years ahead (Ril 406)
risks: Public exposure for delays and overruns (Bundestag questions, press)
Responsibility for go-live decisions with safety and operational consequences
High stress and long hours; career risk when a programme is reset

career.entry: An engineering degree (electrical, transport or computer science), 10+ years in signalling or large projects, a programme management certification (PMI, IPMA, PRINCE2/MSP)
career.chances: Out of tariff about 110,000-180,000 € a year; heads of large programmes 200,000 € and more. ETCS skills are in very high demand across Europe.

kpis: Safety case accepted without major findings
roles.timescale: Quarters to a decade: milestones quarterly, commissionings yearly, the programme 10-15 years

game.title: Going Digital (Digitaler Knoten)
game.loop: Quarterly turns over ten years on the lab's network. The player sequences sections for ETCS and a digital interlocking, books possessions, contracts industry capacity and negotiates with railway undertakings over retrofitting their fleets, whose funding the ministry grants or refuses. Every quarter brings uncertainty: a software baseline change, a late assessor report, a supplier short of engineers, legacy relay interlockings failing more often (from the asset game). Before each go-live the player decides whether to commission with open findings or postpone.
game.win: Passed if, at the end, capacity and punctuality have improved, the overrun is below 20 % and no railway undertaking is locked out. Commissioning a section with an unresolved safety finding fails the round. In the career mode: a post at the ERA or in the ministry.
game.knowledge: ETCS levels and modes; the authorisation chain (ERA trackside approval, NoBo, DeBo, AsBo, EBA); TEN-T deadlines; dependencies between trackside and onboard equipment; critical path and risk buffers
game.bigGame: Takes federal funding from the funding officer and the Bundestag, industry capacity and possessions. Gives equipped lines (more capacity, new failure modes) to the operations and signaller games, and retrofit requirements and costs to the railway undertakings' fleets.

roles.name: Management and engineering consultant
roles.organisation: Management or engineering consultancy, from small engineering offices to large firms
roles.summary: Works for clients across the system (ministries, transport authorities, infrastructure managers, railway undertakings, industry). Delivers studies, cost-benefit assessments, timetable and capacity analyses, project management support, restructurings and bid support, sold by the person-day or for a fixed fee.
decisions: Decide which tenders and clients to pursue, and at what price (day rates or a fixed fee)
Scope the study and choose the methods: counts, demand model, timetable simulation, cost-benefit assessment
Staff the project: seniors or juniors, and how many days
Accept or refuse scope creep and the client's wish for a particular result
Present uncertain results honestly, or smooth them
Decide whether a conflict of interest (advising both sides, or bidding later for the work the study prepares) rules out a mandate
effects: Clients decide on the strength of the study: a line reactivated, a node rebuilt, a tender designed
The consultancy's margin, reputation and follow-up mandates
Public money spent on the basis of the benefit-cost ratio
resources: Day rates of 900-2,500 €; projects of 50-2,000 person-days
A team of 2-20; tools such as demand models, timetable software and cost databases
Authority: none of its own, only the client's trust
limits: The standardised assessment (Standardisierte Bewertung, version 2016+) for public transport funding under the GVFG, including reactivations; the methods of the federal transport infrastructure plan (BVWP)
HOAI for engineering services (since 2021 its fees are orientation values, no longer binding); BGB (service or work contract); procurement law on the prior involvement of bidders (SektVO § 7)
Labour leasing act (AÜG) and bogus self-employment rules when embedded at the client
Confidentiality, compliance and conflict-of-interest rules
risks: Liability and reputational damage for a wrong study; exclusion from tenders
Long hours, travel, pressure to sell
The up-or-out career model

career.entry: A degree in transport engineering, economics or business; graduates start as junior consultants, experienced railway staff join as senior experts
career.chances: Junior about 55,000-70,000 €, senior 80,000-110,000 €, manager 110,000-160,000 €, partner 200,000 € and more. Many move to a client organisation after 3-6 years.

roles.timescale: Weeks to months per project

game.title: The Study (Das Gutachten)
game.loop: The client asks whether the branch line to the town should be reactivated. The player bids a fixed fee, then spends a budget of person-days on analyses that each reveal information: passenger counts and the town's demand (town and passengers), a timetable concept (operations), a cost estimate (infrastructure). Midway, the mayor and the transport authority push for a benefit-cost ratio above 1. The player decides what to deliver and how to present the uncertainty.
game.win: Passed if the margin is positive, the study is delivered on time and the benefit-cost ratio is computed correctly; the true value is revealed when the computer simulates the reopened line. Cooked numbers may please the client now, but a review exposes them, which fails the round with a loss of reputation. In the career mode: partner, or a move to a client.
game.knowledge: The logic of the standardised assessment (benefits from travel time savings, operating costs, emissions and accidents; funding needs a benefit-cost ratio above 1); demand estimation; cost estimating; the value of information
game.bigGame: Takes assignments from politicians, transport authorities, infrastructure managers and railway undertakings. Gives the studies and assessments that decide funding, tenders and projects.

roles.name: EBA-recognised checking engineer and inspector (structures, signalling, electrical)
roles.name_de: Vom EBA anerkannte/r Prüfer/in für bautechnische Nachweise bzw. Prüfsachverständige/r (LST, EIT)
roles.organisation: Independent expert or engineering firm, recognised by the EBA
roles.summary: An independent engineer recognised by the EBA. Checks the designs and calculations of railway structures (bridges, tunnels, earthworks) or of signalling, telecommunications and electrical installations, then their execution and acceptance tests, before the EBA, as construction supervision authority, lets them into service. The EBA relies on the inspector's report; it does not plan or design itself.
decisions: Accept the design documents, return them with defects, or demand recalculations
Release a partial check to keep the construction schedule, or refuse until everything is complete
Classify each finding: a defect that must be fixed, a condition, or a note
Choose how deep to review, and where to place spot checks where the risk is highest
On site: accept an interlocking's acceptance tests (route tables, signal aspects, overlaps, flank protection) or demand repeats
Turn down a mandate because of a conflict of interest
effects: Design errors found before they are built, or an unsafe structure or interlocking in service
Commissioning on time or postponed, with possessions lost and trains delayed
Rework costs for the planner and the contractor
resources: Own time and a small team (1-10 engineers); fees by contract, roughly 100-200 € an hour
Calculation software and test tools; access to design and test documents
Authority: no approval without the inspector's report
limits: EBA administrative rules on construction supervision: VV BAU (structures, track) and VV BAU-STE (signalling, telecommunications, electrical); the railway list of technical building rules (ELTB)
EBO § 2 (generally recognised rules of technology), Eurocodes with national annexes, DB guidelines (Ril 804 bridges, Ril 819 signalling planning, Ril 997 catenary)
Conditions of the EBA recognition: qualification, experience, independence, liability insurance
risks: Criminal liability after a collapse or accident (StGB § 319 endangering construction safety, §§ 222, 229)
Civil liability; loss of the EBA recognition
Pressure from clients and project managers to sign quickly

career.entry: An engineering degree (civil or electrical), typically 10 or more years designing or building railway structures or signalling, and EBA recognition after a check of qualifications
career.chances: Employed about 70,000-110,000 € a year; as partner or self-employed 100,000-180,000 €. Few people are qualified and demand is high.

kpis: Defects found per review, and defects missed but found later
No defect in operation traced back to a review
roles.timescale: Days to weeks per review; hours to days for a site acceptance

game.title: Check the Plan (Planprüfung)
game.loop: The player receives a design package for the lab's station with planted errors: a signalling plan (signal positions, overlaps, distant signal distances, route table entries, flank protection) or a bridge's load case summary. Against a deadline set by the project's possession, the player marks and classifies findings, then signs or refuses. In a second phase a site acceptance test runs on the signaller game's interlocking, and the player chooses which routes and flank protections to test.
game.win: Scored on errors found (weighted by danger), false alarms (which cost the client) and time. Signing a package that contains a dangerous error fails the round, and the error later appears as an incident in operations. Refusing too much costs the possession and the client. In the career mode: assessor or professor.
game.knowledge: Overlaps (typically 200 m on main lines, shorter at low speeds) and braking distances; signal spacing (the distant signal usually 1000 m before the main signal); route tables and flank protection; load cases and safety factors; the review procedure under VV BAU and VV BAU-STE
game.bigGame: Takes design packages from planners and the signalling industry. Gives the review reports that the EBA's authorisation needs and delays to projects; an error that slips through becomes a latent fault in operations.

roles.name: Railway researcher
roles.organisation: University chair (e.g. the Chair of Railway Operations at TU Dresden), DLR, the DZSF (the German Centre for Rail Traffic Research at the EBA) or a Fraunhofer institute
roles.summary: A research associate at a university or research institute, usually working towards a doctorate. Studies questions of railway operations, capacity, digitalisation or safety with models, lab experiments and data, delivers to funded projects, and teaches in the lab and in tutorials.
decisions: Choose the research question and the method: simulation, lab experiment, field data or survey
Design experiments in the lab or the operations simulation: scenarios, number of runs and seeds, measures
Decide what data to request from industry partners under a non-disclosure agreement
Balance project deliverables, the thesis, teaching and supervising students
Publish now (conference) or later (journal), and decide what to share openly
Apply for follow-up funding, or leave for industry
effects: New methods and evidence used by infrastructure managers, authorities and industry
Trained students; a doctorate
Project funding for the chair secured or lost
resources: A position (often 65-100 %) for about 3 years; a project budget for travel, equipment and student assistants (tens of thousands of euros)
The lab, simulation tools and computing; the supervisor's time
limits: Fixed-term contracts in science (WissZeitVG): limits before and after the doctorate
Good research practice (DFG code), doctoral regulations, data protection, confidentiality agreements
Funding rules of the DFG, federal ministries, the DZSF and EU Horizon Europe / Europe's Rail; Employee Inventions Act (special rules for universities, § 42)
risks: Job loss when the contract ends; chains of short contracts
Overwork, a failed doctorate, allegations of scientific misconduct

career.entry: A Diplom or Master in transport engineering or a related field; hired by a chair for a project; doctorate in 4-6 years
career.chances: TV-L E13, about 4,500-6,500 € a month full time (often part time during the doctorate). With a doctorate, good chances in industry and authorities; few professorships.

roles.timescale: Weeks to years: experiments weekly, papers over months, the doctorate over years

game.title: Significant (Signifikant)
game.loop: A research project starts from a question from practice: does a stand-by driver at the depot pay off, does condition monitoring reduce delay? The player designs experiments with ARail's comparing setups, choosing setups, stress tests, days and runs per setup within a computing and time budget. The player reads the results with their spread and decides whether the difference is real. Meanwhile project milestones, teaching duties and the end of the contract draw closer.
game.win: Passed with a correct conclusion (the simulation's hidden truth) backed by enough runs, the deliverable on time and a paper accepted. Claiming an effect that is only noise (too few runs, cherry-picked seeds) fails the round when a reviewer reruns the experiment. In the career mode: a doctorate, then professor, consultant or industry.
game.knowledge: Experimental design; variance and confidence intervals; common random numbers (the same seeds); operational measures such as punctuality and delay minutes; research ethics
game.bigGame: Takes questions and data from infrastructure managers, railway undertakings and funders. Gives findings that unlock better rules or technologies in other roles' games (a dispatching rule, a maintenance interval), and trained graduates.

roles.name: Professor of railway engineering and operations
roles.organisation: University (e.g. TU Dresden, Faculty of Transport and Traffic Sciences "Friedrich List") or a university of applied sciences
roles.summary: Heads a chair: teaches the next generation of railway engineers, leads research and raises its funding, runs the lab, and advises politics and industry as an independent expert.
decisions: Set the research agenda and choose which proposals to write (DFG, federal ministries, EU, industry)
Hire and supervise research associates and doctoral students; renew or end their contracts
Design the curriculum and exams, including what is taught in the lab
Invest in the lab (e.g. a digital interlocking or ETCS equipment) or in staff
Accept expert roles: parliamentary hearings, commissions, expert opinions, advisory boards
Decide whether to accept industry funding, and on what terms for independence and publication
effects: Graduates and their competence across the sector
Methods and evidence that shape rules, timetables and investments
Public debate and policy decisions informed by expert opinions
resources: A chair budget of 50,000-200,000 € a year plus 2-6 state-funded positions
Third-party funding of 0.5-3 m € a year; a staff of 5-30
The lab, the students, reputation and networks
limits: State higher education law (in Saxony the Sächsisches Hochschulgesetz, SächsHSG, which replaced the SächsHSFG in 2023) and the teaching load ordinance (8-9 hours a week at universities, 18 at universities of applied sciences)
Civil service law and the rules on secondary employment (expert opinions, consulting)
Study and examination regulations, accreditation, good research practice, funding rules
risks: Reputational risk from expert opinions and conflicts of interest
Pressure to raise funds for staff; responsibility for other people's contracts
Little personal job risk once appointed as a civil servant

career.entry: A doctorate plus habilitation or equivalent achievements (junior professorship, leading positions in industry), then an appointment procedure; universities of applied sciences require 5 years of professional practice, 3 of them outside academia
career.chances: W2/W3 pay of about 7,000-10,000 € a month as a civil servant plus performance bonuses, with extra income from expert opinions. Few positions, but appointed for life; after retirement often still active as an expert.

roles.timescale: Semesters and years: lectures weekly, proposals yearly, research programmes over 5-10 years

game.title: The Chair (Der Lehrstuhl)
game.loop: Semester turns over 6-10 years. The player splits the chair's time and money between teaching, proposals, staff and the lab. Proposals succeed with a probability that depends on the chair's publications and partners; industry offers money with strings attached (confidentiality, a desired result). Researchers, each with their own career, finish or leave, and students rate the courses. A parliamentary hearing asks for an opinion on a hot topic (the Generalsanierung, a tender, ETCS) under media scrutiny.
game.win: Passed if the chair stays funded, a set number of doctorates and graduates is reached, teaching evaluations are good and the expert reputation stays high. Taking a contract that suppresses unfavourable results, and being exposed, fails the round. In the career mode this is the end of a career; its legacy in the big game is the graduates and the rules the expert helped shape.
game.knowledge: How research funding works; balancing independence and funding; supervision and curriculum design; the substance of the expert topics (questions on rail policy)
game.bigGame: Takes questions from politics and industry, and funds from ministries. Gives graduates (the skill levels students carry into the career mode), expert opinions that influence politicians' decisions, and lab improvements.

roles.name: Student of transport engineering
roles.organisation: University (e.g. the Diplom in Verkehrsingenieurwesen at TU Dresden)
roles.summary: Studies transport engineering (e.g. the 10-semester Diplom at TU Dresden): railway operations, infrastructure, vehicles, planning and economics, with exercises in the railway operations lab, internships and a thesis. Often works alongside as a student assistant or working student.
decisions: Choose courses and a specialisation (e.g. railway systems, Bahnsysteme; planning; logistics)
Decide which exams to take this semester, and when to retake
Balance study time against a job as working student or student assistant
Choose the internship and the thesis topic, at the chair or with a company
Join lab exercises, student societies, or a signaller course in the lab
effects: Grades, time to graduation, the first job
Contacts in the sector that shape the career
As a student assistant: support for research projects and lab sessions
resources: Time: about 1,800 hours a year (60 ECTS credits)
Money: BAföG (up to about 1,000 € a month), working student jobs (15-22 € an hour), scholarships
Access to the lab, lectures, professors and alumni
limits: Study and examination regulations: a limited number of exam attempts; failing the last one ends the degree and bars the same subject elsewhere
BAföG rules (half grant, half interest-free loan, repayment capped); working students keep their social insurance privilege only up to 20 hours a week during the semester
Lab rules (electrical safety, conduct at the panels)
risks: Failing an exam at the last attempt; debt; stress and overload
Little personal liability; occasional accidents on site visits

career.entry: A university entrance qualification (Abitur), or a vocational qualification with work experience (e.g. after the railway apprenticeship)
career.chances: Graduates start at about 48,000-60,000 € a year (DB trainee programmes, consultancies, authorities, industry); unemployment is close to zero.

roles.timescale: Weeks and semesters

game.title: Semester in the Lab (Semester im Labor)
game.loop: A semester played in weeks. The player divides time between lectures, the lab, a job and rest, and meets exams as short games: headway and capacity calculations, braking distances, timetable construction, signals and rules, plus a lab exercise played in the signaller game at training level. Money and stress limit what is possible; an internship offer and a thesis topic come up along the way.
game.win: Passed with enough credits and exams at the end of the semester; failing an exam at the last attempt ends the round. The grade and the topics passed become the player's qualifications in the career mode and open first jobs as planner, consultant or researcher.
game.knowledge: Basics of railway operations and engineering: minimum headway (blocking time), train resistance and braking, signals and Ril 408, capacity (UIC 406), timetables and connections, cost-benefit basics
game.bigGame: The entry point of the career mode. Takes the curriculum from the professor; gives graduates with qualifications to the planning, engineering and management roles.

roles.name: Occupational physician (fitness for duty)
roles.organisation: Occupational medical service of a railway group, or an external service whose doctors are recognised for TfV examinations
roles.summary: Examines staff in safety-critical railway jobs (drivers, signallers, shunters, track workers) for fitness for duty, at hiring and periodically, and decides fit, fit with conditions or unfit. As company physician under the ASiG also advises on health at work, shift work and return after illness, under strict medical confidentiality.
decisions: Decide: fit, fit with conditions (glasses, hearing aid, shorter interval), temporarily unfit or permanently unfit
Order further tests: ophthalmologist, sleep apnoea screening, drug and alcohol tests, cardiology
Judge medication and chronic illness (insulin-treated diabetes, epilepsy, heart disease) against the requirements
Advise on return to work after long illness and on adapted duties (workplace reintegration, BEM)
Advise the employer on shift work, risk assessments and vaccinations
effects: Unfit staff kept away from safety-critical tasks, or a risk overlooked
Staff available or lost: a driver declared permanently unfit loses the job role and needs another one
Disputes and appeals; trust between staff and the medical service
resources: 30-60 minutes per examination; thousands of examinations a year in a large service
Diagnostic equipment: vision and colour vision tests, audiometry, ECG, lab
Authority: the fitness verdict; the employer learns only the verdict, never the diagnosis
limits: TfV and Directive 2007/59/EC Annex II: medical requirements (e.g. distance visual acuity 1.0 with correction, at least 0.5 in the worse eye; colour vision; hearing); examinations at least every 3 years up to age 55, then yearly
EBO §§ 47-48 (fitness of operating staff); the DB group's fitness rules (Ril 107); VDV-Schrift 714 for other railways

Ordinance on occupational medical care (ArbMedVV) and Occupational Safety Act (ASiG): occupational health care (Vorsorge) is not a fitness test, its result stays with the employee; fitness examinations need their own legal basis such as the TfV or the EBO
Medical confidentiality (StGB § 203), GDPR Art. 9 for health data
Zero alcohol in safety-critical service under company rules; rules on cannabis and medication
risks: Liability and criminal investigation if an unfit person causes an accident (e.g. with a known seizure risk)
Management pressure to declare staff fit during shortages
Disputes with staff who lose their job role

career.entry: A medical degree (6 years), specialist training in occupational medicine (5 years), recognition for TfV examinations
career.chances: Employed about 7,000-11,000 € a month; more as head of a medical service. Occupational physicians are scarce and the job is secure.

roles.timescale: Minutes per examination; days for follow-up tests

game.title: Fit for Duty? (Tauglich?)
game.loop: A clinic day. Patient files arrive one by one: a 56-year-old driver with new glasses, a signaller on new medication, an applicant's colour vision result, a shunter after a heart attack. Each comes with findings and a request from the crew planner, who needs the person on duty. The player orders tests (costing time and money) and gives a verdict with conditions. Behind each verdict a hidden risk plays out in the operations simulation over the following months.
game.win: Scored on correct verdicts against the requirements (knowledge), as few unnecessary exclusions as possible (each one costs a driver) and confidentiality kept (telling the manager a diagnosis is a breach). An unfit person in a safety-critical job who causes an incident fails the round.
game.knowledge: The medical requirements of the TfV and Ril 107 (vision, colour vision, hearing, excluding conditions); examination intervals by age; occupational health care versus fitness examination; medical confidentiality
game.bigGame: Takes new staff from the HR recruiter and periodic checks from the crew planner. Gives fitness (available or not) to the crews of the railway undertaking's simulator and to the infrastructure's signallers, and risks to the safety manager.

roles.name: Railway psychologist (aptitude, care after accidents)
roles.name_de: Psychologe / Psychologin im Bahnbereich (Eignung, Betreuung nach Unfällen)
roles.organisation: Medical and psychological service of a railway group, or an external service recognised for TfV examinations
roles.summary: Assesses applicants' aptitude for safety-critical jobs (drivers, signallers) with tests and interviews, and cares for staff after traumatic events, above all drivers whose train has struck a person: first care, return to work, referral to therapy. Also runs programmes against aggression and stress.
decisions: Choose the test battery and judge the results: attention, reaction, multitasking, stress tolerance, personality
Give the aptitude verdict: suitable, suitable with conditions, not suitable
After a person is struck: arrange first care within hours, recommend the days off and when the driver first rides with a colleague
Refer to psychotherapy through the accident insurer, and judge when the person is fit again
Set up peer support (colleagues trained in psychological first aid) and anti-aggression training for conductors and security staff
effects: Fewer human errors from unsuitable staff, or candidates rejected whom staffing needs
Drivers back on duty in good health, or post-traumatic stress, sick leave and early retirement
Crew availability and a culture of care
resources: Computer-based test batteries (about half a day per candidate) and interviews
A few psychologists for thousands of staff, plus peer supporters and the accident insurer's therapists
Authority: the aptitude verdict and recommendations on return to work
limits: TfV and Directive 2007/59/EC (psychological fitness of train drivers), Ril 107, VDV-Schrift 714
DIN 33430 (requirements for job-related aptitude assessment)

Occupational Safety Act § 5 (assessment of mental stress); Social Code VII (a traumatic event at work is a work accident, with care by the accident insurer: the UVB for DB, the BG Verkehr for most private railways, using the DGUV psychotherapist procedure)
Confidentiality (StGB § 203); the Psychotherapists Act if licensed
risks: Vicarious trauma; on-call duty at night
Liability if an unsuitable person causes an accident; disputes over rejected candidates
Caught between the employer's needs and the employee's health

career.entry: A Master or Diplom in psychology, often with a specialisation in traffic or work psychology, or a licensed psychotherapist; recognition for TfV examinations
career.chances: About 4,500-7,500 € a month; more as head of a psychological service. A secure job, and human factors experience is valued in safety roles.

kpis: Validity of aptitude verdicts (later errors and dropouts)
Time to first care after an event
Return-to-work rate and sick days after traumatic events
roles.timescale: Hours after an event; days to months of care; half a day per aptitude test

game.title: After the Impact (Nach dem Personenunfall)
game.loop: Two halves. Aptitude: the player sets the cut-off scores of a test battery for 40 applicants. A strict cut-off rejects people the HR recruiter needs; a loose one admits some who will make errors, and the hidden base rate shows later in operations. Care: in a disruption scenario a person is struck by a train. The player organises first care and recommends the driver's days off, the first ride with a colleague and therapy, while the crew planner presses for an early return.
game.win: Aptitude is scored on accuracy against the hidden truth and on meeting the staff need. Care is passed if the driver returns healthy (low PTSD risk) without unnecessary absence; sending the driver back too early raises the risk of a breakdown or an error, which fails the round. In the career mode: head of the service, or a human factors role in safety.
game.knowledge: Base rates and false positives and negatives; signs of acute stress and PTSD; the accident insurance procedure; peer support
game.bigGame: Takes applicants from HR and incidents from the emergency manager. Gives suitable candidates and returning or absent drivers to the crews of the railway undertaking's simulator, and human factors findings to the safety manager.

roles.name: Railway operations apprentice
roles.organisation: Railway company (infrastructure manager or railway undertaking) together with a vocational school
roles.summary: The most common way into railway operations, and the career mode's entry point for operations staff. A 3-year dual apprenticeship (Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst) at the company, the vocational school and the training centre, ending with the exam at the chamber of commerce (IHK). The track field (Fachrichtung Fahrweg) leads to signaller, the driver and transport field (Fachrichtung Lokführer und Transport) to train driver.
decisions: Choose the field: track (signaller) or driver and transport
Choose the depot or signal box for the practical parts
Split time between rules, practical shifts and exam preparation
In practice, when unsure: ask, or act (in the signal box under supervision)
After the exam: accept the job offered, or go on to a master craftsman or Fachwirt qualification or a degree
effects: A signaller or driver ready after three years, or a dropout
Early habits that shape later safety

The company's own pipeline of operations staff: an apprentice costs several tens of thousands of euros a year in pay, trainers and school time, but is cheaper and more loyal than a driver poached from a competitor
resources: Apprentice pay of about 1,200-1,450 € a month (EVG tariff at DB), free travel
Trainers, the training centre's simulators and lab, the vocational school
limits: Vocational Training Act (BBiG), the training ordinance for Eisenbahner/in im Betriebsdienst, Youth Employment Protection Act (JArbSchG) for those under 18
Medical and psychological fitness checks (Ril 107, TfV); the minimum age for the train driver licence (Directive 2007/59/EC: 20, or 18 with validity limited to the issuing state)
Ril 408, the signal rules, safety rules on the track
risks: Injury on the track or while shunting; failing the exam
Shift work from the start

career.entry: A school-leaving certificate (often intermediate level or Abitur) and passed aptitude and medical tests
career.chances: After the exam, signallers and drivers start at about 3,300-3,800 € a month on the tariff plus allowances. Jobs are secure; further training leads to master craftsman or Fachwirt qualifications or a degree.

roles.timescale: Weeks per module; three years overall

game.title: Three Years in Three Shifts (Drei Lehrjahre)
game.loop: Three short rounds, one per training year: a shunting shift with hand signals and coupling (safety first); a signal box shift at the signaller game's training level with a mentor who answers questions at a cost in time; and the final exam with rule and calculation questions. Between rounds the player chooses where to spend practice time.
game.win: Passed with the IHK exam and the practical assessment. A danger to people during a practical round ends it, and the round must be repeated. In the career mode: the first job as signaller or train driver.
game.knowledge: Signals and hand signals, Ril 408 basics, shunting rules, safety on the track
game.bigGame: The career mode's entry into operations. Takes training places from HR and the instructors; gives new signallers and drivers.

roles.name: Occupational safety specialist
roles.organisation: Railway company (infrastructure manager, railway undertaking, workshop), a rail construction contractor, or an external safety service
roles.summary: Advises the employer on the safety and health of its own workers under the Occupational Safety Act (ASiG): risk assessments for track work, shunting, catenary, workshops and shift work, site and workshop inspections, accident investigations and safety instructions. Distinct from the safety manager (the safety of railway operations under the SMS) and from the track safety supervisor (who runs the protection on site): the Sifa advises and has no command; the duty stays with the employer and the line managers.
decisions: Decide which hazards a risk assessment must cover and propose measures in the order the law sets (STOP: substitution, technical, organisational, personal), e.g. working in a closed track instead of under lookout warning

Review the track safety plans (Sicherungspläne) against the order of protective measures (closing the track, fencing it off, automatic warning systems, lookouts only last) and object where lookouts are planned although noise or sight lines make their warning unreliable
Inspect sites, depots and workshops and report hazards; recommend stopping unsafe work to the line manager, who decides
Investigate work accidents and near misses (struck by a train, electric shock at the catenary, crushing between buffers, falls from vehicle roofs) and propose measures
Choose personal protective equipment (high-visibility clothing class 3, safety shoes, hearing protection) and plan the yearly safety instructions
Prepare the quarterly occupational safety committee (ASA) with the physician, the works council and management
effects: Fewer injured and killed workers, or a fatal accident and a prosecutor at the site
Closures and fencing cost possessions, capacity and money; lookouts are cheap but the weakest protection
Accident insurance contributions and sickness absence
The works council's trust and the staff's acceptance of rules
resources: Care time set by DGUV Regulation 2 (in high-risk groups such as track construction about 2.5 hours per employee a year for basic care), so one Sifa covers a few hundred to a few thousand staff
No budget of its own beyond PPE and training; measures are paid from line budgets
Accident statistics, near-miss reports, measuring devices (noise, dust)
Authority: advice and the right to be heard; if the employer rejects a proposal it must give reasons in writing (ASiG § 8(3))
limits: Occupational Safety Act (ASiG §§ 5-8, 11: appointment, tasks, qualification, independence, the safety committee) and DGUV Regulation 2
Occupational Safety and Health Act (ArbSchG §§ 3-6 risk assessment and documentation, § 12 instruction); DGUV Regulation 1

DGUV Regulation 78 (work in the area of tracks) and DB Ril 132.0118 (protection of work in the track area); DGUV Regulation 3 (electrical installations); the Industrial Safety Regulation (BetrSichV), the Hazardous Substances Ordinance (GefStoffV, e.g. creosote sleepers, quartz dust)
Construction Site Ordinance (BaustellV): a health and safety coordinator (SiGeKo) when several employers work on one site
SGB VII § 193: accident report to the accident insurer (UVB, BG Verkehr or BG BAU) for more than 3 days' incapacity; works council co-determination (BetrVG § 87(1) no. 7)
risks: Criminal investigation after a fatal accident if wrong advice contributed (StGB §§ 222, 229), although the main duty lies with the employer
Exposure on sites next to running trains and live catenary
Being ignored under production pressure; conflict with site managers and planners

career.entry: An engineer, technician or master craftsman with at least 2 years' practice, plus the Sifa training of the accident insurers (about 6-12 months part time)
career.chances: About 55,000-85,000 € a year; head of occupational safety in a large company 90,000-130,000 €. Demand is steady.

kpis: Lost-time injuries per million hours worked, and reportable accidents per 1,000 workers
roles.timescale: Days to a year: inspections weekly, accident investigations within days, the safety committee quarterly

game.title: Safe in the Track (Sicher im Gleis)
game.loop: A week of work from the asset management game and the maintenance story: a signal repair next to a running track, a night tamping shift, vegetation cutting under the catenary, a workshop job on a vehicle roof. For each job the player marks the hazards on the site plan (adjacent track open, catenary live, machine noise drowning out horns, darkness, poor sight lines), reviews the planned protection and proposes changes, each with a cost in possession time or money. The shifts then run against a hidden risk model; near misses and accidents happen, and the player investigates them and proposes measures, which line managers accept or reject with reasons.
game.win: Passed if nobody is killed or seriously injured, the protection follows the legal order of measures, and the extra possession time stays within the budget. Accepting lookout warning where the noise of the machines makes it unreliable fails the round, as does a missed electrical hazard. In the career mode: head of occupational safety, or a move to the safety management system.
game.knowledge: The STOP order of measures; the order of protection for work near tracks (DGUV Regulation 78, Ril 132.0118); the danger zone that grows with line speed; the five safety rules for electrical work; accident reporting and the accident insurers
game.bigGame: Takes work plans and possessions from the asset manager and the possession planner. Gives protection requirements that cost possession time and capacity, accidents and injured staff (missing from crews and maintenance teams), and reports to the safety manager and the accident insurer.

roles.name: Compliance officer (anti-corruption and competition law)
roles.organisation: Compliance organisation of a railway group, an infrastructure manager or a large rail contractor or supplier
roles.summary: Prevents and uncovers corruption, bid rigging and competition law breaches, a real risk where billions are spent on construction and supplies (the rail cartel of the early 2010s cost suppliers about 230 m € in fines from the Federal Cartel Office). Runs the whistleblower channel, checks business partners, gifts and conflicts of interest, investigates suspicions and advises the board on reporting to the prosecutor, excluding suppliers and claiming damages.
decisions: Judge whether a whistleblower report is plausible, open an internal investigation and protect the reporter (acknowledge within 7 days, feedback within 3 months)
Approve or refuse gifts, invitations and secondary jobs under the code of conduct
Set the controls: four-eyes rules and rotation for buyers and construction supervisors, checks of business partners, the query of the competition register before awards
Choose the investigation steps within labour and data protection law (interviews, document review, data analysis only with cause and with the works council where required)
Recommend to the board: report to the prosecutor or the Federal Cartel Office, dismiss staff (within 2 weeks of knowing the facts), claim damages from cartel members
Advise procurement on whether a supplier's self-cleaning is enough to lift its exclusion
effects: Corruption and cartel damage avoided or recovered (cartels typically overcharge by 10-20 %)
Suppliers excluded, so less competition and higher prices for a while
Staff protected, or wrongly suspected and the works council in revolt
The company's reputation, and lower corporate fines when its compliance system works
resources: A team of 2-10 in a regional company, around a hundred in a large group; an external ombudsperson
A budget for forensic investigations (outside law firms and forensic accountants, 0.1 m € to several m € per large case)
Authority: investigation rights within labour law; no power of search or seizure, which belongs to the prosecutor
limits: Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG, 2023): reporting channels for employers with 50 or more staff, deadlines, ban on retaliation
GWB §§ 123-126 (mandatory and optional exclusion, self-cleaning, maximum periods of 5 and 3 years), Competition Register Act (WRegG), cartel damages (GWB §§ 33a ff.)
StGB § 298 (bid rigging), § 299 (commercial bribery), §§ 331-335 where public officials are involved
Administrative Offences Act (OWiG § 30 corporate fines, § 130 breach of supervisory duty); cartel fines up to 10 % of turnover (GWB § 81c)
GDPR and the BDSG for employee data in investigations; works council co-determination (BetrVG § 87(1) no. 6); BGB § 626(2): 2 weeks for a dismissal without notice
risks: Personal criminal liability as guarantor if known offences are not stopped (Federal Court of Justice, 2009)
Conflict with management; being sidelined or blamed when a scandal breaks
Data protection breaches in an investigation; lawsuits by wrongly accused staff

career.entry: A law degree (Volljurist), or business or auditing (internal audit, auditing firm), plus a compliance certification; several years in legal, audit or procurement
career.chances: About 70,000-130,000 € a year; chief compliance officer of a large group 150,000-250,000 €.

kpis: Cases closed and time to close
Reports received (a rising number is a sign of trust, not of more wrongdoing)
No fines or findings by prosecutors and the Cartel Office
roles.timescale: Days to years: reports daily, investigations over months, cartel damage cases over years

game.title: Clean Award (Saubere Vergabe)
game.loop: Over a year of the procurement and project games, signals appear: a buyer whose awards always go to the same contractor, bids in a tender that sit suspiciously close with identical typing errors, a supplementary claim signed off by a construction supervisor whose holiday a contractor paid, an anonymous whistleblower message. With a limited budget the player decides which signals to investigate and how, within labour and data protection law, interviews people and then decides: close, discipline, report to the prosecutor or the Cartel Office, exclude a supplier or accept its self-cleaning, claim damages.
game.win: Scored on real cases uncovered (the simulation's hidden truth), damages recovered, innocent staff not accused, and deadlines kept (7 days and 3 months for the whistleblower, 2 weeks for a dismissal). A case covered up and then exposed by the press, or an investigation that breaks data protection law, fails the round. In the career mode: chief compliance officer, or a move to legal.
game.knowledge: Indicators of bid rigging (cover bids, bid rotation, market sharing); exclusion grounds and self-cleaning; the competition register; HinSchG deadlines; the limits of internal investigations
game.bigGame: Takes awards, bids, claims and invoices from the procurement and project games. Gives excluded suppliers (less competition, higher prices), recovered damages to the finance controller, dismissed staff, and scandals or their absence to the press officer and the politicians.

roles.name: Environmental and noise protection manager
roles.organisation: Environmental department of the infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO) or of a large project, often with environmental planning firms
roles.summary: Makes sure that railway projects and maintenance comply with nature, species, noise and waste law, which often decides whether a project gets its planning approval on time. Commissions the environmental studies, plans avoidance and compensation measures, plans noise protection, handles contaminated soil and waste, and answers residents and environmental associations.
decisions: Commission the environmental studies for a project (species mapping over a full season, noise and vibration forecasts) and start them early enough not to delay planning approval
Propose avoidance and compensation measures: relocating protected species such as sand lizards, replacement habitats prepared in advance (CEF measures), building outside the breeding season
Plan noise protection: barrier heights, rail dampers, acoustic grinding, window insulation; propose sections for the voluntary federal noise remediation programme
Decide whether vegetation work in the breeding season is justified as a traffic-safety exception, or must wait until October
Classify and dispose of old ballast and sleepers (creosote-treated wooden sleepers are hazardous waste) and handle contaminated land
Answer residents' complaints (squealing curves, idling locomotives, night work) and decide on measures
effects: Planning approval granted, or lost in court and delayed by a year or more
Costs: species measures can run to thousands of euros per animal, noise barriers to millions per kilometre
Residents' acceptance of the railway and of night possessions
Fines and criminal cases for killed protected species or illegal waste disposal
resources: Environmental studies of 0.1 m € to several m € per major project; framework contracts with planning firms
Federal noise remediation money on the order of 100-200 m € a year for existing lines
Noise maps (the EBA maps the noise of the federal railways), species databases, the landscape plans
Authority: within the project, the environmental requirements; outside it, only advice and escalation
limits: Federal Nature Conservation Act (BNatSchG): § 39(5) no cutting of hedges and trees from 1 March to 30 September except for traffic safety and other listed cases; § 44 bans on killing or disturbing protected species and destroying their breeding sites, § 45(7) exceptions
Environmental Impact Assessment Act (UVPG) in planning approval; the Habitats and Birds Directives (Natura 2000)

BImSchG §§ 41-43 and the 16th BImSchV for new or substantially changed lines (59 dB(A) by day and 49 by night in residential areas; calculation with Schall 03, without the old rail bonus); voluntary noise remediation on existing lines; the Rail Noise Protection Act (no loud freight wagons since December 2020); the Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC
Circular Economy Act (KrWG), waste wood ordinance (creosote sleepers in category A IV), Soil Protection Act (BBodSchG), Water Resources Act (WHG), Plant Protection Act for herbicides on tracks
Criminal law on environmental offences (StGB §§ 324 ff., BNatSchG § 71)
risks: Blamed for project delays and costs
Criminal liability for killed protected species or illegal waste disposal
Public conflict with residents and environmental associations; hearings and lawsuits

career.entry: A degree in landscape planning, environmental engineering, biology, geography or civil engineering; several years in an environmental planning firm
career.chances: About 50,000-90,000 € a year; head of environment in a large company 100,000-140,000 €. Demand grows with the investment programme.

kpis: Waste and soil handled without findings
roles.timescale: Seasons and years: species mapping follows the seasons, planning approval takes years

game.title: Lizards and Decibels (Eidechsen und Dezibel)
game.loop: A project from the asset game (a second track past the town, a renewal with a new bridge) on a calendar of seasons. The player schedules the surveys (birds in spring, bats in summer, reptiles from spring to autumn), finds protected species with a probability, and chooses avoidance and compensation measures. Then the player plans noise protection for the houses along the line, trading barrier heights and window insulation against cost and the limits, computed by a simplified Schall 03. Residents and the environmental association object in the planning approval hearing, and vegetation must be cleared before the possession.
game.win: Passed if planning approval is granted and survives the lawsuit, the possession date is kept, the limits are met and the costs stay within budget. Clearing the site in the breeding season without a valid exception, or a survey season forgotten, fails the round: the administrative court stops the project for a year. In the career mode: a move to the EBA's planning approval, or project management.
game.knowledge: The species protection bans and their exceptions; the breeding season rule; noise limits and decibel arithmetic (two equal sources add 3 dB, twice the trains add 3 dB); the course of planning approval
game.bigGame: Takes projects and vegetation work from the asset manager, the major project manager and the vegetation coordinator. Gives approval delays, extra costs, seasonal limits on possessions, and residents' acceptance to the mayor and the politicians.

roles.name: Railway property manager (land and buildings)
roles.organisation: Land management of the infrastructure manager (DB InfraGO) or the DB group's real estate unit (DB Immobilien), or of a regional infrastructure manager
roles.summary: Manages the land and buildings of the railway: keeps what operations needs, buys land for projects, leases and sells the rest. Decides, with the authority and the Länder, whether a disused yard or trackbed is released from railway purposes, a decision that can make a later reactivation impossible.
decisions: Decide which surplus land and buildings to sell, lease or keep for future railway use (e.g. a former freight yard by the town centre, the old station building)
Apply for the release of land from railway purposes (Freistellung, AEG § 23), after asking the transport authority and the Land whether a reactivation or a siding might need it
Negotiate sales to the municipality for station-area developments, with buy-back rights or easements for future railway use
Acquire land for projects: negotiate with owners, or apply for expropriation (AEG § 22) once planning approval is granted
Lease land for sidings, terminals, solar parks, masts and cable crossings (Gestattungsverträge)
Offer an unused siding or freight yard (a service facility) for lease when a railway undertaking shows interest
effects: Sale proceeds and lease income, or land kept for the railway's future
A released and built-over trackbed can block a reactivation for good
Projects get their land on time, or wait for expropriation
Towns gain building land and a new station quarter
resources: A large portfolio of operational and surplus land; single deals from 0.1 m € to tens of millions
Land register, cadastre and the railway's land database; surveyors and valuers
Authority: within the company's approval limits; releases are decided by the planning authority (the EBA for federal railways)
limits: AEG § 11 (closing a line for good only after offering it publicly to other infrastructure managers, with the authority's approval), § 22 (expropriation for approved projects), § 23 (release from railway purposes only if no transport need exists and none is expected in the long term; the municipality may also apply)
BauGB § 38: land under railway planning approval is exempt from municipal land-use planning until it is released
ERegG and Directive 2012/34/EU Art. 13(7): a service facility unused for two years must be offered for lease when a railway undertaking shows interest
BGB, land register law (GBO), valuation rules; contaminated land (BBodSchG) and the seller's liability
The company's approval limits and compliance rules for sales below market value
risks: Public anger and political pressure when sold land blocks a reactivation
Corruption allegations around sales
Liability for contaminated land sold; long litigation

career.entry: A degree in real estate, surveying, law or business; real estate qualifications (e.g. valuation); several years in real estate or with a municipality
career.chances: About 55,000-100,000 € a year; head of a regional land office 100,000-140,000 €.

kpis: Land kept for reactivations and sidings (options not lost)
roles.timescale: Months to years: a sale takes months, a release from railway purposes a year or more

game.title: Sell the Yard? (Den Güterbahnhof verkaufen?)
game.loop: Yearly turns over 10-15 years with the land around the lab's town: a disused freight yard by the centre, the old station building, the trackbed of a closed branch line, a strip needed for a second track. Offers and requests arrive: the mayor wants the yard for housing, a logistics firm wants a siding, the Land studies reactivating the branch line, the project needs its strip by a deadline. The player sells, leases, keeps, applies for release, or negotiates and expropriates for the project. Hidden futures play out: a freight customer appears, the Land decides on the reactivation.
game.win: Scored on income, projects supplied with land on time, and railway options kept. Releasing and selling the trackbed of a line that the Land later reactivates fails the round (the reactivation then needs a new planning approval and costs many times more). In the career mode: head of the land office, or a move to a consultancy.
game.knowledge: Closure, release and expropriation under AEG §§ 11, 22 and 23; the planning privilege of railway land; the rule on unused service facilities; the option value of keeping land
game.bigGame: Takes land needs from projects and requests from mayors, terminals and sidings. Gives land (or its absence) for reactivations, sidings, terminals and developments, and sale income to the finance controller.
